Acton FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: October 15, 2026 CONTACT: [email protected] Cleveland.com Fact Check: 4 Lies in Ad Attacking Dr.
Acton COLUMBUS, OH– Yesterday, Cleveland.com called out the Right Direction PAC for airing an attack ad “questioning” the “conduct and leadership” of Dr.
Amy Acton.

Fact-checkers found four instances of this ad airing “claims that are unsupported by the facts.” READ: Fact check: 4 lies in Right Direction PAC’s ad questioning Amy Acton’s conduct and leadership A political action committee backing Republicans is airing an attack ad portraying Democratic gubernatorial nominee Amy Acton as having a substance-abuse problem and questioning her performance as Ohio’s health director during the coronavirus pandemic.
The ad by Right Direction PAC has four claims that are unsupported by the facts.
“You know Amy Acton: the drinking, the drugs.” The ad refers to a 2019 police report involving a dispute between Acton and her husband.
While the report noted that Acton had been drinking and had taken an unknown amount of prescription medication, it did not say she was intoxicated or abusing drugs.
Her campaign has since said she had one glass of wine and was taking migraine medication.
The ad turns a single incident into an allegation of a broader substance-abuse problem that the evidence does not establish.

“She curled up into a ball on the floor during an emergency response meeting.” According to an article cited in the ad, an unnamed former state employee found Acton huddled on a hallway floor before an emergency meeting.
The ad rewrites the alleged incident and asserts it took place during the meeting.

“Amy Acton failed when Ohio needed her most.” The ad uses the previous allegation to imply Acton broke down when state officials needed her during a moment of crisis, although the cited story clearly states she went into the meeting.
That does not establish that she failed to perform her duties.
Republican Gov.
Mike DeWine later praised her work during the pandemic, saying he believed “many, many lives” were saved because of her advice and work.

“Ohio’s governor manages the National Guard, our schools and a 60-billion-dollar budget.” The governor is commander-in-chief of the Ohio National Guard and has substantial authority over education and budgeting, but does not directly manage all three.
State law gives local school boards “management and control” of their public schools, while the General Assembly appropriates state money.
The governor proposes the state budget and can veto individual appropriations.

Express your interest → Explore the roles Two leadership positions Civil and criminal legal leadership Civil matters Civil Legal Lead Help develop plans for civil litigation, constitutional and appellate matters, and legal representation of state agencies.
The intended administrative role would include overseeing civil legal operations and exercising lawfully delegated responsibilities.
Criminal matters Criminal Legal Lead Help develop plans for criminal prosecution, prosecutorial integrity, public-corruption enforcement, and coordination with investigative agencies.
The intended administrative role would include overseeing criminal legal operations, with attention to due process, disclosure obligations, and fair enforcement of the law.
Preparing the administration Both attorneys will work with Gordon to: Review the constitutional, statutory, and ethical requirements governing the office.
Develop a lawful allocation of executive and legal responsibilities.
Prepare proposed appointments, administrative orders, and operating procedures.
Plan for uninterrupted civil and criminal legal services when the administration takes office.
Under Gordon’s proposed structure, he would provide executive leadership over administration, budgeting, resource allocation, and policy priorities.
Duly authorized attorneys would handle legal representation and exercise the professional judgment required of licensed counsel.

Experience and qualifications Candidates must be eligible for admission to the Rhode Island Bar and demonstrate substantial relevant legal experience, sound professional judgment, and the ability to lead legal teams.
Attorneys already admitted in Rhode Island are welcome to express interest.
Experienced attorneys practicing outside Rhode Island are encouraged to express interest.
Candidates should identify their current admissions and the basis for their eligibility for Rhode Island admission.
Any required admission or authorization must be obtained before undertaking duties that require it.
Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to constitutional government, impartial justice, professional ethics, and public service.

Identify whether you are interested in the civil position, the criminal position, or both.

added: Until everyone is covered, having insurance should at least mean you can afford to use it.
Right now a Montanan on a marketplace plan can owe up to $10,600 a year out of pocket for covered care, and that ceiling rises to $12,000 next year.
I support efforts to bring it down significantly; current efforts target $5,000.
I also support giving every patient the same yearly cap on prescriptions that people on Medicare already have.
The savings should come out of the middlemen’s margins, not your premiums.

That means banning spread pricing, where a PBM charges your plan more than it pays the pharmacy and keeps the difference; paying PBMs a flat fee instead of a cut of the drug’s list price; and passing drug rebates straight to you at the counter.
If you use a health savings account, this works with it: HSA-eligible plans stay HSA-eligible, and in a bad health year you’d draw less out of your account, so more of your savings stays yours.
HealthCare.gov; CMS, 2026; IRS Rev.
Proc.
2025-19 Coverage means nothing if there's no doctor One in three of Montana's rural hospitals, 16 of them, is at risk of closing, several immediately.
Take the middlemen’s cut out of your prescriptions.
Ban PBM spread pricing, pay PBMs a flat fee instead of a percentage of list price, and pass rebates through to patients at the pharmacy counter.
Lower what you can be billed in a year.

Support efforts to significantly lower the yearly out-of-pocket ceiling on private plans (current efforts target $5,000) and extend Medicare’s yearly drug cap to every patient, paid for by the middlemen’s margins rather than higher premiums.
And when an algorithm wrongly turns down your care, you’re the one left with the bill, or you go without.

removed: 0 Skip to Content About Amelia Priorities Endorsements Volunteer Register to Vote Contact Contribute Open Menu Close Menu About Amelia Priorities Endorsements Volunteer Register to Vote Contact Contribute Open Menu Close Menu About Amelia Priorities Endorsements Volunteer Register to Vote Contact Contribute AMELIA’S PRIORITIES AFFORDABILITY Arizona families are being squeezed by rising housing costs, utility bills, and the high cost of healthcare.
AMELIA ON THE ISSUES Judy Schwiebert Former State Representative - LD2 I’m proud to endorse Dr Amelia Gallitano for our LD2 State Senate seat.
As a longtime doctor, educator, and working mom, Dr.

Amelia knows the issues personally - and will be ready on Day One to prioritize policies that reduce costs, strengthen our public schools, and make Arizona a sustainable place where everyone gets their chance to thrive.
Vote for her in the July 21 primary Heather A.
Okvat, Ph.D, Licensed Psychologist Dr.
Amelia Gallitano is up to tackling the challenges that face Arizonans.
She is level-headed, principled, and committed to completing difficult tasks despite challenges.
It is critical that Arizonans elect leaders and policymakers who are able to stand up for sensible affordability, full funding of public education, and protection of water, among other issues.
To get meaningful legislation passed and dangerous legislation blocked in the Arizona legislature, we need Dr.
Gallitano to win.
I’m proud to support her.
Austin Mach, PharmD, BCSCP I’m voting for Amelia because she is compassionate, committed, and dedicated to finding solutions to problems for the most vulnerable in our community.
If she can accomplish a small fraction of what she has accomplished as a physician, as a state senator, she will be the best person I will have ever voted for in my life.
I am so proud to call her a my colleague, my candidate, my potential senator, and most importantly, my friend.
Mitzi Epstein, State Senator LD12 Amelia cares about people and it shows.
We need state senators who listen well and seek reliable sources to solve problems.
As an MD, Amelia listens first by training and by her nature.
I am happy to endorse Amelia Gallitano for the AZ Senate, and I’m glad she is running!
“Having worked alongside Dr.
Amelia Gallitano for years at the Phoenix VA, I consistently witnessed her remarkable ability to connect with veterans, providing care that is both clinically precise and deeply compassionate.
She embodies the ideal balance of advocacy, integrity, and heartfelt humanity.
Dr.
Gallitano is a principled leader who felt honored to serve our veterans.
I wholeheartedly believe she is the right person to represent Legislative District 2 in the State Senate.” - Dr.
Karen Kattar, Retired - PTSD Clinic Director for the Phoenix VA Newsletter Block This newsletter signup form needs a storage option.

removed: RSVP Upcoming Events Events Oct 14 Voter Mobilization @ SHSU with Beto Ready to do the work that actually works?
In 2024, our face-to-face voter registration model achieved a massive 79% voter turnout among the Texans we registered.
We aren't just hoping for change—we have the blueprint to create it.
Join us and special guest Beto O'Rourke for the Every Campus Counts tour at SHSU !
We are showing up to talk to students, spark personal conversations, and build lasting progressive power through relational organizing.

At this event, we will: Engage directly with existing and potential student voters Connect with voters using Reach , our relational organizing tool, so we can personally stay in touch with them all the way to Election Day All volunteers are welcome!
There are plenty of vital roles for everyone.

added: As Margaret Mead reminds us: “Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can change the world; indeed, it’s the only thing that ever has.” Affordable Housing Housing affordability remains one of the biggest challenges facing Fort Collins and communities across Colorado.

During my time in the State House, I have championed practical, bipartisan solutions that increase housing supply, expand homeownership opportunities, and protect hardworking families. ​ In 2026, I was proud to pass HB26-1001 , the HOME Act , which removes unnecessary barriers preventing schools, housing authorities, transit agencies, and nonprofits from developing affordable housing on land they already own.
This commonsense reform will help create more housing opportunities while making better use of existing land.
You can read the bill here . ​ I also sponsored HB26-1313 , which modernizes Colorado's affordable housing requirements under Proposition 123.
By establishing more realistic housing production targets, this legislation helps communities maintain access to critical housing funding while accounting for local economic conditions.
In 2026, I helped pass HB26-1224 , strengthening transparency and financial protections for mobile home owners.
This builds on my previous efforts to protect residents and help communities preserve affordable housing.

You can read the bill here . ​ These accomplishments build on two major reforms I helped pass in 2025: HB25-1272 , which reduces barriers to condominium and townhome construction, and HB25-1273 , which modernizes building codes to make smaller multifamily housing developments more feasible. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins ​ These reforms mean more opportunities for first-time homebuyers, stronger protections for mobile home park residents, and greater flexibility to build affordable housing in our community.

Keep Fort Collins a place where people who work here can also afford to live here. ​ I will continue fighting for affordable paths to homeownership, strong renter protections, and increased workforce housing, so that hardworking Coloradans can continue to live and thrive in the communities they call home.

Additionally, I am proud to have supported bills that: ​ Keep firearms out of the hands of those charged with domestic violence Establish the Office of Gun Violence Prevention Raise the age to purchase firearms in our state Mandate safe storage for firearms Require reporting lost or stolen firearms Allow for Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPO) Remove Special Immunity for the Gun Industry Create mandatory waiting periods Close the Charleston Loophole Allow for stricter local gun violence prevention laws In 2026, I helped pass HB26-1144, Prohibit 3D Printing Firearms & Components , which prohibits the unauthorized manufacturing of functional firearms and certain firearm components using 3D printing technology.
This legislation addresses emerging threats posed by privately manufactured firearms while preserving exceptions for licensed manufacturers and accredited gunsmithing programs.
You can read the bill here . ​ In 2025, I passed SB25-003, Semiautomatic Firearms & Rapid-Fire Devices , a bill that strengthened firearm safety regulations for semi-automatic firearms statewide.

You can read the bill here . ​ These laws complement existing measures, such as Extreme Risk Protection Orders and safe storage requirements, that reduce the risk of violence while respecting responsible firearm ownership. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These laws are intended to reduce gun violence, strengthen public safety, and help keep firearms out of the hands of individuals who are legally prohibited from possessing them. ​ Protecting our communities and respecting responsible firearm ownership are not mutually exclusive.
I will continue working toward policies that prevent violence and keep Colorado families safe.

Abortion & Reproductive Health Care Reproductive freedom is a fundamental right, and decisions about pregnancy, abortion, and reproductive health care belong between individuals and their health care providers, not politicians.

I've consistently supported legislation protecting reproductive rights and ensuring Coloradans can make personal medical decisions without unnecessary government interference. ​ In 2022, I stood alongside my Democratic colleagues through more than 24 hours of debate to pass the Reproductive Health Equity Act , protecting the right to abortion under Colorado law ahead of the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v.
Wade.

In 2024, Colorado voters further strengthened these protections by enshrining abortion rights in our state constitution. ​ ​ In 2026, I supported and co-sponsored HB26-1335 , which expands access to medication abortion through student health centers at Colorado colleges and universities.
This legislation helps address barriers students may face when seeking reproductive health care.

You can read the bill here . ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These protections ensure that people in Fort Collins can continue to access reproductive health care safely and legally, without fear of government interference.
Public Education Strong public schools are the foundation of thriving communities and a brighter future for Colorado's children.
As a former public school teacher in a Title I school and a parent of three children in the Poudre School District, I understand firsthand the challenges facing students, educators, and families.

Ensuring every child has access to a quality education remains one of my deepest commitments. ​ ​In 2026, I helped pass SB26-145 , bipartisan legislation that strengthens transparency and fairness in school funding decisions.

This law ensures that charter schools have an opportunity to present their facility needs when school districts consider asking voters to fund capital improvements, while preserving local school boards' authority over funding decisions.

You can read the bill here . ​ In 2025, I was a co-sponsor of HB25-1131, which eliminated enrollment caps at Colorado State University's veterinary medicine program, expanding opportunities for students pursuing careers in veterinary medicine.

You can read the bill here . ​ Throughout my legislative service, I've supported increased public school funding, universal preschool, and full-day kindergarten, helping reduce costs for families while giving students a stronger foundation for success.

I've also advocated for investments that direct resources into classrooms and support the educators who make quality public education possible.​ ​ ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These efforts support students and educators in the Poudre School District, expand educational opportunities at Colorado State University, and help families access quality education from early childhood through higher education. ​ Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, regardless of their family's income or ZIP code.
I'll continue supporting strong public schools, dedicated educators, and educational opportunities that prepare the next generation for success.
Older Adults Older Coloradans deserve to live with dignity, independence, and financial security.

Whether that means remaining in their homes, accessing affordable health care, or staying connected to their communities, I believe we have a responsibility to ensure that seniors and retirees have the support they need. ​ I've worked to lower prescription drug costs and improve access to affordable health care.
In 2026, I helped pass SB26-167 , which will allow eligible prescription drug purchases to count toward patients' insurance deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums beginning in 2028.
You can read the bill here . ​ Also in 2026, I worked across party lines to introduce HB26-1204 , legislation designed to expand affordable housing opportunities for older Coloradans.
The proposal would have provided tax exemptions for qualifying senior cooperative housing developments, helping support alternative housing options for seniors with limited or fixed incomes.

Although the bill did not become law, expanding affordable housing for older adults remains an important priority. ​ ​ Beyond health care and housing, I support strengthening protections against financial exploitation and predatory lending, expanding access to home-based care, and improving transportation services that help older adults maintain their independence. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These efforts address challenges facing older residents in Fort Collins, including rising housing costs, expensive medications, and barriers to independent living. ​ Every Coloradan deserves to live with dignity and security, no matter their age.
I'll continue supporting policies that help older adults remain healthy, financially secure, and connected to the communities they call home.
Transportation & Infrastructure A safe, reliable, and affordable transportation system is essential to Colorado's economy and quality of life.

As your State Representative, I have worked to improve transportation safety, expand public transit, and invest in infrastructure that connects our communities. ​ In 2026, I worked to help pass SB26-172.
Supporting the Front Range Passenger Rail District, this legislation strengthens the district's ability to plan and advance passenger rail service along the Front Range.

By modernizing the district's governance and providing greater flexibility for regional planning and voter-approved funding, this legislation helps lay the groundwork for connecting Fort Collins to communities along the I-25 corridor.
You can read the bill here . ​ I have also passed legislation to improve roadway safety, including measures addressing roundabout safety and transportation challenges in rural Colorado.

These reforms help protect drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. ​ Additionally, I have supported expanding bike trails, e-bike programs, and public transportation options that give Coloradans more affordable and sustainable ways to travel.

I also championed legislation to modernize Colorado's electrical transmission infrastructure, supporting grid reliability and the state's growing energy needs. ​ ​ ​ What This Means for Fort Collins ​ These investments and reforms support safer roads, better regional connections, and more transportation choices for Northern Colorado residents. ​ My goal is to build a transportation system that connects our communities, supports economic opportunity, and makes it easier and more affordable for Coloradans to get where they need to go.
Health Care Affordable, accessible health care should be a reality for every Colorado family, not a privilege reserved for those who can afford it.

Throughout my time in the legislature, I've worked to lower health care costs, strengthen patient protections, and remove barriers that prevent Coloradans from getting the care they need. ​ In 2026, I helped pass SB26-167 , ensuring that eligible prescription medications purchased directly from pharmacies or manufacturers count toward a patient's insurance deductible and out-of-pocket maximum.
Beginning in 2028, this reform will help Coloradans better manage prescription drug expenses and avoid unnecessary out-of-pocket costs.

You can read the bill here . ​ ​ I've also championed legislation to limit excessive hospital facility fees, protecting patients from unexpected medical bills and increasing transparency in health care pricing.

These protections help ensure families aren't burdened with unnecessary charges simply for seeking medical care. ​ Additionally, I helped secure $1 million to expand culturally competent health care for LGBTQ+ Coloradans and underserved communities.
I've also passed legislation protecting health care workers from doxxing and harassment, allowing medical professionals to provide care without fear of intimidation.

Expanding access to affordable mental and behavioral health services remains an important priority, alongside continued efforts to reduce costs and strengthen Colorado's health care system. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These reforms help Fort Collins families access affordable medications, avoid unexpected medical expenses, and receive quality care from protected and supported health care professionals. ​ No one in our state should have to choose between their health and their financial security.
I'll continue working toward a health care system that puts patients and families first.
Workforce & Economic Opportunity A strong economy starts with good-paying jobs, thriving local businesses, and opportunities for every Coloradan to succeed.

I've worked to strengthen workers' rights, support economic development, and ensure that working families have the resources and opportunities they need to build a secure future. ​ In 2026, I helped pass HB26-1014 , bipartisan legislation that helps Colorado attract and retain businesses creating new jobs.
By extending this successful economic development program through 2034, we're encouraging long-term investment, supporting business growth, and creating opportunities for Colorado's workforce.

You can read the bill here . ​ I've also been a strong advocate for workers' rights and collective bargaining, supporting legislation that expands organizing rights for county employees and strengthens workplace protections for public workers.

I've stood alongside striking workers on the picket line and believe every Coloradan deserves fair wages, safe working conditions, and a voice in their workplace. ​ Expanding access to vocational education, apprenticeships, and workforce training is equally important.

These programs help Coloradans develop valuable skills, pursue rewarding careers, and meet the evolving needs of our economy. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins A thriving Fort Collins depends on strong local businesses, skilled workers, and economic opportunities that allow families to build their futures here. ​ Economic growth should benefit everyone, not just those at the top.
I'll continue supporting policies that create good-paying jobs, protect workers, and help Northern Colorado businesses and families succeed.
Civil Rights & Equal Opportunity Colorado should be a place where everyone is treated with dignity, fairness, and respect.

Throughout my time in the legislature, I've supported policies that protect civil rights, combat discrimination, and ensure that every Coloradan has the opportunity to participate fully in their community.
In 2025, I was a co-sponsor of HB25-1239 , the Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act , which strengthens protections for individuals experiencing discrimination, especially Coloradans with disabilities.

You can read the bill here . ​ ​ I've also been a strong advocate for LGBTQ+ equality, supporting protections against discrimination, access to affirming health care, and policies that ensure LGBTQ+ Coloradans can live safely and openly. ​ As federal policies increasingly raise concerns about civil liberties and constitutional protections, I remain committed to protecting the rights of immigrants and refugees in our communities .
Everyone deserves fair treatment under the law, regardless of their background or immigration status.

I will continue supporting policies that safeguard constitutional rights, promote accessibility, and ensure equal opportunities in education, employment, and everyday life. ​ I also recognize the need to address disparities within our criminal justice system, including expanding diversion programs and improving access to mental health and substance use treatment. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These civil rights protections help ensure Fort Collins remains a welcoming, safe community for all residents.
They provide meaningful legal remedies when discrimination occurs and protect individual dignity in education, housing, employment, and everyday life.

Elections & Democracy Colorado has built one of the nation's most accessible election systems, with mail-in paper ballots, opportunities for in-person voting, and safeguards designed to protect election integrity.

I've consistently supported legislation that protects voting rights, strengthens election security, and ensures Coloradans can participate in our democracy safely and confidently. ​ In 2026, I co-sponsored HB26-1084 , legislation addressing transparency requirements for statewide ballot measures.
I also supported HB26-1113 , which updates election administration procedures, strengthens voter registration systems, and expands access to voter information for students.

Both bills became law ​ Previously, I supported the Vote Without Fear Act , which restricts openly carrying firearms near polling locations, and the Election Official Protection Act , which protects election workers from doxxing and intimidation. ​ I also supported the 2022 Colorado Election Security Act , strengthening safeguards against unauthorized access to voting equipment and establishing additional qualifications for individuals responsible for administering elections. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These protections help ensure that Fort Collins residents can participate in elections safely, election workers can perform their duties without intimidation, and voters can have confidence in the integrity of our election system.
Environment & Conservation Colorado's natural beauty is one of the things that makes our state such a special place to live.

From the foothills and trails surrounding Fort Collins to our rivers, forests, and open spaces, protecting our environment means preserving the places that make our communities unique. ​ Protecting Colorado's natural resources requires thoughtful stewardship and a commitment to conservation.
I've supported efforts to improve air and water quality, preserve wildlife habitats, and protect our public lands.

I also believe we can pursue environmental protection while supporting economic opportunity and accommodating Colorado's growing communities. ​ In 2025, I co-sponsored HB25-1318 , which invested $5 million in programs protecting Colorado's native wildlife, including threatened and endangered species.
These investments help preserve biodiversity, restore habitats, and support conservation efforts across the state.

You can read the bill here . ​ I've also supported investments in water conservation, clean energy, and sustainable transportation, recognizing that protecting our environment requires solutions that address both present challenges and long-term needs.

As Colorado continues to grow, we must balance development and outdoor recreation with the responsibility to preserve our natural resources. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins From Horsetooth Reservoir and the Poudre River to our extensive network of trails and open spaces, Fort Collins residents have a deep connection to the outdoors.

Protecting these resources means maintaining access to outdoor recreation, safeguarding wildlife habitats, and preserving the landscapes that contribute to our community's quality of life. ​ Future generations deserve to experience the same natural beauty and outdoor opportunities we enjoy today.
I'll continue supporting responsible conservation policies that protect Colorado's environment and keep our communities healthy and thriving.
removed: As Margaret Mead reminds us: “Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can change the world; indeed, it’s the only thing that ever has.” Affordable Housing The availability of affordable and attainable housing remains one of the top concerns across Colorado.

As a legislator, I have focused on passing practical, bipartisan solutions that increase housing supply, protect residents, and preserve the affordability of our communities. ​ In 2025, I was a prime sponsor of HB25-1272, Construction Defects and Middle Market Housing , legislation that removes long-standing barriers to the construction of condominiums and townhomes.

This reform helps unlock more attainable housing options for first-time buyers, teachers, nurses, and working families by reducing unnecessary legal risk while maintaining strong consumer protections.
You can read the bill here . ​ I was also a prime sponsor of HB25-1273, Residential Building Stair Modernization , often referred to as single-stair reform.
This legislation modernizes outdated building codes to allow safe, well-designed multifamily buildings with a single stairwell.
By lowering construction costs and enabling more flexible designs, this reform will open the door to more affordable rental housing for families, seniors, and working Coloradans.
I have passed legislation to strengthen resident protections and helped secure $35 million in revolving loan funds that allow residents to collectively purchase their mobile home parks.

This preserves affordability while also ensuring access to safe, clean drinking water that meets federal standards. ​ Looking ahead, I am working to advance the HOME Act (HB26-1001), which I am sponsoring to reduce red tape and allow schools, housing authorities, transit agencies, and nonprofits to build affordable housing on land they already own.
This commonsense approach will help increase housing supply without sprawl or higher taxes.

Learn more about the HOME Act here . ​ What This Means for Fort Collins ​ These housing reforms help Fort Collins address rising housing costs by making it easier to build condos, townhomes, and affordable rentals, protecting residents in mobile home parks, and allowing trusted local institutions to develop affordable homes on existing land.

Keep Fort Collins a place where people who work here can also afford to live here. ​ If re-elected, I will continue fighting for affordable paths to homeownership, strong renter protections, and increased workforce housing, so that hardworking Coloradans can continue to live and thrive in the communities they call home.

Additionally, I am proud to have supported bills that: ​ Keep firearms out of the hands of those charged with domestic violence Establish the Office of Gun Violence Prevention Raise the age to purchase firearms in our state Mandate safe storage for firearms Require reporting lost or stolen firearms Allow for Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPO) Remove Special Immunity for the Gun Industry Create mandatory waiting periods Close the Charleston Loophole Allow for stricter local gun violence prevention laws In 2025, I passed SB25-003, Semiautomatic Firearms & Rapid-Fire Devices , a bill that strengthened firearm safety regulations for semi-automatic firearms statewide.

You can read the bill here . ​ These laws complement existing measures, such as Extreme Risk Protection Orders and safe storage requirements, that reduce the risk of violence while respecting responsible firearm ownership. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These gun violence prevention bills help keep Fort Collins communities safer by preventing access to dangerous weapons for individuals prohibited under the law, while supporting responsible gun ownership and reducing firearm injuries.
Abortion & Reproductive Health Care Reproductive freedom is a fundamental right, and health care decisions should remain between a person and their health care provider.
I'm focused on making sure Colorado remains a place where personal decisions stay personal.
Anticipating the overturning of Roe v.

Wade, I stood alongside my Democratic colleagues and fought for 24-plus hours on the floor of the House of Representatives so that we could pass legislation to keep abortion safe and legal here in Colorado.
Colorado has since adopted a constitutional measure that enshrined the right to abortion in the Colorado Constitution.
Decisions regarding reproductive health care and abortion belong solely between an individual and their health care professional.

I will always protect the right to choose here in Colorado. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These protections ensure that people in Fort Collins can continue to access reproductive health care safely and legally, without fear of government interference.
Public Education Public education is the foundation of opportunity for Fort Collins families.

As a former public school teacher in a Title I school, and as a parent with three children in the Poudre School District, I know strong schools make strong communities. ​ In 2025, I was a co-sponsor of HB25-1131, Eliminate Student Cap at Colorado State University’s Veterinary Program , which expanded access to higher education opportunities in our state by removing enrollment caps at CSU’s veterinary program.

You can read the bill here . ​ I have also supported state investments that eliminate the Budget Stabilization Factor, expand early childhood education through all-day kindergarten and free universal pre-k , and increase per-pupil funding so classroom resources follow students and teachers rather than paperwork.

These investments lower out-of-pocket costs for families and give students the support they need to succeed. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These policies help ensure Poudre School District classrooms have adequate funding, expand local access to affordable post-secondary programs, and reduce costs for Fort Collins families.
Strong public schools keep our community competitive and help every child reach their potential.

Older Adults Older adults and retirees are an invaluable asset to our community, and deserve to age in place with grace and dignity. ​ I will work to lower prescription drug prices while protecting and expanding home-based medical services so that older adults can stay in their homes if they choose.
I support affordable housing initiatives and will work to ensure that our older adults are both housing and food-secure.

I will also work to combat predatory lending practices and other financial schemes that specifically target older adults and retirees. ​ I support LGBTQ+ affirming retirement homes and medical services .

I will work to address isolation and loneliness amongst older adults and retirees and am committed to expanding access to transportation services. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These priorities help ensure that older adults and retirees in Fort Collins can age safely and independently in the community they call home.
By working to lower prescription drug costs, expand home-based care, and support affordable housing and food security, this approach helps seniors stay healthy and housed.

Combating predatory financial practices and expanding transportation and social supports also reduces isolation and protects the financial security and dignity of older adults throughout our community.
Elections Colorado has the gold standard for elections and leads the nation in mail-in paper ballots, voter access, and conducting fair and secure elections.
Since being elected in 2021, the Colorado General Assembly has taken decisive action to protect and secure our elections in Colorado.
I am proud to have supported the Vote Without Fear Act in Colorado, which prohibits the open carry of firearms at voting locations.

I have also voted in support of the Election Official Protection Act, which protects election workers from doxxing. ​ In 2022, I supported the Colorado Election Security Act , which improves election security by, among other measures, prohibiting anyone from serving as an election official if they have been convicted of any election offense or any offense or conspiracy to commit sedition, insurrection, treason, or conspiracy to overthrow the government.

This legislation also prohibits election officials or candidates from physically tampering with voting equipment, and from having access to or being present in a room with voting equipment without being accompanied by one or more persons with authorized access. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These policies ensure local voters can cast ballots without fear, protect election workers, and maintain strong confidence in how elections are run in our community.
Climate Change Clean air, land, and water are essential to the health, economy, and quality of life of Fort Collins and communities across Colorado.

As a legislator, I have focused on passing practical environmental protections that safeguard our natural resources while supporting working families and local economies. ​ I have passed legislation to expand and improve recreational trail access across Colorado, strengthening outdoor recreation, supporting tourism, and ensuring that more families can safely enjoy our public lands.
Protecting access to the outdoors is both an environmental priority and an economic investment for communities like Fort Collins. ​ I have also been a leader in responsible oil and gas oversight.

I championed and passed legislation requiring a comprehensive audit of the oil and gas industry , improving transparency and accountability while ensuring state regulators have the information they need to protect public health and the environment. ​ In addition, I sponsored and passed legislation to reduce the use of fresh water in oil and gas operations by increasing the use of recycled and reused water.

At a time when water scarcity is one of Colorado’s greatest challenges, this policy helps conserve limited water supplies while maintaining strong environmental safeguards. ​ In 2025, I was a prime sponsor of HB25-1292 Transmission Lines in State Highway Rights-of-Way , legislation that supports upgrading and expanding Colorado’s electric transmission system.
Modernizing our transmission lines is critical to electrifying our state, integrating more renewable energy, and ensuring reliable and affordable power for homes and businesses.
Investing in transmission infrastructure helps lower long-term energy costs, strengthens grid reliability, and supports a growing clean energy economy.

You can read the bill here . ​ I am committed to continuing Colorado’s transition to clean, renewable energy, while also supporting workers and communities navigating changes in an economy that has historically relied on carbon-based energy.

Environmental responsibility and economic security must move forward together. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins ​ These efforts help protect Fort Collins’ air quality, safeguard our water supply, and preserve the natural spaces and open areas that define our community.

Expanding trails, conserving water, strengthening oversight of industrial activity, and investing in modern transmission infrastructure all support public health, outdoor recreation, and a clean energy economy that creates jobs and opportunity here at home.
Health Care Affordable, accessible health care is essential for Fort Collins families and communities across Colorado.

Every Coloradan, regardless of age or income, should have access to affordable, comprehensive health care, including primary care, prescriptions, hospitalizations, reproductive health care, mental and behavioral health care, dental care, and specialty care.

No Coloradan should risk losing their home or their life savings if they get sick. ​ I have passed legislation to limit hospital facility fees , as well as legislation that provides $1M in funding to our health care providers so that they can provide culturally competent care to LGBTQ+ Coloradans along with other priority populations.

I have also passed legislation that protects health care workers from doxxing . ​ In addition, I have supported Colorado’s efforts to study the implementation of a single-payer health care system , because we must seriously evaluate every option that could lower costs, expand access, and reduce administrative waste in our health care system, especially when federal inaction threatens affordability. ​ My focus remains on making sure Coloradans can get the care they need without fear of financial hardship. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These policies help Fort Collins families avoid unnecessary medical costs, reduce surprise billing, and access more transparent and affordable health care.

Regulating hospital facility fees and strengthening consumer protections means fewer financial shocks for patients and a health care system that works better for people in our community. ​ Workforce & Economic Opportunity Every Coloradan deserves access to a high quality education, a good paying job, and the economic opportunity that goes hand-in-hand with the American Dream.
I support a living wage, the right of workers to organize, and the strengthening of collective bargaining rights.
I supported the expansion of county employees' rights to collective bargaining as well as legislation adding labor protections for public workers .

Each and every worker in Colorado deserves access to a good paying job and a safe workplace. ​ I support job training and retraining programs , the work of unions in advocating for economic justice, an increased focus on vocational education, and apprenticeship programs .

I have joined striking workers on the picket line and will continue to advocate alongside workers in our community. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins This work helps grow local economic opportunities, protecting small businesses like those in Old Town Fort Collins, and expanding job pathways for Fort Collins residents.
Civil Rights Colorado must be a place where every person is treated with respect and fairness.
The work continues to ensure that our great state is a welcoming, safe, and affirming place for LGBTQ+ people.

I support Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, inclusivity training for healthcare providers and insurance companies, and the right of transgender people to access public restrooms and gender segregated facilities that correspond with gender identity.

I support suicide prevention initiatives and recognize the need for more LGBTQ+ affirming mental health resources. ​ Children with disabilities have the right to learn alongside their peers, engage in school activities, sports, and receive an education that is committed to equity, safety, and inclusion in the classroom.
I support equal pay for equal work and am opposed to paying people with disabilities a subminimum wage.

People with disabilities are an asset to the workforce, and I support engagement with the business community and other stakeholders around this important issue so that together we can create an equitable wage and workplace for workers with disabilities.
In 2025, I was a co-sponsor of HB25-1239, Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act , which strengthens protections for individuals experiencing discrimination, especially Coloradans with disabilities.

You can read the bill here . ​ I will continue to support policies that keep immigrants and refugees safe and welcome in our community as national leaders push dangerous overreach that threatens the constitutionally-protected freedoms of people in our community. ​ It is far past time to address the realities of systemic racism in our criminal justice system – including the racial disparities that are well-documented both in terms of sentencing and incarceration rates.
I support diversion programs for non-violent, low-level offenders.

Prison is not a catch-all solution, and the for-profit prison industry continues to wreak devastation on those struggling with mental health issues and/or addiction while disproportionately preying upon minority communities. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These civil rights protections help ensure Fort Collins is a welcoming, safe community for all residents.
They give Coloradans meaningful legal recourse when discrimination occurs and protect individual dignity in education, housing, work, and daily life.
Transportation Colorado’s economy, workers, students, visitors, and retirees all depend on a modern, safe, and sustainable transportation system.

Transportation and infrastructure investments are essential to affordability, economic opportunity, and quality of life across our state. ​ Since joining the legislature, I have passed legislation to improve transportation safety, including bills that increase safety at roundabouts and strengthen transportation safety in rural Colorado .

These commonsense measures reduce crashes, protect drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians, and make our transportation system safer for everyone who uses it. ​ I have also worked to advance Front Range Passenger Rail , recognizing that reliable passenger rail is a critical part of Colorado’s long-term transportation future.

Connecting communities along the Front Range with safe, dependable rail service will help reduce congestion, lower transportation costs, improve air quality, and give people more choices for how they get to work, school, and daily activities. ​ In addition, I support e-bike rebate programs , bike commuting initiatives, and bike share programs that make it easier and more affordable for people to choose active transportation.

I have worked to ensure that bike trails, including powerline trails , are considered whenever a transmission corridor is sited or expanded, helping connect communities and expand safe non-motorized travel options. ​ I also support building affordable housing near public transit , so families can spend less time commuting, reduce vehicle miles traveled, and lower household transportation costs while improving access to jobs, schools, and services. ​ What This Means for Fort Collins These transportation priorities help Fort Collins reduce congestion, improve safety, and expand affordable transportation options.
Investments in passenger rail, biking infrastructure, and transit-oriented housing give residents more choices beyond driving, shorten commute times, and improve air quality.
Together, these solutions support a more connected, accessible, and affordable Fort Collins for families, workers, students, and seniors.

#ago Let's Connect Vote for Anthony Kathol on November 3, 2026 (General Election) Republican Candidate for South Dakota District 27 State Senate A leader who delivers with passion and proven results.
I am Anthony Kathol (last name pronounced caud’l), the Republican Candidate for South Dakota District 27 State Senate.

I am running for State Senate because I believe it is our responsibility to preserve and protect the South Dakota way of life that has shaped generations of South Dakotans through faith, hard work, personal responsibility, and a commitment to one another.
Having lived and worked in District 27 for more than 22 years, I bring more than two decades of firsthand experience with the people and communities I am seeking to represent.

My professional and civic service has taken me throughout the district and given me an understanding of the unique challenges facing our rural communities, including infrastructure, health care, education, economic development, and local government. ​ My professional and civic life has been guided by a commitment to service, responsibility, and faith.
From serving our nation and engineering healthier communities to educating the next generation, I have sought opportunities to serve others.

As a public servant, educator, small-business owner, commissioned lay minister, and registered professional engineer, I have developed an understanding of both the challenges and opportunities facing the people of District 27. ​ ​My candidacy is founded on shared values and common-sense solutions.

I am committed to strengthening rural health care and public infrastructure; supporting local law enforcement, first responders, and the constitutional right to defend oneself and one’s property; advancing an education system that prioritizes student achievement and accountability; upholding the sanctity and value of life from conception to natural death; and fostering sustainable economic growth that protects our agricultural and ancestral heritage, respects private property rights and tribal sovereignty, and preserves local control. ​ ​ I also believe government must be a good steward of the resources entrusted to it by taxpayers.

As a former public servant and registered professional engineer, I understand the importance of planning, accountability, responsible spending, and eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse of hard-earned tax dollars. ​ Integrity, transparency, and accountability are the pillars that undergird my candidacy, and they will remain the foundation of how I serve if elected.

I am running not simply to hold office, but to serve the people of al of District 27 and be a voice for the communities, families, farmers, ranchers, small businesses, and individuals who call this district home. ​ Committed to responsible leadership, I respectfully ask for your vote as we work together to protect the South Dakota way of life and to build a stronger and more prosperous and brighter future for our families and communities. ​ Let's Connect Vote for Anthony Kathol on November 3, 2026 (General Election) Republican Candidate for South Dakota District 27 State Senate A leader who delivers with passion and proven results.

Integrity, transparency, and accountability are the pillars that undergird my candidacy, and will continue to do so if elected.

As a former public servant and registered professional engineer, I will continue to be a good steward of government resources by practicing fiscal restraint and eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse of your hard-earned tax dollars.
Together, we can build a stronger, more resilient community and secure a prosperous future for our families.
Committed to responsible leadership, I respectfully ask for your vote as we move forward united in purpose and for a brighter future.

added: top of page Home About Me Testimonials Blog Donate Contact A Simple Courtesy: Responding to the People You Represent Anthony Kathol #ago 3 min read Rated NaN out of 5 stars.
One of my biggest pet peeves is taking the time to write a letter, send an email, or call someone and not receive even a simple courtesy response.
This is especially frustrating when communicating with our elected officials.
Some politicians are better than others at responding to their constituents’ concerns and questions, but I believe that acknowledging those communications is a basic responsibility of public service.
For example, on March 31, 2025, I emailed Democratic State Senator Red Dawn Foster, urging her and the other state senators to vote YES to override Governor Rhoden’s veto of HB 1169.
The bill would have required a proposed constitutional amendment to obtain petition signatures from each of South Dakota’s 35 legislative districts before qualifying for the ballot.

I supported this requirement because I believe rural South Dakotans deserve a meaningful voice in the constitutional amendment process, rather than having ballot initiatives driven primarily by population centers.
As many of you may recall, the 2024 election cycle featured a large number of proposed constitutional amendments, referred laws, and initiated measures.

I was concerned that out-of-state special interest groups could concentrate their petition-gathering efforts in South Dakota’s more densely populated areas, including Sioux Falls, Rapid City, Aberdeen, and the university communities of Brookings and Vermillion, while giving little attention to rural communities, particularly in the western half of our state.
I believe HB 1169 would have helped address that concern by requiring petition support from all 35 legislative districts.
Despite taking the time to express my concerns and make my position known, I did not receive a response from Senator Foster until January 29, 2026—almost ten months after I sent my original email.
The response acknowledged that she had read my message.
I have attached a copy of that email for readers to see for themselves.
Unfortunately, the lack of timely responses from elected officials is a concern I have heard and experienced in District 27.
As a former public servant, I understand what it means to receive calls, letters, and emails from members of the public.
Responding takes time, but acknowledging someone’s concerns is a matter of common courtesy and an important part of the job.
Even when an official cannot resolve an issue or agrees with a constituent’s position, a timely response demonstrates respect for the person who took the time to reach out.
On the contact page of my campaign website, I have made a pledge to the voters of District 27 regarding communication and responsiveness.
You can read it here: https://www.anthonykathol.com/contact I have also attached an image of that pledge for your reference.
If elected, I intend to make every reasonable effort to respond to the people I represent.
Although an occasional email may be filtered into a spam folder beyond my control, I will do my best to ensure that constituents’ communications receive the attention they deserve.
Neither of my opponents has made a comparable public pledge to the voters demonstrating this same level of commitment to communication and responsiveness.
I believe the people of District 27 deserve elected officials who are accessible, responsive, and accountable to those they serve.
Ultimately, voters must decide what qualities they expect from their elected representatives and who they believe will best uphold those standards.
The pillars that undergird my campaign are integrity, honesty, and transparency .
These are not merely campaign slogans; they are principles I believe should guide our elected officials in carrying out their responsibilities.
If elected as your next state senator, I will do my best to serve you faithfully, listen to your concerns, and respond when you reach out to me.
I ask for your support and your vote on November 3, 2026.
Take care, and God bless.

title.after: Attending the Mass of Nicholas Black Elk, Servant of God, at Holy Rosary Mission

added: top of page Home About Me Testimonials Blog Donate Contact Attending the Mass of Nicholas Black Elk, Servant of God, at Holy Rosary Mission Anthony Kathol Aug 18 2 min read Rated NaN out of 5 stars.

Today, I had the opportunity to attend the Mass commemorating the 10th anniversary of the opening of the Cause for Canonization of Servant of God Nicholas Black Elk at Sacred Heart Church Pine Ridge of t he Oglala Lakȟóta Catholic Community.
Bishop Scott Bullock of the Diocese of Rapid City presided at the 10:30 a.m.
Mass, with many Jesuit priests concelebrating from throughout the diocese.
The Mass was also attended by descendants of Nicholas Black Elk, students from Maȟpíya Lúta – Red Cloud School, and other guests from near and far.
It was especially nice to see familiar faces I hadn't seen in two years at the outdoor reception that followed the Mass.
Many people are familiar with the first forty years of Nicholas Black Elk's life through the 1932 bestseller Black Elk Speaks, written by John G.
Neihardt.
However, many are unaware of the remaining forty-plus years of his life as a catechist for the Catholic Church, teaching the Lakota people the Way of the Good Red Road.
Black Elk took the name Nicholas because he was baptized on December 6, the Feast of St.
Nicholas.
His body is buried in St.
Agnes Catholic Cemetery in Manderson, South Dakota.

In his homily, Bishop Bullock reflected on the Gospel reading from Matthew 5:1–12a, the Sermon on the Mount, specifically the passage: “Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.” Nicholas Black Elk lived as a peacemaker and sought to reconcile his Lakota culture with his Catholic faith.
As an adopted child of God, baptized into the Catholic faith, he went on to share that faith with more than 500 Lakota men, women, and children.
Nicholas Black Elk's Cause for Canonization continues to move forward.
His canonization would require two approved miracles.

You can learn more about his Cause for Canonization through this one-hour, online documentary: https://www.rapidcitydiocese.org/docmentary-nbe/ Special thanks to all the “missionaries of hospitality” who helped put on this anniversary event at Holy Rosary Mission.
Servant of God, Nicholas Black Elk, pray for us.

added: top of page Home About Me Testimonials Blog Donate Contact Enjoying the Journey Across District 27 Anthony Kathol Sep 11 1 min read Rated NaN out of 5 stars.
Yesterday, I put in some long hours installing signs in the farthest reaches of the district.
As I made my way east over Cuny Table in the evening, I got to see the shadows cast across the South Unit of Badlands National Park near the White River Ranger Station.
Anthony Kathol for District 27 State Senate Campaign Sign at South Unit of Badlands National Park, September 10, 2026.
Since I started putting up campaign signs, I’ve reminded myself each day to enjoy the journey.
Despite the hot, humid temperatures this past week, the long days, and the commitments waiting for me when I get back home, there is a lot to appreciate along the way.
I’ve seen beautiful scenery and wildlife, and I’ve met great people eager to learn more about my campaign.
The one-on-one conversations remind me why I am running for State Senate.
Hearing their stories and the challenges they face is one of the greatest rewards I receive as a candidate...not to mention a few honks from vehicles and trucks as I put up my signs.
I look forward to sharing more photos and stories with you as I make my way around the district throughout September and October.
See you at the Homecoming Parade in Martin this Friday!

title.after: Our Community Deserves Better

added: top of page Home About Me Testimonials Blog Donate Contact Our Community Deserves Better Anthony Kathol Aug 11 2 min read Rated NaN out of 5 stars.

This Saturday (August 8, 2026), while at the Bennett County Fairgrounds eating my pork and beef sandwiches, I observed my opponent, a Democratic Socialist, canvassing voters with a posed smile and distributing her campaign literature.
What the voters didn’t see was this post she made on Facebook an hour later.
Apparently, she believes that the children in our local school district are racist.
As someone who has substitute taught in this district for five years and completed my student teaching here, I never once witnessed racist comments from students or teachers.
This comment from one of my two opponents is divisive and only further stokes racial tensions within the people of this district rather than uniting us around a common purpose.
Comments like this fan the flames of racism, while being unsubstantiated and unwarranted.
As a 35-year-old principal and educator at Little Wound Middle School, Candidate Stadnick should know better than to come into a community and accuse our children of being racist.
Yet, rather than recognizing the divisiveness of such a statement, she appears tone-deaf to the racial bias inherent in her own accusation, bringing discredit to the teaching profession.
Candidate Stadnick, “Why do you notice the splinter in your brother’s eye, but do not perceive the wooden beam in your own eye?” (Mt 7:3).
April 29, 2020 - Racist comment as Candidate Stadnick prepares to drive through a Pine Ridge Reservation Highway Checkpoint.
Our community deserves better from our politicians.
I will represent all people in this district regardless of race, color, or ethnic origin.
My campaign is about uniting us around a common purpose and working toward a brighter future.
On November 3, 2026, vote for Anthony Kathol for South Dakota State Senate in District 27.

See More See Less Photo View on Facebook (opens in a new tab) · Share Share on Facebook (opens in a new tab) Share on Twitter (opens in a new tab) Share on LinkedIn (opens in a new tab) Share by Email (opens in a new tab) Representative Ashlee Matthews #ago HB210: Disabled Parking Amendments This bill originated from a constituent that is a disabled veteran who wanted to be able to park in ADA parking spots.

Because the criteria for qualifying for an ADA parking permit requires a mobility disability, but military disability does not (things like PTSD, tinnitis, asthma, etc), we worked with both the Department of Military and Veteran Affairs + the Disability Law Center to come up with solution.

First, we addressed the permits for those with permanent disability and created a permanent placard so they weren't required to go back in to the DMV to renew it every couple of years (it seemed unnecessary since the disability has already been confirmed as being permanent).
The bill also asked state owned buildings to create Veteran specific parking spots near the ADA parking spots.

This bill passed unanimously in every committee and floor vote and went info effect July 1, 2024 You can read the full bill here: share.google/MGS6KpyCCcaFqT6Gf You can see the new placards in action here: www.tiktok.com/t/ZTyKkDcxT/ ...

added: Skip to content The Latest Priorities Anti-Corruption Plan Endorsements Get Involved Volunteer Upcoming Events Media Yard Signs The Latest Priorities Anti-Corruption Plan Endorsements Get Involved Volunteer Upcoming Events Media Yard Signs Facebook X-twitter Instagram Youtube DONATE October 15, 2026 Press Release Republican U.S.

Senator Mel Martinez Endorses Bale Dalton for Congress “I believe the choices we make at this moment should reflect our shared values and rise above partisan politics.” SANFORD, FL – Today, Republican former Senator Mel Martinez announced his endorsement for Navy combat veteran and former NASA Chief of Staff Bale Dalton.
Dalton is running to replace disgraced Congressman Cory Mills in Florida’s 7th Congressional District.
“The desire to give back drove me to public service, and I see that same commitment in Bale Dalton,” said Martinez .
“He has served our country in uniform, helped fellow veterans access the services they deserve, and supported central Florida’s space economy.
I believe the choices we make at this moment should reflect our shared values and rise above divisive partisan politics.
I am proud to endorse Bale Dalton because he understands the responsibility of serving all central Floridians.” Martinez served as Florida’s Republican U.S.
Senator from 2005 to 2009, becoming the first Cuban American elected to the U.S.
Senate.
Before his time in the Senate, Martinez served as Secretary of Housing and Urban Development under President George W.
Bush and as Chairman of Orange County, Florida.
“The only letters next to my name that matter on the ballot are ‘FL.’ I am running for central Floridians, not one person or political party,” said Dalton.

“I am grateful for Senator Martinez’s endorsement and hope to follow his legacy of leadership defined by putting our community first and reaching across the aisle to better serve Floridians.” Download the endorsement videos in English and Spanish here .
ABOUT BALE DALTON: Bale Dalton is a decorated Navy Reserve Captain and former NASA Chief of Staff who has always answered the call to serve America.
One of four raised in a hardworking Central Florida family, Bale graduated from the U.S.
Naval Academy and has served in the U.S.
Navy and Navy Reserve for 24 years.
He deployed to Iraq, Afghanistan, the Horn of Africa, and the Pacific, flying Navy helicopters and directing air combat support with Navy SEALs in Afghanistan.
Following active duty, he worked for Senator Bill Nelson, helping Florida veterans access the care and benefits they had earned.
After an additional stint on active duty, Bale returned to government service as NASA Chief of Staff.
At NASA, he managed 16,500 employees and helped run one of the federal government’s most effective agencies.
After a lifetime of service, Bale is now running to represent his home, Florida’s 7th Congressional District, in the U.S.
House of Representatives.

Senate, has earned the endorsement of the Kentucky Motorcycle Association (KMA), a leading voice for motorcycle riders across the Commonwealth.
The Kentucky Motorcycle Association represents riders from across Kentucky and advocates for policies that promote safety, protect rider freedoms, and strengthen the state’s motorcycle culture.
“I’m honored to have the support of the Kentucky Motorcycle Association,” said Barr .
“As our next Senator, I’ll always make sure that Kentucky riders have a voice in Washington.

I’m committed to protecting our veterans, our freedoms, and our future.” “Kentucky’s motorcycling community values freedom and common-sense leadership—and Andy Barr delivers on this,” said Tommy Williams, President of the Kentucky Motorcycle Association .
“He understands the importance of protecting our rights, supporting veterans, and ensuring that federal policies don’t stand in the way of our way of life.
KMA is proud to stand with him in this race.” “Kentucky riders want a Senator who will stand up for them.
Andy Barr has earned our trust by defending individual liberty, supporting veterans, and fighting for Kentucky values.
We’re proud to support him for the U.S.
Senate,” said David Owen, Secretary of the Kentucky Motorcycle Association .

“Andy Barr has consistently listened to Kentucky riders and understands that the freedom to ride goes hand in hand with protecting individual liberties,” said Dave Newman, Vice President of Legislation .
“He has a proven record of standing up for our members, and we know he’ll continue fighting for common-sense policies in the U.S.
Senate.” “Our members care about freedom, responsibility, and preserving the traditions that make Kentucky special.
Andy Barr shares those values and has always been willing to listen to the motorcycle community,” said Glenda Hobbic, Presidential Public Affairs Liaison .

“I’m proud to endorse him because I know he’ll be a strong voice for riders in Washington.” ### Share this post: Facebook X Linkedin Email Previous post Congressman Andy Barr Endorses Hannah Beth Rivera for Kentucky House District 93 Next post Barr to Champion Kentucky Common Sense Over Socialist Crazy in U.S.

“I’m proud to have Kentucky State House Republicans standing with our campaign,” said Andy Barr .
“These are leaders who know their communities and know what it takes to move Kentucky forward.
I’m grateful for their confidence in me, and I’ll work every day in the U.S.

Senate to make sure Kentucky has a strong voice fighting for our workers, families, farmers, and businesses.” “Andy Barr has proven time and again that he knows how to get things done for Kentucky,” said Kentucky House Speaker David Osborne .
“He understands the industries that drive our Commonwealth, from horse racing and bourbon to agriculture and manufacturing, and he has fought to protect them and help them grow.
I’m proud to support Andy because I know he will take that same determination to the U.S.
Senate and continue delivering for Kentucky.” Barr has earned the support of more than 200 major endorsers in Kentucky and across the country.

added: Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Donate Get Your Yard Sign Volunteer Home Meet Andy Issues Kentucky Coal Plan Military & Veterans Law Enforcement News Contact Donate Volunteer Get Your Yard Sign Join the team Endorsements Donate New Barr Ad: Always Fighting for Veterans Press Release — October 15, 2026 Lexington, KY— Today, the Andy Barr for Senate campaign released a new ad featuring Teresa, a Marine veteran, in support of Andy Barr.
The Republican nominee’s campaign in Kentucky’s U.S.
Senate race released an ad that will be running as a seven figure buy across TV, digital, and radio.
The full text of the ad is below: Teresa: I remember being homeless, ashamed of myself, and I remember contacting Andy Barr.
I said, “I need help.” He doesn’t ask you if you’re a Republican or Democrat.
He just says, “What can I help you with?” Teresa: I started to cry cause I’m like “Oh my god, somebody’s actually listening.” A week to two weeks later, I got a call from the V A.
They were working on my stuff.
Andy Barr saved my life.
I’ll never forget it.
I’m voting for Andy Barr.
Barr: I’m Andy Barr and I approve this message.

added: That's exactly what we demand from our public servants, and I'm ready to lead.
The Stakes My assembly race is going to be one of the closest races in Wisconsin.
In 2024, Republicans won this district by just 365 votes. ​ For the first time in 16 years, Democrats have the opportunity to have the trifecta (State Assembly, State Senate and Governor).

Instead of constantly being on defense, we can put forth legislation that will finally have a positive impact on the lives of Wisconsinites. ​ Please let us know how you would like to help make that change happen.
Also, if you can support this campaign wtih a donation of any size, it will help us get the message out and encourage people to vote in 2026.

added: top of page About Issues Get Involved Volunteer Volunteer Endorsements Open site navigation Back to site Make a Donation Make A Donation My Priorities Healthcare No family should have to worry about getting sick or injured and not being able to afford quality healthcare.
Education As an educator, I know how important Wisconsin's public schools are.

Get Things Done I believe we have more in common than divides us, and as your representative I will listen, work across differences, and bring our shared, common‑sense values to make Madison work better for all of us.
Lower Cost of Living We’re all experiencing rising prices in everyday living expenses like groceries, gas and electricity, housing, insurance, and childcare.
Data Centers We must stop tax breaks for AI data centers and require them to pay for the water and electricity they use.
We need permanent protections and real guardrails that prohibit passing costs onto ratepayers and pollution of our air, water, and land.

I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work to make sure our neighbors, pocketbooks and our environment are safe from any harms that may come from unregulated AI and make sure our communities have a seat at those tables.
Raise Wages Wages are not keeping up with the cost of living.
Americans are struggling with day-to-day expenses like rent and groceries.
I promise to work hard to bring costs down by holding corporations who game the system accountable.
We need to raise wages and lower costs.
Hard-working Americans should be able to live, work and play and be able to give their kids a better life.

added: BECKY Stille's priorities Fighting for Nebraska Values Becky has overcome many obstacles with the support of family and friends.
Her journey from single teenage mother to congressional nominee reflects dedication, perseverance, and lessons she has learned along the way.
She earned a degree in accounting and spent 20 years in the agricultural industry, serving in roles such as accounting clerk, lab technician, quality manager, and production supervisor.
During that time, she helped develop new soy-based products and was certified in rail operations, maintenance, and training.
Now, Becky wants to bring that commitment to the U.S.
House, serving as a voice for the people and helping others pursue the American Dream.
Saving Family Farms Creating Good Jobs Quality Healthcare Women's Rights Becky is building a strong campaign!

description.before: Spend your Sunday afternoon on the river with the Brew Crew! Join Bekki Brewer, candidate for State Representative in District 44, and Bill Ellis, Democratic nominee for Boone County Associate Circuit Judge, Division IX, at Cooper's Landing for a relaxed meet & greet and an open Q&A. We'll be joined by special guest Boone County Recorder of Deeds, Bob Nolte. Bring your questions, bring your neighbors, and come talk about the issues that matter most to working families in District 44.

added: Home About Issues Newsletter Get Involved Contact Contribute Toggle menu About Ben Ben is a native, longstanding resident of Idaho raised by a School Teacher mom and a Physical Therapist dad.
He had simple beginnings, growing up mostly in apartments and mobile homes.

Some of his best memories are fly fishing the curving waterways of the Coeur d'Alene and St Joe Rivers with his father, playing football and basketball for the Lake City Timberwolves, and participating in student government at scenic North Idaho College as Senator, Vice President, and President.
Early Life & Education During his time at NIC, Ben found his two great passions: Political Science and his beautiful wife Elisha, marrying a day before graduating with an Associate of Arts Degree.
He went on to earn a degree in International Business from Gonzaga University while at the same time starting his own family with the birth of their first daughter.
During his time at Gonzaga, he was greatly impacted by statistics indicating that a family of three making under a certain household income would be considered impoverished.
Ben and Elisha were surprised to discover they fell below this line, as they felt they had a sustainable (albeit frugal) livelihood.
This led to a core belief that poverty is a mindset and must be addressed as such.
Shortly after graduating from GU, the Toews family purchased their first home in downtown Coeur d' Alene.

Being just 25 and 23 respectively, owning their own home was an important step toward putting down deep roots, establishing connection with the people around them and building close friends through church and community involvement.
Ben's wisdom and keen insight have brought strategic counsel and solutions to local finance and church government teams and committees.

Family & Entrepreneurship For 17 years, Ben was an integral part of growing a start-up business with his in-laws as a developer & manufacturer of specialty construction tools, starting out as the Vice President and later stepping into the role of President/CEO.
The company sold products around the world and won numerous awards for innovation, exporting and product excellence.

The business' mission was to "Continually improve the lives and livelihoods of tradesman across the globe by providing cutting edge solutions," which was undoubtedly accomplished based on results rendered.
The company was sold in 2019 to a like-minded firm that continues the legacy.
While building the family-owned business, the Toews also grew their immediate family to five, ranging in ages 7 to 22 - all of whom have been homeschooled throughout the years.

It has been Ben's great honor and blessing to be a part of his childrens' education, helping to start a homeschool co-op where he taught economics, government, and leadership classes to high-school-age students and coaching his children's debate club.
Being a part of his children's growth and learning has been one of his highest joys.

Vision for Idaho With the same passion and vision he has taken to task in each of his life endeavors, Ben intends to Raise the Standard that was both made and paid for by those who have gone before us and pledged their lives and sacred honor, so that we could enjoy the fruit of Liberty.

He will be a driving force and clear voice to build a stronger, more conservative Senate, with leadership marked by a proactive stand against federal overreach, tyranny at all levels, and the encroaching elements that are eroding away at the foundations of our great Gem State.
In addition to his Substack , you can learn more about his stances on important topics by reaching out at vote@Ben4Idaho.com or 208-209-7791.
