added: Home About Issues Newsletter Get Involved Contact Contribute Toggle menu Raising the Standard A Higher Standard of Defending the Vulnerable & Innocent Idaho needs to lead the way in protecting unborn children and I’m passionate about fighting to end abortion in Idaho from conception.
Innocent life must be protected as a key foundation to a moral society.
For too long we have allowed the most vulnerable in our society to be killed in the name of women's rights or freedom of choice.
The Idaho I envision believes in fighting for the most vulnerable.
Our children’s innocence is under attack by more than just abortion advocates.
We now see explicit sexual materials in the classrooms, schools and libraries where we send our children.
It is not censorship to make sure that our children aren’t exposed to sexual material - it is common sense.
Anyone who would promote putting material within our children’s reach is either naïve or downright evil.
I will do whatever is possible to protect the innocence of our children in the formative years of their life.

A Higher Standard of Freedom by Fighting Against Federal Overreach Defending State Sovereignty is at the top of my list of governmental values because it is one of the bastions of freedom that stands between us and tyranny.

The 10th Amendment to the Constitution states " The powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people." One of the wonderful things about living in the USA is that each state can, and should, exercise the power to create laws based on the peculiar values and culture of the people who live within its borders.

The result is that citizens don't have to move to a different country to find a place to live where their values are supported but can even "vote with their feet" and move to an area that better matches the values that are important to them.
Decentralizing governmental power is key to keeping our state and our nation free.
A Higher Standard of Education through School Choice Offering choice in how education dollars are spent is critical in creating quality education in our state.
The bottom line is that competition is the best way to accomplish the goal of the most benefit being derived from the money spent.
The ability to choose your school, and vote with your dollars, brings much needed accountability to a system that has operated as a monopoly for the vast majority of our children's education.
As is commonly the case, parents will make the best decisions about what is best for their individual children and circumstances, along with making necessary changes if something isn't working.
This will ultimately improve the level of competency in the next generation of citizens but will certainly upset the status quo which is too often a mechanism for indoctrination instead of education.

A Higher Standard of Representation by Saying No to Special Interests in Idaho Idaho citizens deserve leaders who represent their conservative values and are transparent about what they believe and how they will vote.
The judgment of too many government officials has been clouded by special interest groups lobbying for favors and hand-outs which, in turn, has eroded the public's trust in their representatives.

As District 4 Idaho State Senator I commit to only accept funds* from those who have the well-being, values and rights of my constituents at heart. * Funds received from lobbying groups will not be used by my campaign but will be forwarded to Conservative PAC's and other Conservative Candidates A Higher Standard of Governance by Protecting Citizens Rights Citizens have a fundamental, God-given right to bodily autonomy and privacy regarding their medical decisions.

Furthermore the Right to Bear arms is inextricably tied to the protection of our rights by ensuring Self Defense (Life), Resistance to Tyranny (Liberty) and the Ability to Hunt (Pursuit of Happiness).
The government is formed to protect rights and serve citizens not to provide special favors or redistribute wealth.
Property rights are at the core of our society and property ownership encourages financially and societally responsible citizenship.
Legislative Record Review the bills I have sponsored and my voting history representing District 4.

added: Home About Issues Newsletter Get Involved Contact Contribute Toggle menu Back to News A Letter to my Constituents April 11, 2023 5 min read Dear Constituent, It's been quite a learning experience navigating through my first session serving as your State Senator.

While I spent a fair amount of time working to understand the nuances of the legislative process, I'm happy to report that I was still productive in moving forward the causes you sent me to Boise to champion, including personally sponsoring a total of seven bills that were signed into law.

The following outlines the successes of the 2023 session and highlights key roles I played in specific areas: Education As Vice Chair of the Education Committee, I had the honor of sponsoring and supporting important legislation focused on our children's education.

Although one of my top priorities, Universal Education Savings Accounts ( S1038 ), failed to move forward, there was progress made and I was the senate sponsor for the following bills: H163 - significantly expanded Idaho law protecting parental rights in their child's education.
S1015 - closed a loophole where part-time students could be counted, and funded, as full-time.
S1125 - was the first comprehensive update to open enrollment in 30 years, allowing parents expanded choice in the public school that best fits their child's unique needs.

Additional education-related legislation that was passed through my committees & with my support includes: H314a - protects children from obscene content in schools and libraries (State Affairs - Vetoed) H182a - ensures the right to prayer in our public schools (State Affairs) S1100 - requires students to use bathroom/shower facilities of their biological sex (Education) S1042 / S1043 / H345 - supports and expand Charter Schools (Education) H269 / S1070 - expands Career Exploration & Career Technical Education (Education) Transportation As a member of the Transportation Committee, I helped ensure that your tax dollars are put to the best use in building and maintaining the roadways and bridges that connect our communities.
I sponsored H09 which allowed Commercial Driver's Licenses to be renewed online which will both help lessen congestion at the DMV and waste less of our commercial drivers' valuable time.
In addition, I sponsored H237 which prioritizes utilization of our precious tax dollars for use on local bridges and highways.

State Affairs I was honored to be one of the first freshmen ever assigned to the State Affairs Committee that deals with some of the most important, and controversial, legislation that goes through the Senate.

As a member of this committee, I sponsored H22a which stops Idaho cities from becoming sanctuaries from state felony law, along with H174a which clarifies that policies of state agencies don't carry the force and effect of law.
Other important legislation that I supported in this committee includes: HJM2 - calls on Congress to restrict the jurisdiction of federal courts regarding abortion cases.
H98 - prevents the illegal trafficking of minors to procure a criminal abortion.
H295 - prevents tracking of firearms and ammunition purchases through credit card codes.
Property Tax Reducing property tax, especially for homeowners, was a top priority for myself and many other legislators going into the 2023 session.
Through a long process of negotiations, we were able to come into agreement on a solution ( H292 *) that gives over $350 million in property tax relief to taxpayers.
This didn't lower property taxes to the degree I was hoping for but was certainly a step in the right direction.

It also included a fix to the circuit breaker deduction to make sure seniors on fixed incomes are able to stay in their homes. *Despite being vetoed by Governor Little this important legislation became law after both the House and Senate voted to override the veto.
Protecting Children's Innocence A top focus of mine during my campaign and going into my first legislative session was protection of the children in our community.
Along with the successful legislation that I helped pass, I also sponsored a bill, S1071 , that would have protected our youngest children from radical gender theory and oversexualization.
This bill received overwhelming support in the Idaho Senate passing the Senate Education Committee on a 7-2 vote and the Senate Floor on party lines with a veto proof majority 28-7 vote.
Unfortunately, like many good bills this session, this bill was drawered in the House Education Committee and never received a hearing.
Another important piece of legislation I sponsored was H265 which would have protected minors from exposure to sexual performances.
This bill passed the House 48-21 but never received a hearing in Senate State Affairs.
I plan to continue work on both important pieces of legislation next session.
I would appreciate your prayers and support as I fight for the most innocent and vulnerable in our society.

Despite the long days and significant hurdles, I'm encouraged that we have many good people working in our Capitol and fighting for the rights and conservative values that make Idaho such a great place to live and raise our families.
I welcome your input on concerns and issues you would like me to address going forward, so please don't hesitate to give me a call or send an email.

As always, thank you for the trust that you have placed in me to represent you and I pledge to continue to keep your interests, not special interests, as my top priority as I work to serve the great state of Idaho in the coming year.
Sincerely, Ben Toews Idaho State Senator – District 4 BEN TOEWS - FOR SENATE DISTRICT 4 - Substack Paid for by Benjamin Toews for Senate Treasurer Matthew Weed

title.after: "Extremism" Attacks are a Leftist Technique - I thought this was a Republican Primary - Ben Toews for Senate

added: Home About Issues Newsletter Get Involved Contact Contribute Toggle menu Back to News "Extremism" Attacks are a Leftist Technique - I thought this was a Republican Primary Writer: Ben Toews May 12, 2022 Updated: Mar 22, 2024 3 min read I'd like to go back to the good old days, when people were judged by their actions not whatever the trolls online, the liberal press and their opponents' attack ads said about them.
Then again, maybe there was never a time when that was a reality.
Still, now it is easier than ever to propagate lies because of how fast information spreads.
What makes the lies so dangerous and why do I feel compelled to respond?

Well, it isn't because I think the Dept. of Homeland Security's new Disinformation Governance Board (which plays the same role as The Ministry of Truth from 1984) should get involved in setting the record straight.
It's not because I am a fragile victim who needs to be protected or am afraid and need to defend myself.
It's because people need to know the truth and they aren't going to hear it in the CdA Press or on the nightly news.
Kids are all too often the victims of adults playing stupid games.

I guess I shouldn't have been surprised when my twelve year old told us that he just recently started getting yelled at, flipped off and followed by young adults since my campaign started - he has helped me knock on doors and is in our promotional material.
Simultaneously, I had a car stop and back up to try to spit on me while I was standing beside my truck which prominently displays my campaign signs.
As it turns out, normal citizens like me stepping up to serve our community invariably challenges the established power structure.
Those who have, or want to maintain, power are willing to go to extreme lengths even if it puts an innocent family in danger - but my question was, where is all the vitriol coming from?
Rhetoric Used to Divide It didn't take long for me to figure it out.
A couple of moms of young adults who just became eligible to vote, explained to us that their young adults had gotten 4-5 robocalls recently warning that I was a dangerous extremist.
The goal of these calls is certainly to gain a few votes but the result of spreading lies, fear and inciting anger is more division, in an increasingly isolated and divided community.
Then a letter came today from a former politician in the area, with libelous statements using the same baseless verbiage to try to tarnish my reputation.
Who's the extremist again?
My opponent and her supporters are using buzzwords like "EXTREMIST", a common page from the leftist playbook, to deceive and manipulate people.
I guess I just didn't expect this liberal tactic to be a part of a Republican primary election with two self-proclaimed conservative candidates.
On paper we might as well just combine forces since we are supposedly fighting for the same things: Pro Life, 2A Rights, Public Safety etc.

But, as is usually the case, the reality is far from what appears on the surface, and that becomes increasingly obvious based on the tactics used by my opponent which are identical to those used currently by the Democrat party.
My opponent is a self-proclaimed "Citizen of the world," a fan of the late abortion supporter Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg and is endorsed/supported by leftist activists.
It appears there is a coordinated effort between my opponent's campaign and a group called the Idaho 97 who support Democrat and liberal candidates consistently in political races in Idaho.

They are a group that supposedly "counters disinformation and extremism" according to their website and has endorsed my opponent while labeling me as an "extremist-backed candidate." What they fail to do is explain who is supposedly backing me and how that makes me extreme.
It's easier to just label someone as "Bad" without explaining why.
My greatest concern is that this is a tactic used by true extremists that purposefully infuse division, fear and anger into communities in order to divide and, ultimately, gain control.
Extremist terminology shows accuser's true position.
Nobody that I know wants to be labeled an extremist.
I guess if you really think about it, using this terminology actually indicates where the person using the description is positioned.

A constitutional conservative like myself, who wants to have reasonable conversations (without being shouted down or called names if I have different beliefs than someone else) may seem extreme to someone on the left who believes in micro-aggression and thought-crime.

Based on this line of reasoning my opponent, and her supporters, are really just outing themselves for how liberal they really are, since the vast majority of constituents I speak with in the community, and while going door to door, are like-minded and don't want this type of divide and conquer politics in our beautiful city.

A fair question for constituents to ask: Is someone who uses liberal techniques and unsubstantiated name-calling really the best representative for a community that values respectful discourse and conservative values?

added.text: [image: Bert Mizusawa avatar]Bert Mizusawa@GenBert2026·Oct 15I served 41 years in uniform. This November, I ask that you spend just 41 minutes researching the candidates and voting.

[image: Bert Mizusawa avatar]Bert Mizusawa@GenBert2026·Oct 16Simple solutions can create big results when it comes to affordability. By thinking about the mechanisms of affordability and passing common-sense legislation, we can make an impact! What is Mark Warner's plan to help make life more affordable?! He has been in Congress for three terms already and still doesn't have a plan. And even if he did, he doesn't think you deserve to hear it because, if he did, he would debate me!

removed.text: [image: Bert Mizusawa avatar]Bert Mizusawa@GenBert2026·Oct 13Happy Birthday to the United States Navy! For 251 years, and through numerous wars and conflicts to this day, America’s Sailors have defended us and braved numerous challenges to keep our vital sea routes open and secure. To every Sailor, past and present, and their families and survivors who supported their service and sacrifice: thank you for the steadfast and intrepid support of our great maritime nation. Fair winds and following seas.

[image: Bert Mizusawa avatar]Bert Mizusawa@GenBert2026·Oct 13Mark Warner used a 51% childhood food insecurity claim to advance a political narrative about the White House ballroom. Yet the report behind that figure won’t release its full methodology until 2027. The USDA’s data puts Virginia’s household food insecurity rate at about 13%, a very different picture. These statistics deserve scrutiny, not political spin. Fighting childhood hunger should be about feeding hungry children, not using them as political talking points. Virginians deserve transparency and facts. https://restoration-news.com/warner-s-childhood-hunger-hoax-exposed

added: Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Donate → Home Meet Andy Meet Sine Endorsements News Action Center Issues Media Kit Donate Online Donate By Mail Store Donate Donate By Mail Store Andy Biggs in Bullhead City: “Katie Hobbs Loves Taxes…” October 14, 2026 Press Release Biggs and running mate Sine Kerr join President Trump in Bullhead City to make economic case against Hobbs, who pushed to double state gas tax GILBERT, AZ— Republican nominee for Governor Andy Biggs and his running mate Lt.
Governor nominee Sine Kerr joined President Donald J.
Trump today in Bullhead City to make the economic case against Democrat Katie Hobbs, who has pushed to double the state’s gas tax and increase the state sales tax .

Under Hobbs, Arizona has become one of the least affordable states in the country as her policies have stopped the construction of homes in some parts of Maricopa County and her three vetoes of No Tax on Tips and Overtime delayed benefits for Arizonans.

Over a half mile line of supporters arrived at the rally in Bullhead City, where CNN reported attendees “ overwhelmingly said they are very excited to vote in November ” and noted the high-energy from supporters throughout the state who made their way to the rally.

removed: Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Donate → Home Meet Andy Meet Sine Endorsements News Action Center Issues Media Kit Donate Online Donate By Mail Store Donate Donate By Mail Store Biggs for Arizona Releases New Ad: “Katie Hobbs Chose Predators” September 1, 2026 Press Release :30 ad hits Hobbs on four separate vetoes where she chose to protect pedophiles, predators, and pornographers GILBERT, AZ—The Biggs for Arizona campaign today released a new ad, “ Katie Hobbs Chose Predators ”, calling out Hobbs for vetoing four different bills written to protect vulnerable women and children from predators.

While Hobbs struggles to explain her consistent record of defending pedophiles, predators, and pornographers, Republican nominee for Governor Andy Biggs continues to earn support from the law enforcement community with a recent endorsement from the Arizona Fraternal Order of Police .

Biggs now has endorsements from AZFOP, the Arizona Law Enforcement Association, three Prisons Local Unions across Arizona, and law enforcement leaders like Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell, Maricopa County Sheriff Jerry Sheridan, Pinal County Sheriff Ross Teeple, and Pinal County Attorney Brad Miller.

Watch the new ad highlighting Hobbs’s disturbing record of protecting predators below: Katie Hobbs has a horrifying pattern of protecting predators and pornographers through misguided vetoes since becoming Governor.
Hobbs’s dangerous vetoes include: SB 1583 (2023) – This bill would have required the names of all sex offenders to be published on a website managed by the Arizona Department of Public Safety.
Hobbs’s veto gave cover to sexual predators and reduced the transparency needed to keep children safe.
SB 1253 (2023) – This bill would have required sex offenders to give notice to their child’s school of their status as a sex offender.
Hobbs’s veto endangered children at schools whose parents may not have been aware of a sex offender’s presence in their community.

SB 1155 (2024) – This bipartisan bill “ would have prohibited a person on lifetime probation for a sexual offense from petitioning the court to terminate that probation before 20 years have passed for class 2 and 3 felonies and 10 years for classes 3-6.” Hobbs’s veto increased the likelihood that sexual predators would be able to get off probation and re-terrorize their victims.

HB 2133 (2026) – This bipartisan bill would “ have required websites hosting sexual material, including artificial intelligence-generated sexual depictions, to verify that each person depicted in the material is of legal age and consented to it.” Hobbs’s veto prioritized politicians and pornographers over innocent children who could be exploited on the internet.

title.before: AG Bird dedicates Iowa's $126M from Meta settlement - Brenna Bird Attorney General

removed: Donate Connect with Brenna News Donate News AG Bird dedicates Iowa’s $126M from Meta settlement September 22, 2026 DES MOINES — The state's share — roughly $126 million — of a national settlement with the social media giant Meta over the harms of social media to teenagers will be used to establish payments for Iowa teens, help the state prosecute consumer protection laws, and put more law enforcement officers in schools, Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird announced Monday.
During a press conference Monday at the Iowa Capitol, Bird announced her office's establishment of what she said was the country's first restitution fund created out of the settlement.
Iowa was among the 47 states that sued Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, over teen social media addiction.
Last month, Meta agreed to pay up to $18 million and add stronger safety measures for children to its social media sites.
Iowa will receive $126 million from the settlement, which will be paid out over 10 years, Bird said Monday.

Per the settlement agreement, at least half the funds must be used to address the harms alleged in the lawsuit: namely, that the social media sites contained features designed to hook children's attention.

Bird and her office said Monday that Iowa's share of the settlement funds will include: $25 million paid directly to young Iowans impacted by the social media sites. $11 million into a state fund for the enforcement of consumer protection and child safety laws. $# million toward grants to Iowa schools to address the harms of social media, including but not limited to covering the costs of school resource officers. $# million to assist victims and toward enforcement of state laws governing related to social media and online safety. $3 million to upgrade Iowa Attorney General's Office technology used to enforce child safety online. $7.3 million to address harms related to social media.
Roughly $49 million will be deposited in Iowa's general fund, Bird said.
A portion of the settlement funds also will cover legal and other fees, and the state will hire an administrator to ensure the proper disbursement of the funds, Bird said.
Regarding the payments to impacted Iowa teens, Bird said her office's initial estimates are that the payments could be roughly $100 each.
She said her office will have more information in the future about how Iowa teens can file a claim to receive a restitution payment.

Bird celebrated both the financial terms and policy restrictions detailed in the settlement, the latter of which she called "groundbreaking" in an effort to make social media and the internet safer for teens and children.
"I fight to keep our kids safe, and I hold big tech accountable for what they allow on their platforms for children and teens," Bird said at the press conference.

"Under the terms of the victory (settlement), Instagram and Facebook will be safer for Iowa kids. … "What's happening on social media causes serious mental and physical health problems, and we are taking action." Bird invited to speak at the press conference representatives of the Harlan Community School District and Shelby County Sheriff's Office.
The school district employs a school resource officer in partnership with the sheriff's department.

Harlan School District High School assistant principal and athletic director Anthony Donahoo, and School Resource Officer RJ Bielenberg joined Bird in describing their belief in how resource officers can be helpful in schools.
"A lot of schools want a school resource officer and have seen the good that it does in other schools, but aren't in a position to get that program started," Bird said.

"So my hope is that this grant funding will help schools around Iowa who want a school resource officer and law enforcement agencies that want to be able to do that to be able to work together to get a school resource officer program started, so that every school can have a great program like we just heard about today at Harlan Community Schools.

We would hope that as many schools as possible would have a program like that." When asked whether school resource officers are trained on issues like social media addiction, cyberbullying and online harassment, Bielenberg said the National School Resource Officers Association has basic and advanced classes that cover cyber crimes and technology.
He said the issues are covered "vaguely," and that he would welcome more such training opportunities.
Bird noted her office has active, similar lawsuits against the social media site TikTok and social gaming platform Roblox.

Naig said the implementation of the robotic milking system was part of the Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship Choose Iowa Dairy Innovation Grant Program, where grants are awarded to Iowa farms.
"They were able to secure these grant dollars and then put in two robotic milkers, which is a labor-saving piece of technology," Naig said.

Although the attorney general and secretary of agriculture offices are separate, they still work with each other, according to Bird.

During media availability after the event, Bird said she is campaigning all over Iowa.
"As a prosecutor, I work very closely with law enforcement and county attorneys and also work to help crime victims and keep Iowa safe," Bird said.

"We're hearing good feedback, people appreciate our cold case unit, which focuses on the over 400 unsolved homicides in Iowa, making sure that nobody gets away with murder, and that we are always working to bring those cases to justice and get answers for survivors and families." Iowa Secretary of Agriculture Mike Naig and Attorney General Brenna Bird were given a tour of Cornbelt Dairy located in Cherokee County.
The dairy farm is owned by the Wilcox family and has been selling milk commercially since 1947.
During the tour, the family spoke with Naig and Bird about the automatic milking system that they were able to acquire due to the Choose Iowa Dairy Innovation Grant.

So we were encouraged that was included.
And now the work continues to get that farm bill passed through the full Senate," said Naig.
Naig also talked about water quality across the state and how more needs to be done to tackle the issue.
Emphasizing that if reelected, he plans to accelerate those efforts.
"Iowans are concerned about water quality, and what I want them to know is we are working on this, and we've been making progress, and we need to do more.

We're bringing an extra focus in places like Cherokee on converting cropland that's highly erosive ground or less productive ground into pasture for cattle, which is great for the environment and good for those farm families and the economy.
Cover crops, no-till, putting buffers along streams, and nutrient management is always really important," said Naig.
Naig is currently traveling across the state as a part of his 'Keep Iowa Growing' tour.
Mike Naig has served as Secretary of Agriculture since 2018; this November, he faces Democratic candidate Chris Jones.

An on-site inspection caught the breach, not border safeguards.
The attorneys general say this follows the same pattern as the Heparin crisis nearly #ago that killed or harmed hundreds of Americans.
Recent reports show Chinese manufacturers associated with fentanyl supply chains are finding a new U.S. market in peptides, including cosmetic and weight-loss drugs.

The states question whether entities connected to fentanyl precursor markets moving into peptides could mean GLP-1 ingredients and related peptides are being introduced into the American compounding market.
The coalition asked to be provided with any information to protect their constituents.

title.before: Iowa Medicaid Fraud Control Unit highlights efficiency; critics call for more funding - Brenna Bird Attorney General

removed: Donate Connect with Brenna News Donate News Iowa Medicaid Fraud Control Unit highlights efficiency; critics call for more funding September 24, 2026 Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said Thursday that recommendations about increased staffing and funding for existing Medicaid fraud elimination efforts will come at later meetings of the state Medicaid Fraud Elimination Task Force.
The task force was established by executive order July 1 by Gov.
Kim Reynolds.
It is charged with submitting a final report by Oct.
29, 2026 for the governor and lawmakers with recommendations on how to reduce and prevent incidents of Medicaid fraud.
While the members did not deliberate on any specific planned recommendations, leaders gave updates from work groups about their efforts to find areas for improvement.
Members also got an update on work currently underway by the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit to address fraud within Iowa's taxpayer-funded healthcare program.

Jeremy Ingrim, the director of the unit, said federal evaluations and data have shown Iowa's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit is more efficient than those in other states, "despite being one of the smallest units based on staffing and funding." Ingrim said in federal fiscal year 2025, Iowa's unit was ranked 10th highest in total convictions with 37 total convictions, above the national average among all 53 units of 22.

With total operating expenses for the Iowa MFCU at $1.3 million in FY 2025, he said the approximate government cost for the unit was $36,700 for each conviction, the lowest conviction cost among all units nationwide.

"In other words, the government got the most bang for its buck in Iowa for criminal convictions in federal fiscal year 2025, and the unit remains on track in the current federal fiscal year for similar results," Ingrim said.
Iowa's fraud control unit was created in the 1970s and exists within the Iowa Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL).
Dean Lerner, who served as director of Iowa Department of Inspections and Appeals under former Democratic Gov.

Chet Culver, told reporters after the task force meeting the funding for Iowa MFCU was "woefully inadequate compared to other states with similar budgets." Lerner, as well as Kevin Techau, another former Iowa Department of Inspections and Appeals director, held a news conference in July calling the task force a "sham." Lerner said hiring additional staff and providing more funding for the MFCU would be the most effective way to tackle Medicaid fraud in the state, because 75 cents per dollar spent comes from federal funding, and he said between $4 and $5 are recovered by the unit for each dollar spent.
According to Ingrim, the Iowa MCFU has nine staff members — five investigators, an assistant attorney general, a data analyst who also serves as an auditor, a paralegal, as well as a director.
The unit is authorized to have 11 total staff and currently has two vacancies.

Bird said the task force has not yet made funding or staffing recommendations for the MCFU, but said, "that would be something that would be in a final report." She praised the Iowa MCFU is "a very efficient unit," but said the task force's goal was to provide new avenues to find instances of fraud.
"It's important that we are not just reactive, but we are proactive when it comes to fighting fraud," Bird said.

"And so it is very important that we get those tips from people, and that those are investigated and followed up on — but we also need to be more proactive, looking at where the fraud may be occurring, rather than waiting for someone to discover it and report it. … Even though we have a great and efficient unit, which I do appreciate, we should take a look at everything.

Everything's on the table to make sure that we are doing what we can as a state to eliminate fraud in our state, especially when it comes to taxpayer dollars." Working group leaders shared ideas and discussions they had since the August task force meeting on finding ways to allow Iowans to report instances of fraud, as well as to use data and analytics to identify cases where fraud may be occurring by flagging issues like overlapping claims or unusual billing.
Ingrim also told the task force increasing enforcement of the state's Civil False Claims Act "could increase Medicaid fraud recoveries" in Iowa.

The MCFU already has an assistant attorney general who works to ensure Iowa's participation in nationwide civil cases involving Medicaid programs in multiple states, he said, but said there could be increased efforts to expand enforcement of Iowa Code on actors attempting to present false or fraudulent claims for payment to the state of Iowa.

"Establishing procedures and coordinating available DIAL and Attorney General's office resources to pursue violations of Iowa Code Chapter 685 may serve as a force multiplier to increase Medicaid fraud recoveries and assist in deterring healthcare fraud in Iowa," Ingrim said.
Lerner said the Iowa AG's office is responsible for investigating Iowa Civil False Claims Act cases.
He said Bird should increase a focus on pursuing cases against care facilities that do not provide services Medicaid pays for under this law.
"There are numerous opportunities to file those cases against nursing homes that are providing woefully inadequate care to people and killing people," Lerner said.

"Those dollars that are spent on those nursing homes for Medicaid residents should be sought from the nursing homes and put back into the state coffers, and they're not being done, and that would be one area that should be a big focus." Bird said while the task force will create a report on ways to reduce Medicaid fraud, it will be up to state lawmakers and the governor whether to implement their recommendations.

"This is the first step in the process, but a very important one, because we want to make sure that the solutions that we're proposing, the ideas that task force members have about how to make things better, are things that will work and be effective, and that we are doing everything we can to eliminate fraud in Iowa," Bird said.

removed: Donate Connect with Brenna News Donate News Iowa Medicaid Fraud Control Unit reports $3.9M in recoveries as task force continues work September 24, 2026 Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird said the Medicaid Fraud Elimination Task Force's recommendations are expected later next month.
The group has to send them to the governor by the end of October.
The group held its third meeting Thursday, providing updates on what the work groups are looking into.
"It's important that we are not just reactive but proactive when it comes to fighting fraud," Bird said.

"And so it is very important that we get those tips from people and that those are investigated and followed up on, but we also need to be more proactive looking at where the fraud may be occurring rather than waiting for someone to discover it and report it." The director of Iowa's Medicaid Fraud Control Unit said new federal evaluations ranked Iowa 10th in the country for convictions, despite the unit being among the smallest in terms of staffing and funding.

"For 2026, through the end of August, the unit has already reported recoveries over $3.9 million and total expenditures of nearly $1.2 million," Medicaid Fraud Control Unit Director Jeremy Ingrim said.
"This has resulted in a return on investment of 338%.

In other words, we've recovered $3.38 for every dollar spent to operate the unit." After the meeting, Dean Lerner, who previously served as director of the Iowa Department of Inspections and Appeals, said the unit does not have adequate staffing or funding compared with units in other states with similar budgets.
Lerner said it would be a "mistake" for the task force not to recommend increases in both.

title.after: Iowa sues multiple tech firms over alleged China ties - Brenna Bird Attorney General

added: Donate Connect with Brenna News Donate News Iowa sues multiple tech firms over alleged China ties October 9, 2026 Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird is launching a new wave of litigation against companies she says have concealed ties to the Chinese government.

Bird has filed lawsuits against networking and Smart Home manufacturer TP-Link and security camera company ADI Global and suggests more filings are planned in the coming week against "China-aligned entities." Both companies, she alleges, have violated the Iowa Consumer Fraud Act by misleading customers about the safety of their data.
“Iowans’ sensitive data and our national security is at risk because of TP-Link and their connection to the communist Chinese government,” Bird said in a statement.
“TP-Link tells Iowans its routers are safe, our personal data is secure, and that they have no ties to China.
They are not telling the truth.

It’s time to hold China and China-backed companies accountable.” According to Bird, TP-Link's routers are manufactured in Vietnam, but nearly all components, research and development comes from China, "using firmware that gives the Communist Chinese government access to Iowans' devices and data." ADI, meanwhile, is accused of selling cameras manufactured by Chinese companies on national security watchlists, even switching labels to conceal the products' origins.

"These China-made cameras are making Iowans' private information – everything from where each room is in your home, who lives there, your routine, and even passwords – available to the Chinese government and military," Bird said.
The lawsuits, filed in Polk County, are part of a coordinated multistate push, with at least Florida, Nebraska and Montana also filing lawsuits against TP-Link.
In a press release, the company said the lawsuits are based on "false premises" and that the company is not owned or controlled by any foreign government.

"We stand fully behind the security of our products, the integrity of our company and our people, and our commitment to serving the best interests of our customers in the United States and globally," TP-Link spokesman Steve Kovsky said.
"We look forward to refuting these baseless allegations in court." The Register has reached out to ADI Global for comment.
The TP-Link and ADI lawsuits were announced Oct.
6 and Oct.
7, respectively.
Bird also joined a coalition of Republican attorneys general Oct.
8 to call on the National Judicial College to distance itself from an environmentalist group they allege also has links to China.

The Nevada-based college bills itself as "the nation's leading provider of judicial education." Read more here Share: Paid For By Bird For Iowa PRIVACY POLICY · TERMS & CONDITIONS · RESEARCH · INFORMATION

title.after: Rhode Islanders Deserve Answers from Foulkes on CVS Opioid Case, Not a Spokesperson's Statement | Ken Block for Governor

added: ★ November 3, 2026 Countdown to Election Day # Days # Hours # Minutes # Seconds Home About Issues Appearances Media & Press Ken I Be Honest Polls Donate Donate ← Media & Press Official Press Release Rhode Islanders Deserve Answers from Foulkes on CVS Opioid Case, Not a Spokesperson's Statement CVS has agreed to pay $315 million to resolve federal allegations of illegally filling opioid prescriptions and seeking improper payment from Medicare and other federal healthcare programs Release Date October 15, 2026 Location Barrington, Rhode Island Media Contact michelle@blockforgovernor.com Barrington, Rhode Island — BARRINGTON, RI – Independent candidate for Governor Ken Block today called on Democratic nominee Helena Foulkes to provide more details regarding her actions at CVS in light of the company’s decision to reach a settlement with federal prosecutors in a major opioid case.
“Helena Foulkes ran CVS Pharmacy during a period when serious violations allegedly occurred, and Rhode Islanders deserve more than a short statement from her campaign spokesperson,” said Block.
“The federal complaint says, among other things, that pharmacists faced pressure to fill prescriptions and CVS failed to respond adequately to warnings.
Given the devastating toll of the opioid crisis on families across Rhode Island, she owes the public more transparency and it should come directly from her.” On Tuesday, the U.S.
Department of Justice announced that CVS will pay $315 million to resolve allegations that it illegally filled opioid prescriptions and billed federal health programs for them.
The government's case covers conduct beginning in October 2013 and ending in December 2025.
Foulkes was president of CVS Pharmacy from January 2014 to February 2018, with responsibility for the company's retail business including pharmacy operations.
Foulkes responded to the settlement with a short written statement from a spokesperson .
Yesterday, she declined an interview with NBC 10 .
In early September, before the primary election, NBC 10 asked Foulkes whether CVS, under her leadership, ignored red flags as the lawsuit alleged.
She replied: “No.
CVS will defend itself at some point.
I think the record will show that CVS was a leader in the industry.” CVS agreed to settle the federal case and resolve the government's allegations without defending itself in court.

According to the complaint the Justice Department filed in December 2024 , CVS: (1) filled prescriptions for “pill mill” doctors; (2) dispensed dangerous combinations of opioids, benzodiazepines, and muscle relaxants; (3) ignored red flags raised by its own pharmacists and internal data; and (4) used performance metrics, incentive pay, and staffing levels that put profits ahead of patient safety.
“Six weeks ago, she told Rhode Islanders that CVS would defend its record,” Block said.
“Instead, CVS agreed to pay $315 million to resolve the federal case and accepted additional federal oversight of its controlled-substance dispensing through August 15, 2032 .

I think Rhode Islanders deserve to know what role Helena Foulkes played in approving and overseeing the performance metrics, incentive pay, and staffing policies that allegedly pressured pharmacists to fill prescriptions despite warning signs.” The complaint also describes certain decisions CVS made while Foulkes was in charge.
In 2015 and 2016, CVS tested a program requiring pharmacists to document every prescription they refused to fill because they doubted it was legitimate.
Most participating pharmacists said the program had value and it would have let CVS quickly identify and block high-risk prescribers.
CVS cancelled it .
Of the seven doctors named in the complaint, the alleged misconduct for six fell mostly within Foulkes's tenure, according to a Boston Globe review .
Among them is Dr.
Raymond Kraynak, Pennsylvania's top opioid prescriber in 2014, 2015 and 2016.
According to the complaint , CVS pharmacists and staff escalated concerns about Kraynak 17 times beginning in April 2014, more than any other prescriber in the country.
CVS did not block him until June 2017.
He was indicted that December, and in 2021 he pleaded guilty and admitted that opioids he prescribed resulted in the deaths of five patients.
He was sentenced to 15 years in federal prison .
Asked about Kraynak by name during an August 12 News debate , Foulkes did not address his case.
“Why did CVS keep filling Dr.
Raymond Kraynak's prescriptions for three years after its own pharmacists first raised concerns?” Block asked.

“Was Helena Foulkes aware of this at the time?” In the final days of her primary campaign, Foulkes told the Providence Journal that questions about opioids were “totally fair game.” “She said it herself, these questions are fair game,” Block said.

“Anyone who wants to serve as Governor must be willing to answer difficult questions about their professional record.” CVS admitted no wrongdoing in the settlement, which resolves allegations without a determination of liability.
Foulkes was not named as a defendant in the case.

added: top of page HOME ABOUT BOB BLOG EVENTS ON THE TRAIL WITH BOB FIORETTI VOLUNTEER Fioretti Direct Mail Campaign PODCASTS/MEDIA CONTACT US DONATE Search All Posts safe t act Search On the Trail: Debates in Alton & Galesburg, WSIU Interview, and Charleston Tour #ago 2 min read CAMPAIGN UPDATE • OCT 2026 DISPATCH FROM THE TRAIL Showing Up for the People of Illinois.

From town halls to the Lincoln-Douglas debate stages, Bob Fioretti is crisscrossing the state with an uncompromising commitment: putting justice, civil rights, education, and public safety back into the hands of Illinois citizens—free from special interests.
Fuel the Campaign Grassroots donations keep us independent and competitive in all 102 counties.
Donate Today Join Our Team Volunteer to knock doors, make calls, and spread the message across your community.

Volunteer Now FEATURED MEDIA COVERAGE Listen: Bob Fioretti on WSIU Public Radio Bob sat down with WSIU Radio to address key challenges facing working families across Southern Illinois, outlining decisive solutions for curbing crime, upholding civil liberties, and restoring integrity to the Attorney General's office.

Listen to the WSIU Interview THE LINCOLN-DOUGLAS DEBATE TOUR Debates in Alton & Galesburg—On to Charleston Answering to You This week, Bob traveled to Alton and Galesburg to participate in the Lincoln-Douglas debate series.
Despite his opponent Kwame Raoul declining to attend and face the public, Bob honored his commitment to address voter concerns directly.
Next Stop: Charleston, IL Today, the campaign arrives in Charleston, IL.
Regardless of who shows up on stage, Bob Fioretti remains dedicated to traveling across every corner of our state to present his vision for real accountability and public safety.
OUR CORE PRIORITIES A Principled Agenda for Illinois Justice & Integrity Ending political favoritism and being the People's attorney, not the politically connected.
Consumer Rights for All Protecting Consumers and safeguarding them from fraud.
Public Safety & Law Enforcement Empowering law enforcement and ensuring that victims matter.
Education & Community Safeguarding children, defending parental transparency, and partnering in youth safety.
Stand with Bob Fioretti Bob's independence is his greatest strength.
Bob will answer only to Illinois citizens, not special interests.
Help Bob take this message to every neighborhood.
Bob will fight for you!

11/8/2025 • IN THE NEWS Read More Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Brad Chambers Announces Campaign for Pennsylvania’s 41st State House District with High-Profile Endorsements FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE August 20, 2025 LANCASTER COUNTY, PA (August 20, 2025) - Brad Chambers has announced his campaign for PA HD-41 in 2026.
HD-41—comprising Columbia Borough, East and West Hempfield Townships, Mountville Borough, and part of Manor Township— is recognized as Lancaster County’s most competitive State House District.
Chambers previously ran in 2024 in a campaign that knocked more than 26,000 doors.

Chambers, a labor administrator and community advocate, intends to run on a campaign that fights for housing that is affordable for all, the funding our schools and children deserve, and lifesaving universal healthcare coverage.
Chambers has also obtained a number of significant endorsements from across the 41st District and Lancaster County.
Brad Chamber’s endorsements include: State Representative Ismail Smith-Wade-El (HD-49) - “Brad is my first endorsement of the 2026 cycle, and that’s no accident.
People in Lancaster are tired of politicians who have a lot of bark, but are leashed to their corporate donors.

Hempfield, Mountville, Columbia - they ought to have a State Representative who works for them, and no one works harder than Brad Chambers.” State Representative Nikki Rivera (HD-96) - “It is with great respect and admiration that I endorse Brad Chambers for PA State Representative in House District 41 in 2026.

Brad’s unwavering loyalty to his community, his outstanding work ethic, and his commitment to serving absolutely all of his neighbors earn him a spot on the ballot and the opportunity to serve in the PA General Assembly.” County Commissioner Alice Yoder - “It is my pleasure to endorse Brad Chambers for PA House in District 41.
Brad is hardworking and committed to serving his community and I know he will be an excellent representative for his district— which includes me!

I have been a witness to the way Brad has thrown himself into serving his community outside of politics and his dedication, integrity, work ethic, and genuine commitment to helping people make him an outstanding representative for all of us in the 41st.” Hempfield School Board Member Judy Brady - “Brad’s energy and devotion to building trusting, personal relationships with the Hempfield, Manor Township, and Columbia communities is truly remarkable.

I have full confidence that when elected, as he is ALREADY doing, Brad will tirelessly fight to bring equitable education funding, health care reform, and affordable housing to benefit his district constituents and all Pennsylvanians.

Brad Chambers is the exact person the HD-41 has been waiting for to represent the interests of all residents in this western region of Lancaster County.” Hempfield School Board Member Megan Eshleman - “As a local school board director, I am excited about having a representative like Brad who doesn't just talk about the importance of public education, but will back it up with actions in Harrisburg.” East Hempfield Supervisor Bob Johnson - “I endorse Brad Chambers for the position of PA State Representative for the 41st district in the 2026 election.
Brad is extremely hard-working, dependable, and energetic.

His positions on issues are well thought-out and consistent with what I believe are most beneficial to the residents of our district and the state.” Columbia Borough School Board President Charles Leader - “I give my support to Brad Chambers.
Brad is willing to serve the public.
Brad understands people and realizes their everyday concerns, challenges and issues.
He has the energy and commitment to be a positive force in Harrisburg.
I am convinced Brad will help initiate and bring about the needed changes in both his district and the state.

Giving Brad a chance to prove his ability will show he will work for the people and that is what is needed.” State Senator James Malone (SD-36) - “I'm honored to endorse Brad Chambers for PA's 41st statehouse District.
I've seen Brad's dedication to progress and working people first hand.

I can think of no one better to join me in representing Columbia and Hempfield in the state legislature.” “These past few months have demonstrated to me that the same issues that first called me to run for State Representative last year are more urgent than ever.
Donald Trump and Pennsylvania Republicans continue to gut our health care.
Rent and mortgage costs continue to soar.
Our teachers and students go without the resources they need.
Only when we realize that no one is coming to save us can we truly meet this political moment.

We must step up in any way we can, which is why I've decided I will be running for the 41st PA State House District in 2026.” - Brad Chambers, Candidate for HD-41 The Pennsylvania House Democratic Campaign Committee (PA HDCC) has previously identified Chambers' race in HD-41 as " one of the most competitive races in the state. " James Malone’s win in SD-36 with nearly all precincts in the 41st, as well as the promising primary vote totals in Hempfield and Columbia suggest the same.

11/8/2025 • IN THE NEWS Read More Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Press Releases Brad Chambers 8/25/25 Brad Chambers Announces Campaign for Pennsylvania’s 41st State House District with High-Profile Endorsements FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE August 20, 2025 LANCASTER COUNTY, PA (August 20, 2025) - Brad Chambers has announced his campaign for PA HD-41 in 2026.
HD-41—comprising Columbia Borough, East and West Hempfield Townships, Mountville Borough, and part of Manor Township— is recognized as Lancaster County’s most competitive State House District.
Chambers previously ran in 2024 in a campaign that knocked more than 26,000 doors.

Chambers, a labor administrator and community advocate, intends to run on a campaign that fights for housing that is affordable for all, the funding our schools and children deserve, and lifesaving universal healthcare coverage.
Chambers has also obtained a number of significant endorsements from across the 41st District and Lancaster County.
Brad Chamber’s endorsements include: State Representative Ismail Smith-Wade-El (HD-49) - “Brad is my first endorsement of the 2026 cycle, and that’s no accident.
People in Lancaster are tired of politicians who have a lot of bark, but are leashed to their corporate donors.

Hempfield, Mountville, Columbia - they ought to have a State Representative who works for them, and no one works harder than Brad Chambers.” State Representative Nikki Rivera (HD-96) - “It is with great respect and admiration that I endorse Brad Chambers for PA State Representative in House District 41 in 2026.

Brad’s unwavering loyalty to his community, his outstanding work ethic, and his commitment to serving absolutely all of his neighbors earn him a spot on the ballot and the opportunity to serve in the PA General Assembly.” County Commissioner Alice Yoder - “It is my pleasure to endorse Brad Chambers for PA House in District 41.
Brad is hardworking and committed to serving his community and I know he will be an excellent representative for his district— which includes me!

I have been a witness to the way Brad has thrown himself into serving his community outside of politics and his dedication, integrity, work ethic, and genuine commitment to helping people make him an outstanding representative for all of us in the 41st.” Hempfield School Board Member Judy Brady - “Brad’s energy and devotion to building trusting, personal relationships with the Hempfield, Manor Township, and Columbia communities is truly remarkable.

I have full confidence that when elected, as he is ALREADY doing, Brad will tirelessly fight to bring equitable education funding, health care reform, and affordable housing to benefit his district constituents and all Pennsylvanians.

Brad Chambers is the exact person the HD-41 has been waiting for to represent the interests of all residents in this western region of Lancaster County.” Hempfield School Board Member Megan Eshleman - “As a local school board director, I am excited about having a representative like Brad who doesn't just talk about the importance of public education, but will back it up with actions in Harrisburg.” East Hempfield Supervisor Bob Johnson - “I endorse Brad Chambers for the position of PA State Representative for the 41st district in the 2026 election.
Brad is extremely hard-working, dependable, and energetic.

His positions on issues are well thought-out and consistent with what I believe are most beneficial to the residents of our district and the state.” Columbia Borough School Board President Charles Leader - “I give my support to Brad Chambers.
Brad is willing to serve the public.
Brad understands people and realizes their everyday concerns, challenges and issues.
He has the energy and commitment to be a positive force in Harrisburg.
I am convinced Brad will help initiate and bring about the needed changes in both his district and the state.

Giving Brad a chance to prove his ability will show he will work for the people and that is what is needed.” State Senator James Malone (SD-36) - “I'm honored to endorse Brad Chambers for PA's 41st statehouse District.
I've seen Brad's dedication to progress and working people first hand.

I can think of no one better to join me in representing Columbia and Hempfield in the state legislature.” “These past few months have demonstrated to me that the same issues that first called me to run for State Representative last year are more urgent than ever.
Donald Trump and Pennsylvania Republicans continue to gut our health care.
Rent and mortgage costs continue to soar.
Our teachers and students go without the resources they need.
Only when we realize that no one is coming to save us can we truly meet this political moment.

We must step up in any way we can, which is why I've decided I will be running for the 41st PA State House District in 2026.” - Brad Chambers, Candidate for HD-41 The Pennsylvania House Democratic Campaign Committee (PA HDCC) has previously identified Chambers' race in HD-41 as " one of the most competitive races in the state. " James Malone’s win in SD-36 with nearly all precincts in the 41st, as well as the promising primary vote totals in Hempfield and Columbia suggest the same.

title.before: Hometown Hero

removed: Hometown Hero 2017​ Brian Schimmel: Service is his passion after lesson from son A phrase in the Bible’s Book of Isaiah, “And a child shall lead them,” might explain a mid-life change of career for Intel manager Brian Schimmel.
Three years ago, Schimmel’s son, Zach, chose as his Forest Grove High School senior project an assignment with Sonrise Church’s meals for homeless families program.
Zach found the weekly Sunday meals so meaningful that he said, “Dad, you ought to come with me,” Schimmel recalled.
Zach and his father soon immersed themselves into that project, as well as Meals on wheels, and the father began to notice a change in his life.
“Seeing how some seniors live could feel crushing – but when I would carry a meal inside their house and see their face light up, I felt I was experiencing God,” the soft-spoken Schimmel said.
Forest Grove is an urban metropolis compared to the dairy farm Schimmel grew up on in the remote coast range highlands, “out in the sticks” 20 miles south of Raining, Oregon.

Excellent grades earned him a full Navy ROTC scholarship to Oregon State University, where he showed leadership becoming the unit’s public affairs officer and led the conversion of the NROTC quarterly publication to a digital format A neck injury precluded hs serving active duty after graduating from OSU, and he went to work for Intel for 19 years, rising to become a global business enablement and acquisition manager.
But the community service that his son began role modeling spoke to him.

Schimmel has since contributed hundreds of hours coordinating a meals program, volunteering for Habitat for Humanity and the Forest Grove Senior and Community Center and chairing - and championing the city’s Sustainability Commission.
Schimmel, in 2016, decided to accept an employee buyout from Intel two months later and feels his service passion is just beginning.
And perhaps he is now the one role modeling for another family member.
Brian and Barb Schimmel’s youngest child, Zoe, began volunteering for Meals on Wheels herself.
“She would be with me every week delivering meals, and seniors would call her by name,” Brian said proudly, “and miss her on those days she couldn’t make it.”

removed: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: Independent Party of Oregon Announces Legislative Nominations Across Key Districts, encourages more people to run for the Oregon legislature Contact: ​ ​ Sal Peralta​ 503.437.2833​ oregon.properties@yahoo.com Salem - March 30 or 26 - The Independent Party of Oregon (IPO) today announced the nominations of Brian Schimmel (House District 29; Forest Grove, Hillsboro), Pat Hubbell (House District 40; Gladstone, Oregon City), Patrick Starnes (Senate District 6; Linn, Lane Counties), and Lisa Finkle (Senate District 16; Clatsop, Columbia, Tillamook Counties).
Three of these are currently open seats, without incumbents running.
The party previously nominated Charlie Conrad at its January caucus for House District 12 (Lane, Linn Counties).
The party running its own candidates in state legislative races represents a shift for IPO.
In previous years, the party has largely focused on cross-nominating Democratic and Republican candidates.

In 2022 and 2024, the party sided heavily with Democratic legislators in the Oregon House and Senate, helping the Democrats to secure their current majorities through highly successful campaigns in legislative swing districts.
This year, for the first time, the party is holding caucuses ahead of the state primary to give its candidates more time to build campaigns.
It will hold a fourth caucus in July to consider what major party candidates to cross-nominate, if any.
“A large number of qualified people stepping forward to run is unusual.
It’s a sign that people are frustrated,” said Drew Kaza, the party’s co-chair.
“People are starting to understand that the system is the problem.
The lobbyists, the party machines.
All of it.

They are too polarized, too compromised, and too focused on what agencies or lobbyists want, instead of what Oregon communities need.” “The Legislature is failing to deliver in areas like housing and education despite historic investments,” said Al Densmore, who serves on the party’s elected nominating caucus.
“People see rising costs, struggling schools, and then watch transparency and campaign finance rules get weakened.

It confirms what many already believe: That the system is tilted away from regular people.” (Note: Densmore is a former Mayor of Medford and a State Representative who was the Chief House Sponsor of SB 15, Oregon’s open meetings law.
He is available for media inquiries.) IPO will hold a third nominating caucus for candidates who are not seeking a major party nomination in May.
IPO nominations are open to members of all political parties.
“We are looking for engaged people who have the time to run as Independents.
Oregon needs problem-solvers who are not invested in the current system and who believe we can do better,” Kaza said.

These are the candidates who were nominated in the March caucus: Brian Schimmel (HD 29, Hillsboro–Forest Grove) brings decades of public and private sector leadership focused on housing, economic development, public safety, and community resilience.
His work includes administering public investments and structuring partnerships across government, nonprofit, and private sectors.
“Community institutions require solutions that function at the local level,” Schimmel said.

“Policy-making should reflect local insight and be structured for effective implementation—where outcomes are realized by those closest to the work.” ​ Contact: brian@brianschimmel.org Pat Hubbell (HD 40, Oregon City) is a pharmacist that operates an independent pharmacy in Oregon that is focused on pharmacy reform.
Hubbell highlights the pharmacy access disparity in Oregon and the high cost of medications.

Hubbell states, “Oregon ranks dead last in the number of independent pharmacies in our communities out of all 50 states.” This issue is a combination of poor, misunderstood legislative support and large PBM (Pharmacy Benefit Managers) bullying the state of Oregon.
Not only pharmacy, but physicians, nurses, and health care professionals are under the same level of economic pressures that are causing subpar or complete lack of care for Oregonians.
“I am here to gather healthcare professionals as we push for better work environments and proper reimbursements for positive healthcare outcomes, Hubbell said.

Affordability, the environment, infrastructure, fiscal responsibility and strong, vibrant communities are also top priorities Patrick Starnes (SD 6, Brownsville), a school board member and longtime advocate for campaign finance reform and affordability, is running as an economic populist.
“People are tired of a system where big money and party leadership drive the agenda,” Starnes said.

“If we want to fix affordability, housing, healthcare, education, then we need leaders to open up the process and actually listen to the people we represent.” Starnes has been a relentless advocate for campaign finance reform, which good government groups say was gutted in the 2026 short session.
Melisa Finkle (SD 16, Rockaway Beach) is a state employee and union leader focused on rural healthcare, transparency, and worker advocacy.
Finkle points to growing frustration with closed-door policymaking.
“When decisions are rushed or made in small rooms, people lose trust,” Finkle said.

“Oregonians want leaders who listen, explain their decisions, and work across differences to solve real problems especially in rural communities like mine that often get overlooked.” This slate reflects a growing demand for leadership that is independent of political machine structures, focused on affordability and effective governance, and responsive to people who are left out and ignored by the current system
