alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/826110940_17972713473150272_3423129184639354632_n.jpg|Hillyard Pride, and our table was one of the busiest in the park – thanks largely to the volunteers who staffed it and the campaign dog who held down the chair. Eastern Washington is a place where people look after each other. Pride here is neighbors, kids, dogs on leashes, and a community where everyone belongs. I am proud to stand with it, in Hillyard and in Congress.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/830632499_17973207984150272_7214689790643353596_n.jpg|Lanterns over the water, neighbors on the lawn, and not one dollar from a corporate PAC. Tonight at midnight the fundraising quarter closes. This is the last report before ballots go in the mail, and it is the number every political reporter and every DC group will use to decide whether Eastern Washington is worth taking seriously. They already decided Trump's endorsement was worth spending on. Let's show them what neighbors chipping in looks like instead: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/839559388_17974238577150272_5666357825033501132_n.jpg|Nearly 300 people participated in person at the #WA05 forum at Whitman College in Walla Walla, and they came with real questions about affordability, health care, and datacenters. Thanks to AAUW Walla Walla and Northwest Public Broadcasting for hosting the forum, and Rasa Vineyards and the Network of Exceptional Women for the after party. We'll be back!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/840264308_17974101222150272_2697571734605207110_n.jpg|Valleyfest weekend, sharing a booth with "Rational Rob" Tupper, candidate for the 4th LD. We enjoyed lots of good conversations about what people in Spokane Valley need from their representatives. Thanks to everyone who showed up!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/840589609_17974398468150272_6279657702099450158_n.jpg|Michael Perry & Eric Horsted opened their beautiful home to us on the Autumn Equinox. String lights, a yard full of neighbors, and – we did not see this coming – aerialists! One of the most memorable nights of the campaign. Everyone who came out that night helped put this race in play. We are so grateful!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/841012494_17974711122150272_5119648225189960708_n.jpg|James joined his brother Murphy at the campaign office – it's safe to say both are keenly interested in the yard sign situation. Our office runs on volunteers, coffee, and lately a fair amount of dog hair. Come by and say hello. The welcoming committee is ready.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/841120902_17974435464150272_1153027006282809405_n.jpg|A full hall in Usk for the Pend Oreille County Democrats fundraiser – good food, good company, and a couple of dogs who came along for the conversation. Pend Oreille County is big, rural, and easy for Washington, D.C. to overlook. The people here are organized, generous, and paying close attention to this race. Thank you for having me, and for all the work you are doing to turn out every vote up north.

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/842821366_17974749465150272_5403233037197265969_n.jpg|Thank you to our hosts, the Chases and Kuhlings, for inviting your friends to join us! A beautiful old living room, every chair filled, and neighbors who came ready with good questions and stayed long after the last one. Ballots arrive soon! If you would like to host a gathering like this before then, we would love to come: https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/843073916_17974911462150272_2969102605446429022_n.jpg|A big shout out to We Have The Power Movement for organizing a Rock the Vote postcard event, and special gratitude to Colleen and Stan Woods for coordinating and making it happen. Our volunteers showed up to help kick off the writing. A room full of people, pens in hand, reminding their neighbors to vote. Thank you, volunteers!

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/844544792_17974725390150272_2695542744322842977_n.jpg|Front page of the Seattle Times: "Democrats say U.S. House race is in play." National Democrats consider us a District in Play. Incumbent Michael Baumgartner was the only Republican on the primary ballot, and most voters here voted for change. Nobody handed us this. Volunteers, house party hosts, and neighbors chipping in $26 at a time put this seat on the map. Now let's finish the job. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/cc-soc-2609

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/845923935_17975027922150272_7689748820062227495_n.jpg|People took yard signs home all ValleyFest weekend, and every one of them is telling their whole street where they stand. Thanks to everyone who stopped by, the volunteers who kept it running, and especially to Joanne M. Heye for being our photographer! Want a sign of your own? https://conroy4congress.com/volunteer

alt://instagram.fhio3-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t51.82787-15/846347954_17974876281150272_3750033805782708751_n.jpg|Rain, shine, and new and returning Eagles. We participated in EWU Neighborfest, walked Cheney in a coalition canvass with Karina Wallace (@karina_justfiguringitout), who is running for State Rep in the 9th LD. Go Team! Students, make your vote count HERE. Register online at VoteWA.gov through October 26, or in person through Election Day.

added: Home About Platform News Support DONATE 2026.10.15 - Sheriffs Endorsement PRESS RELEASE: Thursday, October 15, 2026 Sheriffs Endorse Misti Cordell for Congress Law enforcement leaders cite Cordell's focus on public safety MONROE, LA - Sheriff Bryan Linder of Franklin Parish, Sheriff Chad Ezell of Madison Parish, and Sheriff Rob Rushing of Tensas Parish have endorsed Misti Cordell for Congress, saying she will stand with local law enforcement and prioritize public safety for families across the district.
“I will help our law enforcement fight crime and protect Louisiana; that’s why these Sheriffs and others are backing me for Congress,” Cordell said.

“These leaders put the safety of our communities first, and I am committed to standing with them.” “Our deputies and police officers put their lives on the line every day to protect Louisiana families,” Cordell said.
“They deserve the resources, respect, and support to do their jobs.

My position is simple: defend, don’t defund, our law enforcement.” The sheriffs cite Cordell’s strong support for local officers, her commitment to tougher enforcement of criminal laws, and her positions on border security.
They also praise her as honest, ethical, and hard-working.

Cordell, a Monroe-area small-business owner, wife, mother of two, and Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents, has made backing law enforcement and securing the border central priorities of her campaign.
“A secure border is a national security issue that affects communities far beyond the border itself,” Cordell said.
“Fentanyl and other drugs coming across the border are already impacting Louisiana communities.
I support completing the border wall, increasing immigration enforcement, and combating drug cartels.” Cordell’s public-safety platform also includes defending Second Amendment rights.
She recently received the highest rating possible from the National Rifle Association.

added: Home About Platform News Support DONATE 2026.09.17 - WFW Endorsement PRESS RELEASE: Tuesday, September 17, 2026 Winning For Women Action Fund Endorses Misti Cordell for Congress Powerful organization supporting Republican women announces endorsement in Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District ﻿ MONROE, LA - Winning For Women Action Fund (WFW AF) has endorsed Misti Cordell for Congress in Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District, citing Cordell’s business background, community leadership, and conservative political record for their support of her campaign.
“Misti is exactly the kind of candidate WFW AF was built to support, and we are thrilled to back her bid for Congress,” said WFW AF President Danielle Barrow.
“She is an accomplished businesswoman, community leader, and a proven conservative who has spent her career serving her community.

Louisiana’s 5th District deserves a strong voice in Congress, and Misti is ready to deliver on Day One.” Cordell, who has also received the formal endorsement of the Republican Party of Louisiana, is a small-business owner, a two-time delegate to the Republican National Convention supporting President Donald Trump, and Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents.
“Winning for Women Action Fund supports strong, conservative Republican Members of Congress who say what they mean and mean what they say,” said Cordell.
“I look forward to joining those ranks in the Fall and providing Rural Louisiana with a strong voice in the U.S.

House.” A wife and mother of two sons, Cordell has pledged to lower taxes, secure the border, supporte Louisiana agriculture and energy, strengthening rural healthcare, defending constitutional rights, and returning education decisions to parents and local communities among her policy priorities.
Winning For Women Action Fund supports Republican women seeking federal office through political advocacy and related initiatives.
The organization has raised and directed more than $48 million in support of women candidates and officeholders since the 2020 election cycle.

added: Effective July 1, 2027 , the Act delivers unprecedented, direct relief to Idaho households by eliminating the state sales tax on grocery staples at the cash register, zeroing out the 33-cents-per-gallon motor fuel excise tax, and providing a 100% tax exemption on voluntary gratuities and hourly overtime compensation.

Additionally, starting January 1, 2028, the legislation transitions the flat 5.30% income tax rate to a progressive 5% to 11% structure that protects everyday earners under $250,000 while empowering ultra-high earners ($3M+) to utilize an active taxpayer designation option, directing top-tier revenue straight into local school districts or state education lockboxes.
To fully offset these tax cuts while maintaining a projected annual General Fund surplus of over $100 million, the Act establishes strict accountability measures for external commercial entities.
The legislation imposes a 20% infrastructure impact surtax on commercial development projects exceeding $1,000,000.

Furthermore, the legislation establishes a 2% fee on out-of-state commercial long-haul freight carriers exceeding 26,000 lbs. utilizing Idaho interstates, with all revenues flowing directly into specialized accounts alongside a dedicated 9% general sales tax infill transfer.
removed: Effective July 1, 2027, the Act delivers unprecedented, direct relief to Idaho households by eliminating the state sales tax on grocery staples at the cash register, zeroing out the 33cents-per-gallon motor fuel excise tax, and providing a 100% tax exemption on voluntary gratuities and hourly overtime compensation.

Additionally, the legislation transitions the flat 5.30% income tax rate to a progressive 6% to 10% structure that protects everyday earners under $250,000 while empowering ultra-high earners in the $3M+ bracket to utilize an active taxpayer designation option, directing top-tier revenue straight into local school districts or state education lockboxes.
To fully offset these tax cuts while maintaining a projected annual General Fund surplus of over $160 million, the Act establishes strict accountability measures for external commercial entities.
The legislation imposes a 15% infrastructure impact surtax on commercial development projects exceeding $1,000,000.

Furthermore, the legislation establishes a 1.5% fee on out-of-state commercial long-haul freight carriers exceeding 26,000 lbs. utilizing Idaho interstates, with all revenues flowing directly into specialized accounts alongside a dedicated 9% general sales tax infill transfer.

title.after: About Dale Hawkins - Dale Hawkins for Idaho

added: Dale Hawkins for Idaho Home About Issues Governance Get Involved Donate About Dale Hawkins A common man standing up for Idaho's freedom and traditional values The journey to Idaho In 1998, my family made a life-changing decision.
We moved to Idaho seeking something that was becoming increasingly rare in America: the freedom to raise our children according to our values and beliefs.

We wanted the liberty to homeschool our six children, to live out our Christian faith without government interference, and to be part of a community that still believed in limited government and individual responsibility.
Idaho welcomed us with open arms.
Here, we found a state that understood what it meant to respect parental rights, to honor constitutional principles, and to let families make their own decisions.
That freedom is what drew us here, and it's what I'm fighting to protect for every Idaho family.
I'm not a career politician.
I'm not a lawyer looking to climb the political ladder.
I'm a husband, a father, and an everyday citizen who believes that government works best when it stays within its constitutional boundaries and lets people live their lives in freedom.
Faith, family, and freedom My Christian faith is the foundation of everything I do.
It shapes how I view government, how I approach policy, and how I interact with my fellow Idahoans.
I believe that our rights come from God, not from government, and that those rights must be protected at all costs.
As a father of six, I understand what's at stake when we talk about education policy, parental rights, and the future of our state.
Every decision I make in the legislature is guided by one simple question: Is this good for Idaho families?
Will this protect their freedom or diminish it?
I'm pro-life without apology.
I believe in the sanctity of human life from conception to natural death.
I believe in the Second Amendment.
I believe in property rights, self defense, and limited government.
And I believe that Idaho should remain a beacon of freedom in an increasingly regulated world.
Fighting for your freedom Since entering public service, I've worked tirelessly to defend the principles that make Idaho special.

I've fought for homeschooling rights, pushed back against federal overreach, defended the Second Amendment, pushed hard for stronger immigration enforcement, and stood firm on pro-life values even when it wasn't politically convenient.
I believe in accountability and transparency.
Elected officials should answer to the people, not to special interests or political insiders.
That's why I make myself available to constituents and explain my votes, and why I'm willing to stand alone when principle demands it.
Idaho is worth fighting for.
Our way of life, our values, and our freedoms are under constant attack from those who think government knows better than families.
I'm committed to standing in the gap, to being a voice for common-sense conservatism, and to ensuring that Idaho remains a place where freedom thrives.
From Fernwood, Idaho Proud to call Fernwood home and honored to serve the people of Idaho.
Together, we can preserve the freedom and values that make our state exceptional.

title.after: Governance & Leadership - Dale Hawkins for Idaho

added: Dale Hawkins for Idaho Home About Issues Governance Get Involved Donate Proper Governance Limited Government · Individual Liberty · Free Enterprise · Traditional Values The foundation of freedom I am a Republican dedicated to the preservation of our Constitutional Republic.
Governmental power must be limited, defined, and constrained by the state and federal Constitution while being kept in check by an informed electorate.
Our founders were wise to set up checks and balances to limit government, but it is up to every generation to preserve them.
The Constitution isn't a suggestion.
It's not a living document that changes with the political winds.
It's the supreme law of the land, and every elected official takes an oath to uphold it.
That oath means something to me.
It means that when I vote on legislation, I ask first whether it's constitutional, not whether it's popular or politically expedient.
Too often, politicians treat the Constitution as an obstacle to be worked around rather than a framework to be honored.
They expand government power, create new regulations, and pass laws invoking powers not granted to them, all in the name of solving problems government often created in the first place.
Constitutional Limits Government authority must remain strictly within the boundaries established by the Constitution.
When government exceeds these limits, individual liberty suffers.
Protection of Rights Our rights come from God, not from government.
The primary role of government is to protect these God-given rights, not to grant or restrict them based on political whims.
Rule of Law Laws must be applied equally to all citizens.
No one is above the law, and no one should be subject to arbitrary government action.
Due process and equal protection are non-negotiable.
Accountability to the People Elected officials serve at the pleasure of the people, not the other way around.
Government must be transparent, accountable, and responsive to those it serves.
Defending Idaho's sovereignty Idaho is not a subdivision of the federal government.
The 10th Amendment makes this clear: powers not delegated to the federal government are reserved to the states and the people.
Yet time and again, we see federal overreach that treats states as mere administrative units of a centralized government.
Idaho has the right and the duty to push back against unconstitutional federal mandates.
Whether it's land management, healthcare, education, or gun rights, Idaho should be free to chart its own course based on the values and priorities of its citizens.
I've worked to strengthen Idaho's sovereignty by opposing federal mandates, defending our natural resources, and ensuring that Idaho law reflects Idaho values.
I'll continue to stand firm against any attempt to turn Idaho into a puppet of Washington, D.C.
Accountability matters I believe elected officials should be transparent about their positions and accountable for their votes.
If you have questions about what I stand for or want to know how I voted on a particular issue, I want to hear from you.
Reach out: P.O.

Volunteer Opportunities Contact Voter Info Contribute Contact Chicago Tribune and Daily Herald Highlight Hills’ Fight to Strengthen Protections for Children September 30, 2026 For nearly two years, State Senator Darby Hills has been fighting to strengthen protections for children and close what she describes as a loophole in Illinois law.
Her legislation, Senate Bill 2381, would require sex offender registration when an adult is convicted of sexually motivated, unauthorized video recording of a minor.
The legislation advanced through the Senate Criminal Law Committee, but it was never called for a final vote in the Senate.
Hills has continued fighting to move the measure forward, and it currently remains in the Senate Assignments Committee.
Now, following the recent arrests of two local teachers, Hills is renewing her call for lawmakers to bring SB 2381 to the Senate floor for a vote during Veto Session.
The recent cases have brought new attention to the issue and Hills’ ongoing effort to strengthen protections for children.
The renewed push has been highlighted by both the Chicago Tribune and Daily Herald.

Home Meet David Issues Photos News Endorsements News Latest updates from the campaign: 15 Oct Thursday, 9:31 AM · 2026 Rolling Blackouts in Pacifica & Montara In the last week, there have been numerous power outages in Pacifica, Montara and Moss Beach.
According to the SF Chronicle and NBC Bay Area, residents in Montara, Moss Beach and El Granada reported power going out up to six times in a four-day span, including overnight blackouts.
The recent Peninsula-wide power disruption left roughly 6,500 PG&E customers without power and caused major delays on BART services.
PG&E has no valid explanation for the outages, only that it was “checking” its aging infrastructure.
But don’t worry, PG&E has enough extra money to make more than $8,000 in campaign contributions to Marc Berman, the incumbent running for his 6 th term in Assembly District (AD) 23.
Marc is widely known for his “get rid of natural gas and make everything electric” legislation, while the cost of power goes up and service continues to be spotty.
It’s time to end One Party Rule and vote for someone who will hold the Public Utilities such as PG&E to account and who will also demand transparency across every agency in the State.
Vote for David G.

added.text: Endorsements — Deirdre McEachern for NH State Rep.

added: Frequently Asked Questions What office is Deirdre running for?
Deirdre McEachern is running for the New Hampshire House of Representatives in Carroll County, District 6, which includes Wolfeboro and Tuftonboro.
Why is Deirdre running?
Deirdre is running because she believes Wolfeboro and Tuftonboro deserve a representative who listens, brings practical solutions and works constructively on local concerns.

Deirdre is fighting for strong schools, affordable communities, expanded childcare programs, accessible healthcare, protected natural resources like our lakes, and responsive leadership that puts the people of her district first.
What experience would Deirdre bring to the State House?

Deirdre brings more than 25 years of New Hampshire entrepreneurship, extensive educational experience as a pre-K through grade 8 Head of School, advanced training in conflict resolution, and a long history of community service.
She would put those skills to work listening to constituents, evaluating legislation, and creating practical solutions.
What has Deirdre contributed to the local community?

Deirdre is an active member of the Wolfeboro/Tuftonboro Lions Club, serves on the Wolfeboro Festival of Trees Committee, and volunteers on the Development Committee of the Wentworth Watershed Association.
She is also an avid reader and loves the LRNC Book Club!
Deirdre is active in her faith community and serves on the Board of Directors for the Star Island Corporation jointly owned by the UUA and UCC churches.
During the campaign, she has spent time meeting residents, visiting local businesses, attending community events, and listening to people throughout Wolfeboro and Tuftonboro.
What party is Deirdre running with?
Deirdre is the Democratic Candidate for State Representative in Carroll District 6.
She is committed to representing the people of Wolfeboro and Tuftonboro, including residents who belong to another party or no party at all.
Her decisions will be guided by the needs of the district, the facts before the legislature, and the effect a proposal would have on local residents.
Would Deirdre vote with her party on every issue?
Deirdre will evaluate legislation on its merits and consider how it would affect Wolfeboro, Tuftonboro, and New Hampshire as a whole.
She will listen to residents and explain her votes.
Which organizations and community leaders have endorsed Deirdre?

Deirdre is honored to have earned endorsements from American Federation of Teachers NH,The Sierra Club, EMILYs List, New Hampshire Rights & Democracy, the New Hampshire Action Fund, the Sierra Club NH, NH Youth Movement, Move the Goalposts NH, US Congressman Ro Khanna and 350NH Action among others.
A complete list appears on the campaign's endorsements page at Endorsements — Deirdre McEachern for NH State Rep.
What issues is Deirdre most focused on?
Deirdre is running to protect strong public schools while easing the burden on local property taxpayers.
She supports locally driven housing solutions for workers, families, and seniors, while preserving local control.
She is also focused on protecting the district’s lakes, land, and rural character and strengthening local businesses and essential infrastructure.
What is Deirdre's position on public education?
Deirdre believes strong public schools are essential to strong communities.
She supports giving educators the resources they need, strengthening partnerships between families and schools, and keeping the focus on effective teaching and student outcomes.
She also believes the state must meet its constitutional responsibility for education so local property taxpayers do not carry an unfair share of the cost.
She believes public dollars should remain in public school budgets - she does not support private school vouchers.
Learn more .
How would Deirdre address affordability and property taxes?
Deirdre would address affordability by pushing the state to stop reneging on its obligations and fund its responsibilities to schools and towns, easing pressure on local property taxpayers.
She opposes a broad-based sales or income tax.
She supports locally driven housing solutions that help workers, families, and seniors afford to remain in Wolfeboro and Tuftonboro.
She also supports energy programs to focus on renewable energy and reduce expensive fossil fuel dependence for residents What is Deirdre's position on housing?
Deirdre supports locally driven efforts to expand housing that workers, young families, and seniors can afford.
She believes communities can create more housing while respecting property rights, using existing infrastructure wisely, and keeping important land-use decisions in local hands.
She also believes the Housing Champions program needs to be fully reinstated (and funded) by the legislature.
Learn more When is the general election?
The general election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

added: Skip to content Endorsements Priorities Latest News Events Volunteer Endorsements Priorities Latest News Events Volunteer Facebook X-twitter Instagram Donate Press Release DENISE POWELL ANNOUNCES MASSIVE END OF QUARTER FUNDRAISING HAUL OF NEARLY $2.4 MILLION October 14, 2026 As Republicans abandon Brinker Harding, Powell enters the home stretch with nearly $1 million cash on hand Omaha, NE – Today, Denise Powell’s campaign announced raising nearly $2.4 million in Q3 into the campaign’s committee and victory fund, and will enter the home stretch of the race to represent Nebraska’s Second Congressional District with nearly $1 million cash on hand.
This announcement comes following a winning debate performance from Powell and as Republicans continue to abandon their flawed and failed nominee, Brinker Harding .
“As national Republicans abandon their flawed and failed nominee Brinker Harding, our campaign has the resources needed to compete and win.

At the most crucial part of the campaign, we have the ability to meet voters where they are and aggressively communicate Denise’s winning message of lowering costs, standing up against Trump’s corruption, and bringing a fresh perspective to Washington.
Our campaign is all gas, no breaks, and these funds will allow us to run through the tape and deliver a win for working families in Nebraska,” said Campaign Manager Ryan Longenecker.
In addition to impressive fundraising and a professional and sophisticated “Get Out the Vote” strategy, Denise’s campaign has a broad and growing coalition of supporters.

Denise’s campaign has over 60 local and national endorsements, including The Nebraska Farmers Union, EMILY’s List, CHC BOLD PAC, Elect Democratic Women, New Dem Action Fund, The Bench, former Democratic nominee Tony Vargas, and members of Congress from across the country.

About Denise Denise Powell is a mom, former executive, small business owner, public school champion and healthcare advocate who knows that a strong work ethic and a love of family and community is the Nebraska way of life.
She also knows the Good Life is getting harder to come by.
It’s why after Trump’s election she left a successful career in corporate America to focus on fighting for what makes Nebraska such a special place to live and raise a family.

Over the past decade, she has supported hundreds of Nebraskans running for local office, protected our public schools and the families they serve, and helped stop extremists from passing abortion bans in the state.

Every day, we see more of our friends and neighbors struggling to make ends meet while Donald Trump and MAGA extremists are focused on trade wars that are increasing our cost of living and passing massive tax breaks for billionaires like Elon Musk.
Strong families, strong businesses, strong communities – they ALL require work and investment, but everything we’ve fought for here at home is under threat.

From dismantling Medicaid and making it harder for seniors to get the benefits they’ve earned, to dismantling education, from the University of Nebraska to our public schools, to attacking our veterans and ripping away women’s rights — Denise is running to fight for the people of Nebraska.
We don’t need lip service from politicians, we need action.
For more information, visit deniseforcongress.org .
For a high-resolution picture of Denise, click here .

All Posts Latest Political News Culture and Opinions Events Your Community Vaccines & Health Search DiPietro: ‘No-Vote’ on Majority’s Omnibus Corrections Bill David Dipietro Jun 12, 2025 2 min read Omnibus bill A.8871 fails to address main causes of strikes In response to the Majority’s passage of a sweeping omnibus bill on correction reform, Assemblyman David DiPietro (R,C-East Aurora) issued his criticism, calling the legislation “a blatant failure to address the very issues that forced thousands of correctional officers to risk their livelihoods and walk off the job.” The bill comes in the wake of the largest correctional officer strike New York State has seen in decades.

But according to DiPietro, the legislation does nothing to correct the underlying problems that drove the strike to begin with: the dangerous consequences of the HALT Act and the inhumane practice of mandatory overtime that has left correction officers overworked, underappreciated and unheard.
“This bill is window dressing, plain and simple.
The governor and the Majority are pretending to solve a problem they still don’t understand because they never listened in the first place.

The officers walked out in desperation, begging the state to address mandatory triple shifts, being denied sick and vacation time and the devastating impact this job is having on their families and mental health.
Instead of compassion or reform, they got punishment." “The governor’s executive order blacklisting officers from state employment was vindictive, authoritarian and disgraceful.
Terminating 2,000 officers didn’t solve the crisis, it escalated it.
And now, this so-called reform package completely ignores their pleas for help.
There are no OT protections, no staffing mandates and no HALT Act reforms." “If you want safe prisons, you need to start by treating our officers like human beings.
The Majority failed these men and women.

I stand with the officers, those who are still serving and those this state cast aside.” DiPietro vowed to continue fighting for correctional officers and pushing for real reform that includes a repeal of the HALT Act, mandatory overtime protections, mental health support and restoration of employment opportunities for wrongfully terminated officers.
Assemblyman David DiPietro represents the 147th Assembly District, which includes parts of Erie and Wyoming counties.

David Dipietro Dec 12, 2025 1 min read This Isn’t Enough — And New Yorkers Deserve the Truth As the Ranking Minority Member on the Assembly Corrections Committee, I’ve reviewed the prison package now sitting on the Governor’s desk.
After reading the coverage here , I need to set the record straight — because what’s being presented to the public is simply not enough, and in some cases, flat-out misleading.

This bill does nothing to address the real crisis inside our prisons: • chronic understaffing • Zero recruitment efforts • forced overtime • escalating assaults • unsafe conditions for officers and incarcerated individuals • and the complete lack of meaningful reforms recommended by the state’s own corrections experts Albany can pat itself on the back for passing another “transparency” bill, and parts of the bill are good, but transparency without action is just political theater.
New Yorkers deserve genuine reform — not a headline.
I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: if we don’t fix staffing, safety, and the day-to-day realities inside our facilities, we are not solving anything.
This package ignores the root problems, and pretending otherwise does a disservice to the men and women who keep our prisons operating.
Bottom line: This isn’t reform.
It’s a distraction.

And I’ll keep fighting for real solutions that protect our officers, improve safety, and bring honesty back to our corrections system. — Assemblyman David DiPietro Ranking Minority Member, NYS Assembly Corrections Committee Tags: New York Assembly Albany Hochul corrections DiPietro prison officers Culture and Opinions Latest Political News Recent Posts See All DiPietro Blasts Hochul for Shielding Criminals and Ignoring Victims DiPietro: ‘No-Vote’ on Majority’s Omnibus Corrections Bill Hochul’s Budget Betrays Western New York’s Correctional Officers Donations by mail can be sent to: DiPietro For You PO Box 700, E.

added: Katie & Aaron, Appleton WI Rachael is amazing!
She is down-to-earth and loves her community.
As her friend, we know that she will serve with integrity and honesty.
She has our full support for WI Assembly, and we are so excited to see the difference she can make!
Jordy Raddatz, Menasha Resident and Local Real Estate Agent I'm endorsing Rachael Dowling to represent Wisconsin’s 53rd Assembly District.
We need someone who doesnt just follow party lines.
We need a a representative that actually represents the community.
She's a mother, a wife, a neighbor, a small business owner, and she is extremely involved in the community she lives in!
That's who we need to represent us.
Not a career politician.
Bill, Appleton WI I have worked, professionally, with Rachael in many different arenas.
Communication has always been a priority, for her.

Then transparency is a close second with responsibility together with accountability, tying all of them together. ​ She’s outstanding in a team effort where a goal is outlined and all the moving parts are working toward that goal.
Rachael is also adept at guiding effort, that has lost its way and might need some reminders about its mission.

She’s successfully managed to raise a family with her husband Josh and run a few businesses out of desire or need when life pushed back on them and forced them to pivot. ​ Rachael like all of us, has some weaknesses, like how great kids and babies are, oh and festivals or community get togethers.
Usually where people from anywhere, can kick back and relax.
She loves connecting with people, so much so, that she might lose track of time, listening to your WHOLE story.
That’s time well spent.

She’s leaned into using her best attributes to find success in the details and in supporting all the people whom she can help. ​ What we need is her empowered with more collective responsibility and ability to enact changes.
This is so she can get done for us what needs doing.
It’s a fight she’s willing to take on and a story that she’s willing to help write.
Because your needs, your stories and your lives, matter, to her, as if they were her very own. ​ She’s not flashy and she’s not going to ask you for your money.
Rachael is asking for your support, your vote, so that together, as a community, she can lead the charge to change. ​ I’m voting for her, because I believe in her, will you join me?
Brian, Neenah WI Do you ever look at candidates for political races and think to yourself, “Nothing is going to change no matter who gets elected”?
We have been short changed in every election the possibility of a candidate that is not beholden to special big party interests and lobbyists.
Because they are always going to be there, pulling strings with whoever wins.
Rachael Dowling has no strings connected to any lobbying marionettes.
I originally came across her working with her on the Winnebago County Board of supervisors.
We got to know each other pretty quickly and I was especially impressed with her ability to use critical thinking to both staff and policy.
I find that to be a very important detail for anyone that is holding public office, is simply to have the ability to think critically.
Since she is not connected to any political action committees, what you get is just a regular person, wanting to make a positive impact with the state government, so it can serve you better.
THAT is refreshing.
It's the type of candidate you should vote for, in a time where we have a political climate that's built on nothing but attack ads and smoke and mirrors.
To me, the choice is easy.
Rachael Dowling gets my vote.

In the News Bills sponsored by Rep.
Stokesbary signed into law From the Auburn Reporter : Three bills sponsored by Rep.
Drew Stokesbary, R-Auburn, have been signed into law by Gov.
Jay Inslee.
House Bills 1263 , 1637 and 1940 passed the House and Senate with strong bipartisan support.

“I am pleased the governor signed these bills into law and believe they will strengthen public safety, improve government efficiency and protect those who live in flood-prone areas like the Auburn and Sumner valleys,” Stokesbary said.
“I came to Olympia committed to getting things done on behalf of my constituents, and to promote efficient and accountable government.
I believe having three bills signed into law during my first term is a step in that direction.

I look forward to continuing work on these and other important issues facing our state.” House Bill 1263 removes duplicative regulations that would have caused many accountants to face regulation by two separate state agencies.
House Bill 1637 grants tribal police and prosecutors access to a prescription-drug monitoring database for use during criminal investigations.
Federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies already have such access, and now tribal police will be able to use this tool to combat prescription drug abuse in their communities as well.
House Bill 1940 ensures critical flood control infrastructure can continue being built in King and Pierce counties.
Flood control districts in the 31st District are responsible for constructing and maintaining levees along the Green, White, and Puyallup rivers.
Due to the complex method of allocating property tax dollars in Washington state, the King County Flood Control District would have lost all of its revenue to other agencies beginning in 2018.
Bills go into effect 90 days following the adjournment of the regular legislative session.

Vick Issues Events News Voter Information Contact Photos 🗺️ Drive 95: The 95-County Listening Tour Headline: Faith First.
Tennessee Always.
Coming to YOUR County!
My campaign is not about Nashville or big-city politics—it is about the heart of Tennessee, and the heart of Tennessee beats in all 95 counties .
I made a promise to lead as a true servant, and to do that, I must hear directly from every community.
That is why I am launching Drive 95 , a mission to visit every single corner of our great state between now and the November 3, 2026, election.
Why Drive 95 Matters As a Christian Independent and a 40-year veteran of Tennessee public education, I know that real solutions are found on the ground, not in a capital building.

I want to look you in the eye, listen to your concerns about Mental Health , Homelessness/Poverty , and Education , and other issues that face our state and discuss how we can bring New Results to our communities.
This is a low-budget, grassroots campaign relying on the spirit and hospitality of Tennesseans.
Every stop is a chance for fellowship, listening, and prayer.
Dr Vick's prayer is simple: "May God Stir Your Heart to Vote for Dr.
Vick for Tennessee." 🗓️ Get Ready: Check Back for the Schedule!

Vick Issues Events News Voter Information Contact Photos 🗺️ Drive 95: The 95-County Listening Tour Headline: Faith First.
Tennessee Always.
Coming to YOUR County!
My campaign is not about Nashville or big-city politics—it is about the heart of Tennessee, and the heart of Tennessee beats in all 95 counties .
I made a promise to lead as a true servant, and to do that, I must hear directly from every community.
That is why I am launching Drive 95 , a mission to visit every single corner of our great state between now and the November 3, 2026, election.
Why Drive 95 Matters As a Christian Independent and a 40-year veteran of Tennessee public education, I know that real solutions are found on the ground, not in a capital building.

I want to look you in the eye, listen to your concerns about Mental Health , Homelessness/Poverty , and Education , and other issues that face our state and discuss how we can bring New Results to our communities.
This is a low-budget, grassroots campaign relying on the spirit and hospitality of Tennesseans.
Every stop is a chance for fellowship, listening, and prayer.
Dr Vick's prayer is simple: "May God Stir Your Heart to Vote for Dr.
Vick for Tennessee." 🗓️ Get Ready: Check Back for the Schedule!

Past events OCT 13 TUE Happy Hour Tuesday, October 13, 5:30 PM 2894 On Main , 2894 Main St, East Troy Why I Am Running I was nine when my parents came to America with few resources to begin a new life.
Nine was a wonderful age to learn and grow into American citizenship.
With hard work I earned a bachelor's and master's in engineering as well as a law degree.
I have been shaped by those who have guided me while learning American values and the many opportunities offered by our great nation.
Now, I wish to give back!
I call myself a Servant Leader and I am committed to serve all communities across the 11th District.
PAST EXPERIENCE Volunteer, New Orleans post-Katrina cleanup Volunteer, Rutgers University, Cambiando Vidas Patent Examiner, U.S.
Patent & Trademark Office, Alexandria, VA Editor, Polish Global Village, Washington, D.C.
Metro Area Law Clerk, Sughrue Mion, PLLC, Washington, D.C.
As your Senate candidate for the 11th District, I am committed to help everyone realize a prosperous future, one that offers opportunities for all.

DISTRICT 11 CHALLENGES High state income taxes Unallocated surplus funds for schools and farmers Escalating fuel, energy, and food costs Division and mistrust between citizens and government Wisconsin's GOP majority has failed to manage the State's massive surpluses needed to support economic growth.
As a result, taxpayers, including those in the 11th District, face continuing school and municipal referendums, while surpluses sit idle.
As inflation continues to devalue the State's surplus, business owners and homeowners, as well as our farmers, are required to pay additional real estate taxes.
It is disingenuous to boast about surpluses when, in fact, local schools, taxpayers, businesses, and municipalities require referendums to fund basic needs.
Increasing property taxes is avoidable when surpluses are utilized as shared revenue.
As a Servant Leader, I value your insight for ideas that will support future growth across the 11th District.
Please know, I am uninterested in political infighting that turns neighbor against neighbor.
By working together, we can build and achieve a sound economic future.
I would be honored to represent you and your families in the 11th District and I respectfully ask for your support in the November 3, 2026 General Election .

Getting Things Done.
From passing groundbreaking laws to standing up to powerful interests and delivering for Western New York, Pat Burke has a record of fighting for the people he represents.
Getting Stuff Done Big Fights Protecting Survivors Delivering for WNY Clean Air & Water Accountability Recognition Working People 01 / A record of action Getting Stuff Done.
Real legislation.
Real protections.
Results that make a difference.
A First-in-the-Nation Plastics Ban Banning Microbeads On the Erie County Legislature, Burke helped pass pioneering legislation to stop plastic microbeads from polluting our waterways.
Standing Up for LGBT Youth Protecting Young People Helped enact groundbreaking Erie County legislation protecting LGBT youth from harmful practices.

Backing Our Troopers Historic Mental Health Legislation Championed groundbreaking, first-in-the-nation legislation giving New York State Troopers up to 30 days of paid recovery time after traumatic critical incidents, ensuring those who protect our communities have the time and support they need to heal.
The PENCE Act Passing the PENCE Act Protecting LGBT youth in Erie County by banning the harmful practice of conversion therapy on minors.
02 / No backing down Taking on the Big Fights.
When powerful institutions need to be held accountable, Pat Burke doesn't look the other way.

He Took on Utility Monopolies Pat Burke is taking NYSEG to court to stop a massive rate hike, standing up for hardworking Western New Yorkers who are sick of being squeezed by a monopoly utility that keeps demanding more of their money.

He Challenged the Diocese Pat Burke was the first elected official to call for Bishop Malone’s resignation and has never stopped fighting for survivors of abuse at the hands of the Catholic Church, demanding accountability from powerful institutions and justice for those they failed.
He Stood with Survivors Advocated for stronger statewide investigations of institutional and historical sexual abuse, including alleged cover-ups and failures to report.
Protecting vulnerable people Protecting Survivors of Assault & Abuse.
From strengthening survivors' rights to supporting local services, Burke's record includes legislation, advocacy and funding for people affected by abuse and assault.

Strengthening Survivors' Rights Child Victims Act & Adult Survivors Act Burke supported passage of the Child Victims Act and Adult Survivors Act, expanding opportunities for survivors to seek civil justice.
Closing Gaps in the Law Rape Is Rape Act Helped advance the Rape Is Rape Act, updating New York law to recognize more forms of nonconsensual sexual penetration as rape.

Standing with Survivors Demanding Diocese Accountability Burke was the first elected official to call for Bishop Malone's resignation and has continued pressing for accountability for abuse and institutional failures.

Supporting Survivors Locally Investing in the Family Justice Center Directed discretionary funding to the Family Justice Center to support its work with people experiencing domestic violence and abuse.
Personal Safety & Confidence Funding Women's Self-Defense Classes Supported self-defense classes for women through discretionary funding, helping make practical safety training accessible.
Protecting LGBT Youth The PENCE Act In Erie County, Burke helped ban the harmful practice of conversion therapy on minors—part of his broader work to protect vulnerable young people.

Institutional Accountability Institutional Sexual Assault Accountability Act Burke proposed the Institutional Sexual Assault Accountability Act (ISAAA) to expand specialized State Police investigations of institutional and historical sexual abuse, including alleged cover-ups and failures to report.
This is proposed legislation, not an enacted law.
03 / Bringing resources home Delivering for WNY.

As the first Chair of the Assembly Cities Committee in the Assembly’s history to come from outside New York City, Burke is bringing resources home to our cities, schools, neighborhoods, first responders and public spaces.

#M+ More than $25 million in additional funding for Buffalo each year for three years #M+ More than $100 million in additional funding for upstate cities each year for three years $#.#M Pedestrian safety funding for Ridge Road and Seneca Street Historic Support for Our Cities As Chair of the Assembly Cities Committee, Burke helped secure major new resources for Buffalo and other upstate cities.
Safer Streets for Students Worked with student advocate Richie Schack and local stakeholders to advance pedestrian safety improvements near West Seneca West High School.
Schools, Parks & Recreation Supporting improvements to the places where Western New York families learn, play and come together—and fighting to keep youth sports affordable for families.
Public Safety & Infrastructure Advocating for investments in fire and police services, safer communities and essential local infrastructure.
04 / Our natural heritage Protecting Our Clean Air & Water.
Western New York's lakes, rivers and neighborhoods deserve strong environmental protections.
Protecting the Great Lakes Defending Our Water Making protection of Lake Erie and the Great Lakes a priority in public service.
Less Plastic Pollution Taking on Microplastics His early work on microbeads helped put Western New York at the forefront of local plastics policy.
Polluters Should Pay Holding Polluters Accountable Supporting stronger accountability for pollution that threatens public health and natural resources.
A Cleaner Future Conservation That Lasts Working alongside conservation advocates to protect the places that make Western New York home.
05 / Government should serve the public Taking on Corrupt Officials.
Public service shouldn't be a private club.
Government should be open, accountable and answerable to the people.

“Public jobs should not be political favors.” The OPEN Appointments Act Proposed legislation requiring public notice, an open application period, and greater transparency when filling government appointments.
Demanding Local Accountability Challenging opaque appointment processes and pressing local officials to explain decisions made on behalf of taxpayers.

06 / Recognized for results Recognized for His Work. ★ Legislator of the Year Recognized by the New York State Troopers Police Benevolent Association for his work on behalf of law enforcement officers and their families.
07 / Standing with working people Supported by Working People.
Proud to have support from organizations representing the workers who build, teach, protect and care for our communities.
A Record Worth Fighting For.
Pat Burke is focused on delivering results for Western New York.

removed: About Priorities Record Events Contact Volunteer Donate Washington's 1st legislative district Re-elect Davina Duerr for State Representative I'm Davina Duerr — a licensed architect, three-term state representative, chair of the House Local Government Committee.
I write bills that build affordable homes, cut emissions from the buildings we already have, and shorten commutes on the roads you drive every day.

Davina Williams Duerr grew up in upstate New York, earned a Bachelor of Arts in architecture with a minor in environmental geography from Syracuse University, and moved west to build a career in design.
A licensed architect, she brings a builder's eye for how housing, land use, and climate fit together to every bill she writes.
She stepped into civic life through the Bothell Landmarks Preservation Board — ten years of service, eight as chair.
She co-founded the M.I.L.K.
Money campaign through the Northshore Schools Foundation, a program that raises money for students experiencing homelessness and still serves thousands of kids each year.
In 2016 she ran for Bothell City Council and won.
Her colleagues elected her deputy mayor.
When state Rep.
Derek Stanford was appointed to the Senate in 2019, the King and Snohomish County Councils appointed Davina to fill his seat.
Voters elected her to a full term in 2020 and re-elected her in 2022 and 2024.

removed: Skip to content Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE DONATE About Meet Greg Martin The Principled Conservative for District 26 Meet Greg Martin, who represents the Tennessee State House of Representatives for District 26 , which encompasses Hixson, Stuart Heights, Rivermont, Big Ridge , Sale Creek, Shady Grove, Dallas, Possum Creek, Lupton City, Riverview , Bakewell, Lakesite, Middle Valley, Harrison, Soddy Daisy, North Shore and Downtown Chattanooga .
He previously served on the Hamilton County Commission for District 3 from 2016 to 2022.
This district encompasses Hixson, Big Ridge, Middle Valley, and Lakesite.
Greg served District 3 as the representative on the Hamilton County School Board from 2012 to 2016.
He also served on the Long Beach, MS School Board from 1993 to 1996.
Greg is a 1981 graduate of Hixson High School, has a B.A.
Degree from Bryan College, and Master’s and Doctoral Degrees from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary.
Greg and his sons have been educated in the public schools in District 3.
He is the son of Dianne Killough Martin and the late John Martin, both of Hixson.
Greg’s wife, Sheila, is a teacher in Hamilton County Schools.

Greg is the Immediate Past President and current member of the Hixson Kiwanis Club , the Immediate Past Chairman of the Board of Directors of Adult and Teen Challenge of the MidSouth, and serves on the Advisory Board of Directors of the Friends of Hixson.
He previously served on the Board of Directors of the Hixson Council of the Chamber of Commerce.
He was named the 2015 PTA School Board Member of the Year in the State of Tennessee and was inducted into the Hixson High School Hall of Fame in 2018.
Greg has served as the Vice President of the Soddy-Daisy High School Boys Basketball Booster Club.
He coached basketball in the Soddy-Daisy Kid’s Club.
Greg is a member of the Hamilton County Republican Party and the Hamilton County Pachyderm Club.
Greg is active in his church, Calvary Chapel Northside .
He is a REALTOR with Berkshire Hathaway Home Services Realty Center in Hixson.

removed: Skip to content Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE Home About Issues Volunteer News Home About Issues Volunteer News DONATE DONATE Issues The Facts On Greg Taxes Public Safety Education School Safety Immigration The Facts on Greg’s Voting Record Greg Martin is running against a Liberal Democrat on the November 5 ballot.
Rather than focus on her progressive ideas for State Government , Greg’s opponent has now launched a baseless, negative attack on his voting record.
Do not believe the rhetoric and misleading claims being made in this race.

Now, more outside Progressive PACs and Liberal Groups are targeting District 26 with more negative rhetoric and misleading claims to convince you to vote for a Progressive Democrat who will take us backwards and reverse the conservative policies that have made Hamilton County and Tennessee one of the best places to live, work, play and retire.
You can read more HERE .
We created this page to help answer some questions we are getting about these misleading attacks and mischaracterizations of his views and voting record.
As always, voters can reach Greg Martin directly via email at info@ElectGregMartin.com or (423) 596-7338 .
HB127: Expansion of restraints I am a product of Hamilton County Schools as are my children.
My wife is a public school teacher , and almost every night we have a conversation about how we can help improve public school education.
My wife and I know that the greatest schools are the schools where parents are engaged and involved in their child’s success .

This past year, I supported and voted for legislation that brought the largest salary increase for teachers in our state’s history, directly impacting 7,588 teachers and raising the minimum salary from $28,000 to $50,000 by school year 2026-2027 — which will move Tennessee into the Top 10 states with the highest paid teachers.
Click to Learn the Facts on HB127 Click to Learn the Facts on HB127 HB1202: AUTHORIZATION FOR TEACHERS TO CARRY HANDGUN ON SCHOOL GROUNDS.
Yes, Representative Greg Martin did vote for HB1202 for several reasons but most of them had nothing to do with District 26.
Greg’s opponent leaves out that this law is 100% voluntary and cannot be implemented without local control.
Locally, Hamilton County Superintendent and our Hamilton County Sheriff have already stated they would not support arming teachers in Hamilton County.
The bill allows them to do exactly that, and that is why this is a non-issue for District 26.
Greg supported the bill because many school systems across Tennessee – in areas you may never pass through – do not have the same resources as Hamilton County and other metro areas.
They too deserve every tool available to allow the teachers and administrators in these schools that ability to protect their children.

This law is about empowering teachers and principals who want to be prepared to defend the children they love should a situation ever unfold where someone threatens or tries to harm students inside the school.
As of today, 32 states have passed some type of law that allows teachers to carry under certain and limited circumstances.
And, there is no record of any accidents.
We can all rally around PROTECTING CHILDREN and not allowing our schools to be the targets for the savage and deranged.
And yes, we all want our students to just be kids, have fun, and learn in a safe place so they can get the education they deserve.
Today, more than 500 schools across TN have the funds for an SRO but they can’t find sworn officers to take the job.
This law is just another tool that local school districts can use if the sheriff, superintendent, and principals deem it necessary.
We are fortunate in Hamilton County to have an abundance of SRO, and this option is not needed in our community.
Greg’s wife, Sheila, works in education, including several years teaching your children in District 26 schools.
I promise her and you that I will always do everything within my power to make sure our students, faculty, and administrators are safe and protected.
You can count on Greg Martin to stand tall for the best policies and every resource necessary to protect our schools.

DONATE James Gallagher for Congress Announces Endorsement From California Farm Bureau Yuba City CA – James Gallagher for Congress announced today the endorsement of the California Farm Bureau for his campaign in the Special Election for Congressional District 1.
The California Farm Bureau is a leading voice for farmers, ranchers, and rural communities across the state.

In announcing the endorsement, California Farm Bureau President Shannon Douglass highlighted Gallagher’s deep understanding of the agricultural community and the urgent need for strong rural representation in Congress.
“The passing of Congressman Doug LaMalfa left a huge void in Congress when it comes to understanding the challenges faced by farmers and ranchers.

James Gallagher has the experience, knowledge, and proven record to help fill that void and be a strong voice for farmers and rural communities,” said Shannon Douglass, President, California Farm Bureau.
Gallagher said he is honored to earn the support of the California Farm Bureau and remains committed to fighting for the families, businesses, and communities that keep California agriculture strong.
“I am honored to receive the endorsement of the California Farm Bureau,” said James Gallagher.

“Farmers and ranchers are the backbone of our rural economy and way of life, and they need leaders in Congress who understand the real challenges they face every day — from water and regulatory burdens to rising costs and threats to their livelihoods.

I will always fight to protect our agricultural heritage, strengthen rural communities, and ensure the voices of our farmers and ranchers are heard in Washington.” As a longtime advocate for agriculture and rural California, Gallagher has built a record of standing up for farmers, ranchers, and the communities that depend on them.

His campaign for Congress continues to gain momentum with strong support from leaders and organizations who recognize the importance of having a proven conservative voice fighting for the North State in Washington.

Home Endorsements Events News Get Involved!

DONATE McGuire Backs Out Of Candidate Forum Next Week In Plumas County CHICO, CA — Today, Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) called out State Senator Mike McGuire for backing out of next week’s candidate forum in Quincy hosted by the Plumas County League of Women Voters.
In August, the League invited Gallagher and McGuire to participate in the Plumas County forum.
After both candidates accepted the invitation, the League rented a venue and began promoting the forum .
However, yesterday, the Gallagher campaign was notified by forum organizers that McGuire had abruptly dropped out.
“The voters of Plumas County and throughout the First District deserve transparency and a chance to hear directly from the candidates,” said Gallagher campaign manager Rachel Lederer.

“But after his poor performance in Ukiah, it’s clear that McGuire is scared to talk about his failed career serving as Gavin Newsom’s puppet in Sacramento.” The Gallagher campaign will move forward with hosting an event in Plumas County next week.
In an interview with Action News Now following the candidate forum back in May, McGuire himself said that more debates were needed because they are ‘really powerful for democracy’.
Click here to watch the interview clip.

McGuire has now declined, cancelled, or backed out of forum invitations from: The Butte County League of Women Voters The Plumas County League of Women Voters KCRA Channel 3 Action News Now The Yuba-Sutter Chamber of Commerce Gallagher remains committed to participating in debates held to neutral, fair standards that allow a real back-and-forth on ideas.
He believes it is important for candidates to challenge one another on the issues and put their records in front of voters.
Gallagher challenged McGuire to five debates across California’s newly redrawn 1st Congressional District.
Only one forum has occurred since the primary.

added: 0 Skip to Content Home District Key Issues Affordability Fair State Funding Public Education Labor & Working Families Health Care, Rights & Freedoms Water, Coast & Climate Service: Veterans & Military Families Hear from Jessica Volunteer 6 for the 6th Lawn Sign Form Volunteer Endorsements Voter Registration DONATE Open Menu Close Menu Home District Key Issues Affordability Fair State Funding Public Education Labor & Working Families Health Care, Rights & Freedoms Water, Coast & Climate Service: Veterans & Military Families Hear from Jessica Volunteer 6 for the 6th Lawn Sign Form Volunteer Endorsements Voter Registration DONATE Open Menu Close Menu Home District Folder: Key Issues Back Affordability Fair State Funding Public Education Labor & Working Families Health Care, Rights & Freedoms Water, Coast & Climate Service: Veterans & Military Families Hear from Jessica Folder: Volunteer Back 6 for the 6th Lawn Sign Form Volunteer Endorsements Voter Registration DONATE In Conversation , • 10/15/26 I would be the FIRST WOMAN elected to this seat In its entire history, the 6th Plymouth District has never been represented in the state legislature by a woman.
If I win, I will be the first woman to represent the towns of Duxbury, Marshfield, Pembroke, Hanson, and Halifax on Beacon Hill.
In our entire state's history, only 243 women have ever served in the state legislature out of more than 20,000 elected legislators.
I think it's well past time that we moved toward a little bit more parity there.
I would be so honored to have the privilege of being the first woman to represent this district, and I hope I can earn your vote.

Platform Contact News Platform Contact News Events Endorsements Volunteer Merch Media Kit Donate Media Kit Voters in Indiana’s 5th Congressional District should see districtwide on OTT/CTV streaming, digital, and read in the mailbox that Victoria Spartz is everything Hoosiers have come to hate about Washington.
Instead of serving us she's enriched herself and driven up our costs in the process.
Spartz traded $5 million in stocks in industries she regulated while in Congress.
Additionally, her campaign has been flooded with money from insurance and pharmaceutical companies, and she's done their bidding.
Hoosiers need to know: Victoria Spartz is a Washington insider who sold us out.

1) Corruption & Self Dealing ​ Voters need to know that Victoria Spartz has traded $5 million in stocks in industries she regulated while in Congress and fought against reforms that would stop members of Congress from insider trading.

For years, she refused to sign onto efforts that would have banned members of Congress from insider trading, including even violating existing rules that required disclosing trades she made while in Congress.
It's the worst kind of Washington greed: a politician using her office to get rich while your costs keep climbing.

2) Prescription Drugs & Health Care Voters need to know that Victoria Spartz let the insurance and pharmaceutical industries flood her campaign with tens of thousands of dollars, and then did their bidding, voting to protect their profits, drive up premiums, kick 650,000 Hoosiers off care, deny coverage for pre-existing conditions and protect the high cost of prescription drugs.
When Hoosiers needed somebody to take on special interests and stand up for us, Spartz sided with the health care industries.
Targeted — Data Centers Republicans outside of Hamilton County need to read in their mailboxes and see on their phones that Victoria Spartz sold them out to the big data-center companies.
Spartz took campaign money from Big Tech and the companies that build data centers, then stayed silent as they moved in.

As the state passed the largest tax break in the country to lure data centers to Indiana, Spartz said nothing while they built over our farmland, drained local water, and passed their soaring utility costs onto ratepayers.
Instead of fighting to give communities a voice, Spartz took Big Tech's money and stayed silent.

added: Home News Latest News 60 Seconds With John Ley About Me Donate 60 Seconds With John Ley Issues The $14 Billion Crime Scene: Why the I-5 Interstate Bridge Project Is Taxpayer Insanity October 15, 2026 by John Ley The huge waste of taxpayer money on the IBR By Representative John Ley The story you are about to see is true.
The names have been changed to protect the innocent.
But the waste?
That part is entirely real, and it is coming straight out of your pocketbook.
Behind me stands the I-5 Interstate Bridge.
For decades, it has served as a vital artery connecting Southwest Washington and Oregon.
But the current proposal by the Interstate Bridge Replacement (IBR) program is steering us straight toward a fiscal disaster.
We are looking at a project projected to cost an astronomical $14 billion to $15 billion .
And what are taxpayers getting for that staggering price tag?
A plan to replace an over-congested three-lane bridge with… another three-lane bridge.
That is the definition of insanity.
A Lower Bridge and Million-Dollar “Buy-Offs” The problems start with the physical design itself.
The existing bridge provides 178 feet of clear headroom for maritime traffic.
The IBR’s proposed design drops that clearance down to 116 feet .

Because that lower clearance restricts large vessels, the project has baked in a deal to pay $140-plus million to four upriver firms just to buy them off—and essentially buy their approval for a bridge that is built too low.
Meanwhile, look at the track record of spending so far: they’ve burned through about $280 million of your tax dollars , and we still don’t have a final design.
That follows right on the heels of the $200 million wasted on the defunct Columbia River Crossing project.
Where Is the Money Actually Going?

Thanks to a public records request uncovered by a Portland economist at the City Observatory, we have a clear look at the laundry list of unneeded, bloated add-ons stuffed into this project that have nothing to do with a simple replacement bridge.

(These were Cortright data costs, as the IBR has moved money around even more). $320 million for a Ruby Junction maintenance facility for TriMet (roughly 20 miles away from the corridor). $356 million for light rail track systems. $296 million to remove the current two bridges, plus another $56 million removing the North Portland Harbor Bridge. $188 million for new light rail vehicles. $132 million for a Hayden Island guideway. $104 million for a waterfront park-and-ride facility. $96 million for a separate North Harbor Transit bridge connecting North Portland with Hayden Island. $87 million for an Evergreen park-and-ride at the end of the light rail line.
This is supposed to be about a five-mile bridge influence corridor.
Instead, it has morphed into a massive regional transit wish list funded by drivers who just want a functioning highway.
The Common-Sense Alternative: A $2 Billion Solution We don’t need a $15 billion boondoggle.

If we built a simple, streamlined replacement bridge, it could be done for roughly $2 billion , delivering massive value and keeping funds free for transportation projects across the rest of Washington state.
Even better, we could repurpose the existing two bridges : Restripe them down to two lanes each.
Slow local traffic down to 45 mph.
Create a dedicated local connection for Vancouver and Hayden Island residents to shop, commute, and enjoy the waterfront without clogging up the main freeway.
To put this in perspective, look at Kentucky and Cincinnati, Ohio.
They are spending about $4 billion to build a brand-new 10-lane bridge over the Ohio River—with no tolls and no heavy transit bloat .
Delivering Value, Stopping the Crime Taxpayers in Southwest Washington deserve fiscal sanity, transparency, and real solutions.
Accepting a crippled three-lane design for nearly fifteen billion dollars is a crime against taxpayers.
I’m Representative John Ley, and I’m fighting to deliver real value for your transportation dollars, stop the runaway spending, and shut down this boondoggle.
I’ll keep you updated as we uncover even more details about where your money is going.

DONATE SUPPORT MICHELE'S FIGHT FOR CONSERVATIVE VALUES All Posts Search Legislative Recap: Conservative Fiscal Discipline at Work Team Reneau Jun 14 3 min read While Washington racks up trillions in debt and prints money to cover its mistakes, Tennessee continues to do something very important: we balance our budget.
That matters.

A state government should not spend money it does not have, and Tennessee’s commitment to a zero-debt, balanced budget helps keep our state on stronger financial footing than many others across the country.
This year, the General Assembly passed a $# billion balanced budget without raising taxes.
I voted for the budget because it funded important priorities, maintained Tennessee’s strong fiscal position, and avoided new debt.
But I also believe we could have done more to reduce spending.
Tennessee families are making difficult decisions every day.
Grocery bills are higher.
Housing costs are higher.
Insurance, utilities, gas, and basic necessities are taking more out of family budgets.
When families have to cut back, the government should be willing to do the same.
There were good investments in this budget.
The state appropriated more than $890 million in new dollars for infrastructure, transportation, and economic development.
That includes $400 million for new and existing transportation projects, bringing TDOT’s total General Fund allocations to $5 billion.

It also includes $81.2 million to support aviation infrastructure, $25 million for Nuclear Industry Initiative Grants, and $20 million for upkeep and infrastructure of our shortline railroads, including investments that support rural communities and farmers across Tennessee.

For K-12 education, the budget added $339 million in new recurring dollars, bringing the total Tennessee Investment in Achievement formula to $7.1 billion and the overall public education budget to more than $9.4 billion for the 2026-27 school year.
The budget also raised the minimum starting teacher salary to $50,000.
For health care and children’s services, the budget directed $205 million in Shared Savings to fund initiatives, including Rural Health Transformation Resiliency Grants.
It provided $230 million to TennCare to cover increasing costs tied to medical inflation, higher prescription drug prices, Medicare payments, and expanded services.

It invested $34.5 million in the Department of Children’s Services to reduce caseload ratios and help protect Tennessee’s most vulnerable children, plus $10.7 million to enhance staff safety at DCS facilities serving delinquent youth.
The budget also provided $7 million to the Summer EBT program for 2027.

We also funded a three-year pilot program to support family caregivers’ lost wages and expenses and approved a $# million Volunteer Firefighter Vehicle Grant Program through HB 2446 to help local communities meet match requirements for federal grants.
These are real needs, and some of these investments will benefit Tennessee families, communities, and infrastructure.
But conservative fiscal discipline requires more than balancing the budget.
It requires asking whether the government should be spending the money in the first place.
It requires a willingness to examine every program, every new initiative, and every recurring expense to determine whether it is necessary, effective, and respectful of the taxpayers who fund it.
In my view, we should have trimmed more.
We should have looked harder for places to reduce the size and cost of government.
And we should be looking for more ways to return money to Tennessee citizens, whether through reducing the sales tax on food or other forms of tax relief that help families directly.
A balanced budget is good.
A zero-debt budget is important.
But the ultimate goal should not be for the government to keep more of the people’s money simply because revenues are available.
The goal should be to fund core responsibilities, reduce unnecessary spending, and leave more money in the hands of the people who earned it.
Tennessee is still one of the best-managed states in the country, and I want to keep it that way.
But staying fiscally conservative means we cannot become complacent.
As families across Tennessee tighten their belts, state government should be willing to tighten its belt too.

removed: top of page Home About Platform Menu Close PLATFORM DONATE VOLUNTEER If you work hard, you should be able to afford to live here.
Working families are doing everything right and still falling behind.
Rent keeps rising.
Groceries cost more every month.
Utility bills hit harder every year.
Meanwhile, wages haven’t kept up—and tax systems continue to favor those at the top.

Ezequiel supports: Policies that lower the cost of housing and keep families from being priced out Fair taxation so working people aren’t carrying the load alone Investments in infrastructure and utilities that reduce long-term costs Affordability isn’t about buzzwords.
It’s about whether you can pay the bills and still have something left.
A fair day’s work deserves fair pay and safe conditions.
You deserve to be treated with respect—and paid fairly.
Ezequiel’s background with the United Farm Workers and his current work as an electrician give him a clear understanding of how often workers are ignored, underpaid, or put in unsafe conditions.

He will fight for: Stronger enforcement of wage theft and labor protections Safe working conditions in agriculture, construction, and skilled trades The right to organize without intimidation or retaliation Apprenticeship and workforce training programs that lead to real careers The people who build this state should have a real voice in how it’s run.
No family should live in fear.
The 14th Legislative District is overwhelmingly Latino, and immigrant families are central to its strength.
Yet fear has become a constant reality for too many people—fear of separation, fear of detention, fear of simply living their lives.
Ezequiel believes that no family should live in fear because of where they were born.

He supports: Strong state-level protections that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement Keeping schools, hospitals, and courthouses safe and accessible for everyone Defending due process and basic human rights Standing up to policies that use fear and division as political tools Ezequiel has been outspoken about ICE activity because silence is not an option when communities are under threat.
Representation that answers to the community—not corporations.
Ezequiel isn’t interested in party loyalty for its own sake.
He believes both parties have failed working people when they stop listening.

Ezequiel will: Put working families ahead of corporate donors Question policies that don’t deliver real results Stay accountable to the people of the 14th District—not Olympia insiders Good leadership starts with listening—and with having the courage to stand firm when it matters.
