title.after: Abbarno recibe un amplio abanico de apoyos para su reelección | Peter Abbarno

added: Familias más fuertes.
Comunidades más fuertes.

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir Una de las responsabilidades más importantes de un cargo electo es unir a la gente para resolver problemas.
En el clima político tan polarizado de hoy en día, eso puede resultar difícil.

Con demasiada frecuencia, los debates sobre políticas públicas se plantean como una confrontación entre empresarios y trabajadores, entre empresas y sindicatos, o entre los intereses de una comunidad y los de otra.
Y con demasiada frecuencia se difunden historias falsas en Internet y en los medios de comunicación para distraernos y dividirnos.
Por eso es un honor para mí recibir el apoyo de una amplia coalición de organizaciones que representan perspectivas muy diversas en todo el estado de Washington.

Estos apoyos no solo son un reflejo de nuestra campaña, sino también un reconocimiento al trabajo que hemos hecho en Olympia para forjar relaciones, encontrar puntos en común y promover soluciones prácticas para la gente del suroeste de Washington.

Entre estos apoyos se encuentran dos organizaciones que a menudo se consideran representantes de bandos opuestos en los debates sobre políticas públicas: la Asociación Empresarial de Washington (AWB), la mayor asociación empresarial del estado, y el Consejo de Oficios de la Construcción del Estado de Washington, que representa a miles de trabajadores cualificados de todo el estado.
Me siento orgulloso de ser el único legislador del suroeste de Washington que ha recibido el respaldo de ambas organizaciones.
Su apoyo demuestra que un liderazgo eficaz no consiste en tomar partido.

Se trata de escuchar, generar confianza y defender políticas que fortalezcan nuestras comunidades, generen oportunidades económicas, apoyen a nuestra población activa y mejoren la calidad de vida de las familias de Washington.

Durante todo mi mandato en la Asamblea Legislativa, he trabajado para impulsar el desarrollo económico, la formación profesional, las inversiones en infraestructuras y las políticas que ayudan a las empresas a crecer, al tiempo que garantizan que los trabajadores tengan acceso a empleos con un sueldo que permita mantener a una familia.
Esos objetivos no tienen por qué ser incompatibles.
Las empresas sólidas necesitan trabajadores cualificados, y los trabajadores necesitan empresas prósperas.
Cuando ambos prosperan, nuestras comunidades también lo hacen.

También estoy muy agradecido por haber recibido el respaldo de la Asociación de Agentes Inmobiliarios del estado de Washington, la Asociación de Contratistas Generales de Washington y el Comité de Acción Política (PAC) de la Asociación de Enfermeras del estado de Washington.

En conjunto, estos respaldos reflejan el apoyo de los profesionales que construyen nuestras comunidades, prestan servicios sanitarios, crean oportunidades de vivienda e impulsan el crecimiento económico en todo el estado de Washington.
La asequibilidad de la vivienda sigue siendo uno de los retos más acuciantes a los que se enfrentan las familias de todo nuestro estado.

Para aumentar la oferta de viviendas, apoyar un desarrollo responsable, invertir en infraestructuras y fomentar las oportunidades de acceso a la propiedad, es necesaria la colaboración entre constructores, contratistas, agentes inmobiliarios, administraciones locales y las partes interesadas de la comunidad.
Estos apoyos reflejan el compromiso con políticas prácticas que ayuden a que la vivienda sea más asequible para las familias trabajadoras.
Del mismo modo, el acceso a una asistencia sanitaria de calidad sigue siendo una prioridad para las comunidades de todo Washington.

El apoyo del comité de acción política (PAC) de la Asociación de Enfermeras del Estado de Washington reconoce los esfuerzos por mejorar el acceso a la asistencia sanitaria, apoyar a los profesionales sanitarios, mejorar los servicios de salud mental y garantizar que los pacientes reciban la atención que necesitan cerca de casa.
Creo que estos respaldos significan algo más que un simple apoyo institucional.
Reflejan la convicción de que el gobierno funciona mejor cuando los líderes se centran en los resultados en lugar de en la retórica.
Demuestran que es posible unir a empresarios y trabajadores, a sindicatos y empresas, a profesionales sanitarios y a constructores en torno a soluciones sensatas.

En un momento en el que las divisiones políticas suelen acaparar los titulares, estos apoyos transmiten un mensaje diferente: personas de distintos sectores y orígenes pueden trabajar juntas para abordar la asequibilidad, ampliar las oportunidades de vivienda, mejorar el acceso a la sanidad, crear empleo, proteger los derechos y la seguridad de los trabajadores y construir comunidades más sólidas.
El suroeste de Washington se merece líderes que trabajen con cualquiera que esté dispuesto a hacer avanzar a nuestras comunidades.

Sigo comprometido a forjar esas alianzas, a escuchar diferentes puntos de vista y a defender políticas prácticas que fortalezcan a las familias, generen oportunidades económicas y mejoren la calidad de vida de la gente a la que servimos.

Juntos podemos seguir construyendo un futuro más sólido para el suroeste de Washington. ← Artículo anterior Artículo siguiente → Entradas más recientes Cuando las prioridades locales se convierten en inversiones estatales Oct 7, 2026 | Elegir a Peter Abbarno Para la Cámara de Comercio de C-C Una de las cosas más importantes a la hora de representar a nuestra comunidad en Olympia es escuchar a los líderes locales, identificar las necesidades reales y, después, trabajar juntos para convertir esas prioridades en resultados....

title.after: Mantengamos los bosques en funcionamiento por el bien del condado de Lewis | Peter Abbarno

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir En la Cámara de Comercio de Centralia-Chehalis , por el diputado Peter Abbarno En el condado de Lewis, nuestros bosques son mucho más que un simple paisaje.

Son la piedra angular de nuestra economía, una fuente de empleos con un sueldo que permite mantener a una familia, un mecanismo de financiación fundamental para los colegios y los servicios locales, y una parte importante de una gestión medioambiental responsable.
Durante generaciones, los bosques en explotación han contribuido a construir nuestras comunidades.
Dan trabajo a leñadores, camioneros, trabajadores de aserraderos, operadores de maquinaria, silvicultores y un sinfín de pequeñas empresas que dependen de una economía maderera sólida.
En comunidades rurales como la nuestra, la industria maderera no es solo parte de nuestra historia, sino que sigue siendo una parte esencial de nuestro futuro.
En todo el condado de Lewis, la industria de productos forestales genera casi 6.000 puestos de trabajo, con unos salarios anuales totales que superan los 450 millones de dólares.
En el estado de Washington, la industria maderera genera más de 102.000 puestos de trabajo y genera más de 6.000 millones de dólares en salarios al año.

Los bosques en explotación sustentan la tercera industria manufacturera más grande del estado y aportan más de 300 millones de dólares al año en impuestos y tasas que ayudan a financiar los servicios públicos.
Estos puestos de trabajo e ingresos son especialmente importantes en condados como el de Lewis, donde los recursos naturales siguen desempeñando un papel significativo en la economía local.

Por eso he expresado mi profunda preocupación por las recientes decisiones del Departamento de Recursos Naturales del estado de Washington y del comisionado de Tierras Públicas, Dave Upthegrove, que suspendieron la venta de madera en los bosques más antiguos y, posteriormente, destinaron aproximadamente 77 000 acres de bosques estatales más antiguos, que forman parte del patrimonio del estado, a una gestión orientada a la conservación en lugar de a la tala tradicional.
Los bosques en explotación también benefician directamente a los colegios y a los ayuntamientos.
La tala de madera genera ingresos fiscales que ayudan a financiar la educación, la seguridad pública, las carreteras y otros servicios esenciales.

En muchas comunidades rurales, los ingresos procedentes de la madera llevan mucho tiempo ayudando a mantener los distritos escolares y las instituciones públicas que, de otro modo, tendrían dificultades para mantener sus servicios.
Cuando nuestra industria maderera prospera, nuestras comunidades también prosperan.
Por desgracia, con demasiada frecuencia el debate sobre los bosques se centra únicamente en la disyuntiva entre conservación y producción.
La realidad es mucho más matizada.
La silvicultura sostenible demuestra que la gestión medioambiental y las oportunidades económicas no son incompatibles.
Los bosques en explotación modernos están gestionados con esmero por silvicultores profesionales, bajo algunas de las normativas medioambientales más exhaustivas del país.
Estos bosques proporcionan materiales de construcción renovables, al tiempo que protegen el hábitat de los peces, la calidad del agua y la fauna silvestre.
En Washington, los bosques en explotación ayudan a proteger más de 60 000 millas de arroyos y millones de acres de hábitat.
Por cada árbol talado, se plantan varios en su lugar, creando un ciclo continuo de crecimiento y renovación.
Los silvicultores de Washington plantan unos 52 millones de árboles cada año, lo que supone tres árboles por cada uno que se tala.
Además, cada vez hay más pruebas de que los bosques gestionados de forma activa pueden desempeñar un papel importante en la lucha contra el cambio climático.
Mucha gente da por hecho que los bosques más viejos y sin gestionar son los que más beneficios aportan al clima.

Sin embargo, cada vez hay más estudios que demuestran que los bosques gestionados de forma sostenible suelen capturar el carbono de manera más eficiente, ya que los árboles más jóvenes y en crecimiento absorben el carbono a un ritmo más rápido.
Además, los productos de madera talada siguen almacenando carbono durante décadas.

Según estudios citados por organizaciones forestales de Washington y la Universidad de Washington, los bosques gestionados de Washington crecen mucho más rápido y capturan más carbono por acre que los bosques federales no gestionados.
Los bosques y los productos de madera de Washington compensan una parte importante de las emisiones de carbono del estado.
La gestión forestal activa también reduce el riesgo de incendios forestales.
Washington ha sufrido incendios devastadores alimentados por bosques demasiado densos, un sotobosque excesivo, enfermedades y madera muerta.
Los bosques sin gestionar suelen tener una mayor mortalidad de árboles y generan más carga de combustible, lo que aumenta la probabilidad de que se produzcan incendios catastróficos.
Esos incendios no solo amenazan a las comunidades y a la fauna, sino que también liberan a la atmósfera cantidades enormes de carbono almacenado.
Las prácticas forestales sostenibles, como el clareo, la tala, la reforestación y la reducción de combustible, ayudan a mantener los bosques sanos y resistentes.
Por eso creo que debemos seguir apoyando políticas que mantengan en funcionamiento los bosques productivos.

Eso significa fomentar la gestión forestal activa, apoyar la tala responsable, invertir en la salud de los bosques, proteger los puestos de trabajo en el sector forestal que garanticen un sueldo suficiente para mantener a una familia y asegurarnos de que las políticas reguladoras se basen en datos científicos sólidos.
El condado de Lewis lleva mucho tiempo siendo consciente del valor de las tierras de cultivo.
Nuestra industria maderera ayudó a construir colegios, negocios y barrios.
Hoy en día, sigue ofreciendo oportunidades laborales, apoyando a los ayuntamientos y contribuyendo a un medio ambiente más saludable.
Los bosques en explotación no son una reliquia del pasado.
Son un recurso renovable que beneficia a nuestras comunidades hoy y a las generaciones venideras.

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir Junio es el Mes de la Concienciación sobre el TEPT, un momento para reconocer el impacto del trastorno por estrés postraumático (TEPT), apoyar a las personas afectadas y fomentar el acceso al tratamiento y la recuperación.
Como abogado de Althauser Rayan Abbarno y diputado estatal por el suroeste de Washington, he visto de primera mano cómo las experiencias traumáticas pueden cambiar vidas.
Aunque mucha gente asocia el trastorno de estrés postraumático (TEPT) con el servicio militar, el TEPT puede afectar a cualquiera que sufra o sea testigo de un suceso traumático.

Esto incluye a las víctimas de accidentes graves de tráfico, lesiones laborales, violencia doméstica, agresiones sexuales, delitos violentos, maltrato infantil, desastres naturales y otros incidentes traumáticos.
El trastorno de estrés postraumático (TEPT) es una afección médica real y que a menudo se malinterpreta.

Los síntomas pueden incluir ansiedad, depresión, pesadillas, recuerdos recurrentes, trastornos del sueño, dificultad para concentrarse, aislamiento emocional y reacciones intensificadas ante el estrés.
Estas lesiones invisibles pueden afectar a las relaciones, la vida profesional, la salud física y la calidad de vida en general.
En mi práctica jurídica, he representado a personas cuyas vidas cambiaron para siempre a raíz de lesiones graves y sucesos traumáticos.
Aunque las lesiones físicas pueden curarse con el tiempo, el trauma emocional puede persistir mucho después de que las heridas visibles hayan desaparecido.

Las víctimas de violencia doméstica, agresiones sexuales y delitos violentos suelen enfrentarse a importantes retos emocionales y psicológicos que merecen la misma atención y cuidados que las lesiones físicas.
Reconocer estas lesiones invisibles es un paso importante hacia la curación y la recuperación.
Como legislador, me he esforzado por dar a conocer mejor el trastorno de estrés postraumático y ampliar el acceso a los servicios de tratamiento y apoyo.

Un ejemplo es el proyecto de ley 1002 de la Cámara de Representantes , una iniciativa que presenté para reconocer los retos específicos en materia de salud mental a los que se enfrentan los forenses y los médicos forenses de los condados.
A estos profesionales se les suele llamar a los lugares donde se producen accidentes mortales, homicidios, suicidios y otros sucesos traumáticos.
En comunidades más pequeñas, como muchas del suroeste de Washington, la tragedia puede ser aún más personal.
Un forense o un médico forense puede llegar a un lugar donde haya un amigo, un vecino, un compañero de trabajo o incluso un familiar.

La exposición repetida a situaciones traumáticas puede tener consecuencias duraderas para la salud mental, y quienes sirven a nuestras comunidades en estas difíciles funciones merecen reconocimiento y apoyo.

También presenté el proyecto de ley 2430 de la Cámara de Representantes para restablecer la tasa penal para víctimas de delitos que se aplica a los delincuentes condenados por delitos contra las personas.
Esta tasa ayuda a financiar servicios para las víctimas de delitos, incluidas las víctimas de agresiones, violencia doméstica, agresiones sexuales y otros delitos violentos.
Muchas personas que han sobrevivido a estos delitos sufren trastorno de estrés postraumático y otras secuelas emocionales a largo plazo.
Garantizar que haya recursos disponibles para servicios de asesoramiento, defensa y recuperación es una parte importante de ayudar a las víctimas a reconstruir sus vidas.

Este año también voté a favor del proyecto de ley 2405 de la Cámara de Representantes , que estableció un programa piloto a través del Departamento de Trabajo e Industrias para mejorar el acceso al tratamiento y la investigación del trastorno de estrés postraumático (TEPT).

La ley permite que los trabajadores que cumplan los requisitos y presenten reclamaciones por TEPT como enfermedad profesional puedan recibir evaluaciones de salud mental y tratamiento mientras se revisan sus reclamaciones.
La intervención temprana puede marcar una gran diferencia en los resultados y ayudar a las personas a recibir apoyo cuando más lo necesitan.

El estado de Washington ha logrado avances importantes en el reconocimiento del trastorno de estrés postraumático (TEPT) entre los equipos de primera intervención y otros profesionales que se enfrentan habitualmente a situaciones traumáticas.

En los últimos años, los legisladores han ampliado las protecciones relacionadas con el TEPT para bomberos, agentes de policía, personal de emergencias, operadores de telecomunicaciones de seguridad pública y ciertos trabajadores sanitarios.
Estas medidas reflejan una creciente conciencia de que la salud mental merece la misma atención y respeto que la salud física.

Ya sea que el TEPT se desarrolle tras haber respondido a una emergencia, haber sobrevivido a un delito violento, haber escapado de la violencia doméstica, haber sufrido un accidente catastrófico o haber pasado por un incidente traumático en el trabajo, la intervención y el tratamiento tempranos son fundamentales.
Durante el Mes de Concienciación sobre el TEPT, sigamos trabajando para reducir el estigma, fomentar el tratamiento, apoyar a las víctimas y ampliar el acceso a la atención sanitaria.
Al reconocer el TEPT y abordar las heridas invisibles con compasión y comprensión, podemos ayudar a las personas, las familias y las comunidades a sanar y prosperar.

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir Junio es un mes especial para las familias.

Al celebrar el Día del Padre y reconocer el papel que desempeñan los padres, abuelos, padrastros y modelos masculinos positivos en la formación de la próxima generación, también es un recordatorio importante de una de las cosas más significativas que los adultos pueden hacer con un niño: leer juntos.

Hace poco, asistí a los Días de Dolly, organizados por United Way del condado de Lewis y la Fundación Rotaria del condado de Lewis, que ayudaron a concienciar y recaudar fondos para la Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton y los esfuerzos de alfabetización de la primera infancia en todo el estado de Washington.
El evento celebró algo más que libros.
Celebró familias más fuertes, comunidades más fuertes y futuros más brillantes para los niños.

Como padre, comprendo lo significativos que pueden ser esos momentos sentándose al final de un día ajetreado a leer un cuento antes de dormir, ayudando a un niño a pronunciar palabras por primera vez o viendo cómo su imaginación cobra vida página a página.
Esos momentos crean recuerdos que duran toda la vida.

También ayudan a los niños a desarrollar el lenguaje, la alfabetización y las habilidades de comunicación que necesitan para tener éxito en la escuela y más allá. Ésa es una de las razones por las que copatrociné y aprobé con orgullo el proyecto de ley 2068 de la Cámara de Representantes en 2022, que estableció y amplió el programa Biblioteca de la Imaginación de Dolly Parton en Washington.
El programa proporciona libros gratuitos y adecuados a la edad todos los meses a niños desde el nacimiento hasta los 5 años, independientemente de los ingresos familiares.
El concepto en el que se basa el programa es sencillo pero potente.
Todos los meses se envían libros directamente a los hogares de los niños, lo que ayuda a las familias a crear bibliotecas domésticas y anima a padres y cuidadores a pasar tiempo leyendo juntos.
Desde su creación por Dolly Parton en 1995, el programa se ha expandido internacionalmente y ahora sirve a millones de niños.
En Washington, la participación sigue creciendo porque las comunidades reconocen el valor a largo plazo de la alfabetización temprana.
La investigación demuestra sistemáticamente que la lectura temprana es importante.

Los estudios han descubierto que los niños a los que se lee con regularidad antes de la guardería tienen muchas más probabilidades de desarrollar un vocabulario, una comunicación y una alfabetización sólidos.

Según los expertos en desarrollo infantil, casi el 90% del desarrollo cerebral se produce antes de los 5 años, por lo que esos primeros años son de vital importancia para el crecimiento cognitivo y emocional.
Los niños expuestos a los libros y a la lectura a una edad temprana tienen más probabilidades de entrar en la guardería preparados para aprender.
También es más probable que obtengan mejores resultados académicos más adelante.
Leer juntos refuerza la capacidad de atención, mejora la capacidad de escucha, fomenta la curiosidad y ayuda a los niños a desarrollar la empatía y la creatividad.
Y lo que es igual de importante, leer juntos fortalece a las familias.
En el ajetreado mundo actual, las familias compiten constantemente con pantallas, horarios y distracciones.
Reservar aunque sea unos minutos cada tarde para leer juntos crea valiosas oportunidades de conexión y conversación.
Especialmente para los padres, leer con los hijos ayuda a crear confianza, comunicación y vínculos emocionales que pueden influir positivamente en el desarrollo del niño durante años.
Por eso el Día del Padre es un momento tan apropiado para hablar de alfabetización y aprendizaje temprano.
Ser padre es algo más que proveer económicamente.
También consiste en estar presente, comprometido e implicado en la vida de un niño.
Leer juntos es una de las formas más sencillas y eficaces de hacerlo.
Por desgracia, la mayoría de la Asamblea Legislativa no apoyó el programa.
Pero la buena noticia es que asociaciones locales como United Way del condado de Lewis, Centralia Rotary, Chehalis Rotary y Twin City Rotary están dando un paso adelante.
Gracias a los simpatizantes y patrocinadores locales, el programa sigue dando resultados locales para nuestros niños y familias.
Apoyar la alfabetización también es importante para nuestro futuro económico a largo plazo.
Los niños que desarrollan pronto sólidas capacidades de lectura y comunicación están mejor preparados para la educación, la formación laboral y las oportunidades profesionales futuras.
El aprendizaje temprano no es sólo una cuestión educativa.
También es una cuestión de desarrollo de la mano de obra, una cuestión familiar y una cuestión comunitaria.
Animo a nuestra comunidad a unirse a la Biblioteca de la Imaginación.
Con sólo 30 $ al año pondrás libros en manos de un niño durante todo un año; y con sólo 150 $ te asegurarás de que los niños tengan un libro cada mes desde que nacen hasta que van a la guardería.
Es una inversión increíble, y puedes invertir en general o inscribir a un niño o a una familia en el programa en lewiscountyuw.com .
Al celebrar el Día del Padre en junio, dedica tiempo a leer con los niños.
No hace falta tecnología cara ni programas complicados.

title.after: Una infraestructura energética fiable impulsa el futuro de Washington | Peter Abbarno

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir La puesta en servicio de la nueva subestación del Distrito de Servicios Públicos del Condado de Lewis, cerca de Winlock, es más que un hito para el sur del condado de Lewis.

Es un ejemplo del tipo de inversiones en infraestructuras a largo plazo que Washington debe seguir haciendo si queremos electricidad asequible, fiable y segura para las familias, las empresas y las generaciones futuras.
El 23 de junio pusimos en marcha la subestación y vimos cómo todo ese esfuerzo y colaboración se hacían realidad.

Como miembro adjunto de mayor rango de la Comisión de Presupuesto de Inversiones de la Cámara de Representantes y miembro de la Comisión de Medio Ambiente y Energía de la Cámara de Representantes, he trabajado para dar prioridad a las inversiones que refuerzan la red eléctrica de nuestro estado, al tiempo que preparo a las comunidades para un crecimiento continuo en los ámbitos residencial, comercial e industrial.

Desde mi primer mandato legislativo en 2021, defendí la necesidad de aumentar la capacidad eléctrica en la zona de Winlock, porque estaba claro que el sur del condado de Lewis estaba a punto de experimentar un crecimiento importante.

En colaboración con el PUD del condado de Lewis, los ayuntamientos, los responsables de desarrollo económico y mis compañeros de la Asamblea Legislativa, ayudé a conseguir financiación del presupuesto de inversión estatal para hacer posible este proyecto.

Al invertir fondos estatales, contribuimos a reducir la carga financiera de los usuarios locales, al tiempo que garantizamos que nuestras comunidades dispusieran de la capacidad eléctrica necesaria para dar cabida a nuevas viviendas, empresas, colegios y puestos de trabajo con salarios dignos.
Las infraestructuras casi nunca aparecen en los titulares hasta que faltan.

Disponer de electricidad fiable es esencial para casi todos los aspectos de la vida moderna: desde hospitales y servicios de emergencia hasta fábricas, centros de datos, agricultura, pequeñas empresas y familias que teletrabajan.
A medida que nuestra economía crece y la demanda de electricidad sigue aumentando, Washington debe construir las infraestructuras necesarias para suministrar energía de forma segura y fiable.
Eso significa invertir tanto en la producción de energía como en su transporte.
Con demasiada frecuencia, las políticas públicas se centran casi exclusivamente en cómo se genera la electricidad, pasando por alto la red de transporte que la lleva a los hogares y las empresas.

Ni siquiera la fuente de energía más limpia o eficiente puede abastecer a las familias de Washington si no contamos con las subestaciones, las líneas de transporte y la infraestructura de distribución necesarias para llevar la electricidad allí donde se necesita.
Washington necesita una estrategia energética que abarque «todas las opciones».

La energía hidroeléctrica sigue siendo la columna vertebral de nuestro sistema de energía limpia, pero también necesitamos energía nuclear, gas natural, hidrógeno, energía eólica, solar, geotérmica, biomasa, tecnologías emergentes y una innovación constante.

Una cartera diversificada refuerza la fiabilidad, protege contra las interrupciones en el suministro, ayuda a estabilizar los costes y garantiza que nuestra red eléctrica siga siendo resistente durante los periodos de alta demanda o condiciones meteorológicas extremas.
Igual de importante es modernizar nuestra red de transporte.
La nueva generación, sin la capacidad de transporte adecuada, solo crea cuellos de botella.

Las inversiones estratégicas en subestaciones, corredores de transporte, modernización de la red y almacenamiento de energía determinarán si Washington podrá satisfacer las futuras demandas energéticas sin dejar de ofrecer precios asequibles y fiabilidad.
Estas prioridades son una de las razones por las que el año pasado tuve el honor de recibir el Premio al Defensor de las Infraestructuras de la Junta de Obras Públicas.

Este reconocimiento reflejaba años de trabajo apoyando inversiones en infraestructuras públicas que mejoran la calidad de vida, fortalecen las economías locales y preparan a las comunidades para el crecimiento futuro.
La infraestructura no se limita a carreteras y puentes, sino que incluye los sistemas energéticos que abastecen de energía a nuestros hogares, empresas, colegios y hospitales.

La nueva subestación de Winlock es un ejemplo de lo que se puede conseguir cuando las empresas de servicios públicos locales, los líderes comunitarios, las organizaciones de desarrollo económico y el gobierno estatal trabajan juntos por un objetivo común.
Es una inversión no solo en la fiabilidad de hoy, sino también en las oportunidades del mañana.
El futuro de Washington depende de que se mantenga un suministro eléctrico seguro, fiable y asequible.

Para ello, será necesario seguir invirtiendo en infraestructuras modernas de transporte de energía y contar con una política energética equilibrada que apueste por diversas fuentes de producción de energía, en lugar de depender de una sola tecnología.

Si planificamos con antelación y hacemos inversiones inteligentes en infraestructuras hoy, podemos asegurarnos de que Washington siga siendo un lugar donde las familias prosperen, las empresas inviertan y las comunidades sigan creciendo durante las próximas décadas.
Enhorabuena a Lewis PUD por su increíble trabajo.

Un Washington más fuerte Sobre Peter Cuestiones Artículos de interés LEGISLATURE VOTER INFO Blog de Peter DONATE Seguir Seguir Seguir Todas las elecciones son importantes, pero las elecciones primarias de 2026 son especialmente importantes para el futuro de nuestras comunidades y de nuestro estado.
Las decisiones que tomemos hoy ayudan a marcar el rumbo que tomará Washington mañana.
Si queremos… Familias más unidas.
Comunidades más unidas.
Un Washington más unido. , todo empieza con un gesto sencillo pero muy poderoso: votar.
Con demasiada frecuencia, las elecciones primarias las decide un pequeño porcentaje de los votantes con derecho a voto.
Eso significa que un puñado de votos puede marcar el futuro de millones de habitantes de Washington.
Tanto si tus prioridades son la asequibilidad, la seguridad pública, unas escuelas de calidad, unas infraestructuras fiables o el crecimiento de nuestra economía, tu opinión merece ser escuchada.
Animo a todos los votantes con derecho a voto a que rellenéis y enviéis vuestra papeleta en cuanto la recibáis.
Votar por adelantado ayuda a garantizar que se cuente tu voto, reduce los problemas de última hora y envía un mensaje claro de que los votantes de Washington están comprometidos y atentos.
Fechas importantes de las elecciones primarias de 2026 17 de julio: Se envían las papeletas por correo y empieza el periodo de votación de 18 días.
27 de julio: Fecha límite para inscribirse o actualizar los datos de votante por internet o por correo.
4 de agosto: Inscripción de votantes en persona y actualización de datos electorales disponibles hasta el día de las elecciones.
4 de agosto (20:# h): Día de las elecciones primarias.
Las papeletas deben depositarse en un buzón oficial antes de las 20:# h o tener matasellos de ese mismo día.
La democracia funciona mejor cuando los ciudadanos participan.
Cada voto representa una voz, una familia, un barrio y una comunidad a la que le importa el futuro de Washington.
Hagamos oír nuestra voz desde el principio, con fuerza y de forma respetuosa.

removed: top of page Chip in to Elect Randy CONTRIBUTE About Randy Issues Voting Guide Media Endorsements Get Involved Menu Close CONTRIBUTE ABOUT.
Randy Novak has spent his life serving the community he calls home.
A lifelong LaPorte County resident and graduate of Rogers High School, Randy didn’t set out to be a politician, he set out to be useful.
That instinct led him to a 33+ year career in public safety with the Michigan City Fire Department, where he rose through the ranks to become Fire Chief.
It was demanding work that required calm under pressure, teamwork, and accountability.
Values that still guide his leadership today. ​ Public service didn’t stop at the firehouse.

Randy went on to serve as President of the LaPorte County Council, where he helped oversee multimillion-dollar budgets, worked with department heads on long-term planning, and focused on responsible spending that delivered real results for taxpayers.
Whether it was public safety funding, infrastructure, or economic development, Randy approached every decision with a simple question: Does this make life better for the people who live here?
Alongside his public service, Randy has worked for more than 25 years as a licensed real estate broker in Indiana and Michigan.
That experience gave him a firsthand understanding of housing, local economies, and the challenges working families face when costs rise faster than paychecks.

He knows what it’s like to juggle responsibilities, stretch a dollar, and make long-term decisions with real consequences. ​ Randy has also remained deeply involved in the community beyond elected office.

Over the years, he has served as Chairman of the LaPorte County Fire Chiefs Association, President of the LaPorte County Redevelopment Commission, Vice President of the LaPorte County 911 Advisory Board, and on numerous boards focused on public safety, economic development, and community support.

He has long been an advocate for mental health and addiction recovery services, and he makes it a point to attend Problem-Solving Court and Veterans Court graduations because he believes second chances matter.
Family is at the center of Randy’s life.
He has been married to his wife, Debbie, for 46 years.
Together, they raised two sons in LaPorte County and now enjoy watching their four grandchildren grow up.

Randy is proud to say he’s missed only one County Council meeting in eight year, to be there for the birth of his grandson. ​ In October 2025, Randy was sworn in as State Representative for Indiana House District 9, representing Michigan City, northern LaPorte County, and parts of eastern Porter County.

He brings to the Statehouse the same approach he’s carried throughout his life: show up, listen, work hard, and treat people with respect. ​ Randy believes government works best when it is practical, transparent, and focused on improving quality of life.
He’s known for working across party lines, staying accessible to constituents, and keeping his word.
At a time when politics often feels disconnected from everyday life, Randy remains rooted in the community he’s always served and committed to making sure Indiana works for the people who live here.

added: 0 Skip to Content Meet Eric Priorities Get Involved Events Answers Newsroom CONTRIBUTE Open Menu Close Menu Meet Eric Priorities Get Involved Events Answers Newsroom CONTRIBUTE Open Menu Close Menu Meet Eric Priorities Get Involved Events Answers Newsroom CONTRIBUTE Questions Answered I’M LISTENING These are your questions — from town halls, from neighbors, from people online who wanted answers.
I’m here to serve you - openly and transparently.
These are my answers.

TOPICS Cost of Living • Healthcare • Housing • Water, Land, and Agriculture • PG&E, Wildfires, Energy & Climate • AI & Technology • Immigration • Corruption & Democracy • Veterans, Seniors, and Workers • Safety, Surveillance, Education, and Foreign Policy • Money and Independence • Experience • Eric’s Story • District Ties • Running Against the Establishment • Where Eric Stands • Campaign Conduct • Eric’s Opponent, Mike Thompson • Getting Involved Cost of Living What will Eric Jones do to lower the cost of living?
To lower the cost of living, Eric Jones will go after the root causes and pay for every dollar of it without new debt.
Here's the plan.
Cut taxes for working families.
End the federal income tax on the first $150,000 you earn.
That puts about $10,000 back in the pockets of working Californians and Americans.
Lower your power bills.
End Pacific Gas and Electric's (PG&E) monopoly, use every federal tool to cut what PG&E charges, end ratepayer-funded bailouts, and get lobbying off your bill.
Expand Medicare.
Cover vision, hearing, dental, and in-home care, and bring care into the home at 65, for everyone.
Lower drug costs.
Make generic drugs free, and let Medicare negotiate the price of newer drugs.
Make housing affordable.

Make rent tax-deductible, open a zero-down mortgage for first-time buyers through Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, create a National Housing Construction Bank, build 2 million homes a year, and cut the red tape that blocks local builders.
Protect our farms and the people who work them.
A farm workforce plan that protects workers from exploitation and lets growers hire legally, and lower energy costs for growers.
How it's paid for: by stopping corporate tax cheats, restoring fair corporate tax rates, and eliminating waste and fraud.
Never by borrowing.
And none of it works unless we get money out of politics.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
So he answers to you.
Does Eric Jones have a plan to address affordability?
Yes.
Eric Jones has a detailed plan to lower the cost of living, and every piece of it is paid for without new debt.
He would cut taxes for working families, take on PG&E to lower your power bills, expand Medicare, make generic drugs free, and make housing affordable.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living .
Does Eric Jones support cutting taxes for working families?
Yes.
Eric Jones is a Democrat running on a working-class tax cut.
He would end the federal income tax on the first $150,000 you earn, which puts about $10,000 back in the pockets of working Californians and Americans.
It's paid for by making corporate tax cheats pay what they already owe.
No new debt.
He will never cut Social Security, Medicare, veterans' services, or any program working families depend on.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
So he answers to working families.
Does Eric Jones want to cut or raise taxes?
Eric Jones wants to cut taxes for working Americans.
He would eliminate the federal income tax on the first $150,000 you earn, which puts about $10,000 back in the pockets of working Californians and Americans.
He pays for it by enforcing the corporate tax code, so corporate tax cheats finally pay what they owe.
No new borrowing.
Social Security and Medicare stay untouched.
How does Eric Jones pay for his proposals?
Eric Jones will never propose a policy without a plan to pay for it.
Every dollar is paid for, with no new debt.
We find the money three ways.
Crack down on corporate tax cheats.
End corporate welfare.
Cut the waste, fraud, and abuse that bleed the budget, starting with the price-gouged government contracts that can't survive a clean audit.
He will never cut Social Security, Medicare, veterans' services, or any program working families depend on.
What he would cut is corporate welfare and price-gouging in government contracts.
Getting money out of politics is how we make it stick.
That's why he takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Why should Eric Jones, a wealthy person, be trusted on affordability?
Eric Jones can be trusted on affordability because he has lived the struggle so many families are going through.
He grew up in poverty in rural Maine, with hundreds of thousands of dollars in medical debt.
He watched his dad cut pills in half to make them last longer.
He knew how to balance a budget as a kid, because he knew exactly how much money his family didn't have.
He fought with his mom over the thermostat because they couldn't afford the heating bill.
He knows education can change a life.
He knows hard work can and should be rewarded.
And he knows the American Dream is real and worth fighting to preserve for every family in this district.
Healthcare Does Eric Jones have a plan for healthcare?
Yes.
Eric Jones has a healthcare plan built on access.
He would expand Medicare to cover vision, hearing, dental, and in-home care, make generic drugs free, let Medicare negotiate prices, and protect Medicaid.
He supports Medicare for All as the goal, done the right way and fully paid for.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living/expand-medicare .
How would Eric Jones lower drug prices?
To lower drug prices, Eric Jones will make generic drugs free for everyone.
They're proven, and they cost almost nothing to make.
No American should pay out of pocket for one.
Let Medicare negotiate the price of newer drugs, the way every other wealthy country already does.
End the patent games drug companies use to block cheaper competition.
It largely pays for itself.
Free generics keep people out of far costlier emergency care, negotiation saves billions, and we close Big Pharma's tax loopholes.
Eric Jones takes no money from Big Pharma's PACs, no corporate PAC money, and no special interest money.
Will Eric Jones protect Medicaid?
Yes.
Eric Jones will protect Medicaid.
His family relied on Medicaid when he was growing up.
He knows exactly what it means to families in this district, and he will protect it.
What is Eric Jones's plan for rural hospitals and clinics?
Eric Jones's plan for rural hospitals and clinics is more federal funding for rural hospitals and a real focus on in-home care for seniors.
Rural hospitals are closing.
Bringing care to the patient, at home, lowers costs and improves care.
A nurse's visit instead of a 90-minute drive.
The pharmacy already in town instead of six specialists who never talk to each other.
That's the model he helped pilot with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS).
It's how we keep care close to home in every county of CA-4.
Does Eric Jones support Medicare for All?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports Medicare for All, and he believes every American deserves healthcare.
It has to be done the right way, though.
Any path to it must be fully paid for, honestly and without budget gimmicks, the same way he pays for every promise in this campaign.
Right now, Eric Jones is fighting the insurance and drug industries, and they are spending against him because they know he is a threat.
But watch the words.
Plenty of politicians say "Medicare for All." Many of them, especially the ones taking millions from the insurance lobby, clearly mean Medicare Advantage.
That's the one part of Medicare that hands huge profits to the insurance industry.
The real question for them is whether they would ever vote to take the insurance industry out of your healthcare.
Our current congressman has taken $1,819,641 from insurance PACs, more than any other California House Democrat.
Eric Jones knows Medicare doesn't cover enough: he will fight to expand it to cover vision, hearing, dental, and in-home care, and bring care into the home at 65, for everyone.
That's why we need to get money out of politics and elect a new generation of leadership.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Housing What is Eric Jones's housing plan?
Eric Jones's housing plan is to make housing affordable for renters and first-time buyers and to build more of it.
Make rent tax-deductible, the same kind of break homeowners already get.
Open the door to homeownership with a zero-down, fixed-rate mortgage for first-time buyers through Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.
It's modeled on the VA loan that has helped veterans buy homes for decades.
Add a first-time homebuyer tax credit for the closing costs and repairs that pile up around a purchase.
Create a National Housing Construction Bank to finance homes at scale, and build 2 million homes a year.
Cut the red tape and modernize permitting so local builders can build.
And get Wall Street and foreign money out of our neighborhoods.
It's paid for without new debt, by closing the speculation and corporate real-estate loopholes the biggest investors use.
Water, Land, and Agriculture Where does Eric Jones stand on California water policy?
Water is survival in an agricultural district.
On California water policy, Eric Jones will fully fund the projects our district has been waiting on, including Sites Reservoir in Colusa County.
Keep our water local and stop the corporate water grab: our water should serve the families, farms, and towns of this district first.
Invest in storage, delivery, and drought and flood resilience before the crisis hits.
And bring farmers and conservationists back to the same table, because both want water that lasts.
What will Eric Jones do for growers and winemakers?
For growers and winemakers, Eric Jones will write farm policy for the crops we actually grow.
Specialty crops like fruit, nuts, and wine grapes deserve real parity in the farm bill for research, pest and disease response, and market development.
Cut the energy bill that runs the pump, one of the biggest costs a grower can control.
Fix crop insurance so it works for vineyards and orchards, including losses from smoke, frost, and drought.
Break the chokehold of a few giant distributors in the middle of the wine business.
Give producers the right to exit a distribution agreement that isn't working, and let winemakers ship directly to the people who want to buy.
Does Eric Jones support protecting farmland from corporate and foreign buyers?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports protecting farmland from corporate and foreign buyers.
Our farmland should belong to the families who work it.
It should not be an asset for corporations or foreign investors to flip.
He'll work to limit corporate and foreign buy-ups of our farmland, and give local farmers the first shot at land that comes up for sale.
Does Eric Jones support or oppose California Forever?
Eric Jones strongly opposes California Forever.
Eric Jones has said so before, and he'll keep saying it.
Our farmland and our water should be protected.
Does Eric Jones support the H-2A farmworker visa program?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports the H-2A farmworker visa program, and he'll support expanding it once we fix it.
No expansion of the H-2A program until workforce housing and wage moderation concerns are resolved.
Workers have to be protected from exploitation.
Enforce the wage, safety, and housing laws already on the books, and strengthen monitoring against human trafficking and labor exploitation.
Make the program work for growers too, with one filing portal and a hard deadline for the government to answer.
Once those concerns are resolved, the program should extend to year-round work like dairies, packing houses, and nurseries.
PG&E, Wildfires, Energy & Climate What will Eric Jones do about PG&E?
Eric Jones will take PG&E on with every federal tool there is.
Some politicians say the federal government has no authority over utility rates.
That's not true: federal regulators set what PG&E earns on its high-voltage lines.
Here's his plan.
File a federal complaint to cut PG&E's profit rate on its high-voltage lines, and push for refunds.
Demand a federal audit of PG&E's books.
Pass a law: no executive bonuses in any year your rates rise faster than inflation.
Ask the Justice Department to review how PG&E treats towns that try to leave, and make it cheaper for towns to own their own power.
Write the first federal law against price gouging on power bills.
And put strings on PG&E's federal loan guarantee of up to $15 billion.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E, and he never will.
Our current congressman has taken $97,871 from PG&E's PAC, more than any other federal politician in American history.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living/end-pge-monopoly-lower-bills .
How will Eric Jones end PG&E's monopoly?
Eric Jones will end PG&E's monopoly by breaking it open and giving people a way out.
Use Congress's oversight and antitrust power to break the monopoly.
Push the Justice Department to review how PG&E blocks towns that try to leave.
Expand federal financing and support for municipal utilities and rural cooperatives, so it's cheaper for a town to buy its own power lines and run them as public power.
The Sacramento Municipal Utility District (SMUD), right next door, charges about half what PG&E does.
Half the price.
Challenge PG&E's federal profit rate, open its books, and put strings on its federal loan guarantee so the savings reach you.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E, and he never will.
Our current congressman has taken $97,871 from PG&E's PAC, more than any other federal politician in American history.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living/end-pge-monopoly-lower-bills .
How would Eric Jones lower utility bills?
To lower utility bills, Eric Jones will cut what PG&E charges you.
And break its monopoly.
Challenge PG&E's federal profit rate and push for refunds.
Get lobbying, trade-group dues, and political costs off your bill.
Make data centers pay their own grid costs.
End ratepayer-funded bailouts.
And make it cheaper for towns to own their power: SMUD, right next door and publicly owned, charges about half what PG&E does.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E, and he never will.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/lower-cost-of-living/end-pge-monopoly-lower-bills .
What will Eric Jones do about wildfire prevention and recovery?
On wildfire prevention and recovery, Eric Jones will use federal power to make PG&E pay for its failures.
You should never foot the bill.
Set federal wildfire safety standards for high-voltage lines, with penalties that make cutting corners cost more than doing the work.
Make sure customers never pay a utility's fines or legal bills.
End ratepayer-funded bailouts.
Write a law that lets federal judges keep repeat-offender utilities under supervision.
And put the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CalFire) and independent experts in charge of prevention, because a monopoly only has a reason to overspend.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E, and he never will.
No corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
What is Eric Jones's climate and environment agenda?
Eric Jones's climate and environment agenda is to protect our family farms, our land, and our water.
Eric Jones backs a bundle for rural California: federal grants for family farms, water infrastructure, replanting, and regenerative agriculture.
He'll back subsidies that help farmers replant with regenerative and sustainable agriculture, because what's good for the farmer and what's good for the land are the same thing.
He'll protect our water, and he supports a moratorium on new data centers in California.
After the moratorium, new data centers should be allowed only once every one of them generates its own clean, green energy on site.
AI and Technology Does Eric Jones have a plan to protect our future?
Yes.

Eric Jones has a plan to protect our future: strong rules for AI and Big Tech, a moratorium on new data centers in California, defending Social Security and Medicare, serving our veterans, securing our water, living within our means, ending the death and destruction of blank-check wars, and ending the surveillance state.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/protect-our-future .
What is Eric Jones's position on regulating AI?
Eric Jones's position on regulating AI is to regulate it.
And regulate it strongly.
AI must never be able to harm or kill people, and the people who control it must never be able to use it against us.
We have to protect the jobs we have and build the ones that come next.
That means strong, enforceable federal rules.
It means keeping kids off addictive social media and AI until 16, making Big Tech pay its fair share, and giving you ownership of your own data.
The biggest danger is a handful of companies owning this technology and buying the government too.
That's why it matters that he takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money, including nothing from Big Tech's PACs.
His full plan is on the Make Big Tech Build Responsibly page at ericjones.us/priorities/protect-our-future/make-big-tech-build-responsibly .
What will Eric Jones do about AI and jobs?
On AI and jobs, Eric Jones will protect the jobs we have and build the ones that come next.
That's why we have to regulate AI strongly now, before a handful of companies decide our future without us.
Give workers real notice and a real say before a machine takes their place.
Make the corporations profiting most from automation pay for union-powered training, so workers in this district are ready for the jobs that come next.
It also takes people in Congress who don't take money from Big Tech.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
So he can stand up for workers and families in CA-4 instead of the companies building AI.
Will Eric Jones hold the tech industry accountable?
Yes.
Eric Jones is running to regulate Big Tech and hold it accountable.
He supports strong federal rules on AI and a moratorium on new data centers in California.
He'll keep kids off addictive social media and AI until 16, make Big Tech pay its fair share in taxes, and give you ownership of your own data.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money, including nothing from Big Tech's PACs.
Does Eric Jones support a moratorium on new data centers in California?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports a moratorium on new data centers in California.
No more of them here.
Data centers use enormous amounts of electricity and water.
Families shouldn't pay higher power bills or lose water so Big Tech can build.
He wants a federal moratorium that holds until there are strong national standards.
On-site clean power kept off our grid, strict limits on water use, and protections for jobs.
Big Tech should pay its own way.
The cost should never land on you.
Does Eric Jones's data center moratorium cover all of California?
Yes.
The whole state.
The data center moratorium Eric Jones is fighting for would cover the entire state of California, every district included.
It would hold until there are strong national standards: on-site clean power kept off the grid, strict water limits, and job protections.
Where does Eric Jones stand on data centers using our water and power?
Eric Jones is against data centers taking our water and power.
Our water and our power should serve the families, farms, and towns of this district first.
That's why he supports a moratorium on new data centers in California, held until there are strong national standards.
On-site clean power kept off the grid, strict water limits, and job protections.
You shouldn't pay higher bills or lose water so Big Tech can build.
Does Eric Jones take money from data centers or support building them?
No on both counts.
Eric Jones takes no money from the data center companies.
His position is simple.
No more data centers in California.
He supports a federal moratorium on new data centers until there are real national standards.
On-site clean power that stays off our grid, strict limits on water use, and protections for jobs.
Our water and our power should serve the families, farms, and towns of this district first.
Have Eric Jones's views on data centers changed or flip-flopped?
No.
His position hasn't changed.
It's clear: California is not the place for data centers, and there should be no more of them here.
He supports a federal moratorium on new data centers until we have strong national standards, including on-site clean power kept off the grid, strict water limits, and job protections.
His focus is on the immediate risk to this district and on stopping new data centers now.
He has always believed in strong federal regulation for AI, done in a way that protects our bills, our water, our jobs, and our future.
Can California regulate AI, or should only the federal government?
Eric Jones believes California can and should regulate AI, and that the country needs one strong federal framework underneath it.
The federal rules should set a floor every company has to meet, and states like California should be free to go further.
What Washington should not do is loosen the rules in a way that undermines California's stronger protections.
Eric Jones takes no money from Big Tech's PACs, so he is free to write those rules for the people of CA-4.
Is AI or tech money behind Eric Jones's campaign?
No.
AI and tech money are not behind Eric Jones's campaign.
People's money is.
Every dollar comes from individuals and from his own family, and he rejects all corporate PAC money.
Compare that to our current congressman.
Across his career, he has taken $143,624 from technology PACs, including the PACs of Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta, the companies building, funding, and profiting from AI.
Microsoft is OpenAI's biggest backer, and Amazon and Google are the biggest investors in Anthropic.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
What is Eric Jones's position on California Forever?
Eric Jones strongly opposes California Forever.
Our farmland and our water should be protected, and he'll keep standing with the farmers and families of this region.
Would Eric Jones support a project like California Forever in CA-4?
No.
Eric Jones would oppose a project like California Forever in our district.
Immigration What is Eric Jones's position on immigration?
Eric Jones's position on immigration is that a strong border and compassionate reform are not opposites.
We need both, and security comes first.
Secure the border, with a hard focus on fentanyl, human trafficking, and organized smuggling.
Violent criminals and anyone who preys on children should be removed immediately, and the Justice Department is exactly who should do it.
Return immigration enforcement to the Justice Department, where it lived until 2003.
So the law is enforced by the people meant to enforce it.
Then fix what's broken.
Modernize the visa system, clear the backlogs, and create an earned path to legal status for people who have been here for years, working and paying taxes.
Protect the farm workers our agriculture depends on, and let growers hire legally.
Hold Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) accountable, and keep families together.
Our farms do not run without immigrant labor, and both parties' establishments have left this broken for decades.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money and no special interest money, and he'd rather fix this than keep it as a campaign issue.
Corruption and Democracy What does Eric Jones mean by ending corruption?
When Eric Jones talks about ending corruption, he means getting money out of politics and ending career politics, starting with term limits.
Term limits: 12 years, for everyone in Congress.
Eric Jones has already signed a 12-year term limit pledge.
Public service shouldn't be a 28-year career.
Ban members of Congress from trading stocks , and put conflicts of interest in the daylight in real time.
Ban corporate PAC money and special interest money.
He takes none, and he never will.
Overturn Citizens United.
Close the revolving door between Congress and lobbying, and give the ethics rules real teeth.
End partisan gerrymandering , everywhere.
End the corruption, and we can lower costs.
Lower costs, and we can protect the future our kids deserve.
Term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, and an end to gerrymandering: that's where it starts.
Does Eric Jones have a plan to fight corruption?
Yes.
Fighting corruption is at the center of Eric Jones's campaign.
He backs term limits, a ban on members of Congress trading stocks, an end to gerrymandering, and overturning Citizens United.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
The full plan is at ericjones.us/priorities/fight-corruption .
Does Eric Jones support term limits?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports term limits: 12 years for every member of Congress, and he has already signed a 12-year pledge for himself.
He'll cosponsor a constitutional amendment for term limits, and when his time is up, he'll hand the seat back to the people.
He will not pick a successor to inherit it.
Nobody should earn a lifetime appointment in Congress just for showing up.
Does Eric Jones support a congressional stock trading ban?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports banning members of Congress from trading stocks.
It's legalized insider trading, and he'll ban it.
Eric Jones has already sold every publicly traded stock he owned.
Where does Eric Jones stand on gerrymandering, including in California?
Eric Jones would ban all partisan gerrymandering, everywhere, in every state, red and blue.
He is not ashamed of supporting Prop 50.
He backed it as a necessary response to the gerrymandering effort in Texas.
What he hated was how the Democratic establishment carried it out, holding it over the heads of the very voters it was disenfranchising.
Redrawing a map to cancel people's representation should be treated as a solemn duty, not a celebratory parade.
That's why he wants independent redistricting commissions in every state, California included, and a ban on mid-decade redistricting everywhere.
How would Eric Jones reduce the national debt and the deficit?
To reduce the national debt and the deficit, Eric Jones would make the people who aren't paying their share pay it.
The national debt has passed $37 trillion, and the interest alone now costs more than our entire military.
He pays for it by enforcing the corporate tax code, so corporate tax cheats finally pay what they already owe.
End corporate welfare.
Cut the waste, fraud, and abuse in federal contracts.
He will never cut Social Security, Medicare, veterans' services, or any program working families depend on.
And he will never propose a policy without a plan to pay for it.
Does Eric Jones support cutting government waste, fraud, and abuse?
Yes.
Eric Jones supports cutting government waste, fraud, and abuse.
There's real money being wasted, and most of it isn't where politicians point.
It's in price-gouged government contracts that can't survive a clean audit.
It's in outright fraud: hospice billing schemes, benefits still going out to people who have died, and bad actors at home and abroad charging the government for services that were never delivered.
And it's in the subsidies and carve-outs written for the largest corporations.
Cutting it is how we pay for lower costs without new debt.
And the contracts stay corrupt for one reason: the contractors fund the politicians.
That's why getting money out of politics matters, and why he takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Does Eric Jones support sunsetting federal programs?
No.
Eric Jones does not support sunsetting federal programs.
Not the VA.

He believes in an idealized version of the Democratic Party: one that works to maximize economic opportunity for the most people, and maximize liberty for the most people.
Right now, he believes both parties are failing at that.
That's why we need a new generation of leadership that takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Has Eric Jones always been a Democrat?
Yes.
Eric Jones has always been a registered Democrat.
He is also an independent politician running against the Democratic establishment, because he believes his party has lost its way.
Is Eric Jones a progressive or a moderate?
Eric Jones is an anti-establishment candidate and an independent politician.
He doesn't take orders from party bosses or from donors.
He takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
So he is free to do what's right for CA-4: get money out of politics, fight corruption, lower the cost of living, and protect our future.
That means the reforms voters of every party want: term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, and an end to gerrymandering.
Is Eric Jones a Democratic Socialist?
No.
Eric Jones is not a Democratic Socialist, and he is not a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).
Is Eric Jones a communist?
No.
Eric Jones is not a communist, and he condemns communism.
Does Eric Jones condemn communism?
Yes.
Eric Jones condemns communism.
He is not a communist and never has been.
Why did Republican and independent primary candidates endorse Eric Jones?
Republican and independent primary candidates endorsed Eric Jones because they know he will work to best serve the voters in this district.
They're also frustrated that our current congressman is one of the least effective members of Congress, with little to show for nearly 30 years.
They know he'll be mindful of the debt, cut taxes for working people, work to get money out of politics, fix corruption, lower costs, protect our future, and take on PG&E.
All of his Republican and independent opponents in the primary have endorsed him.
These aren't Democratic or Republican values.
They're the values of CA-4.
What did Eric Jones commit to when a Republican candidate endorsed him?
When a Republican candidate endorsed him, Eric Jones committed to the same things he'd commit to with any voter.
Ray Riehle, the top Republican vote-getter in the primary, asked him to prioritize fiscal discipline and investment in local infrastructure, and he agreed.
Eric Jones is mindful of the national debt.
It's an urgent issue, and he cares about it.

As he said when Ray endorsed him: "I made commitments to Ray that I intend to keep, because they are the same commitments I would make to any voter in this district." Putting this district ahead of special interests.
Public debates.
No lobbyist money.
Has Eric Jones changed his positions?
No.
Eric Jones hasn't changed his positions.
He has expanded them.
His website now explains 27 policy positions in detail, with more than 50,000 words on where he stands and why.
When voters have given him feedback, the campaign has edited to make the language clearer, and he'll always listen to make sure his words match his intentions.
His positions have stayed consistent: get money out of politics, fight corruption, lower the cost of living, and protect our future.
And he takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Why has Eric Jones's website changed?
Eric Jones's website has changed because he has expanded it.
His website now has 27 detailed policy pages, with far more depth and clarity on every position.
More than 50,000 words on where he stands and why.

The positions are the same: get money out of politics, fight corruption, lower the cost of living, and protect our future, with no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Does Eric Jones say different things to different audiences?
No.
Eric Jones does not say different things to different audiences.
His message is consistent and public, here on his website and across his social media.
He talks with voters about their own priorities and looks for common ground, because that's what a representative should do.
You can't walk into a room of farmers and talk about space.
So he talks with growers about agriculture, with winemakers about wine, and with young families about the cost of living and housing.
The message never changes: get money out of politics, fight corruption, lower the cost of living, and protect our future, with no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Campaign Conduct Who runs Eric Jones's campaign, and are any of them lobbyists?
Eric Jones's campaign is run by a team drawn from anti-establishment leaders in both parties, and none of them are lobbyists.
Not now, not ever.
Just like his money, his team answers to the people of CA-4.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Does Eric Jones use AI-generated media in his ads?
No.
Eric Jones does not use AI-generated media in his ads.
They feature Eric Jones, real actors, real props, and classic animation.
Does Eric Jones run negative ads?
Eric Jones went on the air with contrast ads only after his opponent went negative, with lies and false accusations.
Eric responded with his opponent's record.
Just the record.
There's a bigger reason, too.
For the first time in nearly 30 years, our current congressman has a real opponent, and voters finally get to see his record side by side with a choice.
Telling you who funds him, and what he has and hasn't done in Washington, isn't a personal attack.
It's information voters deserve.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
So he can tell you the truth about that record with no donor holding the other end of the leash.
Will Eric Jones debate our current congressman?
Yes, and Eric Jones asked for many more.
He called for a full series of 9 real debates across CA-4, so voters could see the choice for themselves.
Our current congressman agreed to exactly one: a single 30-minute debate.
After nearly 30 years in the seat, the people of this district deserve far more than half an hour to see the two candidates answer for their records side by side.
Did Eric Jones approve of a volunteer going to Rep.
Mike Thompson's home?
No.
Eric Jones did not know about it, and he would never condone it.
As soon as he found out, he ensured this behavior ended and the campaign took action immediately.
He immediately took responsibility and apologized publicly in the Napa Valley Register.
This campaign is about ideas and the future of this district.
Eric’s Opponent, Mike Thompson Who is Eric Jones's opponent?
Eric Jones's opponent is Rep.
Mike Thompson, the Democrat who has held this seat since 1999 and has sat on the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee since 2005.
This is the first time in nearly 30 years he has faced a serious challenge.
It's the first time in nearly 30 years voters get a real look at his record.
How much money has Mike Thompson taken from PG&E?
Mike Thompson has taken $97,871 from PG&E's PAC over his career, the most of any federal politician in American history.
He has taken PG&E money in every one of the 15 election cycles of his career.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E.
Not ever.
(Source: Federal Election Commission (FEC), PG&E Corporation Employees ENERGYPAC, C00177469.) Did Mike Thompson keep taking PG&E's money after its crimes?
Yes.
After PG&E pleaded guilty in 2020 to 84 counts of involuntary manslaughter for the Camp Fire, Mike Thompson kept taking its money, $29,519 more, with the first check arriving 43 days after the plea.
He also kept taking PG&E's money after its 2016 federal felony conviction, and after the 2017 wildfires that killed dozens of people in his own district.
Eric Jones takes nothing from PG&E, and he never will.
(Source: FEC filings, and PG&E's guilty plea, U.S.
District Court, 2020.) How much PAC money has Mike Thompson taken?
More than half of every dollar Mike Thompson has ever raised came from a PAC, over $14.5 million across his career.
Among California's House Democrats running for re-election, no one has taken more PAC money than he has.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money, and he never will.
That's the whole difference: one of them answers to the PACs, and one of them answers to you.
(Source: FEC, all cycles 1998–2026.) Is Mike Thompson funded by corporations and special interests?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken more corporate PAC money than any other Democrat in California's House delegation.
He has taken $1,819,641 from insurance PACs, more than any other California House Democrat.
He has also taken $470,110 from pharmaceutical PACs and $143,624 from technology PACs, including Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta, the companies building, funding, and profiting from AI.
Eric Jones takes none of it.
(Source: FEC filings.) Has Mike Thompson taken money from data center companies?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken technology PAC money from Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Meta, four of the largest data center builders in the country.
That money has risen every cycle.
Their data centers are a big reason power demand and electric bills keep climbing in California.
Eric Jones supports a moratorium on new data centers until each one generates its own clean power on site, and he takes nothing from these companies.
One candidate takes the data center money.
The other wants the data centers to stop raising your bills.
(Source: FEC filings.) Has Mike Thompson taken money from Big Tech?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken $143,624 from technology PACs over his career, including Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta, and that money has risen every cycle.
Eric Jones takes nothing from Big Tech's PACs.
(Source: FEC filings.) Has Mike Thompson taken money from AI companies?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken technology PAC money from Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta.
They are the companies building, funding, and profiting from AI.
Microsoft is the biggest backer of OpenAI, and Amazon and Google are the biggest investors in Anthropic.
Eric Jones takes nothing from them.
(Source: FEC filings.) Has Mike Thompson taken money from Big Pharma?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken $470,110 from pharmaceutical PACs over his career.
Eric Jones takes nothing from the drug industry, which is how he can fight to make generic drugs free and let Medicare negotiate prices.
(Source: FEC filings.) Has Mike Thompson taken money from the insurance industry?
Yes.
Mike Thompson has taken $1,819,641 from insurance PACs, more than any other California House Democrat.
Eric Jones takes nothing from the insurance industry.
(Source: FEC filings.) What has Mike Thompson actually passed in Congress?
Since 2007, the only bills Mike Thompson has authored and signed into law are six post office renamings and one congressional gold medal.
He has sat on the committee that writes the nation's tax code since 2005.
He ranks near the bottom of the House in federal money brought back to this district.
(Source: Congress.gov and federal spending data.) Has Mike Thompson only named post offices?
Just about.
Since 2007, the only bills Mike Thompson has authored and gotten signed into law are six post office renamings and one congressional gold medal, which he handed out in 2020.
That is the whole list from nearly two decades on the committee that writes the nation's tax code.
You can check it yourself on Congress.gov , filtered to bills he sponsored that became law.
(Source: Congress.gov .) Is it true that Mike Thompson brings back less federal money to his district than his peers?
Yes.
Mike Thompson brings back less federal money to this district than his neighbors do.
Federal spending data shows this district has received billions of dollars less since the 2022 redistricting than California's 1st, 2nd, and 3rd districts, parts of which are now folded into CA-4.
After nearly 30 years in Washington, this district still ranks near the bottom for money brought home.
(Source: USAspending.gov , federal awards excluding Social Security.) How is it determined that Mike Thompson brings back less money to his district than his peers?
It comes from federal spending data.
The measure is the federal money that actually reaches a district: contracts, grants, and direct federal awards, pulled from USAspending.gov .
It excludes Social Security, because those benefits are paid to individuals everywhere no matter who holds the seat.
So the comparison reflects the dollars a member of Congress actually helps steer home.
By that measure, this district trails its neighbors by billions since the 2022 maps took effect.
(Source: USAspending.gov , federal awards excluding Social Security.) Is Mike Thompson an effective member of Congress?
No.
Mike Thompson ranks near the bottom of Congress, and near the bottom among California's members, in the Center for Effective Lawmaking's rankings.
He also ranks below his peers in federal money brought back to his district.
That counts the contracts, grants, and awards a member actually helps steer home, setting aside Social Security, which is paid everywhere no matter who holds the seat.
Nearly 30 years in Washington, and very little to show for it.
(Source: Center for Effective Lawmaking, and USAspending.gov .) How long has Mike Thompson been in Washington?
Mike Thompson has been in Congress since 1999, nearly 30 years.
Eric Jones has signed a 12-year term limit pledge, because public service should be a duty.
It was never meant to be a career.
Nobody should earn a lifetime appointment just for showing up.
How does Eric Jones source his data on Mike Thompson?
It comes straight from the government's own public records.
Campaign finance comes from the Federal Election Commission ( FEC.gov ).
The legislative record comes from Congress.gov .
Federal money brought back to the district comes from USAspending.gov .
When Eric compares what a member brings home, he sets Social Security aside, since it is paid to people everywhere no matter who represents them.
That way, the number reflects what a member actually helps deliver.
Does Eric Jones use misleading data about Mike Thompson?
No.
Eric Jones uses only public government records, from FEC.gov , Congress.gov , and USAspending.gov .
When he measures federal money brought home, he sets Social Security aside on purpose.
It is paid to people everywhere regardless of their representative, so the comparison is apples to apples.
Despite what you may read in a letter to the editor, the numbers come straight from the government's own sites.
Getting Involved How can I volunteer for Eric Jones?
You can volunteer for Eric Jones at ericjones.us/volunteer.
You can make calls, knock doors, put up a lawn sign, or join the campaign's student fellowship.
How can I donate to Eric Jones?
You can donate to Eric Jones at ericjones.us by clicking Contribute.
Every dollar comes from individual people, and the campaign accepts no corporate PAC money, no special interest money, and no foreign money.
Who has endorsed Eric Jones?
Eric Jones has earned an unusually broad coalition.
It spans local leaders from both the left and the right, elected officials and grassroots activists alike, a handful of voices from across California, and a building trades union.
That starts with all of his Republican and independent opponents from the primary, led by Ray Riehle, the top Republican vote-getter.
His endorsements also include local progressive leaders and activists, and Democratic and nonpartisan officials in Petaluma and elsewhere in California.
They include Republican elected officials in Yuba and Sutter counties, former local party chairs from around the district, and groups like Our Revolution and Indivisible Yolo.
We're also proud to be backed by the Pipefitters and Steamfitters, a building trades union.
How can I contact Eric Jones's campaign or invite Eric to an event?
You can contact Eric Jones's campaign or invite Eric to an event by emailing info@ericjones.us .
For press inquiries, email press@ericjones.us .
Where can I find Eric Jones's upcoming events?
All of Eric Jones's upcoming town halls and events are at ericjones.us/events .

added.text: California State Senator Angelique Ashby knows fir [image: California State Senator Angelique Ashby knows firsthand the challenges working families face. A former single mom who worked her way through college and law school, she went on to serve 12 years on the Sacramento City Council before making history as the first woman elected to represent Sacramento in the State Senate in more than 20 years! Representing Senate District 8, Angelique has focused on affordable housing, education, public safety, economic opportunity, and supporting women and children experiencing homelessness. Thank you, Senator Ashby, for your dedication to public service and the Sacramento region! #AngeliqueAshby #CaliforniaStateSenate #Sacramento #WomenInLeadership #PublicService #WorkingFamilies #California @angeliqueashby @senatorashby]

Senator Durazo has spent her life fighting for working families. From the labor movement to the State Senate, she has been a powerful voice for her district and for communities across Los Angeles. I’m honored to stand with her. Now it’s on us. Election Day is November 3. Make a plan: mail in your ballot, drop it at a ballot box, or head to a vote center.
