(The weather is supposed to be GREAT!) 1 Oct Tuesday, 1:39 PM · 2024 Supporting Our Heroes Connecticut's law enforcement officers and first responders work in unique occupations.
When they leave for their shift, the loved ones they left at home do not know if they will ever return alive or in what shape.
They risk their safety daily to ensure ours.
In short, they are our HEROES, and I'm proud to support them with the resources they require to perform their duties safely and effectively.
As your representative, I've worked to take care of the needs of our law enforcement and first responders.

I've supported legislation to give law enforcement agencies flexibility when dealing with emergencies, led the fight to correct our “use of force” statute, helped pass legislation holding criminals more accountable if they are found to have intentionally hurt or killed a canine officer, helped pass legislation creating a fallen officers fund to support the families of officers tragically killed in the line of duty, and helped pass legislation expanding the ability of local police and fire chiefs to declare line-of-duty deaths as a result of an emergency.
26 Sep Thursday, 1:21 PM · 2024 Fighting for Tax Relief for Families and Small Businesses I'm proud of my record of delivering tax relief to Connecticut families and small businesses.
With inflation high and the cost of consumer goods continuing to rise, you deserve a break from the government reaching into your wallet.
It is my belief that government should operate within its means, and not place the burden of unnecessary excess on the backs of hardworking families and entrepreneurs.
Taxes should cover essential state and community needs, not pet projects or political favors.

Senator Catherine Cortez Masto Endorses Attorney General Aaron Ford for Governor Oct 16 2026 PRESS RELEASE The American Prospect: AG Ford Focuses on Working-class, Promises to Expand Affordability “[Ford has] the only 2026 platform I know of that features a promise to repeal his state’s “right-to-work” law.” A new deep dive by The American Prospect highlights how the Nevada Governor’s race is a contest between a working-class champion in Aaron Ford and a doormat for Trump and his “billionaire friends” in Joe Lombardo.

The reporting emphasizes how Ford is focusing his campaign on lowering the sky-high costs Nevadans are paying for gas, groceries, and housing in the Lombardo-Trump economy, while Lombardo hides behind debunked attack ads to mask his record of raising Nevadans’ costs.
The American Prospect also details Ford’s strength among unions.
READ MORE The American Prospect : Can Nevada Democrats Roll a Trifecta?
Ford is campaigning on working-class economic themes that stand out, even amidst all the other such campaigns that Democrats are waging across the nation this fall.

Ford’s attacks on Lombardo center on the governor’s opposition to policies that would make life in Nevada more affordable, like his support for subsidies to data centers and his vetoes of bills passed by the Democratic legislature.

This includes bills that would have capped the cost of prescription drugs at levels negotiated, or to be negotiated, by Medicare; provided paid family leave to Nevada workers; prohibited private equity and big banks from the mass purchase and ownership of housing; and established universal free breakfasts and lunches for K-12 schoolchildren.
Lombardo’s campaign, by contrast, doesn’t focus on policy very much.
Rather it’s rooted in attacks on Ford, less for the policies he’s supported than for what it claims are Ford’s self-interested and alien-to-Nevada priorities.
Ford is not only running on a working-class platform; he also touts his working-class roots.
When he was growing up in Houston, he told the Teamsters, “My dad [who worked at a supermarket] brought home old, unsold candy bars for me to eat.
I was no highfalutin rich kid with a silver spoon in my mouth.
We didn’t even have a spoon.” DURING HIS MEETING WITH THE TEAMSTERS, one member asked Ford what his “three top issues” would be if he became governor.
“I have only one top issue,” he replied.
“Affordability.
We have to deal simultaneously with housing costs, the price of health care, and utility bills.
We ain’t got the time to go one at a time.” ### Powered by RUN! website builder Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.

added: Home About Cal Events News On the Issues Photo Gallery Contact News / 2021 Statehouse Report #16 27 Mar Sunday, 6:57 PM · 2022 2021 Statehouse Report #16 n the House In recent weeks, I have reported to you about a bill by Representative Tommy Pope that allows law enforcement to receive worker’s compensation for PTSD and other stress-related mental illnesses caused by traumatic events while on duty.
This week, we added firefighters to the bill, which then passed the House.
This is a great effort to take care of our law enforcement and first responders, and I was proud to vote in favor of this bill.
It’s Electric!

This week, the House passed a group of incentives to help drivers of electric vehicles by ensuring that when they produce electricity, they are not considered to be a utility, as the law currently states.

We passed an amendment that creates a study committee to investigate aspects of electric vehicles such as the reliability of the grid system, electricity security, and the impact of electric cars on infrastructure, bridges, and roads.
Tuition Rates for Veterans Currently, a veteran can enroll in a public institution of higher education within 3 years after the veteran's discharge and receive educational assistance.
Our veterans deserve better!
I was proud to support S.
241 this week, which eliminates the time requirements for South Carolina’s veterans to receive a reduced tuition rate for higher education.
This unanimously passed the House.
Other Legislative News S.
685 - This bill allows college athletes to be compensated for the use of their name, image, or likeness.
This passed the House by a vote of 103-15.
H.3591 - This bill requires every educator preparation program to publish a report card that details how the program is preparing their student teachers for success in the classroom.
The report card must include a variety of data that provides a comprehensive picture of how well each educator preparation program prepares effective educators and meets state goals.
This passed by a vote of 110-1.
On the Governor’s Desk: Education Reform This year is a year full of education reforms.
Although improving our schools is always a top priority, the pandemic has highlighted the urgency of many educational issues.
This week, the Governor signed a bill that originated in the House, sponsored by Representative Rita Allison.
I voted in favor of this bill and I am glad the Governor signed it into law.
This bill is important, as it allows for more “Schools of Innovation'' to arise around the state, giving students more opportunities to succeed.

The House also received Representative Sylleste Davis’ bill back from the Senate, which allows Palmetto Fellow Scholarship recipients to use their scholarship at a Technical College (which is currently not allowed).
The House sent the bill to the Governor’s desk and it takes effect upon his signature.
In Case you Missed It!
On Wednesday night President Biden addressed Congress in a joint session to review what has happened in his first 100 days of presidency.
Directly after, our Senator, Tim Scott gave the Republican response.
As a former member of the South Carolina House Republican Caucus, Senator Scott explained our Republican values on a personal level, bringing a message of hope and unity to the American people.
Thank you Senator Scott for your leadership and honorable representation of South Carolina.
I'm at your service!
It is my honor to be of service to you and to serve District 39.

If you need assistance navigating through the flow of information on COVID-19, navigating state government, or have any thoughts or concerns about what we are doing, please do not hesitate to contact me.

added: Home About Cal Events News On the Issues Photo Gallery Contact News / 2021 Statehouse Report # 17 27 Mar Sunday, 7:01 PM · 2022 2021 Statehouse Report # 17 BREAKING NEWS: SC Returns to Pre-Pandemic Unemployment Program In order to address ongoing workforce shortages throughout South Carolina, Governor Henry McMaster directed the S.C.
Department of Employment and Workforce to discontinue South Carolina’s participation in all federal, pandemic-related unemployment benefit programs.
This takes effect June 30, 2021.
There are currently 81,684 open positions in the state of South Carolina.
With this, I am hopeful South Carolinians will be encouraged to get back to work.

Read more here: https://governor.sc.gov/ news/2021-05/south-carolina- return-pre-pandemic- unemployment-program-address- workforce-shortages Week at a Glance We are edging closer to the Sine Die deadline, with just one week left to-go.
We wasted no time this week, taking up some of our state’s most pressing issues, such as Santee Cooper, the death penalty, and bringing new business to South Carolina.
As we move into next week, I am excited to finish strong after a very successful year of conservative legislation.
As always, it is an honor to serve our district and if you have any questions about what we are doing in Columbia, feel free to contact me.
Cheers!
Gallo Wine Comes to SC Wine connoisseurs and business communities alike are saying ‘cheers!’ this week, as we passed S.
This bill alters our state’s archaic liquor laws and will allow for standalone tasting rooms and fewer regulations on micro-distilleries in SC.
A huge success for SC, this bill ushers in a major, international economic player and world-wide wine brand to South Carolina.
E & J Gallo Winery will invest over half a billion dollars and 500 jobs in Chester County, SC where they plan to build their winery.
I look forward to seeing how our state and local economies will grow because of this new law.
When Lethal Injection Supply is Low...

Under current law, those convicted of a heinous crime and sentenced to death, are likely to spend the rest of their life waiting on death row due to the lack of availability of lethal injection materials.
Not only is justice not being served for the victims and their families, but State resources are being wasted.
This week, the House passed S.
200, a bill that allows electrocution when lethal injection is not available.
The firing squad was also added into the bill, as we work to find the most humane and quick way to serve justice.
I supported this bill, which passed on Wednesday.

Once and For All: Santee Cooper The issue of reforming Santee Cooper has been ongoing for years, and this week, the House passed amendments on a bill that outlines reform, governance, and a sale process.
This ensures that there is transparency and accountability in the agency -- ensuring that every ‘i’ is dotted and each ‘t’ is crossed.
This bill prescribes a process for how the agency should operate, allowing for oversight from the government and transparency for ratepayers.

Although there is no offer on the table from a buyer right now, it is important that we do not tie our hands and limit future possibilities, which is why there is also a sale amendment that outlines how that process might work.
We passed this on Tuesday, but our amendments were rejected by the Senate.
The bill will now go to a conference committee, where members of the House and Senate will meet to find compromise on the issue.
Other Legislative News S.

231 Suicide Prevention Hotline - We passed a bill that ensures the National Suicide Hotline is printed on school issued student ID cards in public schools and public and private colleges in South Carolina.
S.
689 Income Tax Filing Deadline - On Wednesday, the House passed a joint resolution to extend the income tax filing due date until the same date as federal returns and payments are due.
I'm at your service!
It is my honor to be of service to you and to serve District 39.

If you need assistance navigating through the flow of information on COVID-19, navigating state government, or have any thoughts or concerns about what we are doing, please do not hesitate to contact me.

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Event A Stolen Life: Teresa Fox October 10 Tacoma Event to Honor Victims, Law Enforcement and the Families Left Behind On October 10 in Tacoma, Teresa Fox and Agnes Gibboney will stand with ICE, honor victims and the families left behind, and recognize the law-enforcement officers who continue to serve.
October 10, 2026 Campaign Staff For Every Name on a Cross.
For Every Mother Who Buried a Child.
For Every Agent Who Still Does the Job.
On Saturday, October 10, congressional candidate Teresa Fox will stand with victims, their families and federal law-enforcement officers at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma.
Joining Fox will be Angel Mom Agnes Gibboney, founder of Angel Families of America and the mother of Ronald da Silva.
A STOLEN LIFE Ronald was 29 years old when he was shot and killed in 2002 while standing in a driveway with a friend.

His mother later testified before Congress that the man who killed Ronald had previously been deported from the United States and returned. https://docs.house.gov/meetings/GO/GO06/20170427/105888/HHRG-115-GO06-Transcript-20170427.pdf For more than two decades, Angel Mom Agnes Gibboney has carried her son’s story across the country, advocating for victims, their families, immigration enforcement and public safety.
The Federation for American Immigration Reform preserved Ronald’s story in the video A Stolen Life: The Ronald da Silva Story.
WATCH A STOLEN LIFE: THE RONALD DA SILVA STORY https://www.fairus.org/media/10476 Ronald’s story is one reason October 10 matters.
Behind every immigration statistic, every political argument and every policy debate are real people.
There are victims whose lives cannot be restored.
There are mothers, fathers, children and families who live permanently with what was taken from them.
And there are law-enforcement officers who continue to report for duty every day to enforce the laws of the United States.
Ronald da Silva’s story has been documented in California Globe coverage and in FAIR’s A Stolen Life: The Ronald da Silva Story.
STAND WITH ICE The October 10 gathering is unapologetically in support of ICE and the men and women of law enforcement.
It is also a day to remember victims and to give their families a voice.
Fox and those gathering in Tacoma will honor lives lost, stand beside families left behind and recognize the federal officers who continue doing a difficult and increasingly politicized job.
The purpose is not simply to discuss immigration as an abstract political issue.
It is to remember who bears the consequences when federal immigration laws are not enforced.
OCTOBER 10 IN TACOMA A separately organized demonstration opposing ICE activity is also scheduled in Tacoma that afternoon.
Organizers of that march have announced plans to gather near the Puyallup Tribe Administration Building before marching to the detention center.

The demonstration is being organized by individual tribal and community members and is not an official event of the Puyallup Tribal government. https://www.kiro7.com/news/local/organizers-announce-another-ice-out-be-held-tacoma-oct-10/RZD2GEW325FIRFVH3SO4HBMB4E/ ] With both gatherings taking place on October 10, Tacoma will become a focal point for a national debate over immigration enforcement, public safety, federal law enforcement and the responsibilities of Congress.
Fox believes that debate should be open, peaceful and substantive.

AN OPEN INVITATION TO CONGRESSWOMAN EMILY RANDALL Teresa Fox is publicly inviting Congresswoman Emily Randall, the incumbent representative for Washington’s 6th Congressional District, to attend and engage in a civil, substantive discussion.
Randall has herself focused publicly on the Northwest ICE Processing Center, including raising concerns about the treatment of "brown people" and conditions at the facility.
Fox welcomes the opportunity for the two candidates to discuss these issues for the first time this campaign, directly and civilly before the voters they are asking to represent.

If Randall accepts, October 10 could provide voters with a rare opportunity before the November 3 general election to hear directly from both candidates about immigration enforcement, public safety and the role of Congress.
Washington’s statewide voting period begins October 16, when ballots are required to be mailed to registered voters.
Whether or not that conversation takes place, the purpose of the afternoon will not change.
Remember the victims.
Stand with their families.
Support the men and women enforcing our nation’s laws.
And make sure the stories behind the statistics are never forgotten.

EVENT DETAILS Stand With ICE Saturday, October 10, 2026 2:00–4:30 PM Northwest ICE Processing Center 1623 E J Street Tacoma, Washington Featured Guest: Angel Mom Agnes Gibboney, Founder of Angel Families of America Members of the public, media, elected officials, veterans organizations, civic organizations and community leaders are invited to attend.
The Fox campaign asks everyone present, regardless of viewpoint, to remain peaceful, respect lawful instructions and allow those with opposing views to exercise their First Amendment rights.

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Press Release Clean Sweep - CD6 Republicans Unified Teresa Fox Secures Unanimous Support from All Six Republican County Parties in Washington’s 6th Congressional District July 1, 2026 Campaign Staff FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Teresa Fox Secures Unanimous Support from All Six Republican County Parties in Washington’s 6th Congressional District BREMERTON, WA, June 30, 2026 — The Teresa Fox for Congress campaign is proud to announce an important milestone in the race for Washington’s 6th Congressional District: the unanimous endorsement of the candidate by all six Republican County Parties across the district.
It’s a clean sweep!
These endorsements represent the unified support of party Republican organizations in Clallam, Grays Harbor, Jefferson, Kitsap, Mason, and Pierce counties.
We stand strong together, signaling overwhelming grassroots momentum for Fox’s mission to bring practical, responsible, results oriented leadership to Washington, D.C.
“I am honored and humbled to have the full backing of our Republican county parties,” said Teresa Fox.

“This collective endorsement represents more than just organizational support; it reflects a shared commitment from the hardworking people of this district to reject the status quo of career politics.

Families and citizens of the district are ready for leadership that prioritizes the needs of our communities over ideological activism.” Fox, a safety professional and emergency manager, has built her platform on providing practical solutions to the issues impacting the 6th District: Affordability and Economic Development: Fox is committed to stopping the runaway government spending fueling inflation.
She advocates for policies that foster a strong, stable economy to ensure Washington’s working families can thrive.
Public Safety and Law Enforcement: Believing that public safety is the foundation of a healthy community, Fox is dedicated to restoring law and order.
Her plan includes ensuring proper staffing and resources for law enforcement, particularly in rural communities, to guarantee that neighborhoods remain safe for all residents.
“From our shipyards to our rural communities, the message from the 6th District is clear: we need change,” Fox added.
“We are focused on fiscal restraint, naval readiness, and protecting our families.

With this united front, we are ready to take our common sense message directly to the voters and ensure that Washington has a representative who puts the people first.” ### About Teresa Fox Teresa Fox is a hands-on safety professional and emergency manager who has spent her career protecting workers and strengthening institutions in high-accountability environments.
Not a career politician, she is running to restore citizen service to Congress, focusing on fiscal responsibility, public safety, and practical solutions for the 6th Congressional District.

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Press Release Emily Randall Calls ICE Agents Fascists In a social media post US Representative Randall stoked the flames of polarization by referring to ICE Agents as fascists July 15, 2026 Campaign Staff FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE In a social media post US Representative stoked the flames of polarization by referring to ICE Agents as fascists.
Teresa Fox calls to lower the temperature.
BREMERTON, WA, July 15, 2026 — The climate of politics has become more about demonization than constructive debate.
Right here in the 6th Congressional District our US Representative Emily Randall stokes the hyperbole of polarization in the face of tragedy and confusion.

In a recent statement Randall referred to Federal ICE Agents as a "fascist police force." Teresa Fox stepped forward to run for US Representative in the 6th Congressional District to bring responsibility, accountability, and maturity back to the 6th District.
She said of the Randall statement: “Representative Emily Randall's statement following the tragic deaths in Texas and Maine is deeply disappointing.

Rather than allowing independent investigations to establish the facts, she immediately declared these incidents to be "murders" and labeled federal law enforcement officers "fascists." Every loss of life deserves a thorough, transparent, and independent investigation.
If mistakes were made or excessive force was used, those responsible should be held accountable.
That principle applies to every law enforcement agency, including ICE." "Inflammatory rhetoric that presumes guilt before investigations are complete serves neither justice nor public safety.
It undermines due process and further divides an already polarized nation.

Congress should be focused on ensuring accountability and improving transparency, including expanding the use of body cameras, and protecting both the public and the law enforcement officers who put themselves in dangerous situations every day.

Investigations into both incidents are ongoing, and key facts remain disputed." "Americans can support secure borders while also insisting that law enforcement operate professionally, transparently, and within the law.
Those goals are not mutually exclusive.
Representative Randall's decision to prejudge these cases and demonize an entire federal agency does not bring us closer to the truth.

It only fuels anger before all the evidence is known." ### About Teresa Fox Teresa Fox is a hands-on safety professional and emergency manager who has spent her career protecting workers and strengthening institutions in high-accountability environments.
Not a career politician, she is running to restore citizen service to Congress, focusing on fiscal responsibility, public safety, and practical solutions for the 6th Congressional District.

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Opinion The Tragedy on Our Streets Why It’s Time to End the 'Homeless Industrial Complex' and Restore Public Safety June 9, 2026 Campaign Staff The Tragedy on Our Streets: Why It’s Time to End the 'Homeless Industrial Complex' and Restore Public Safety I am running to represent Washington’s 6th Congressional District because, like many of you, I look at our communities today and barely recognize them.

Everywhere I go, from Bremerton to the furthest corners of our six-county district, the questions I hear most are centered on a singular, urgent crisis: public safety and the catastrophic state of homelessness on our streets.
For me, this crisis isn't abstract or merely political.
It is deeply personal.
I have friends whose children are dead—stolen away by an unchecked drug epidemic.
We are on the verge of losing an entire generation to narcotics and the crime that follows in their wake.
What we are witnessing is a human tragedy on a scale previously unknown in the United States.
While there are many pathways to homelessness, the horrific reality for those trapped on our streets is universal.
They are subjected to repeated rapes, robberies, and murders.
They are preyed upon by human traffickers, plagued by devastating health conditions from severe drug abuse, and shuffled from corner to corner with no stability.
It is clear to anyone paying attention: the current approach is not just failing—it is actively enabling a humanitarian disaster.
The Cost of a Broken Status Quo For years, our state's failed laws and lenient policies have directly fueled this crisis.
We have asked our law enforcement officers to do more with less, while tying their hands.
Meanwhile, our homeowners, families, and local businesses pay the price through damaged property, lost livelihoods, and a pervasive sense of insecurity.
We can no longer throw billions of taxpayer dollars at this problem without demanding quantifiable results.
For too long, we have funded a "homeless industrial complex"—a network of unaccountable programs and NGOs that profit off the continuation of the crisis rather than its cure.
We must stop enabling dependency and stop encouraging individuals to migrate to our district for limited resources.
It is time to keep more hard-earned money in your pockets and expect real solutions, not endless lip service from career politicians.
A Comprehensive, Accountable Way Forward As your representative in Congress, I will leverage federal avenues to address this public safety and humanitarian emergency.
However, federal intervention cannot be top-down or disconnected from local reality.
Since launching my campaign in February, I have spent my time on the ground, listening to citizens, business owners, and law enforcement personnel across all six counties.
My approach to legislation is built on three cornerstone principles: Inclusive Stakeholder Engagement: Effective policy cannot be written in a vacuum.
It must include the voices of all constituents—including law enforcement, medical professionals, and local business leaders.
Quantifiable Metrics: We must tie every federal dollar to measurable outcomes.
If a program isn't reducing homelessness, curbing addiction, or improving safety, it will lose its funding.
Restoring Law and Order: We must support our police and enforce the law to protect both the public and the vulnerable populations currently being victimized on our streets.
Finding Common Ground This is a complex crisis with no overnight fix, but the first step toward a solution is admitting that the status quo is broken for everyone.
We must approach this challenge with mutual respect for our varying perspectives, look past partisan divides, and find the common ground required to heal our communities.
Public safety is not a partisan issue; it is a fundamental human right.
I ask for your vote as your 6th Congressional Representative so that we can finally prioritize safety, accountability, and compassion for all of us.
To learn more about our platform, share your perspective, or find upcoming campaign events, please visit FOXFORWA.COM .

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News In the News Washington State Republican Party Endorses Teresa Fox for Congress The Washington State Republican Party has endorsed Teresa Fox for Congress in Washington’s 6th District, building on support from all six county Republican parties.
August 16, 2026 Campaign Staff The Washington State Republican Party has endorsed Teresa Fox for U.S.
Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District , adding statewide Republican support to a campaign already backed by Republican organizations across all six counties of the district.

The endorsement marks another important step forward for the Fox for Washington campaign as it enters the general election and continues building support across Clallam, Grays Harbor, Jefferson, Kitsap, Mason, and Pierce counties.
Teresa has already earned the support of the Republican Party organizations in all six counties that make up Washington’s 6th Congressional District.
The Washington State Republican Party endorsement now adds the support of the state party as Teresa takes her campaign directly to voters throughout the district.
“I am deeply grateful for the support of Republicans across this district and now from the Washington State Republican Party,” Teresa said.

“This campaign has always been about the people we represent, the communities we serve, and making sure their voices are heard in Washington, D.C.” The endorsement comes as Teresa continues emphasizing public safety, constitutional rights, responsible government, strong representation for all six counties, and a campaign centered on People over Politics .

Her message throughout the district has been consistent: Washington’s 6th Congressional District deserves a representative who will listen to its communities, defend individual liberty, and put the people of the district ahead of political interests.
The growing Republican support also reflects the campaign’s expanding organization heading into the general election.
Six counties.
One district.
A campaign for the people.

Teresa Fox and the Fox for Washington campaign are grateful for the confidence placed in her by Republican leaders and organizations throughout Washington and look forward to carrying that momentum into November.
About Teresa Fox Teresa Fox is the Republican candidate for U.S.
Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District, representing Clallam, Grays Harbor, Jefferson, Kitsap, Mason, and portions of Pierce County.
Learn more about Teresa, her campaign, and upcoming events at foxforwa.com .

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Opinion Washington State is in Real Trouble While Emily Randall Celebrates Good Trouble Event Saturday in Bremerton, Kitsap County Democrats hosted Emily Randall, Bob Ferguson, and Nick Brown for an event titled Good Trouble May 3, 2026 Campaign Staff May 3, 2026 CONTACT: info@foxforwa.com foxforwa.com Washington State is in Real Trouble While Emily Randall Celebrates Good Trouble Event Saturday in Bremerton, Kitsap County Democrats hosted Emily Randall, Bob Ferguson, and Nick Brown for an event titled Good Trouble with the rising clenched fist of resistance as the graphical accompaniment.
Good Trouble they tell you in Kitsap County.
The national gas price average is $4.43 while in Washington State sits at $5.88.
That is a $1.45 gap tied directly to policy choices of the majority Democrat Party.
They want you to look away from the fact that Emily Randall and the majority Democrats voted for the taxes that make up that national average gas price gap.
Good Trouble indeed.
Good Trouble they tell you in Kitsap County.
The majority Democrat Party in Washington state has spent $5 billion in the last decade on homeless prevention, with $4 billion of that coming in just the last few years.
Just look around at our city streets - Has the homelessness crisis improved or spread?
Is this Good Trouble?
Good Trouble they tell you in Kitsap County.
Emily Randall and the majority state Democrats are champions of transgender treatments for teenagers and sporting participation for biological boys in girls sports.
Emily Randall paints this policy choice as an issue of “fairness,” but looks away from the permanent harm induced, and the clear civil rights violations placed upon girls and women.
Just tell the voters it’s Good Trouble perhaps.
All of this Good Trouble is painted in the guise of a clenched raised fist of resistance.
Merely a marketing ploy capturing voters in a lie.
Randall and the Majority Democrat Party in Washington State have created this mess we find ourselves in.
They aren’t the minority few fighting the oppressive power of government - They ARE the oppressive power of government.
We have allowed our governance to be taken over by extreme partisan political activists like Emily Randall.
I stepped forward to run for Congress in the 6th Congressional District because I believe enough is enough.
The clever marketing can no longer hide the gross negligence representing us in Washington State.
It’s easy to see the governance cycle of Emily Randall and the majority Democrat Party: Tax - Waste/Fraud/Abuse - Budget Shortfall - Repeat.
Responsible budgets and accountable spending have been pushed aside for fringe ideological policy activism cloaked in Orwellian newspeak propaganda.
I personally want to end the cycle of new taxes to cover reckless abuses that perpetuate shortfalls.
Responsibility and accountability through representation - THAT sounds like Good Trouble to me.

Will both candidates take their seats?
October 15, 2026 Campaign Staff FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE | October 15, 2026 WILL RANDALL FINALLY SIT STILL FOR A CANDIDATE FORUM?
GIG HARBOR, WA – Mark your calendars!
Another congressional candidate forum is scheduled for Monday, October 19, at Heron's Key in Gig Harbor.

Despite months of outreach and invitations, Republican congressional candidate Teresa Fox says incumbent Congresswoman Emily Randall has yet to participate in a single face-to-face forum, debate, town hall, or meeting with her throughout the 2026 election season.
Not once.
Both candidates have been invited to Monday's event.
With Election Day just weeks away, voters have yet to see these two congressional opponents share a stage.
The question remains: Will Randall finally sit still long enough for voters to hear from both candidates?

added: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Our Mission Protecting Puget Sound for Future Generations Teresa Fox is dedicated to safeguarding the economic and environmental ecosystem of the Puget Sound and Olympic Peninsula.
We are the stewards of our future, together.

A Mission Built on Results, Not Rhetoric Fiscal Restraint Stop runaway government spending Naval Readiness Fund workers, not Washington bureaucrats Crime & Safety Proper police staffing for rural communities Title IX Protection Fair competition and privacy for all Healthcare Access Real solutions for rural healthcare deserts Term Limits End career politics and restore citizen service Support the Campaign Help Teresa Fox bring practical leadership and real-world experience to Washington's 6th District.
DONATE NOW Stay Informed Get updates on the campaign and learn how you can help bring real leadership to Congress.
SUBSCRIBE Pragmatism, Restraint, Accountability Income Tax?
Climate Commitment Act?
Washingtonians are being burdened by big government.
It's time to say enough!
Stop the Government Growth Machine From Washington State to Washington DC, Democrat politicians grow government like it's their private business.
This ideological framework is choking our real businesses.

Lower Taxes Keep money in family pockets, not bureaucrat budgets Less Regulation Let businesses operate without constant government interference Real Accountability Make government answer to taxpayers, not the other way around Readiness vs.

Red Tape "Modernizing the Navy shouldn't mean more middle management in D.C.; it should mean more tools and higher pay for the pipefitters and welders in Bremerton." The Problem The Navy's Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) is a multi-billion dollar, 20-year project.
While billions are allocated, the money often gets swallowed by "consultant fees" and "administrative oversight" in DC before it ever hits the dry docks.
The federal government is more interested in "process" than "production." The Solution Move the money from the office buildings in Virginia to the dry docks in Bremerton.
Fund actual shipyard workers, not DC consultants Invest in tools and equipment, not bureaucratic overhead Prioritize readiness over red tape Blue-Collar Environmentalism vs.
Green Experiments Federal mandates that prioritize unproven "Green" maritime technologies over the immediate maintenance needs of the existing fleet put both national security and local jobs at risk.
Rapid electrification of support vessels threatens job stability.
Forcing "experimental" tech onto the shipyard before the infrastructure is ready is dangerous.

"We need ships that can fight today, not social experiments that might float tomorrow." Police Staffing & Rural Safety "It's unacceptable that Washington ranks last in police staffing." The Problem In places like Mason and Jefferson Counties, response times are a matter of life and death.
Washington ranks last in police staffing nationwide, leaving rural communities dangerously underserved.
When you call 911, help should come fast—no matter where you live.
The Solution I'm advocating for a 'Federal Public Safety Floor'—direct federal incentives for local agencies to hire and retain officers.
A 911 call should be answered just as fast in Port Angeles as it is in Seattle.
Protecting the 50-Year Legacy of Title IX Fairness for All, Not Preference for Some Fair Competition Title IX was created to ensure biological women had a fair playing field.
Allowing biological males to compete effectively erases the progress of the last 50 years.
Privacy and Safety Most voters in the 6th District believe that girls should not be forced to undress in front of biological males.
This is about basic privacy and safety.
Rural Healthcare Access Whether it's the lack of OB-GYN services in Clallam County or mental health shortages in Mason County, healthcare access is a non-partisan crisis here.
Healthcare deserts are becoming too common.
Keep rural clinics open.

Focus on telehealth expansion and federal incentives for doctors to practice in "medical deserts." This bypasses partisan debates by focusing on the physical presence of care where people actually live.

Expand Telehealth Services Bring specialists to rural communities through proven technology Federal Incentives for Rural Doctors Create real financial reasons for healthcare providers to serve underserved areas Support Local Clinics Keep community healthcare facilities operational and accessible Congressional Term Limits Congress should be a service, not a career.
End Career Politics Term limits speak to constituents across party lines about the never-ending corruption and the disconnected political class.
Signing the U.S.
Term Limits Pledge distinguishes real public servants from career politicians in the making.
An Outsider in DC Career politicians have created a system that serves themselves, not the people they represent.
It's time to return Congress to what the founders intended: temporary service by citizens who live with the consequences of their decisions.
Ready to Fight for the 6th District Teresa Fox isn't running to advance a national political agenda.
She's running to deliver practical solutions for the people who work hard, play by the rules, and deserve better from their government.
Results Over Rhetoric.
Service Over Career.
People Over Politics.

added: Meet Andrew Issues Endorsements News Contribute News 10/16/2026 Fudge Campaign Enters Final Stretch with Broad Coalition, Labor Support, and Expanded Voter Outreach Independent Party cross-nomination, Republican leadership endorsements, Teamsters and SMART support, and Oregon Right to Life PAC recommendation highlight campaign developments as ballots arrive.

WEST SALEM, Ore. — With ballots arriving in mailboxes across Oregon House District 20, Republican and Independent Party nominee Andrew Fudge is entering the final weeks of the 2026 election with an expanding coalition of supporters, an energized volunteer operation, and a comprehensive campaign focused on bringing new leadership and accountability to Salem.

Since securing the Republican nomination with nearly two-thirds of the vote in a contested primary, Fudge has earned the cross-nomination of the Independent Party of Oregon, formal endorsements from prominent Republican leaders and organized labor, and a recommendation from Oregon Right to Life PAC.
"Our campaign has come a long way since the primary," said Fudge.
"We set out to build a coalition that goes beyond political labels, and that's exactly what we've done.

Republicans, Independents, working families, and Oregonians who are frustrated with the direction of our state are coming together around a common message: it's time for accountability and results." Building a Coalition Beyond Party Lines Fudge's nomination by the Independent Party of Oregon represents a significant milestone in a district where independent and nonaffiliated voters play a major role in determining election outcomes.

The campaign has also secured support from Republican legislative leaders and elected officials, including State Representative Ed Diehl and Angela Plowhead, Polk County Commissioners Craig Pope and Lyle Mordhorst, and Commissioner-elect John Swanson.
Fudge has additionally been formally recommended by Oregon Right to Life PAC and is included in the organization's 2026 digital voter guide.

Beyond partisan politics, the campaign has earned the backing of organized labor, including Teamsters and SMART transportation representatives, reflecting shared priorities involving workplace safety, transportation infrastructure, and protecting Oregon workers.
"Having the support of both Republican leaders and organized labor speaks to what this campaign is about," Fudge said.
"We don't have to agree on every issue to work together on the things that matter.
Safe workplaces, responsible government, good schools, and an affordable future aren't exclusively Republican or Democratic priorities.

They're Oregon priorities." Rail Safety Demonstrates Common Ground with Organized Labor One example of the campaign's commitment to practical, bipartisan solutions is Fudge's support for legislation requiring two trained crew members aboard freight trains.
Senate Bill 723 would have established a two-person crew requirement in Oregon, subject to applicable exceptions.
Similar safety requirements have been enacted in several neighboring Western states.
The legislation was supported by rail workers concerned about the safety of train operations, emergency response, and the movement of hazardous materials through Oregon communities.
Despite these concerns, the measure failed to advance through the Oregon Legislature.

Fudge has publicly supported the legislation, arguing that having two trained crew members available provides additional safeguards for rail workers, first responders, and communities along Oregon's freight corridors.
"When something goes wrong on a train carrying hazardous materials, having a second trained crew member available can make a meaningful difference," Fudge said.
"This is about protecting the workers operating those trains and the communities they travel through.

It's exactly the kind of common-sense public safety legislation that deserves bipartisan support." Fudge has emphasized that his approach to public safety extends beyond traditional law enforcement to include transportation safety, emergency preparedness, and preventing avoidable tragedies.

Campaign Expands Outreach as Ballots Arrive With support from Oregon House Minority Leadership, the Fudge campaign has launched an expanded social media and digital communications effort, including professionally produced videos, issue-focused advertising, and direct voter outreach.
These efforts complement an ambitious grassroots operation reaching voters throughout West Salem, Independence, Monmouth, and surrounding communities.
Volunteers are distributing campaign materials, engaging residents at their doorsteps, and mobilizing for the final weeks of voting.
The campaign's distinctive brick-inspired "Building Awesome Together" imagery has also become a recognizable part of its community outreach.
Fudge has continued developing relationships with local businesses and community organizations, including joining the Monmouth-Independence Chamber of Commerce.

On Saturday, October 17, volunteers and supporters will gather for The Final Push for Fudge , a campaign organizing and canvassing event at Roth's Event Center in West Salem, from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
"We're not taking a single vote for granted," Fudge said.
"While our digital outreach is reaching more voters than ever, nothing replaces a conversation on someone's doorstep.

We're working hard to earn the trust of voters throughout the district." A Clear Choice Following Recent Developments The final weeks of the election have also brought renewed attention to incumbent Representative Paul Evans, who was arrested October 4 following an incident in Independence and subsequently charged with driving under the influence of intoxicants, reckless driving, and failing to stop after causing property damage.
Evans has pleaded not guilty.
His attorney has stated that he entered a residential treatment program in Arizona, with an anticipated stay extending through Election Day.
His campaign has indicated he intends to remain in the race.
Fudge emphasized the importance of accountability while recognizing the seriousness of the circumstances.
"I sincerely hope Representative Evans receives the care and support he needs," Fudge said.
"But the residents of House District 20 also deserve a representative who is present, engaged, and prepared to serve.

This election is about the future of our communities, and voters deserve a serious conversation about leadership, judgment, and accountability." The campaign continues to emphasize Fudge's professional qualifications as a Certified Public Accountant and experienced state government budget manager, as well as his four central priorities: improving affordability, strengthening education, pursuing effective solutions to housing and homelessness, and protecting public safety.

Looking Toward November 3 With fewer than three weeks remaining before Election Day, the Fudge campaign is focused on its volunteer operation, voter outreach, and communicating its priorities to the residents of House District 20.
"Eight years working inside state government have taught me that good intentions aren't enough.
We need clear priorities, responsible spending, and leaders willing to measure results," Fudge said.
"Back in June, I promised we would build a broad coalition and take our case directly to voters.
We've delivered on that promise.
Now we're asking the people of House District 20 to help us take the next step." "It's time for a change in Salem.

And I'm ready to deliver accountability you can count on." About Andrew Fudge Andrew Fudge is a native Oregonian, husband, father, Certified Public Accountant, and state government budget professional with eight years of experience in public service.
He is the Republican and Independent Party of Oregon nominee for House District 20, representing West Salem, Independence, Monmouth, and surrounding communities.
For more information, volunteer opportunities, or campaign updates, visit www.fudge4oregon.org .

added: Skip to content Chip in to support chris Instagram X-twitter Facebook-f Youtube Threads Meet Chris Endorsements The Mission Plan 2027 Mission One: Lowering the Cost of Living on Long Island Mission Two: Prepare Long Island for the Future Mission Three: Protect Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, and Affordable Health Care Mission Four: Supporting Veterans and Military Families Mission Five: Supporting Labor and Working Families​ Mission Six: Restoring Trust in Government Events News Room Team Gallant Toolkit Shop Shop Meet Chris Endorsements The Mission Plan 2027 Mission One: Lowering the Cost of Living on Long Island Mission Two: Prepare Long Island for the Future Mission Three: Protect Medicare, Medicaid, Social Security, and Affordable Health Care Mission Four: Supporting Veterans and Military Families Mission Five: Supporting Labor and Working Families​ Mission Six: Restoring Trust in Government Events News Room Team Gallant Toolkit Shop Shop donate On Republican Long Island, Democrat Chris Gallant bets on public service over politics New York’s Long Island, which is just 50 miles from the Stonewall Inn, is a reliably red enclave where President Trump won easily in 2024.

Chris Gallant, an openly gay Democrat running for New York’s 1st Congressional District, which includes the eastern side of Long Island, is trying to capitalize on what he sees as growing frustration with the Republican Party and its ability to deliver for everyday Americans.

The Blade sat down with Gallant to discuss his move from civil servant to the fight for public office, how he has been personally impacted by the changes from the Trump administration, and the recent release of photos from his past that have brought the national spotlight his way.
Gallant has a long record of public service that, on paper, would make him an unconventional but compelling candidate for a heavily Republican district.

His résumé includes New York Army National Guard service that began when he was 17, multiple overseas deployments, including multiple tours in Kuwait, work as an FAA air traffic controller, union leadership and service as a volunteer firefighter.

That record of service is central to how Gallant describes himself — particularly as he navigates the unusual combination of being an openly gay candidate, a military veteran, and a Democrat running in a district where Republicans have historically held the advantage.

“My fiancé and I both serve in the military and we built our relationship through trust, timing, and a lot of miles between us,” his campaign website says, highlighting the idea of family values that has become a central part of winning the area.
“I’ve been openly gay in the military since just after ‘Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell’ ended, and I’ve learned to speak plainly, hold the line, and back up what I say.

I’ve also learned how to listen — and how to bring people with very different views to the table and actually make progress.” Gallant said that record, rather than his sexual orientation, is what should define his candidacy.
“I think who I am as a person is an asset,” he told the Blade when asked if his sexuality has played any role in his decision to run.
“I’m not running because I’m gay.
I’m running, and,’Oh, I’m gay.’ It’s part of my identity.
It’s just a part of who I am.
But it’s not necessarily on the table because that shouldn’t make a difference on how I’m going to respond in Congress or how I’m going to run into a burning building.
I don’t think those things necessarily matter so much.” For Gallant, the campaign is ultimately about something broader than identity politics.
He said he is running because he wants to restore Americans’ confidence in a government that he says has become less about its people and more about the wealthy leaders in charge.
“I’ve always said that part of the reason why I am running for Congress is because I want to restore faith in our government,” he said.
“We’re all drastically exhausted with what’s going on in this world, and particularly with Donald Trump being in office, [his] type of politics, and the way he works, essentially.

When Biden got into office after Trump won, it was like the release of a pressure cooker… the pressure cooker is just even worse now this second time around.” He also explained that his experience working inside the federal government has shaped how he believes Washington should approach its problems.

Gallant pointed specifically to the Trump administration’s efforts to reduce the size of government and the role of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), arguing that cutting government spending should not mean indiscriminate cuts.
“I understand that we as a nation need to save money, or at least fix the budget or balance it.
We are getting further and further in debt … The budget is always a huge issue and something that we definitely 100% need to fix.

But we need to do it with experts and, you know, attack these issues with a scalpel, not a chainsaw.” The chainsaw Gallant mentioned is a clear reference to controversial Trump supporter Elon Musk, who announced he would be heading the highly politicized DOGE agency, where he, the first-ever trillionaire, brandished a shiny chainsaw symbolic of them cutting government spending with no regard for the impact on everyday Americans.
That philosophy, of scalpel over chainsaw, is also part of Gallant’s argument to voters who may be more accustomed to voting Republican.
He does not present himself as a traditional politician, but rather as someone whose career outside politics could be an asset in Congress.
“I’m not a politician.
This is my first foray into politics, and I think that’s what our politics need.
We need fresh new faces, not career politicians.
Someone who has brand new ideas, not tainted by politics.

So I would say, give me the opportunity to prove myself, because, you know, until I actually get there and I can actually do a job, we won’t know.” Gallant also shared signs that the political landscape on Long Island may be shifting.
He pointed to gains Democrats made across the district last November and said economic concerns could further erode Republican support.
“Last November, in this district we [Democrats] gained 13 and 14 points across the district ..And this district lost by 10 points last year.

So even just in one year, you can tell that there’s a difference.” The swapping of support from the Republican side to Democratic reflects the real concern voters have about the economy — impacted by the war in Iran, tariffs, and growing inflation.
“People are feeling it here in their pockets.
The cost of living here on Long Island is already high, and things are just getting worse.

There’s a lot of promises that were made with this administration that weren’t kept.” Gallant said that frustration has directly translated into support from some voters who previously backed President Donald Trump.
“I know a lot of people who have voted for Donald Trump that have my lawn sign on their front lawn today.

If that’s the change that they’re looking for, I’m going to provide it.” But Gallant’s campaign has been complicated by a very different kind of political issue: the publication of photos from his past that have become a national story.
The photos, which include pictures of Gallant wearing various fetish gear for Mr.
S Leather — including a harness and a collar — were shared with the New York Post .
Gallant has consistently rejected the idea that he should be ashamed of the images or that they undermine his qualifications for public office since their Sept.
13 publication.
Instead, he has argued that his record of service should be considered alongside a private chapter of his life from #ago.
“I mean, look, I’m totally not ashamed of who I am as a person.
Those pictures were taken in my private life.
I can still run into a burning building faster than most people.
I can still fly a helicopter.
And those are from #ago, right?

I built an entire life based around my commitment to the military and the Army National Guard.” Rather than allowing the controversy to define him, Gallant said he hopes it can become part of a broader conversation about privacy and the consequences of living in a digital age — and indicated that this sort of scenario would become something semi-regular for those who grew up with technology.
“The reality is that we live in a digital age.This is what our generation is going to be stuck with.
I laugh all the time because this is the reason why Congress and the Senate are about to die in their chairs.

They didn’t have cameras and pictures and photos like that.” “If I have to be the person to wave the banner now to fight and advocate for not only our community but anybody that could be put in this situation, that realizes now that we’re living in a digital age and this is what the future is going to be.
It’s, you know, everything’s left online now.” That argument extends beyond his own campaign.
Gallant said he worries that the prospect of having a digital footprint scrutinized could discourage highly qualified and passionate potential public servants from seeking office.
“I understand that getting into public life means that the rest of your life becomes public.
I get it, I do.

But I also feel bad because there’s a lot of good people out there wanting to do a job in the public world, and they’re just afraid of what their digital footprint might have on them or might—what might exist because we’ve done things when we’re 12 or 15, or 20, or 30, or whatever.” “I think living in this digital world, I would love to advocate for people to say, ‘How do we prevent some of these things from coming out into the public view so people can still maintain some kind of a private life?’” For an openly gay candidate, the issue also carries a particular significance.
Gallant said his experience has made him more interested in advocating for other LGBTQ people who may hesitate to enter public life because of what could eventually surface online.
His own LGBTQ policy priorities are relatively focused.

He said adding further protections for same-sex marriage in federal law would be one of the issues he would want to pursue if elected, particularly as questions about the Supreme Court’s future approach to marriage equality continue to loom.
“My partner, who’s my fiancé, is currently deployed.

We got engaged before he left in December because if the question came up to the Supreme Court– whether gay marriage was going to be a thing– we had to question whether, when he got back from deployment after Christmas this year, whether we were actually going to be able to legally get married.” “I mean, these are questions that shouldn’t even be questions anymore.
So if we can put something like [codifying same-sex marriage] into law, where it’s just not a Supreme Court decision and it can get overturned, like Roe v.
Wade, then let’s do it.” Gallant’s opponent, Rep.
Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.), is the two-term incumbent and has a mixed record on LGBTQ rights.
LaLota has been vocal in his opposition to overturning Obergefell v.
Hodges , the Supreme Court case that established the constitutional right to same-sex marriage, but he has also been outspoken in his opposition to transgender rights.
He co-sponsored and voted for H.R.
28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which would restrict participation in women’s sports based on sex assigned at birth rather than gender identity.

Gallant, on the other hand, has few official positions on LGBTQ issues but assured the Blade that, if elected, he would become “an advocate, particularly for the LGBTQ community.” He also said he believes same-sex marriage should be codified into law and that nondiscrimination protections should be expanded.

“I would definitely be pushing no discrimination against anyone for any reason — and that should not have any place in any workplace — especially on the federal government level.” For Gallant, however, LGBTQ rights are only one part of a broader platform centered on public service, affordability and restoring trust in government.

He repeatedly returned to the idea that a member of Congress should be accessible to the people they represent — something he believes his experience holding town halls and working directly with members of his community demonstrates.
“I always find that a record of service and showing up every day at work and in our communities is what’s going to be key and important.
And I think that’s what a representative needs to do.
As a representative you’re supposed to represent and work with the people that elect you to office.

added: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/849773309_2212284006014432_7172732666286756856_n.jpg|Mahalo, Molokaʻi! 🤙🏽 I had a wonderful time visiting Molokaʻi, connecting with the community, listening to the people, and hearing your stories. These conversations are a reminder of why listening to our communities and putting the people first matters. A heartfelt mahalo for the endorsements and to everyone who welcomed me and took the time to share their thoughts with me. Your voices matter, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to hear them. Let’s build a better future for Hawaiʻi, together. Vote Gary Cordery for Governor!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/844646257_18075966707748599_5770882034073883105_n.jpg|Speed Bumps, Are these really a priority? #hawaiipolitics #hawaii #teamaloha #garycorderyforgovernor

What issues matter most to you and your family? We want to hear YOUR story! Share why you support and what you hope to see for the future of Hawaiʻi. Your voice deserves to be heard, and your story may inspire others in our community. Share your story using the link in our bio. Let’s make sure Hawaiʻi’s voices are heard.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/848547578_18075891983748599_3322747924729423860_n.jpg|As Governor, the first thing I will do is establish an Office of Transparency so the people of Hawaiʻi can clearly see what their government is doing. The people deserve to know how decisions are made, how taxpayer dollars are spent, and whether their government is delivering on its promises. Government works for the people, and the people deserve answers. Vote for me for Governor. — Gary Cordery

Comment WE NEED A DEBATE and tag @drjoshgreen @govjoshgreen Sign the request to debate petition. Link in bio! Josh Green could become the first Hawaiʻi governor in 40 years to refuse a debate. Historical research identified gubernatorial debates from 1986 through 2022, though 1990 remains unconfirmed. Hawaiʻi voters deserve answers, not silence. Leadership means showing up, answering tough questions, and being accountable to the people.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/847287205_18075806933748599_5985224361460303487_n.jpg|We have been taking our message statewide to the people all week! BIG ISLAND, WE’RE COMING YOUR WAY! 🌺 Waimea, get ready! Join me, Gary Cordery for Governor, and Daniel Anthony for Lieutenant Governor, for an evening of meaningful conversation, community, and connection. These Meet & Greet's are an opportunity to share your thoughts, learn more about our vision for the future of Hawai'i, and be part of a growing movement built on leadership, integrity, and aloha. Come talk story, meet neighbors, and enjoy a welcoming evening together. Together, we continue building a better future for Hawai‘i. RSVP link in bio.

Voting is a fundamental right, and every voice deserves to be heard. Take the time to be informed, understand your options, and make your voice count. Let’s look out for our community! An informed community is an empowered community. Let’s make sure everyone has the information they need to participate!

removed: top of page DONATE SUBSCRIBE VOLUNTEER Menu Close GARY CORDERY FOR 2026 GARY CORDERY FOR 2026 GARY CORDERY FOR 2026 GARY CORDERY FOR 2026 HOME KEY ISSUES EVENTS ABOUT LOCAL BUSINESSES VISION ABOUT GARY LISTEN TO GARY BLOG LOCAL BUSINESSES VISION ABOUT GARY LISTEN TO GARY BLOG VOTE + LINKS CONTACT Menu Close All Posts Affordable Housing Cost of Living Education Honoring Native Hawaiian Plan for Transparency Government Transparency Community Honoring Native Hawaiian Voices Aug 4, 2025 1 min read Real Stories, Real People: Honoring Native Hawaiian Voices Real Stories, Real People: Honoring Native Hawaiian Voices Gary Cordery is committed to addressing Native Hawaiian issues with respect, cultural understanding, and action that uplifts and empowers our community.
Listening First, Leading with Respect.

From the shores of Waimea to the valleys of Hāna, Gary has spent time meeting with Native Hawaiian leaders, cultural practitioners, and families who carry the traditions, history, and values of these islands.
These conversations are not political checkboxes—they are the foundation of how he shapes his vision for Hawai‘i’s future.

Cultural Preservation as a Priority Gary believes that protecting sacred sites, supporting ʻōlelo Hawai‘i (Hawaiian language) programs, and preserving cultural practices is not optional—it is essential.
Cultural heritage is the heartbeat of Hawai‘i, and it must be safeguarded for future generations.
Equitable Access to Resources** From land use to water rights, Gary is committed to ensuring Native Hawaiian communities have fair and transparent access to the resources they are entitled to.
This includes prioritizing housing opportunities for Native Hawaiian families and supporting initiatives that address long-standing inequities.
Empowering Native Hawaiian Leadership Representation matters.
Gary is dedicated to ensuring Native Hawaiian voices are not only heard but are central to decision-making at the state level.
Empowerment begins with trust, respect, and shared responsibility.
Stand With Native Hawaiian Communities Join Gary in honoring cultural heritage and building a future rooted in respect, equity, and shared values.

title.before: Borrello, Assembly member host small business roundtable

removed: top of page All Posts Search Borrello, Assembly member host small business roundtable nate1457 Dec 3, 2021 1 min read DANSVILLE — State Sen.

George Borrello and Assemblywoman Marjorie Byrnes hosted a roundtable on small business Wednesday to gather input on the challenges owners face as state and local economies work to recover from the financial hardships of the past two years.
Representatives from the region’s hospitality, manufacturing, health care and insurance/financial sectors participated in the forum.

“Small businesses employ more than half of New Yorkers, so it is critically important that we listen to them and work in partnership to help them succeed and thrive,” Borrello, R-Chautauqua County, said.
“When they do well, New York state does well.” A focal point of the discussion were persistent staffing shortages in a number of industries, which several participants cited.

Borrello said the state has a labor shortage despite the fact that New York still has one of the worst unemployment numbers in the nation at a recession-level rate of 6.8%, while the national average is 4.6%.
“That is a clear sign that our economic recovery is being severely hindered by bad government policy out of Albany,” the senator said.

added: top of page All Posts Search Borrello Earns Endorsement of Corrections Officers Union lhill5000 Sep 4 1 min read I am deeply honored to receive the endorsement of NYSCOPBA, the union representing New York’s corrections officers.
Our correction officers perform one of the most difficult and dangerous jobs in public service.

They walk into some of the most volatile environments imaginable every day, working long hours under extraordinarily challenging conditions to keep their fellow officers, inmates and our communities safe.

I have tremendous respect and appreciation for these men and women, and I have been proud to stand with them as they have fought for adequate staffing, common-sense safety measures and the repeal of the HALT Act which has contributed to the crisis inside our prisons .
Their concerns have too often been ignored in Albany.
I will continue to be a strong voice for our correction officers and stand with them in the fight for the support and reforms they need to do their jobs safely.

We are also proud longtime members of NFIB, which makes this endorsement especially meaningful to me.
NFIB represents 11,000 small business owners across New York who create jobs, strengthen our communities and employ nearly half of our state’s workforce.

I’ve made it a priority to stand up for them and push back against policies that make it harder to grow, compete and succeed here.
I’m grateful to NFIB NY for their support and proud to continue working alongside them to make New York a better place to do business.

title.before: Borrello’s Nourish NY Win Is A Win Both For The Senator And For His District

removed: top of page All Posts Search Borrello’s Nourish NY Win Is A Win Both For The Senator And For His District nate1457 Dec 8, 2021 1 min read Sen.
George Borrello’s pre-Thanksgiving trip to New York City was far from a sight-seeing trip.
The Sunset Bay Republican spent Sunday in Queens to see Gov.
Kathy Hochul sign legislation Borrello sponsored making the Nourish New York farm-to-food bank program permanent.
It’s a notable accomplishment for Borrello, who has earned a reputation for his tough questions and harsh criticism of many Democratic Party priorities in the state capitol.
Residents of the 57th Senate District should be glad Borrello is in Albany asking those tough questions, but his outspokenness could be seen as a hinderance to getting his own legislation passed.
But Borrello, the ranking member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, worked with Sen.
Michelle Hinchey, D-Kingston and Senate Agriculture Committee chairwoman, to progress the bill through the state Senate while also working with Assemblywoman Catalina Cruz, D-Corona.
The Nourish New York program is good for New York farmers and families who need access to fresh food.
It’s good policy.

It’s also good policy for Borrello to show he can work across the aisle on legislation so that Democrats see the local senator is more than just a one-trick pony who spends his days lambasting Democrats but accomplishing little.
Notching legislative wins like the Nourish New York bill is good for Borrello — and by extension, good for the 57th Senate District.

title.after: Bruce Blakeman Joins Borrello, Sempolinski, Republican Candidates to Call for End to New York's Fracking Ban

added: top of page All Posts Search Bruce Blakeman Joins Borrello, Sempolinski, Republican Candidates to Call for End to New York's Fracking Ban lhill5000 Jun 12 3 min read Leaders say New Yorkers are paying the price for failed energy policies through 48 utility rate hikes and electricity costs 70% above the national average OLEAN, N.Y. – Bruce Blakeman, the Republican nominee for Governor of New York, joined State Senator George Borrello, Assemblyman Joe Sempolinski, Republican Comptroller candidate Joseph Hernandez, Republican Lt.

Governor candidate Sheriff Todd Hood, and representatives of New York's energy industry Friday to call for an end to New York's ban on hydraulic fracturing and a return to energy policies focused on affordability, reliability, and economic growth.

The leaders gathered in Olean to highlight what they described as the economic and energy consequences of New York's decade-long ban on fracking despite the state's location atop the Marcellus Shale, one of the largest natural gas formations in the world.
"The solution to New York's affordability crisis is sitting right beneath our feet.

The Marcellus Shale holds more than 9 trillion cubic feet of clean-burning natural gas, but Kathy Hochul's fracking ban keeps that prosperity locked in the ground," said Bruce Blakeman, Republican Candidate for Governor and Nassau County Executive.
"Instead of lowering energy costs, the Hochul administration approved 48 utility rate hikes and raised energy taxes by $4,100.

Meanwhile, Pennsylvania used natural gas to reduce emissions, create hundreds of thousands of high-paying jobs, and save families nearly $9 billion on energy bills last year alone," Blakeman continued.

"As Governor, I will bring fracking back to New York, unleash our energy economy while protecting the environment, and cut utility bills in half." According to speakers, the policy has deprived Southern Tier communities of jobs, investment, and economic opportunity while contributing to some of the highest energy costs in the nation.

Pennsylvania's natural gas and oil industry now supports more than 400,000 jobs, contributes more than $77 billion annually to that state's economy, and has generated nearly $3 billion through its impact fee program for local governments, infrastructure improvements, emergency services, and other projects.

"New York sits atop one of the largest natural gas formations in the world, yet Kathy Hochul and her Democrat colleagues have spent years ensuring New Yorkers cannot benefit from it," said State Senator George Borrello, who represents the 57th District.
"Pennsylvania is just a stone's throw from where we're standing today.
The communities on the other side of that border sit atop the same resource, yet their economy has been transformed by the jobs, investment, and growth that natural gas development has brought.
Here in New York, Kathy Hochul and her party chose radical environmentalism over opportunity.

The result has been energy costs that are 70 percent higher than the national average and growing concerns about the reliability of our electric grid." Speakers also pointed to recent warnings from the New York Independent System Operator regarding dangerously shrinking reserve margins, declining generation capacity, and increasing reliability concerns as electricity demand continues to grow.
"The choice facing New Yorkers could not be clearer," Borrello said.
"We can continue down Kathy Hochul's path of higher utility bills, shrinking energy supplies, and economic decline, or we can choose a new direction.

Bruce Blakeman and our Republican team are ready to unleash New York's energy potential, lower costs for families and businesses, create good-paying jobs, and restore the affordable, reliable energy that is essential to economic growth.

New York's energy crisis was created by bad policy, and it can be solved with new leadership." ### Recent Posts See All Hundreds Turn Out for Blakeman Rally in Dunkirk Borrello Earns Endorsement of Corrections Officers Union Borrello Earns NFIB Endorsement Contact Us Borrello for Senate PO Box 181 Irving, New York 14081 voteborrello@gmail.com 607-438-2701 Connect with us SUBSCRIBE Join Thanks for submitting! george borrello for new york state senate © # PAID FOR BY BORRELLO FOR SENATE AND NYS SENATE REPUBLICAN CAMPAIGN COMMITTEE bottom of page

This is our chance to save New York.
Let's get it done!
