She emphasized her ongoing fight for Oregon families, workers, immigrants, and children, and her efforts to bring down costs and deliver more opportunity for Oregonians.
“We can’t play around with our children’s futures, and we can’t afford to throw away people’s hard-earned dollars,” said Rep.
Bynum.
“The last thing Oregon needs is a rubberstamp for Republicans in Congress.

Tonight was about making sure that the people of CD-5 have a fighter in their corner – and I’m ready to keep giving Washington hell on their behalf.” During the debate, Bynum blasted Adair for rubber-stamping the corruption and harm coming out of the White House and for failing to stand up for Oregon families.

added: Empower Rural Infrastructure I support changing the way Albany distributes water and sewer infrastructure funding to local municipalities from the current grant-based model to a dedicated distribution based on need.

This would immediately reduce expenditures by local governments and ensure greater fairness in how these funds are distributed, especially between urban and rural areas (smaller communities are less likely to have grant writers on staff).
Highway funds (CHIPS) are already distributed this way.
Water and sewer (SWAP) should be, too.
removed: Empower Rural Infrastructure Safe, sufficient and affordable infrastructure is key to economic development and quality of life.

Janet supports increasing housing stocks of all types; lowering energy costs through better regulating NYSEG and AI data centers and thoughtfully increasing renewable energy infrastructure; and changing the way Albany distributes funding to be more equitable for small rural communities like ours.

added: 0 Skip to Content Meet Janet Priorities Events Updates Endorsements Donate Register to Vote Get Involved Open Menu Close Menu Meet Janet Priorities Events Updates Endorsements Donate Register to Vote Get Involved Open Menu Close Menu Meet Janet Priorities Events Updates Endorsements Donate Register to Vote Get Involved Constitution Pipeline threatens upstate, doesn’t lower our costs OpEd / Letter to the Editor Oct 15 Written By Heather Phelps-Lipton As seen in the Thursday, October 8, 2026 Altamont Enterprise To the Editor: Last week I joined the Women’s Water Walk to protest the Constitution Pipeline.
For those who aren’t familiar, the Constitution Pipeline is a proposed 125-mile natural gas (fracked gas) pipeline, which will run through many of our upstate communities.
The pipeline, if built, would connect two other pipelines, sending natural gas through existing infrastructure to other states and New York City.
No new service lines are proposed to be built in the New York counties where this pipeline is proposed.
One of the key priorities listed by developers for this energy is powering AI data centers.

Once again, we rural residents of upstate New York are being asked to host infrastructure that threatens our water, our farmland, and the air we breathe, without even receiving any benefit from this increased risk.
Like so many others, I am concerned about rising energy costs.
But the Constitution Pipeline does not address energy needs in our communities.
It takes land from its current owners via eminent domain.
It endangers the environment and does nothing to lower our energy costs.
And who benefits?
Oil and gas companies.
Data centers.
Corporate greed.
Who loses?
We the citizens, and nature.
The Women’s Water Walk is a two-week-long prayer and protest march through the towns that will be affected by the Constitution Pipeline, and it ended Oct.
6 in Albany.
The day that I spent with the Women’s Water Walk was humbling and enlightening.
Led by indigenous leaders and grandmothers, organizers emphasized the truth that our human world is entirely dependent on the natural world.
We can live without endless AI data centers.
We cannot live without clean water and air.
I oppose the Constitution Pipeline and urge the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, New York state, and any other agency with a stake in this decision to refuse permission to this project.
We need clean, affordable energy that serves human needs and protects our natural world.

OpEd / Letter to the Editor Oct 15 Written By Heather Phelps-Lipton As Seen in the Wednesday, October 7, 2026 Reporter The pain has arrived: Across New York state, hundreds of thousands of us – including many in Delaware County – have lost our health insurance because of federal cuts to the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid.
More cuts are on the way.

Meanwhile, health insurance corporations keep raising their premiums, deductibles, and co-pays, driving even more people off insurance—and stressing out the rest of us with their maddening bureaucracy.
County and local governments are feeling the pain too, as they try to plug the gaps left by federal cuts.
Their budgets are straining to cover the rapidly rising cost of their own employees’ healthcare.
“We’re in trouble,” said Colchester’s supervisor in a front-page story in The Reporter Sept.
The town’s healthcare costs are expected to rise by nearly 18% in 2027.
But a new analysis shows that passage of a single bill – the New York Health Act – could solve this problem.
The analysis found that if this bill is enacted, our towns and school districts would spend 80 to 85% less on employee healthcare.
The county would spend 90 to 95% less.
NYHA would save local governments between 12 and 14% of their total budgets.

The NY Health Act would create a “Medicare for All” healthcare system within New York state, providing expanded health insurance coverage (including vision, dental, and long-term care) for every resident of the state.
Costs would be covered through a statewide progressive payroll tax.
A study of the plan by the Rand Corporation found that despite this expanded coverage, under NYHA 90% of New Yorkers will spend less on healthcare than they do now.
Savings come from bypassing insurance industry bureaucracy and profits.
The NY Health Act might sound pie-in-the-sky, but it isn’t.
The bill has been passed multiple times by the NY State Assembly.
And it’s popular: Recent polls show a majority of Americans now support Medicare for All—and that includes a high percentage of independents and Republicans.
We’re all fed up with our current healthcare system.
Fortunately, this year, people in Delaware County have three candidates for the state legislature who have pledged to support the NY Health Act.

NY State Assembly candidate Janet Tweed, a physical therapist, has a close-up view of our health insurance dysfunction and has been eloquent in her support of the NY Health Act—as has Michele Frazier, who is running for NY State Senate.
Vicki Davis, who is running for Assembly in a district that includes Sidney, Masonville, and Deposit, is also a vocal supporter of NYHA.
If you want to get health insurance companies off your back and support healthcare for all, vote on Nov.

item_pages.value: Jeff Spiegelman for Delaware State Representative #ago DelDOT Traffic Alert: Closure of Big Oak Road between Route 13 and Big Woods Road Smyrna - The Delaware Department of Transportation announces the closure of Big Oak Road between Route 13 and Big Woods Road, starting on Monday, October 26th and continuing through January 9th, 2027 (weather permitting).
The closure is needed to allow for intersection improvements and the installation of new drainage, curbing, and a shared use path.
Detour - All traffic wanting to enter Big Oak Road from US13/South DuPont Boulevard will need to go north on US 13 and use Smyrna Leipsic Road to head west.
At the intersection of Smyrna Leipsic Road and Big Oak Road, turn right to head back east on Big Oak Road to access the closed portion of Big Oak Road or access Big Woods Road.
For more information, please visit www.deldot.gov or the project website at tinyurl.com/3bwt29bp . ...

added: PRESS RELEASE FOR IMMEDIATE DISTRIBUTION OCT 2nd, 2026 JENN MACK CALLS FOR NEW ENFORCEMENT DIVISION TO PROTECT TEXAS AGRICULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURE, FARMERS, AND RANCHERS Campaign to push Legislature and work with Texas Department of Agriculture to safeguard the industry that keeps Texas the nation's agricultural leader SPRING, TX — Texas farmers, ranchers, and the rural communities that depend on them are facing growing pressure from encroaching development, water competition, and land-use conflicts that threaten the infrastructure holding up the state's agricultural economy.
Jenn Mack today called for a new, dedicated enforcement capability to protect that foundation.
"Texas leads the nation in agriculture because generations of farmers and ranchers built it that way,” Jenn said.

“If elected, I will push the Legislature in conjunction with the Texas Department of Agriculture to establish an enforcement division to protect our agricultural infrastructure, our farmers and ranchers, the communities that allow Texas to be the leading agricultural source in the United States.” Contact: Derek Ayala 817-683-4169 info@jennmackfortexas.com 2129 FM 2920, STE 190-319, SPRING, TX 77388 713-364-8065 info@jennmackfortexas.com

title.after: Press Releases

added: PRESS RELEASE FOR IMMEDIATE DISTRIBUTION OCT 2nd, 2026 JENN MACK CALLS FOR DAY-ONE PARTNERSHIP WITH AG TO EXPAND TRANSPARENCY ENFORCEMENT BEYOND WATER REPORTING TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT CONDUCT SPRING, TX — The Texas Attorney General's office has opened a statewide investigation into hundreds of data center developments for failing to comply with mandatory state water-use reporting — with nearly 83% failing or refusing to respond to the state’s mandatory survey.

Across Texas, homeowners, legacy landowners, and multiple organizations are sounding the alarm on a wave of AI data centers, 765kV transmission lines, battery storage sites, and wind and solar farms moving forward with little public input and even less transparency.

Jenn Mack said “This process is broken, and it's moving too fast for anyone to catch the damage before it's done.” The Texas Office of the Attorney General (OAG) has responsibility regarding municipal noncompliance and public transparency.

Actions available to their office include, but are not limited to: Challenging local government actions taken in violation of the Open Meetings Act, filing mandamus actions under the Public Information Act to compel the release of records, or filing quo warranto petitions to challenge officials exceeding their authority.
There have been countless reports of overstepping by City Councils, Economic Development Corporations, and County Officials across our country.
I want Texas to lead the way in transparency and cooperation.
Texans deserve to know what their city councils, economic development corporations, and county governments are doing with public money and public authority.

If elected, one of my first actions as Governor will be to collaborate with the Office of the Attorney General to investigate the numerous complaints of TOMA violations occurring, lack of transparency, and violations of our citizens’ rights.

I will call for an immediate moratorium on 765kV transmission approvals, large-scale battery storage siting, and data centers, both new and in progress, until we can have a special session, putting real enforceable guardrails in place, while assessing the damage already caused to the citizens of Texas — and I will appoint PUC and TCEQ commissioners who will honor that pause.
Citizens are encouraged to contact the Attorney General’s Office and CC our office with their documented TOMA violations.
Our team will add them to an ongoing list held by our campaign office to be made public on our website October 7th.
Contact: Derek Ayala 817-683-4169 info@jennmackfortexas.com 2129 FM 2920, STE 190-319, SPRING, TX 77388 713-364-8065 info@jennmackfortexas.com

added: PRESS RELEASE FOR IMMEDIATE DISTRIBUTION OCT 2nd, 2026 JENN MACK CALLS FOR NEW ENFORCEMENT DIVISION TO PROTECT TEXAS AGRICULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURE, FARMERS, AND RANCHERS Campaign outlines statutory tools already available to address the Texas data center crisis — and the transparency Texans deserve before deals are signed SPRING, TX — There are statutory and constitutional authorities available to the Texas Comptroller’s Office regarding municipal non-compliance, environmental protection, and public transparency that could help with the current Texas data center crisis; Jenn Mack says tools that should be put to work now.
Adding businesses to the Divestment Statute List 2.
Immediate suspension or clawing back grant disbursements of Businesses found in violation and still receiving grants through the Comptroller’s Office 3.

Referring the Issue to the Office of the Attorney General for Fraud and antitrust violations investigation To better tailor this analysis or move forward with a specific inquiry, they may request from developers and cities relevant details regarding: - The specific county, aquifer, or floodplain involved. - The specific developer, local agency, or entities executing the agreements. - Any structural evidence of immediate damage or specific contractual clauses of concern.

If elected, I will direct every state agency under the Governor's authority to make public the terms of any statelevel agreement, incentive, or tax arrangement involving data center developers — and I will publicly call on the Comptroller's Office, the General Land Office, and TCEQ to do the same with records already in their control.
Texans have a right to know which aquifers, floodplains, and counties are being targeted before the deal is signed, not after the wells run dry.

added: PRESS RELEASE FOR IMMEDIATE DISTRIBUTION OCT 2nd, 2026 JENN MACK TO ORDER FIRE SAFETY INSPECTIONS OF DATA CENTERS AND BATTERY STORAGE SITES IN TEXAS ON DAY ONE Campaign cites direct gubernatorial oversight of the Texas Department of Insurance and State Fire Marshal's Office as an immediate tool for landowner safety SPRING, TX — Jenn Mack said, “In accordance with Texas Government Code Sec.

417.008, I will, on my first day in office, direct the Texas Fire Marshal’s Office to conduct examinations of all data centers and battery storage facilities under construction or preparing for construction in the State of Texas.” I will ask for the Texas Department of Insurance to conduct an extensive audit of national reports relating to fires caused by or related to data centers and battery storage facilities across the US to determine our state’s preparedness and risk management protocols.
This audit must be provided before the end of the 2027 general session for our lawmakers to make appropriate decisions related to data center guardrails that they have promised their constituents.
This audit must be conducted using independent research, one without affiliation to the industry and another guided by the industry, for full transparency.

Any data centers or battery storage facilities found to be a significant threat of safety to their local community will be investigated, injunctions filed, and held to compliance by the proper authorities.

added: Home About Platform News Support DONATE DONATE Home About Platform News Support DONATE Thursday, October 15, 2026 More Than 100 Local Elected Officials Across SC-01 Endorse Jenny Costa Honeycutt Mayor Cogswell: “Solving local problems takes a partner in Washington who understands how the work actually gets done on the ground.

That’s why I am supporting Jenny.” CHARLESTON, SC – Jenny Costa Honeycutt, the Republican nominee for South Carolina’s First Congressional District, announced today that she has secured the endorsements of more than 100 local elected officials from communities across the district.

The endorsements – from mayors, city council members, county officials, and state legislators – highlight Costa Honeycutt’s longstanding working relationships in the Lowcountry and her desire to fight for the issues that most impact Lowcountry communities.
“As I have said from the start of my campaign, I am running to serve the people I love and the place I call home,” said Costa Honeycutt.
“Every community in the Lowcountry has its own needs, challenges, and opportunities.
Serving in local government has taught me how important it is to listen to the people closest to those challenges and understand what it takes to get results.

I will not have to learn on the job what the Lowcountry needs.” Among the ten mayors endorsing Costa Honeycutt is Charleston Mayor William Cogswell, who stressed the need for a proven local problem solver in his support.
“Flooding, traffic and the cost of housing are local problems, but solving them takes a partner in Washington who understands how the work actually gets done on the ground,” said Cogswell.
“Our next representative needs to understand these issues firsthand, not learn them on the job.
Jenny has spent years in the details of local government, and she knows the Lowcountry because she was raised here and has served here.
The Lowcountry needs someone in Congress who will show up, do the homework and deliver.

Jenny Costa Honeycutt will do that, and I'm proud to support her.” The full list of local endorsers of Costa Honeycutt are as follows: Mayors: William Cogswell – Charleston Tim Goodwin – Folly Beach Mary Miller for congressional seat in 2026 news article Local Democrat to challenge Mary Miller News article Hundreds protest Trump policies, Miller in Mahomet PRESS RELEASE Jennifer Todd Launches Listening Tour Across Illinois's 15th Congressional District Oct 15 2026 PRESS RELEASE Jennifer Todd Gains Momentum for Illinois 15 Jennifer Todd, Democratic Candidate for Congress in Illinois-15, has outraised any Democratic candidate running who has run against the Republican incumbent Mary Miller.
The end-of-quarter FEC report total is $192,472.81, with contributions from the 3rd quarter totaling $81,432.27.

The campaign has continued raising money since then, and the current total raised as of the morning of October 15th is $203,544 Todd said, “While we are not raising Texas-sized money, we have raised more than any other candidate has against Mary Miller.
More importantly, I am hearing from Democratic, Independent, and Republican voters across the district that they are so happy to be heard.

As a result, they are turning out at events across the district and turning up to support our campaign.” In addition to donor support, Todd is racking up endorsements, including support from her Primary Partners (the candidates she defeated in the primary election): Paul Davis, Randy Raley, and Kyle Nudo.

To date, Todd has been endorsed by: The Justice Coalition Illinois Federation of Teachers (IFT) National Women's Political Caucus (NWPC) Coles County Democratic Central Committee Logan County Democratic Central Committee Citizen Action Liuna Downstate Illinois Laborers' District Council National NOW PAC Illinois AFL-CIO Illinois NOW PAC Illinois Nurses Association Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers & Trainmen Illinois State Legislative Board Warren County Democratic Central Committee She has been recommended by AFSCME.
Todd, a second-generation nurse, mom, daughter of a veteran, raised in a union household, won the Democratic nomination for Congress in the 15th Congressional District.
Her former Democratic primary opponents have subsequently joined together in support of her campaign.
For more information, visit JenTodd2026.us .

added.text: Trump’s Diesel Insult to Lindsey Graham

added: Meet Jesse Issues News Volunteer Contribute News Latest updates from the campaign: 15 Oct Thursday, 9:53 AM · 2026 Trump’s Diesel Insult to Lindsey Graham "I'm focused on the local impact of unaffordable government.
Most, if not all, of our tax burden—from damaging energy policies like CEJA to steep tolls, high state gas taxes, and unaccountable spending on NGOs—originates out of Springfield.
By contrast, the rising cost of diesel fuel is tied directly to the Iran conflict and a domestic shortage of refineries.
The former can be addressed in the short term; the latter requires serious, long-term planning.
What won't fix high diesel prices is a bad deal with Putin.
The proposed supply increase amounts to a single day's worth of fuel—an insignificant gain.
Such a deal would reward a dictator whose track record proves he cannot be trusted, especially while he actively targets civilians and critical infrastructure.

The Russian economy is already buckling under the weight of wartime spending; throwing Putin an economic lifeline will only prolong the war." Read more 13 Oct Tuesday, 10:38 AM · 2026 Democrats Have No School Choice Excuse If Illinois political leadership passes on this credit, the students who would benefit the most will be left behind.

added: Meet Jesse Issues News Volunteer Contribute The board of Illinois Family Action is pleased to endorse the following candidates in the 2026 General Election.

These candidates emerged as those who will best support and uphold pro-family and pro-faith principles. https://illinoisfamilyaction.org/2026/10/ifas-2026-general-election-endorsements-2/ Illinois Family Action "In House District 83, Democratic incumbent Matt Hanson, a former Kane County Board member from Montgomery, is running for his third term against Republican Jesse Rodriguez, a small-business owner from Aurora.
Hanson's performance in Springfield has been adequate but not distinguished.
Rodriguez got into the race out of his frustrations with Springfield's approach to small business.
His campaign is centered on improving the business climate and restraining government overreach.

He has our endorsement." added: Skip to content About Jill Voting Info Issues News Events Get Involved Donate Instagram Facebook YouTube LinkedIn People over politics Newsletter • October 15, 2026 Good governance isn’t partisan Lately, politics have become too much about picking a side.
That’s not how I approach public service.
I believe in listening, looking at the facts and making decisions based on what’s best for the people I represent — not governing from the extremes.
That’s how I led Greenwich’s finance board.
I worked across party lines and was unanimously elected by both parties to serve as chair.
As a leader, I don’t ask whether an idea comes from a Democrat or Republican.
I ask whether it makes sense and if it’s right for the town.
I’ll bring that same approach to Hartford.

Here’s what I believe is important: practicing fiscal discipline and keeping taxes low; supporting strong public schools; fostering a healthy business environment; protecting local zoning; and taking care of our neighbors.
I’m not running to represent the left or the right.
I’m running to represent you.

PRESS RELEASE Benson Wins Debate, Exposes John James’ Record of Putting Himself Ahead of Michigan Families For the second time, Jocelyn Benson took the debate stage tonight and shared her plans to lower costs, raise wages, and end corruption.
Meanwhile, John James offered a whole lot of excuses for a record that has made life more expensive for Michigan families.

Read more Oct 15 2026 PRESS RELEASE MICHIGAN CHRONICLE: Jocelyn Benson Is the Clear Choice for Governor of Michigan Today, Michigan Chronicle, the state’s largest Black newspaper, endorsed Secretary of State and Democratic nominee for Governor Jocelyn Benson to be the next governor.

Citing her proven record as an effective administrator, her life-long dedication to protecting civil rights, and her drive to secure economic prosperity for all Michiganders, they named her the “clear choice” in this race.

She has real plans to lower costs, raise wages and protect the freedoms Michiganders care about.
She knows who she works for, and she’s ready to take on anyone to get results for Michigan families.
“John James showed up with the same old playbook: lie about his record, dodge responsibility, and hope voters don’t notice that his votes in Washington have helped make life more expensive.

“Jocelyn is running to do the job.

Capitol Police Officers Endorse Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Jocelyn Benson Statement on Donald Trump Pausing Federal Dollars for Thousands of Working of Michiganders PRESS RELEASE ICYMI: Jocelyn Benson Launches Gubernatorial Campaign with Momentum and Support Across Michigan PRESS RELEASE End Citizens United Endorses Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE EMILYs List Endorses Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Michigan State Lawmakers Endorse Jocelyn Benson for Governor PRESS RELEASE Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson Announces Run for Governor Oct 15 2026 PRESS RELEASE MICHIGAN CHRONICLE: Jocelyn Benson Is the Clear Choice for Governor of Michigan Today, Michigan Chronicle, the state’s largest Black newspaper, endorsed Secretary of State and Democratic nominee for Governor Jocelyn Benson to be the next governor.

Citing her proven record as an effective administrator, her life-long dedication to protecting civil rights, and her drive to secure economic prosperity for all Michiganders, they named her the “clear choice” in this race.
As Secretary of State, Jocelyn stood up to anyone — no matter how wealthy or powerful — who threatened the rights and safety of Michiganders and fixed broken systems costing people time and money.
That’s exactly what she’ll do as governor.

According to the Chronicle, Jocelyn “brings … concrete policy proposals to lower household costs, and a steadfast commitment to government transparency,” and is the only candidate in this race with a plan to tackle the Black maternal health crisis, build generational wealth, and ensure every kid has access to a quality education that prepares them to take on the world.
Meanwhile, John James has spent his time in Congress voting repeatedly to raise costs and hurt Michiganders.

As Michigan Chronicle made clear, “John James’s underlying policy framework … disproportionately harm[s] Black and low-income families.” Key point: “Benson brings a proven track record of administrative transformation, concrete policy proposals to lower household costs, and a steadfast commitment to government transparency.

More importantly, she understands that for Black Michiganders, effective governance is a matter of survival, wealth-building, and unyielding civil rights defense, whereas James hasn’t demonstrated that in his voting record throughout his time in Washington.” In case you missed it… Michigan Chronicle: Endorsement: Jocelyn Benson Is the Clear Choice for Governor of Michigan [Editorial Board, 10/15/26] Benson brings a proven track record of administrative transformation, concrete policy proposals to lower household costs, and a steadfast commitment to government transparency.

More importantly, she understands that for Black Michiganders, effective governance is a matter of survival, wealth-building, and unyielding civil rights defense, whereas James hasn’t demonstrated that in his voting record throughout his time in Washington.
Governance, Benson said in her interview with the Michigan Chronicle, is not just about passing laws; it is about making government work efficiently for everyday people.
When Benson assumed office as Secretary of State, the department was infamous for multi-hour wait times and systemic inefficiencies.

Over her eight years, she transformed a notoriously broken agency into a customer-centric operation, noting that she was able to “take something that seemed unfixable and fix it” and see government as something that can “show up for you”.
This distinction between policymaking and execution is critical for working-class residents and Black families who interact with state agencies daily.
Whether navigating state health benefits or renewing a driver’s license, bureaucratic friction disproportionately harms those with the fewest resources to spare.
Benson has shown her ability to fix broken state systems, and it provides confidence that she can reform complex agencies like the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).

She’s also pledged to voluntarily subject the Governor’s office to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), issue executive orders mandating agency compliance, and push for comprehensive sunshine laws. [...] Black Michiganders can’t afford abstract political promises.
We require targeted structural interventions.

Benson’s agenda speaks directly to the specific, systemic disparities that Black families face in this state: · Treating Black Maternal Health as a Crisis: The disproportionately high rate of pregnancy-related deaths among Black women in Michigan is an ongoing tragedy.
Benson has stated she will prioritize and address this crisis with urgency.

Her plan includes expanding Medicaid-covered doula and midwife services, requiring bias training for maternal health providers, and improving access to culturally competent healthcare. · Expanding Generational Wealth and Homeownership: Benson has connected economic opportunity and homeownership to the unfinished work of the civil rights movement.

To help Black families build financial security, she has proposed expanded tax credits to assist first-time homebuyers with down payments and efforts to lower housing costs. · Empowering Black-Owned Businesses: Recognizing Black-owned businesses as a priority, Benson has committed to removing barriers to entrepreneurship and increasing access to capital and state contracts.

She proposed directing more state economic development resources toward local entrepreneurs instead of large, out-of-state companies. · Equitable Public School Funding: Recognizing that the current system fails urban districts, Benson has pledged to replace Michigan’s one-size-fits-all school funding approach with a weighted, needs-based system.

This will direct additional resources toward low-income students and English learners in communities like Saginaw and Benton Harbor. · Strengthening Voting Rights: Benson has committed to passing a Michigan Voting Rights Act to establish stronger state-level protections against voter suppression and racial discrimination. · A Seat at the Table: Benson pledged that Black Michiganders would have a continued voice in her administration, calling on Black community leaders and residents to help shape her priorities and hold her accountable.

She’s already championed this through the formation on a Black Women’s Coalition based in Detroit. [...] [John James’] legislative record and proposed state policies run counter to the best interests of Black, low-income, and working-class Michiganders: 1.

Corporate Interests over Local Control: During his time in Congress, James voted four times to block local municipalities from placing regulations or guardrails on data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure, while personally purchasing stock in data center companies.
In contrast, Benson’s proposed data center moratorium prioritizes neighborhood air quality and water preservation.
Siphoning Resources from Public Schools: James champions “Education Freedom” tax credit vouchers.

These voucher schemes historically siphon critical funding out of urban public school districts – where the vast majority of Black children are educated – and direct public dollars toward private institutions that lack public oversight.
Safety Nets and Work Requirements: James confirmed his support for imposing strict work requirements on Medicaid and SNAP recipients.
Strict administrative hurdles routinely disenroll working poor families and caregivers due to paperwork red tape, deepening poverty rather than encouraging work.

Tariff Policies: James has consistently supported broad federal tariff strategies that spike raw material costs and consumer prices, threatening Michigan supply chains and auto jobs. [...] Moving our state forward requires leadership that combines operational skill and the desire to look out for the most vulnerable by meeting them where they are.
John James’s underlying policy framework relies on trickle-down economics, public school deregulation, and safety-net reductions that disproportionately harm Black and low-income families.
Jocelyn Benson has proven how she can take complex, neglected public systems and make them work.
Moreover, she offers a specific, structural blueprint designed to protect Black lives, build generational Black wealth, and combat systemic inequities.
For these reasons, the Michigan Chronicle proudly endorses Jocelyn Benson for Governor of Michigan.

added: John Henkelman Receives AFL-CIO Endorsement Jul 25 Written by John Henkelman ‍ ‍ FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE ‍ ‍ MEDIA CONTACTS: ‍ ‍Rebecca Flood Andrews, Rebecca Flood Andrews for Maine House 141, rebecca@rebecca4maine.com , 207-719-0092 ‍ ‍John Henkelman, John for Maine House 143, John@JohnForMaine.com , 207-608-9249 ‍ ‍‍ Maine AFL-CIO Endorses Slate of Candidates for Sanford and Springvale House Districts ‍ ‍ SANFORD, ME - Candidates Rebecca Andrews (House District 141) and John Henkelman (House District 143) announced that they have received the full endorsement of the Maine AFL-CIO for their campaigns to represent the people of Sanford and Springvale in the 133rd Maine Legislature. ‍ ‍ The Maine AFL-CIO, representing over 40,000 working Mainers across the state, grants endorsements to candidates who demonstrate a steadfast commitment to supporting working families, protecting union rights, advocating for fair wages, and addressing the rising cost of living. ‍ ‍ With this unified slate of endorsements, working people in Sanford and Springvale have strong champions in all three local House districts. ‍ ‍ "I am deeply honored to earn the trust and endorsement of the Maine AFL-CIO," said Rebecca Andrews, candidate for House District 141.

added: PRIVACY POLICY & TERMS PRIVACY POLICY: Friends of John Lowery (“we,” “us”) is the candidate committee for John Lowery, candidate for the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 47.
Our address is 326 Sandlin Drive, Lumberton, NC 28358.
Information we collect.
We collect the information you give us, such as your name, email address, mobile phone number, and ZIP code, when you sign up on our website, contribute, or volunteer.
When you make a contribution, we also collect the information North Carolina campaign finance law requires.
How we use it.
We use your information to send campaign updates, event invitations, volunteer opportunities, voting information, and requests for contributions by email, phone, and text message.
We also use it to meet our legal reporting requirements.
Text messaging.
We will not share mobile information with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
We will not distribute or sell your text messaging opt-in data, related personal information, or consent to any third party, except when legally required to do so.
Contributions.
North Carolina law requires us to report certain contributor information to the State Board of Elections, and those reports are public.
Opting out.
Reply STOP to any text message to stop receiving texts.
Click “unsubscribe” in any email to stop receiving emails.

We will not share text messaging originator opt-in data and consent, provided that the foregoing does not apply to sharing (1) with vendors, consultants and other service providers who need access to such information to carry out work on our behalf (and who will not use such information for their own purposes); (2) if we believe disclosure is required by any applicable law, rule, or regulation or to comply with law enforcement or legal process; and (3) if the user consents to our sharing of such information.
Contact.
Friends of John Lowery, 326 Sandlin Drive, Lumberton, NC 28358.
SMS TERMS AND CONDITIONS: Program.
Friends of John Lowery sends text messages with campaign updates, event invitations, volunteer opportunities, voting reminders, and requests for contributions to people who opt in.
Opting in.
You opt in by giving your mobile number through the signup form at johnlowerync.com.
Consent is not a condition of any contribution or purchase.
Message frequency varies and may increase around elections.
To stop, reply STOP at any time.
You’ll receive one message confirming you’ve been unsubscribed, and no further texts unless you sign up again.
For help, reply HELP or email us.
Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
Privacy.
See our Privacy Policy at https://www.johnlowerync.com/privacy.
Msg & data rates may apply.

added: 0 Skip to Content About John Voting Information Issues Get Involved Store News Endorsements Contact Team Moolenaar Updates DONATE Open Menu Close Menu About John Voting Information Issues Get Involved Store News Endorsements Contact Team Moolenaar Updates DONATE Open Menu Close Menu About John Voting Information Issues Get Involved Store News Endorsements Contact Team Moolenaar Updates DONATE About john I am proud to represent Michigan's Second Congressional District.
I currently serve on the House Appropriations Committee and as Chairman of the House Select Committee on China.
In Congress, I have led the fight to stop the Chinese Communist Party from buying American farmland and to protect Michigan jobs.
I have worked to secure the border, cut taxes for working families, and reined in wasteful spending in Washington.
I graduated with a Chemistry Degree from Hope College, later earning a Master’s Degree in Public Administration from Harvard University.
During my career I have been a chemist, school administrator, business developer, and served on the local, state, and federal levels.
This extensive experience allows me to look at policies with a practical lens, not just a political one.
I have lived in Michigan my entire life, raising six kids, and now have four grandchildren.
My wife, Amy, and I are proud to call West Michigan home.

Crane’s Allegiance to Billionaires PRESS RELEASE Nez Helps Cut Ribbon for New Hospital Serving Rural Arizona PRESS RELEASE Nez Slams Crane’s Harmful Policies as Jobs Report Shows Arizona Workers Getting Squeezed PRESS RELEASE Jonathan Nez Issues a Statement in Response to Attack Misidentifying Him PRESS RELEASE Mistake by Trump PAC Mocked by Media Draws More Attention To Nez's Bipartisanship, Surging Campaign PRESS RELEASE GOP Super PACs Pour Over $# Million into AZ-02 as Jonathan Nez Draws Over 75,000 Grassroots Donors Oct 15 2026 PRESS RELEASE GOP Super PACs Pour Over $# Million into AZ-02 as Jonathan Nez Draws Over 75,000 Grassroots Donors FLAGSTAFF, AZ - GOP super PACs are scrambling to save Congressman Eli Crane’s reelection campaign, flooding a district Donald Trump won by 15 points with over $3 million in outside spending , while the grassroots campaign of Jonathan Nez has received over 75,000 unique donors .
Nez recently made an appearance on MSNOW’s The 11th Hour with Ali Velshi , where Nez discussed his plans for working across the aisle to solve Arizona’s complex water problems and lower costs.

Crane, meanwhile, flew with President Trump on Air Force One , the Qatari-gifted jumbo jet valued at an estimated $400 million, to a city outside his district, further proving Crane’s complete disregard for his own constituents and his willingness to cozy up to political elites while his constituents face rising costs, healthcare cuts, and a worsening water crisis. “ I hope Crane was asking Trump to reverse these dangerous Colorado river cuts, but I’m sure he’s asking for millions to fund his campaign because he knows he broke his promises to lower costs, stop endless wars, and release the Epstein files,” said Nez .

“He did it all in the name of cozying up to his billionaire party elites.” The desperate cash infusion from GOP super PACs suggests that former Navajo Nation President Nez's bipartisan campaign, built on tackling the water crisis, tackling corruption, and fighting high costs, is surging.
Polls show Nez is statistically tied with Crane, and up 22 points with independents.

The spending surge follows a disastrous attack ad rollout by Trump-aligned No Going Back PAC Inc. that repeatedly misidentified Nez with his Republican former vice president ahead of Indigenous Peoples’ Day, drawing national attention to Nez’s bipartisan record and the lengths Crane’s billionaire backers will go to protect their seat .

added: Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT More Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT Home About District ISSUES Voting DONATION REQUEST A SIGN CONTACT Queens Congressional Districts Queens does not have one representative in Congress.
The borough is divided across several congressional districts, and each one covers a different set of neighborhoods.
That is why "who is my congressman in Queens" does not have a single answer, and why the reliable way to find yours is by address.
Finding your district and your representative Enter your address at voterlookup.elections.ny.gov to get your congressional district number.
Once you have the number, the House of Representatives directory at house.gov lists the current member for every district in the country, with their office contact details.

The 6th District New York's 6th Congressional District covers central and northeastern Queens, including Flushing, Forest Hills, Rego Park, Elmhurst, Fresh Meadows, Jackson Heights, Kew Gardens Hills, Bayside, Auburndale, Oakland Gardens, Maspeth, Middle Village and Woodside.
Joseph Chou is running for Congress in the 6th District .
You can read where he stands on the issues , or get in touch with the campaign.
This page deliberately does not name the current officeholder.
Whether to name an opponent on the campaign's own site is the campaign's decision, not a website one.

added: Skip to content Meet Justin News Priorities Ready Fall Festival Donate Meet Justin News Priorities Ready Fall Festival Donate October 15, 2026 Ready Report: Candidate Spotlight, Early Voting Coming & Help for Carroll Community… I wanted to share with you some reminders and candidate spotlights about the coming election – it is so important that you go vote for change in Maryland, supporting our Republican team as we try to bring balance back to the state.
Early Voting starts one week from today on October 22 nd , runs through October 29 th and then Election Day is Tuesday, November 3 rd .
Please go vote!
More below…also have an update on state funds our Carroll Delegation secured for Carroll Community College that have now been officially allocated.
Candidate Spotlight One of the most important offices on your ballot, and yet one that gets little attention sometimes, is our Board of Education.
These are non-partisan offices on your ballot, meaning it doesn’t say “Republican” or “Democrat” or other parties.
However, there are clear differences and choices.

In Carroll County, we will be electing three members of our five member Board of Ed- and I am supporting Cleveland Friday , Marsha Herbert and Shannon Hinkhaus who will do a great job standing up for taxpayers, protecting parents’ rights and working to ensure that resources stay focused on the classroom, students and teachers, not eaten up in bureaucracy.
I’d encourage you to click on their names to visit their websites to learn more.
I also represent a small portion of Frederick County and know we have many folks on this email list from there.
I support the “Orange Ballot” candidates there for the four spots up on the Frederick County Board of Ed, Heather Fletcher , Shelley Potter , Geoff Seidel and Tyler Walker .

Electing these seven candidates between Carroll and Frederick would have a strong impact on protecting students, keeping schools focused on academics and results and they are people who won’t advocate for raising taxes either.
ICYMI: Vote AGAINST Question 3 I recently wrote a letter in the Baltimore Sun and Carroll County Times highlighting the importance of voting against Ballot Question #3 on the ballot in November.

This is something that should have the careful consideration of every Marylander as it would change the political landscape of our state long-term, only strengthening the already super-majority party’s numbers.
You can read the full letter by clicking here.
Please join me in voting against Ballot Question #3 in next month’s election.

State Funds Secured by Delegation are Officially Approved for Carroll County On Wednesday, October 7 th , the Maryland Board of Public Works considered and approved $1,905,000 to replace building systems and a building envelope on the main campus of Carroll Community College.
These systems include heating and cooling equipment, the fire alarm system, and the building envelope of Building A.
These replacements will address deferred maintenance issues, improve student comfort, and reduce operating costs.

Ultimately, these repairs will result in increased life-safety protection, additional expansion capability, uniform communication and alarms, improved maintenance and troubleshooting, and more reliable systems.
The Carroll County Delegation, working alongside Carroll Community College, were responsible for securing this key funding through the Capital Budget process during the 2026 Legislative Session.

National Prescription Drug Take Back Day – October 24 th National Prescription Drug Take Back Day is on October 24, providing Maryland residents with an opportunity to safely dispose of unwanted and expired medications.
More information about this day can be found by clicking here.
For residents who need a disposal option before or after the event, MyOldMeds.com offers free, year-round resources for safe medication disposal.
Through the MyOldMeds locator , residents can find 425 secure medication disposal sites across Maryland.
Many of these sites are located in places people already visit regularly, such as pharmacies, grocery stores, and medical clinics.
MyOldMeds.com also has a Maryland resource page that provides information on safely managing medications at home and properly preparing them for disposal.
It is an honor to represent you in the Maryland Senate.
As always, feel free to reach out to my office anytime with questions or concerns.
Please be sure to follow me on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter/X for the most up-to-date information.

added: Skip to content Meet Justin News Priorities Ready Fall Festival Donate Meet Justin News Priorities Ready Fall Festival Donate September 13, 2024 Ready Report: September 11th, MPRP Update & ARC Visit 2,977 people didn’t come home on September 11, 2001.
Many many more lost their lives or were disabled as a result of combing through wreckage to find, rescue, or recover those in the rubble.
I will never forget where I was when I first heard nor the way this entire period made me feel about the blessing of America and the responsibility we have to stand up for our freedoms.
May we pass this on to the generations that are now coming up and may we never forget the sacrifice of so many that day and in the years that followed.
God bless America.

Unknown Entity Attempting to Buy Land Near MPRP Project Route Carroll residents living along the proposed MPRP transmission line project have reported being contacted by an unknown entity requesting to buy their land. possible real estate high pressure sales and scams aimed at capitalizing on fear and uncertainty surrounding the proposed power line routes.

I agree with these suggested steps from Stop MPRP you should take if contacted: “We strongly advise everyone who receives these unsolicited offers to take the following steps: Say No: Do not accept any unsolicited offers for your property.
Notify Local Officials: Send a copy of the offer to your local elected officials.
This helps them understand the questionable practices being used and the potential impact on our community.
Inform Stop MPRP: Email a copy of the offer to Stop MPRP, Inc. at [email protected] .

Your information will help us track these activities and respond appropriately.” I certainly want to hear directly from anyone who is approached in this way, feel free to message me here on Facebook or email my office at [email protected] .
You can read more about this by clicking here.
Ready in the Press – MPRP Opposition Earlier this month, I was on Fox 45 discussing widespread, bipartisan opposition to the MPRP project and calling on Governor Moore to publicly join with us.
It is extremely important that all elected officials stand together in this fight.
Watch by clicking here .
Ready in the Community – ARC of Carroll County On Monday, I had a wonderful visit to the ARC of Carroll County.

Members of our delegation met with their board, were briefed on their progress towards more housing for independent living developmentally disabled adults, programs they’ve been running to help their clients advocate for themselves and gain additional life skills.
We toured their facility and saw lots of amazing clients and staff.
Our delegation has been able to bring capital improvement funds back from Annapolis to help ARC and other DDA providers and we will continue to make that a priority.
I always leave interactions with ARC inspired and encouraged!

Info here: https://secure.anedot.com/republicanclubofcarrollcounty/redwhiteblue2024 October 10 th – Greg Malveaux for Carroll County Board of Education Race to the Finish – final pre-election fundraiser.

added: 0 Skip to Content Just Jennifer for Carroll 2 About My Why Property Tax Cap Question 2 Education: Beyond the classroom Issues Endorsements Team and Events Donate Letters to the Editor Contact Open Menu Close Menu Just Jennifer for Carroll 2 About My Why Property Tax Cap Question 2 Education: Beyond the classroom Issues Endorsements Team and Events Donate Letters to the Editor Contact Open Menu Close Menu About My Why Property Tax Cap Question 2 Education: Beyond the classroom Issues Endorsements Team and Events Donate Letters to the Editor Contact Beyond the Classroom… There is more to school education than just funding.
Having extracurricular activities and programs is vital to developing successful caring adults along with the classroom work.
Best Buddies is one such program and every high school should have a chapter.
Thanks for leading the way in Carroll 2 Kennett HS!!
Go to their website New Hampshire - Best Buddies International and consider sponsoring a chapter and/or participating in one of their events.
Background: While serving as the PTSA President during my son’s junior and senior year of high school, a conversation led to the discussion of starting a Best Buddies Chapter.

It was an easy yes for me to engage with contacting the organization, finding a fabulous 1st Vice Principal to sponsor along with other teachers, engage the PTSA in providing funds for t-shirts, etc… See the growth of all students who are partnered with others and building beautiful relationships beyond the classroom still warms my soul thinking about.

Kennett High School Football O͏c͏t͏o͏b͏e͏r͏ ͏1͏0͏ ͏a͏t͏ ͏9͏:͏4͏1͏ ͏A͏M͏ · In ONE WEEK we play for something BIGGER than football… Best Buddies, the world’s largest organization dedicated to ending the social, physical, and economic isolation experienced by people living with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD), provides everything from integrated employment opportunities to family support and inclusive living programs for the more than 200 million people living with IDD worldwide.
In 2023, Dave Hausman of Big Dave’s Bagels & Deli teamed up with Kennett High School to bring Best Buddies New Hampshire to the Mount Washington Valley.
Since then, the Kennett High School Chapter has welcomed nearly 100 students to the organization.
Through the One-to-One Friendship Program, students with and without IDD have formed meaningful, lasting friendships.
Thanks to the Leadership Development Program, students with and without IDD have learned what it takes to become leaders, public speakers, and advocates for diversity and inclusion.
This year, Kennett Football is proud to raise money for the Kennett chapter of this very worthy organization.
Join us Saturday, October 17th for the first Kennett Cares Game which will feature a halftime Punt, Pass, and Kick Competition, along with even more exciting activities.
Players are currently collecting pledges and will continue to do so through game day!
Can’t make the game?
Don’t know a player?
Not to worry!
Donations can be made right on our fundraising website at https://kennett-football-boosters.square.site/ As always, thank you for your continued support of Kennett Football!!
Copied from their Facebook page.

added: Skip to content Home Meet Kasie In Action On the Issues Newsroom Contact The Team Financials Statewide Tour: Upcoming Events X Donate Now The Cold Shoulder Mainstream media has us in a blackout.
We’re working hard to overcome it.
It’s hard to write this post because I certainly don’t want to come off as whining or criticizing people for doing their jobs.
I know people have made some efforts for me.
After I tweeted to Judi Gatson and Greg Adaline, they included me in their election night coverage during the GOP runoff.
Then, weirdly, my part of the show was cut out of the YouTube post.
When questioned, their news director said the live feed went down right then, so YouTube didn’t have the segment.
My campaign manager watched the live feed on YouTube and saw my interview as it aired.
We’re getting the cold shoulder from traditional media.
I reached out to the Post & Courier’s Pee Dee reporter and spent a lovely 30 minutes with her during which she recorded our conversation and said she’d work up an article.
That was August 13th.
Nothing has ever been posted.
Then I had a phone interview with The State’s reporter.
Another lovely, recorded conversation, with the conclusion that an article would be written.
That was September 3rd.
Nothing has ever been posted.
The two young women reporters with whom I spoke are not to blame.
I feel certain it’s their editors who decided not to waste the space on a Libertarian.
Press coverage for Jermaine Johnson at the State House I have been campaigning since March 29, 2025.
Here’s a link to a banger of a speech I delivered on very short notice at the Statehouse in August of last year.
It’s not like we’re not trying.
It’s that they’re ignoring us.
We want to reach as many voters as possible.
We know we can do that with traditional media.
Despite “new” media heralding the end of local news, local television, and all things traditional, turns out they still have a wide reach.
How do I know?
My mother-in-law called me after the WIS mention.
“Kasie!
You were on TV!” Being on TV is still a big deal.
Even if they pronounce your name wrong. ::facepalm:: We have been sending weekly media alerts for months.
Telling all the news outlets where I will be all week long.
No one has shown up.
At the SCETV debate, we knew the Republican and Democrat candidates were going to ignore me.
They ignored me in their social media posts leading up to the event.
Just kept talking about how they were going to debate each other.
Then, on stage, neither ever acknowledged me or mentioned me by name.
They used the constant snipes at one another to tack # seconds on to every response so they kept getting to speak for # seconds and I kept getting just 60.
Their strategy worked, they got significantly more air time than me.
Our strategy worked, too.
I stayed out of the fray, answered the questions, told real stories and gave real solutions.
A few times I referenced what they’d said, but never by name and so when they asked for rebuttal to my remarks, they were denied.
Then we went to the media spin room and I was much more comfortable on equal footing with my peers and delivered a few great moments there.
In the “spin room” after the debate on SCETV Sunday, October 11th; none of the footage has ever been posted.
None of those ever made it to coverage either.
Except one article that took two of my quotes, fact checked them, and wrote a piece making me sound like a liar and Annie Andrews like an expert.
Awesome.
Thing is, when you know a lot about a topic, it’s hard to get the answer out in a minute.
And when I said, “No one will buy our debt,” that was true #ago.
But last Thursday, a bunch of 30-year bonds were gobbled up by foreign investors.
The point of the comment was to illustrate how bad our debt is.
The fact check made it seem like the buying of the bonds proved me wrong.
It doesn’t.
They bought the bonds because yields went up and so now our debt is even more expensive than it was before the bonds were sold.
When you know a lot, it’s hard to give short answers.
When you know nothing, you say basically nothing.
Okay, back to the media thing.
So I wasn’t prepared for the blackout to be so complete, but of the news outlets that covered the debate, many didn’t put me in the story.
Wait, what?
You didn’t tell the story about the “only grown up on the stage” who “gave actual answers to the questions” and “didn’t just sling mud” (those are quotes from Facebook comments).
Apparently the Libertarian looking like the only adult in the room wasn’t the story the traditional media wanted to push.
Check out the headlines and links below for evidence.
The exception was our new friends at FOX Carolina who not only told the whole story but dispatched a camera crew to my meet-and-greet in Greenville on Monday night.
So thank you, FOX Carolina.
In the most egregious post-debate story, this article talked about how the Democrat and Republican spent the entire debate talking about how unqualified the other one was.
And yet, there I was, on stage, imminently qualified, and actually answering the questions.
The article reduced my presence to a “oh, she was there, too.” Infuriating.
See my tweet.
My response to a ridiculous “news” article about the debate The laziest story about Sunday night’s debate was the two of them sniping at each other.
Yet it’s the story every outlet ran.
Come on, journalists, do better.
As I told the outlet linked above, 22 year-old sports writer me could have written a better game story than that.
So what should we do?
My campaign has been relying on independent media and sharing all the links and highlights all over our channels.
And we’re asking folks to re-post, re-tweet, and re-blog everything we put out to extend it into your networks, too.
Maybe the digital landscape will give us some ground we’re not getting from TV coverage.
A lot of the mainstream press is behind a paywall, so that could work to our advantage if we show up on blogs and other free news sources.
But I’m also on the road meeting people in real life.
Not an organized event that’s all about Kasie.
Community forums where I get to listen and learn about you .
Small group meetings where I get to learn what’s keeping you up at night.
What worries you about the future?
What’s hitting your bank account the hardest?
What do you think I should do about it?
Not me on a stage, arriving one minute before the thing starts, speaking scripted talking points into a microphone, accepting applause, and disappearing before the questions start flying.
But me walking the streets in these towns, knocking on business doors and introducing myself.

Visiting the big events they have – Red Rose Festival in Lancaster, Pageland Watermelon Festival, Uniquely Union, Newberry Oktoberfest, Westminster Bigfoot Festival – and enjoying the fun and joy people get from their community coming together.
We’re sharing our pride in South Carolina.
And that’s so powerful to me that I wish I could bottle it, shake it up, and spray it all over the polls and the political machinery that keeps telling ya’ll I can’t possibly win.
The Path to Victory is Simple: We do this Together.
This election is plurality voting.
That means most votes wins.
And you have one vote to spend.
I won’t tell you how to do it.
I think that’s your freedom, liberty, and autonomy.
I will just say that if I earn enough votes, I can win.
And if enough of us believe it, vote it, and trust our fellow South Carolinians to do the same, we’re going to make history.
Again.
And apparently that’s scaring some establishment folks who have ramped up their spending, ramped up their commercials, and started emailing me to drop out or risk electing the wrong bad candidate.
It’s even gotten the media to ignore me harder, if such a thing were possible.
We will stay the course.
I didn’t get into this to play political games.
I got into this to fix the national debt.
You would think that goal was met with the way the debt is in the news.

But it’s popular now because everyone is campaigning and it’s a popular campaign thing to say, “I’m concerned about the debt,” knowing full well that 1) your party did this (both parties are complicit) and 2) you will never, ever get anyone to talk about the debt after November 3rd.
No one except me.
I told ReZsaun Lewis last week that I will stomp all over the Capitol knocking on doors until Congress gets serious about the debt.
I’ve been saying that the skills to campaign are not the same skills to govern.
The second truism here is that spending is not viability.
Money raised, size of the team, ads, signs, all that stuff cannot replace hard work.
And I promise I won’t get outworked.
Not on the campaign trail and not in Washington.
I’ll be working when the cameras aren’t on.
When the social media cheerleaders aren’t cheering.
When things get hard, and they will, I’ll keep working.
I don’t need media witnesses.
I have all of you as my witness.
So thanks for showing up and thanks for being in this with me.
Ready to get in the game?
We could use your help.

Donate Privacy Policy Effective Date: August 14, 2026 About This Policy This Privacy Policy explains how Friends of Kathleen Clendaniel collects, uses, and shares information submitted through this website.
In this policy, “we,” “us,” and “our” refer to Friends of Kathleen Clendaniel.

Information We Collect We may collect information that you choose to provide, including your first and last name, email address, message, volunteer interests, and any other information you submit through a campaign form.

Our website platform and service providers may also collect technical information such as your browser type, device information, Internet Protocol address, pages viewed, referring website, and information collected through cookies or similar technologies.
Donations Campaign contributions are processed through ActBlue rather than directly through this website.
Information submitted on ActBlue is governed by the ActBlue Privacy Policy and ActBlue’s other applicable terms.

How We Use Information We may use information to respond to questions and requests, send campaign news and updates to people who choose to receive them, coordinate volunteers and events, operate and improve the website, comply with campaign finance requirements and other applicable laws, and protect the rights, safety, and operations of the campaign and others.

How Information May Be Shared We may share information with vendors and service providers that help us operate the website, communicate with supporters, manage campaign activities, process contributions, or comply with legal obligations.
We may also disclose information when required by law, legal process, or a government authority, or when reasonably necessary to protect the campaign, website visitors, or others.
Mobile Messaging Mobile information, including text messaging opt in data and consent, will not be sold, rented, or shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
This information may be shared only with service providers necessary to operate and deliver the messaging program.
Message frequency may vary, up to one message per week.
Message and data rates may apply.
You may opt out of text messages at any time by replying STOP.
For help, reply HELP or contact info@katieclendaniel.com .
Message and data rates may apply.
Your Choices You may unsubscribe from campaign emails by using the unsubscribe link in an email or by contacting us at info@katieclendaniel.com .
You may request that we review or update information you previously submitted by contacting us.
Third Party Websites This website includes links to third party websites, including ActBlue, social media platforms, and government election resources.
We are not responsible for the privacy or security practices of those websites.
Their own privacy policies apply when you visit them.
Security We use reasonable measures to protect information under our control.
No website, electronic transmission, or storage system can be guaranteed to be completely secure.
Please do not send sensitive personal or financial information by email.
Children’s Privacy This website is not directed to children under thirteen, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under thirteen.
Changes to This Policy We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time.
Changes become effective when the revised policy is posted on this website.
Contact Us Questions about this Privacy Policy may be directed to info@katieclendaniel.com or 410-205-4770.
Paid for by Friends of Kathleen Clendaniel, Cathy Frey, Treasurer.
Approved by Katie Clendaniel.

She grew up in Trappe, went to school in Cambridge, and is raising her daughter here.
She knows rent, mortgages, and health care keep climbing faster than paychecks.
For twenty years, she’s helped Shore communities turn local priorities into funded projects.
In the State Senate, she’ll bring down housing and health care costs, strengthen our schools, and bring good-paying jobs home.

26CLN001 S T A T E S E N ATE D IST R IC T 37 good for the Shore Katie knows what it’s like to sit at the kitchen table and choose between the power bill and groceries.
No Shore family should have to make that choice.

In the State Senate, Katie will fight to lower your utility bills by making big data centers and powerful corporations pay the full cost of the electricity and grid upgrades they need, instead of passing those costs onto you.
She’ll work to support our schools and bring more doctors closer to home.
Katie has already helped secure more than $9 million for projects and programs here on the Shore.
In Annapolis, she brought home funding for local priorities, worked to address the housing shortage, and helped create a new fund to support downtown Main Street organizations and small businesses.
That’s how Katie leads: bringing people together, solving problems, and delivering results for the Shore, not playing partisan games.
Data centers should pay for the power they use, not you.

Find answers to common questions about casting your ballot in Maryland.
How do I return my mail ballot?
Follow the instructions included with your ballot and sign the required oath.
If you mail your ballot, it must be postmarked on or before November 3.
A ballot placed in a drop box or delivered in person must arrive by 8 p.m. on November 3.
You cannot return a voted ballot online, by email, or by fax.
Read the mail voting instructions.
Can I still register to vote?
Eligible Maryland residents can register during early voting at an early voting center in their county, or on Election Day at their assigned polling place.
Bring a document proving where you live, such as an MVA license or ID, paycheck, bank statement, or utility bill.
See registration and address guidance.

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases As Arizona Tunes In to the World Cup, Katie Hobbs Places Six-Figure English and Spanish Ad Buy Tuesday, June 16, 2026 PHOENIX – As Arizona tunes in to the World Cup, Gov.
Katie Hobbs recently placed a six-figure digital and streaming buy to air both English- and Spanish-language ads during the games.

The ads “Work” and “No Se Rinde” are playing across Arizona through the end of the World Cup on July 19, as part of a multi-million-dollar statewide media campaign focused on meeting Arizonans where they are.
The World Cup highlights stories of resilience, hard work, and what we can accomplish when we support each other as a team.
It’s a story Katie Hobbs knows well.

Both spots show how Katie Hobbs’ working-class background — from driving for Uber to support her family to helping domestic violence survivors rebuild their lives through social work — motivates her as governor to fight to lower costs, erase medical debt, reduce prescription drug prices, and create good-paying jobs across Arizona.

“The World Cup is one of the biggest events in the world, and Arizona families will be tuning in at watch parties and carne asadas in every corner of our state,” said Nicole DeMont, Katie Hobbs’ Campaign Manager.
“By placing these ads during one of the most-watched events of the year, Katie Hobbs is meeting Arizonans where they are and talking about the issues that matter most in their daily lives.

While Washington continues to push chaotic and expensive policies, Katie is focused on lowering costs, expanding affordable housing, and rewarding the work ethic of Arizona families fighting to get ahead.” Watch “Work” here and “No Se Rinde” here and read a full transcript of both below: WATCH “WORK”: HOBBS: My parents didn’t make a lot of money.
My sister and I started working and helping out early.
VO: Governor Katie Hobbs.
She worked fast food and drove Uber to get by.
Helped families in need as a social worker.
VO: As governor, she balanced the budget without raising taxes.
Expanding school lunches and community college scholarships.
Reducing electricity bills and cutting red tape to build more affordable housing.
HOBBS: And I’ll keep working to make Arizona work better for you.

WATCH “NO SE RINDE”: VO: Katie Hobbs… es la mamá que manejó para Uber, decidida a sacar adelante a sus hijos. ( Katie Hobbs… she’s the mom who drove for Uber because she was determined to take care of her kids.) VO: Hobbs… es la trabajadora social que ayudó a cientos de mujeres a reconstruir sus vidas tras la violencia doméstica.
(Hobbs… is the social worker who helped hundreds of women stand on their own after surviving domestic violence.) VO: Eso explica por qué no se rinde.
Hobbs luchó por: ( That explains why she doesn’t back down.
Hobbs fought to:) Cancelar millones en deudas médicas.
(Erase millions in medical debt.) Reducir el costo de medicamentos.

(Lower the cost for prescription drugs.) Y crear oportunidades para trabajos mejor pagados. ( And open doors to better-paying jobs.) VO: Katie Hobbs… porque defender a nuestras familias es lo que hace. ( Katie Hobbs… because defending our families is what she does.) title.after: “De Puro Sudor”: New Spanish-Language TV and Digital Ads Highlight Gov. Hobbs’ Record of Standing Up for Arizona Workers - Katie Hobbs for Governor

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases “De Puro Sudor”: New Spanish-Language TV and Digital Ads Highlight Gov.
Hobbs’ Record of Standing Up for Arizona Workers Friday, September 11, 2026 PHOENIX – Today, Gov.

Katie Hobbs’ campaign and the Navajo County Democratic Committee released a new Spanish-language ad, “ De Puro Sudor ” (“Drenched in Sweat”), highlighting Katie Hobbs’ record of lowering costs, cutting taxes, and putting money back in the pockets of working families. “ De Puro Sudor ” features small business owner Alex Macias, who took over the furniture store his parents founded and credits Katie Hobbs’ firsthand understanding of Arizona families’ struggles as the driving force behind the results she’s delivered.

Every year in office, Hobbs has worked across the aisle to cut taxes for small businesses, veterans, seniors, and families, eliminating taxes on rent, tips, and overtime pay while fighting to lower costs and help small businesses grow.

“Katie Hobbs believes Arizonans who work hard every day to build a better life for their families deserve someone fighting just as hard for them,” said Michael Beyer, Communications Director for the Hobbs campaign.

“That’s why she’s cut taxes for small businesses and middle-class families and worked across the aisle to lower costs — because hardworking Arizonans deserve a fair shot to get ahead.” The Hobbs campaign has prioritized early, robust communication to the Latino community in its paid media program.

These new ads build on a previously announced multi-million-dollar Spanish buy highlighting how Katie Hobbs’ working-class background — from driving for Uber to support her family to helping domestic violence survivors rebuild their lives through social work — motivates her as governor to fight to lower costs, erase medical debt, reduce prescription drug prices, and create good-paying jobs across Arizona.
She also launched Familias Primero, a coalition of Latino leaders, community members, and local elected officials working to re-elect her.
Watch “De Puro Sudor” here .
Full transcript below: WATCH “DE PURO SUDOR”: VO: Mis padres construyeron este negocio… My parents built this business… VO: con el sudor de su frente.
Y nunca perdieron la fe.
With the sweat of the brow.
And they never lost faith.
VO: Ahora, este sueño… y la responsabilidad… recaen sobre mí.
Today, the dream, the responsibility, falls on me.
VO: La gobernadora Katie Hobbs sabe lo que es luchar… Governor Katie Hobbs knows what it’s like to struggle.
VO: Tiene sentido común.
Está luchando para bajar los costos.
She has common sense.
She’s fighting to lower costs.
VO: Hobbs recortó los impuestos para las pequeñas empresas… Hobbs cut taxes for small businesses… VO: y para la clase media.
And the middle class.
VO: Para todos los que trabajan con el sudor de su frente… For everyone who works by the seat of the brow… VO: Katie Hobbs está de nuestro lado.
Katie Hobbs is on our side.

added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases “Dinerito Extra”: New Spanish-Language TV and Radio Ads Spotlight How Gov.
Hobbs Cut Taxes for Working Arizonans Wednesday, August 12, 2026 PHOENIX – Today, Gov.

Katie Hobbs’ campaign and the Navajo County Democratic Committee released new Spanish-language TV and radio ads, “ Dinerito Extra ” (“Extra Cash”), spotlighting her work to eliminate taxes on tips and overtime pay, cutting taxes for Arizona’s working families. “ Dinerito Extra ” showcases the hardworking Arizonans who power our state and depend on tips to make ends meet — from restaurant workers and delivery drivers to musicians, skilled trades, and creative professionals — and highlights how Gov.
Hobbs delivered real relief for them.

By working across the aisle to negotiate a bipartisan budget she signed into law, she eliminated taxes on tips and overtime pay, putting more money directly into the pockets of working families across Arizona.
“Katie Hobbs knows what it’s like to stretch every dollar because she’s lived it,” said Michael Beyer, Communications Director for the Hobbs campaign.
“She’s worked two and three jobs to make ends meet, so she knows that every dollar counts when you’re trying to pay rent or put food on the table.

That’s why she fought for middle-class tax cuts to eliminate tax on tips and overtime pay, and put more money back in working families’ pockets.” Watch “Dinerito Extra” here and listen to “Dinerito Extra (radio version)” here .
Full transcript below: WATCH “DINERITO EXTRA”: VO: ¿Eres mesero, cantinero, guardia o el héroe de la cocina?
Are you a waiter, bartender, bouncer, or the hero of the kitchen?
VO: ¿Repartes pedidos—comida… o un compa pasado de copas?
Do you deliver orders — food… or a buddy who has had a few too many?
VO: ¿Cantas de charro con todo y bigote?
Do you sing mariachi in full charro gear, mustache and all, even if it’s fake?
VO: ¿O haces magia con uñas, cabello o piel?
Or do you perform magic on nails, hair, or skin?
VO: Con Katie Hobbs, las propinas ya no pagan impuestos.
Cero.
Nada.
With Katie Hobbs, tips are no longer taxed.
Zero.
Nada.
VO: Ese dinerito extra… se queda contigo.
That extra little cash… stays with you.
VO: Porque Katie Hobbs sabe lo que es chambear duro.
Because Katie Hobbs knows the meaning of hard work.
VO: Y está enfocada en el presupuesto familiar, para que la lana te rinda más.
And she’s focused on the family budget, so your hard-earned dollar goes a little bit farther.

LISTEN TO “DINERITO EXTRA”: VO: Buenas noticias para todos los que le chambean duro Great news for everyone working hard out there… VO: No importa si eres mesero, cantinero, o trabajas en la cocina sacando pedidos sin parar… It doesn’t matter if you are a waiter, a bartender, or back in the kitchen cranking out orders non-stop… VO: Si repartes comida…o manejas a alguien que ya se pasó de copas… If you deliver food… or drive someone home who’s had a few too many… VO: Si cantas de charro… If you sing in a mariachi band… VO: O trabajas en uñas, cabello o tatuajes que cuentan historias… Or work doing nails, hair, or tattoos that tell a story.
VO: La Gobernadora Katie Hobbs eliminó los impuestos en las propinas.
Governor Katie Hobbs eliminated taxes on tips.
VO: Así de claro: Cero.
Nada.
Plain and simple: Zero.
Nada.
VO : Ese dinerito extra… se queda contigo.
That little extra money… it stays with you.
VO: Pero sí, ya sé – no todos viven de propinas.
But yeah, I know — not everyone lives off tips.
VO: Por eso Katie Hobbs también eliminó impuestos al pago de horas extra.
That’s why Katie Hobbs also eliminated taxes on overtime pay.
VO: Porque esas horas de más…son tiempo lejos de tu familia.
Because those extra hours… mean time away from your family.
VO: Y gracias a la nueva ley de Hobbs en Arizona, ese dinerito se queda en tu bolsillo también.
And thanks to the new Hobbs law in Arizona, that money now stays in your pocket too.
VO: Porque en esta economía, nos toca jalar juntos.
Because in this economy, we have got to stick together.
VO: Katie Hobbs: enfocada en el presupuesto familiar, pa’ que la lana te rinda más.
Katie Hobbs: focused on the family budget, so your money stretches further.
