added: Meet Katie Meet John Store Join Email Signup Volunteer Text Message Updates Voter Information Updates Election Updates 2026 Press Releases In the News Contribute Campaign Updates - Press Releases Katie Hobbs Campaign Announces Historic $6 Million Investment in Latino Voter Outreach and Turnout Thursday, October 15, 2026 Investment includes Spanish-language paid media, bilingual field and mail programs, Familias Primero coalition, and events across the state PHOENIX – Today, the Katie Hobbs campaign announced a historic $6 million total investment in Latino voter outreach and turnout across Arizona, spanning paid media, organizing, direct mail, communications, and community engagement to reach and mobilize Latino voters ahead of Election Day.
That investment reaches across every arm of the campaign.

Since the beginning of the campaign, Hobbs has invested in English- and Spanish-language mail and campaign literature, hired Spanish-speaking organizers and communications staff, regularly engaged Spanish-language media, and met directly with Latino voters, community leaders, and small-business owners across Arizona.

This builds on the campaign’s historically early investment in Spanish-language television, radio, digital, and streaming advertising, as well as English-language advertising that reaches Latino audiences.
“Latino families are an essential part of Arizona, and earning their votes means showing up, listening, and talking about the issues that matter in their everyday lives,” said Katie Hobbs.
“That’s what we’ve done throughout this campaign, and it’s what I’ve done as governor.

While Washington is driving up costs, I’ve remained laser-focused on cutting costs for Arizona families, and in a second term, I’ll keep fighting to make our state more affordable.” Hobbs’ first interview after launching the re-election campaign and the first interview announcing Hobbs’ running mate was with Univision.

In July, Hobbs launched Familias Primero as the first coalition of her re-election campaign, bringing together more than 60 Latino leaders, community members, labor leaders, and elected officials from across Arizona to organize and mobilize Latino voters.
Hobbs has also met directly with Latino small business owners to hear how rising costs are affecting their businesses and the families they serve.
In March, she visited Latino-owned food trucks at Comida Park in Tucson to hear firsthand how rising food and fuel costs were cutting into small businesses’ bottom lines.

In August, Hobbs and her running mate, John Giles, visited La Purísima Bakery in Glendale and spoke directly with managers about how rising costs were affecting the longtime Mexican bakery’s day-to-day operations and ability to thrive.
Hobbs has also made Spanish-language paid media central to her campaign from the outset.
In May, the campaign launched “No Se Rinde,” its first Spanish-language television, radio, and digital ads, as part of a multi-million-dollar statewide media campaign.

That was followed by a six-figure English- and Spanish-language buy during the World Cup, plus additional Spanish-language ads including “Pancitas Felices,” “Listos o No,” “Dinerito Extra,” and “De Puro Sudor” focused on lowering costs for working families.
That investment is matched on the ground.

Through Copper State Victory, the campaign has hired Spanish-speaking organizers who recruit Spanish-speaking volunteers, knock doors, and talk directly with voters across Arizona, with campaign literature available in both English and Spanish.
The campaign is also reaching Latino voters through English- and Spanish-language direct mail and has hired Spanish-speaking communications staff to work directly with Spanish-language media.
“From the beginning, we’ve made the investments necessary to engage Latino Arizonans across every part of our campaign,” said Nicole DeMont, campaign manager for Katie Hobbs.
“We’re reaching voters in Spanish and English on television and radio, online, in their mailboxes, at their doors, and in their communities.
This historic $6 million investment reflects the robust campaign we’ve built to earn Latino votes across Arizona.” As governor, Hobbs has focused on lowering costs for Arizona families.

This year, she signed a bipartisan budget providing $1.4 billion in tax relief, including a larger standard deduction for 88 percent of taxpayers, a new $6,000 deduction for Arizona seniors, and eliminating taxes on tips and overtime pay.

She has also helped eliminate nearly $1 billion in medical debt for approximately 700,000 Arizonans, lowered prescription drug costs through AZRx, worked to lower utility and housing costs, and expanded access to apprenticeships and community colleges that prepare Arizonans for good-paying jobs.

Hobbs has also strengthened border security and public safety, including launching Task Force SAFE and Operation Desert Guardian to crack down on cartels and criminal organizations, stopping more than 18 million fentanyl pills from reaching Arizona communities, and delivering more than $215 million to local sheriffs and police departments to combat drug smuggling, human trafficking, and other border-related crimes.

The campaign will continue expanding its Latino voter outreach and turnout operation through Election Day with additional paid media, mail, organizing, community events, Spanish-language communications, and direct voter contact across Arizona.

Hobbs Visits Tucson Food Truck Owners Amid Rising Costs” Monday, March 23, 2026 Affordability “ at the forefront ” of Hobbs agenda as chaos in DC causes prices to skyrocket KVOA is highlighting Gov.

Katie Hobbs’ Thursday visit to Tucson food truck hub Comida Park, and what she’s hearing from food truck owners who’ve been battered by high tariffs for months and are now being squeezed by Washington’s fuel crisis.

“We’ve shown you how the rising cost of food and fuel is hitting the Tucson food truck scene hard, and Governor Katie Hobbs and Tucson Mayor Regina Romero got the chance to see that first hand,” KVOA reported . “[Hobbs and Romero] met with some of the owners of food trucks to learn more about how the current economy is cutting into their bottom lines.” Gov.

Hobbs told KVOA: “I’ve heard from these small business owners, what I’ve heard from so many folks around Arizona – that being a small business owner is so meaningful for them … but also that they’re struggling right now.
It’s why I’m fighting so hard as governor to bring down prices for Arizonans.
When Arizonans are squeezed, they’re not supporting small businesses as much because they don’t have the extra money to do so.

And these guys all rely on that support.” This coverage follows new national reporting from the Associated Press discussing how Hobbs is running for re-election “with a focus on costs.” “She criticized GOP Reps.

Andy Biggs and David Schweikert, who are vying for the nomination to challenge her, for ‘cheering on these reckless tariffs.’ Both lawmakers voted against a measure last month to end the national emergency Trump declared to impose tariffs on Canada.” The AP report continued, “Hobbs said the cost concern was about more than tariffs, noting Medicaid cuts, rising health costs and a spike in gas prices in the wake of the war in Iran.” See here for more from the AP and below for more on the visit in Tucson.
Gov.

Hobbs meets Que Se Antoja food truck owner Jenifer Cardenas, who told Hobbs: “People don’t understand that pistachio cream is actually imported from the Middle East, so it’s very expensive for us… We don’t want to be overpriced or underpriced.

My opponent would be just another rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s costly mistakes.]

I look forward to working with a new Democratic House majority to protect reproductive freedom, defend healthcare and constitutional rights, end the war, and hold ICE accountable.]

added: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/847415791_18636339172025688_8413500367556784058_n.jpg|🌴 Relationships open doors, and this week proved it. 🤝 I'm at the 2nd Annual Bush Cook conference, meeting locals and hearing from the experts: farmers, academics, consultants and non-profit leaders. So much to learn from the people doing this work every day! 🌱 And so many people here come from Georgia! 🍑 I keep meeting fellow Georgians in the Virgin Islands. On Wednesday, I met with the leadership team at the U.S. Virgin Islands Economic Development Authority (USVIEDA), thanks to the generous introduction of Senator Carla J. Joseph of the Virgin Islands Legislature. 🙏🏾 One thoughtful introduction, and I was at the table sharing ideas, albeit virtually since we were on different islands. That is the power of collaboration ‼️ I came to listen and learn how the Virgin Islands is using technology and AI to build workforce capacity, especially in agriculture. Georgia is working through many of the same challenges, and we are stronger when we learn from each other. My action items: see what Georgia resources we can share, and bring back what is working in the Virgin Islands to Georgia and to HD-95. We have farms! 🚜 Thank you, Senator Joseph, for opening the door, and thank you to the USVIEDA team for your time and warm welcome. I am optimistic about what comes next! 💛 #BushCook #Agriculture #Collaboration #USVI #HD95 ———— 📩 Visit www.KendrickForGeorgia.com — link in bio! Sign up for my email blast and learn more about Rep. Kendrick and HD 95.
removed: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/792029865_18621554434025688_792072216928877262_n.heic|🏛️✨ INCREDIBLE HONOR! ✨🏛️ I've been selected as a 2026 ELECTED WOMAN OF EXCELLENCE by the National Foundation for Women Legislators (NFWL)! 🖤🙌🏾 Humbled. Grateful. And so thankful to NFWL for lifting up women legislators across this country. Last month, I had the pleasure of moderating an AI panel at an NFWL event with a room full of sharp, strategic women legislators asking the right questions about the future. 🤖⚡ Now looking forward to the 2026 NFWL Annual Conference in Nashville, TN! 🎶🏛️ Recognition is beautiful. But the WORK continues. 🔥 To my HD-95 family — this honor belongs to YOU as much as me. Thank you. 🖤 ———— 📩 Visit www.KendrickForGeorgia.com — link in bio! Sign up for my email blast and learn more about Rep. Kendrick and HD 95.

added.text: Klicker: The clear choice for 16th District

added: alt:|Writer: Logan Dozier
All Posts Search In the end we (Union-Bulletin) recommend Klicker for the state House, Position 1.
Logan Dozier Sep 29, 2020 2 min read Voters of the 16th Legislative District are the clear winners in the race to replace Rep.
Bill Jenkin, R-Prosser, in the state House.
Republican Mark Klicker and Democrat Frances Chvatal, both of Walla Walla, are outstanding candidates.
Klicker and Chvatal are extremely bright and articulate with the skills needed to serve in the Legislature.
Still, there is a clear difference in the candidates — Klicker is conservative and Chvatal is liberal.

Beyond that, Klicker has a breadth and depth of knowledge on agriculture and environmental issues, as well as a clear understanding of how the Legislature really works (as in hardball politics), that is impressive.
Klicker has been a farmer in several capacities with his farming family.
He worked for 17 years as a regional director for the Washington State Farm Bureau followed by a stint as a project coordinator for Monson Fruit Company.
Klicker now operates and owns a forest management business.
His years with the Farm Bureau brought him in touch with government officials, and he spent a lot of time in Olympia working on agricultural issues.
His views on business, agriculture and environmental protection are pragmatic.
He comes from the perspective of a need to protect the environment so farms — particularly small farms — will survive.
His approach to business is similar in that he believes it is critical to establish a business-friendly environment so small and large employers can stay in business.
Chvatal, who is also from a farm family (in the Touchet area), has similar sensibilities when it comes to agriculture.
Her overriding focus, however, is health care.
She has had a long and successful career as a nurse and hospital administrator in Walla Walla.
When it comes to talking health care, and understanding the nuances of issues, it would be difficult to find anyone more fluent.
Again, voters can’t go wrong.
We see Klicker as the stronger candidate in this race because of his wide array of experiences.
His conservative politics are also more in line with the conservative 16th Legislative District.
However, Chvatal is sharp and understands the District and, if elected, would certainly be responsive to all regardless of their political views.
Klicker would too.
What stands out most about both candidates is their sincere willingness to work across the political aisle seeking collaborative solutions.
They understand that won’t be easy in the hyper-partisan Legislature, but they both contend this is how they roll in their careers and personal lives.
We don’t doubt them for a second.
Both candidates have many strengths, but in the end we recommend Klicker for the state House, Position 1.

added: Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact Donate Donate Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact 💖 We need your help to power our campaign, chip in today! $10 $100 $250 Meet Kristina Gabriel Kristina Gabriel is an Oklahoman, a community advocate, and citizen of the Cherokee Nation who believes public service should be rooted in integrity, lived experience, and accountability to the people.
Kristina has dedicated her career to improving the health and well-being of communities across Oklahoma and Indian Country.

Before running for office, she worked as a public health researcher focused on strengthening health outcomes in Indigenous communities, helping inform state, federal and tribal policy to restore Food Sovereignty and expand access to culturally grounded, community-driven solutions.

Kristina holds a Master of Science in Forensic Investigation and a graduate certificate in Public Health from Oklahoma State University, a Bachelor of Science in Biology from Fort Lewis College, and an Associate of Arts from Tulsa Community College.
She is trained in Community-Based Participatory Research and has published peer-reviewed research on Indigenous health.
Her work has been supported by national institutions including the National Institutes of Health and the U.S.
Department of Health and Human Services, and she has partnered with tribes and community organizations across the country.
But Kristina's path to public service didn't begin in academia, it began in community.

She has a background in grassroots organizing, has volunteered with Planned Parenthood, and has supported local progressive campaigns focused on expanding healthcare access, protecting voting rights, and building a more equitable Oklahoma.
Kristina lives in Tulsa's White City neighborhood.
She is a renter who understands firsthand the pressures families face, rising costs, access to healthcare, and the need for thriving communities.
Kristina is running because she believes Oklahoma deserves leadership that listens, collaborates, and delivers real results.
She is committed to strengthening tribal-state relationships, expanding healthcare access, protecting fundamental rights, and ensuring every community has the opportunity to thrive.

added: Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact Donate Donate Home Meet Kristina Priorities Affordability Healthcare Accessibility Tribal-State Partnerships AI Data Centers Endorsements Support Us Volunteer Donate Vote contact 💖 We need your help to power our campaign, chip in today! $10 $100 $250 Priorities Affordability Oklahoma families are working harder than ever, yet too many are still struggling to keep up.
Housing costs in the Tulsa area have risen significantly, putting pressure on renters and first-time homebuyers alike.
U.S.
Census data show that median gross rent in Oklahoma has steadily increased over the past decade, while wages have not kept pace for many working families.
1 Oklahoma ranks near the bottom nationally in median household income.
2 When housing, childcare, groceries, and utilities rise faster than paychecks, families are forced to make impossible choices.
I support: Expanding affordable housing through smart incentives and zoning reform - We don't have a housing shortage because we lack land.
We have a housing shortage because we've made it too hard to build the kinds of homes regular people can afford.
I support reforms that make it easier to build starter homes while protecting existing neighborhoods and preventing predatory practices.
Lowering childcare costs through state-supported partnerships - Childcare is one of the biggest monthly expenses families face.
If we want parents to work and businesses to grow, we have to make sure childcare is accessible and affordable.
That means partnering with employers, strengthening subsidies, and supporting providers so they can keep their doors open.
Protecting consumers from predatory fees and utility rate spikes - When your electric bill spikes, you don't get to shop around.
You don't get to negotiate.
That's why oversight matters.
If utilities want guaranteed profits, they also need guaranteed accountability Healthcare Accessibility Oklahoma consistently ranks near the bottom nationally in overall health outcomes.
3 The state also has one of the highest uninsured rates in the country.
4 Mental health services, maternal healthcare, and specialty care remain strained.
The Oklahoma Maternal Mortality Review Committee continues to document preventable pregnancy-related deaths.
5 We must: Invest in community-based mental health and substance use services - Prevention and early treatment save lives and save taxpayer dollars.
Community-based care is the smart, humane way to address mental health and addiction in Oklahoma.
Strengthen maternal healthcare access - Maternal healthcare isn't just about babies, it's about families, communities, and equity.
Strengthening access saves lives and builds stronger Oklahoma families.
Tribal-State Partnerships Oklahoma is home to 39 federally recognized Tribal Nations.
Tribal governments are major employers and contribute billions annually to the state's economy.
6 Following the U.S.
Supreme Court's decision in McGirt v.
Oklahoma (2020), strong government-to-government cooperation is more important than ever.
7 Public safety, infrastructure, healthcare delivery, and economic development all depend on respectful collaboration.
When Tribal Nations thrive, Oklahoma thrives.

I am committed to: Protecting tribal sovereignty and honoring treaty obligations - Tribal sovereignty is not just a legal principle, it's the foundation for strong communities, safe neighborhoods, and economic growth.
Honoring treaties and partnering with Tribal Nations benefits everyone in Oklahoma.
Increasing collaboration on infrastructure and broadband - Collaboration is key.
When the state and Tribal Nations plan and invest together, we can close gaps in roads, utilities, and broadband, bringing opportunity, safety, and prosperity to every neighborhood.
Strengthening partnerships in healthcare, education, and workforce development - Our state thrives when we work together.

By strengthening partnerships in healthcare, education, and workforce development with Tribal Nations, we create opportunities for all Oklahomans, better schools, stronger healthcare, and jobs that support families.
AI Data Centers Artificial intelligence and data infrastructure are expanding rapidly, including in Oklahoma.
While data centers bring economic opportunity, they also require significant electricity and water resources.
The U.S.
Department of Energy reports that data centers account for roughly 2 percent of total U.S. electricity consumption, with demand projected to grow due to AI expansion.
8 Large facilities can also consume millions of gallons of water annually for cooling.

As Oklahoma attracts technological investment, we must ensure: Transparent economic incentive agreements - If we're going to offer incentives for high-tech development, everyone deserves to know the cost, the benefit, and the timeline.
Transparency isn't optional, it's smart governance.
Responsible water and energy use standards - Innovation shouldn't come at the expense of our neighbors.
Responsible energy and water standards make sure high-tech development benefits everyone, not just corporate bottom lines.
Grid reliability protections for residential consumers - We want tech companies to bring jobs and investment, but not at the expense of your electricity bill or power reliability.
Grid protections make sure the community comes first.
Workforce training so Oklahomans benefit from job growth - We want tech growth in our state, but it has to work for Oklahomans.
Training and apprenticeships ensure that new jobs stay in our communities and lift up our people.

Kristin Kassner has done her homework, knows those needs, and has spent much of her adult life addressing them.

“These provisions are the result of collaboration with planners, municipal leaders, legal experts, housing advocates and development partners, and they create a clear, consistent framework for reviewing by-right projects.” - Rep.

Kristin Kassner Read More News Kristin Kassner 7/15/26 News Kristin Kassner 7/15/26 State Grants Ipswich $350K to Protect Drinking Water The Town of Ipswich has been awarded a $350,000 state grant to help fund the purchase of a conservation restriction on the former Candlewood Golf Course, a 26-acre property critical to safeguarding the town’s public drinking water supply.
“This grant is more than an investment in infrastructure — it is an investment in the long-term resilience of our region.
It will expand our opportunities to safeguard drinking water, strengthen our ability to manage drought, and protect the natural resources that define and sustain our communities.” - Rep.

Kristin Kassner Read More News Kristin Kassner 7/10/26 News Kristin Kassner 7/10/26 ICYMI: House Passes Pro-Housing Eco-Dev Bill; Moves to Senate Wednesday was a big day on Beacon Hill as the House of Representatives passed H.5562 – An Act Relative to Economic Development in the Commonwealth by a vote of 148-2.

This bill is the House’s version of the Mass WINS Act filed by Governor Healey in April, and authorizes over $500 million in spending along with a slew of policies designed to stimulate new housing production and economic growth across the Commonwealth.

While there are several important provisions in this bill, we are particularly excited to see that Yes in God’s Backyard (YIGBY) and the codification of site plan review are included in the final bill.

“In her work with the Health Connector, she cared for our residents, and she continues that same commitment as an engaged and active member of the Hamilton community.
Nancy brings people together.

“I was thrilled to nominate the Reverend Dr.
Rebecca Pugh.

“He became a helicopter pilot and flew 900 missions in Vietnam, at least half being medical evacuations.
His heroism saved the lives of countless soldiers, allowing them to come home to their families.
His bravery and dedication to duty earned Leland the Distinguished Flying Cross.” - Rep.

“A key part of planning for our future is bringing people together to learn from one another, to see what’s possible, to understand where our work intersects, and to identify opportunities to enrich, protect, and strengthen our communities and our region.

But because of the way income taxes work, here’s how that claim is not unusual.

Connecticut collects more through income tax, sales tax, and investment funds without ever changing a rate.
The Legislature may not have voted for it, but you’re likely paying more income and sales tax each year.
Towns are different.
Costs rise with inflation, but property-tax revenue doesn’t keep pace on its own.
Every budget has to go through a local process and voter approval.
Michelle evaluates budgets based on needs and resources, not ideology.
Some years that means cuts, some years an increase, and some years no increase at all.
And that’s the difference.

Senator Larry Stutts MEET LARRY Conservative Leadership Delivering Results for Our Community Larry Stutts was born at Colbert County Hospital (now Helen Keller Hospital) in Sheffield, Alabama.
Growing up in Cherokee, Alabama, the son of an accountant and a registered nurse, Larry always enjoyed working on the family farm.
At home, he was instilled with the core values of honesty, hard work, belief in God, and respect for others.
These core values define him today.
Larry’s interest in service through government grew as he represented Cherokee Vocational High School at the American Legion’s Boys’ State.
He was also an avid athlete, playing basketball and running track for Cherokee.
Upon high school graduation, Larry moved to Auburn to attend Auburn University.
His dedication to his studies was rewarded through early acceptance to veterinary school.
While attending veterinary school, Larry served in Student Government, was elected Inter-Fraternity Council President, and tapped into the Spade Honorary (Top 10 Men at Auburn).
After graduation, Larry married Jackie, an Auburn pharmacist.
The couple moved to Larry’s hometown of Cherokee.
Larry opened a veterinary practice with Charles C.
King of Leighton.
Their practice grew, and Larry put the skills of hard work to use.
He built a business over the next three years.
Larry and Jackie attended First Presbyterian Church in Tuscumbia, with their eldest daughter, Elizabeth (Thompson), born in 1982.
While in veterinary practice, Larry was active in the Tuscumbia Kiwanis Club, Shoals Area Quarterback Club, and Shoals Area Auburn Alumni Club, where he was President.
He also taught Biology classes at Northwest Shoals Community College in the evenings, passing on his love for science and also raising extra money to pay for his past school expenses.
In 1983, Larry and Jackie welcomed their second daughter Rebecca (Hovater).
After careful consideration and much prayer, Larry applied to medical school and was accepted to the University of South Alabama College of Medicine.
While in Mobile, Jackie worked to assist with living and medical school expenses.
Larry worked weekends and summers at numerous veterinary practices around Mobile to cover school expenses too.
Larry was elected class representative all four years of medical school and served as President of the Medical Student Body his senior year.
While in Mobile, Larry and Jackie, and their two daughters were founding members of Christ Presbyterian Church.
In 1987, Larry’s third daughter, Sarah (Philbin) was born.

As graduation neared, Larry was encouraged by the faculty to consider further research in comparative medicine – researching and studying similarities in animals and humans, using both his doctoral degrees.
But rather than a career in academics, Larry desired to pursue a private practice of medicine.
Larry and Jackie moved to Birmingham with their three daughters.
They lived in the Medical Center housing next to the hospital in downtown Birmingham.
Jackie worked as a home health pharmacist while Larry was completing his residency.
To obtain extra money to support the family and pay off student loans, Larry continued to work on weekends at smaller regional hospitals in the emergency room.
In 1989, their last child was born, a son, Collins.
Larry received the honor of Chief Resident while at Carraway Medical Center.
He was also asked to present his senior research project at the World College of Gynecologic Laparoscopy in Las Vegas.
After completing his residency program, Larry and Jackie moved back to the Shoals, as it was a place they wanted to raise their children and be active in the community.
Tuscumbia became their hometown.
Their family is active in their church, First Presbyterian of Tuscumbia.
He has served as an elder and currently serving as a Sunday School teacher.
In 1992, Larry opened Colbert OB/GYN in Sheffield.
Today, his practice has served over 22,000 patients.
He has delivered more than 12,000 babies and performed over 7,500 gynecologic surgeries.
He has earned a sterling reputation as a doctor that women of Northwest Alabama trust.
In 2014, Larry answered the call of the Lord, the Republican Party, and Northwest Alabama to wage a campaign that few thought possible.
Challenging an incumbent that had been in Montgomery for more than three decades.
Larry took a message of faith, values, and conservative principles directly to the voters.
Though he was vastly outspent, Larry delivered a shocking 70 vote victory.
As our Senator, Larry has led the fight to reduce the size of government, champion the right to life, protect our Second Amendment rights, and keep our taxes low.
Larry has also proven to be an effective legislator in representing the interests of Senate District 6.
Over the past four years, the region has prospered due to the policies Larry has supported and unemployment in Northwest Alabama is at an all time low.
On every campaign promise, Larry has delivered in a MAJOR way!

Laura Gillen Announces New Leadership Endorsements in Re-Election Campaign FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: February 12, 2026 CONTACT: press@lauragillen.com ROCKVILLE CENTRE, NY – Congresswoman Laura Gillen’s re-election campaign to represent New York’s Fourth Congressional District received resounding support from U.S.

House Democratic leaders, including House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark, House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, and Representative Gregory Meeks (NY-05), who used to represent part of the district.
The members highlighted Gillen’s fierce dedication to serving Nassau County families.
“Congress needs leaders like Laura Gillen, who stand their ground and remain relentlessly focused on solving the challenges facing everyday Americans.
Congresswoman Gillen has been a champion for Long Island families.
She’s fighting to lower costs, improve community safety and secure federal investments.
She has shown a fierce commitment to commonsense solutions that deliver results.

We are proud to stand with Congresswoman Gillen and fully endorse her re-election in our march to take back the House majority,” said House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, House Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar.
“I’m proud to call Laura Gillen a colleague and friend, as someone who shares her commitment to working families.
Her partnership in Congress to lower taxes, make health care affordable, and push back against Republicans’ disarray in Washington has proven that she is the leader our region needs.
I am honored to endorse her re-election to Congress,” said U.S.
Representative Gregory Meeks.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE October 2, 2026 ELMONT, NY – On Friday, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) joined volunteers and candidates in Elmont, New York to open a new campaign office ahead of the 2026 election.
Gillen was joined by Assemblywoman Michaelle Solages, Legislator Cynthia Nunez and candidates for the Town of Hempstead Supervisor and Clerk, Joe Scianablo and Dr.
Joylette Williams, to launch a community canvass and speak with voters.
“We are so thankful for the volunteers and community members who came out to launch another canvass with us this evening,” said Rep.
Gillen.

“These supporters – parents, healthcare workers, business owners and students – are ready to make a change and they know it all starts with voting!” “It was great to see the energy and excitement that everybody has for electing our candidates up and down the ballot,” said Asw.
Solages.

“We have real momentum in this election, and we will prove that when we work together we win together.” Laura Gillen is running for re-election in New York’s Fourth Congressional District because she’s willing to work with anyone to get things done for Long Island.
One of the most competitive congressional seats in the country, Rep.
Gillen flipped this district in 2024 by 2.4%.

GILLEN RELEASES NEW TV AD DETAILING DRISCOLL’S COMPLETE ALLEGIANCE TO TRUMP “Driscoll calls Trump’s agenda “Wonderful,” even though it’s crushing Nassau County.” ROCKVILLE CENTRE, N.Y. – Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen released a new ad, “Serve,” detailing Jeanine Driscoll’s 100% allegiance to President Trump and the economic policies he has implemented.
“Serve” is part of a multimillion-dollar ad campaign that will run through Election Day on broadcast, cable, streaming, and digital platforms.
The ad details how Trump’s agenda has caused gas prices to spike, healthcare costs to skyrocket and food prices to shoot up 33% with no relief in sight.
Long Islanders know that the numbers on every bill are a direct result of the policies that Driscoll praises.
“Nassau County families are getting crushed by rising costs for groceries, gas and healthcare,” said Congresswoman Gillen.
“That hasn’t stopped Jeanine Driscoll from pledging her total support for the hyper partisan agenda that is driving prices higher.
Long Island needs an independent leader in Washington, not a rubber stamp for Trump’s agenda.” Rep.
Gillen has cosponsored and introduced multiple bills to lower costs for commuting, car insurance, federal taxes and more.
Rep.
Gillen wrote the bill to permanently restore the full State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction so Long Islanders can keep more of their hard earned money in their pockets.

GILLEN RELEASES NEW TV AD TOUTING BIPARTISAN RECORD, DEDICATION TO DELIVERING FOR LONG ISLANDERS “I’m Laura Gillen and I’ll work with anyone if it lowers your costs and helps Nassau families.” ROCKVILLE CENTRE, N.Y. – Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen released a new ad, Top Priority, highlighting her commitment to delivering for Nassau County families.
“Top Priority” is part of a multimillion-dollar ad campaign that will run through Election Day on broadcast, cable, streaming, and digital platforms.
“Nassau County families need a common sense leader,” said Congresswoman Gillen.
“I’ll continue to work with anyone to make life safer and more affordable on Long Island, bring more of our tax dollars back home and deliver real results for Nassau County.” Rep.
Gillen has a consistent record of working with leaders from across the political spectrum to find common ground and ways her constituents can benefit from legislation.
Rep.
Gillen earned an “A” grade from Bridge Grades, labeling her one of the most collaborative House members.
She is ranked the third most bipartisan Democrat in Congress.
Ad transcript: New York City is just a few stops away, but it can seem like another planet.
Look, I know you don’t want crazy, just someone who’ll deliver for Nassau County.
That’s why in Congress I’m working across the aisle to cut middle class taxes.
Going after the insurance companies ripping us off.
And taking on the special interests buying up homes and pricing families out.
I’m Laura Gillen and I’ll work with anyone if it lowers your costs and helps Nassau families.
That’s why I approve this message.

Rural communities are far too often overlooked in Washington; they deserve a voice in Congress, and their local concerns should be turned into practical law.
Postal reform has long been a concern for rural Americans, and ZIP codes are a simple, effective way to address an everyday issue affecting Coloradans.

In Colorado and across rural America, something as simple as a ZIP code can determine whether a community has a clear identity, accurate mail delivery, proper emergency services, and a fair shot at economic growth.
For too long, countless small towns have been forced to share ZIP codes with larger neighboring communities, leading to confusion, delays, and a lack of recognition.
That is why I introduced H.R.
3095 , the Unique ZIP Code bill.
This legislation would direct the Postal Service to create single, unique ZIP codes for scores of communities that have waited far too long for basic recognition.
The Unique ZIP Code bill is personally significant because it underscores the importance of listening to constituents and addressing the problems that matter to everyday Americans.
My bill passed the House of Representatives with strong bipartisan support.
The Senate companion, S.
4505 , introduced by Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA), advanced out of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, led by Chairman Rand Paul (R-KY).
I am grateful for the progress and remain focused on getting this bill across the finish line and onto the President’s desk.
This effort brought together a bipartisan group of the Colorado delegation to help Coloradans.
Original cosponsors for my legislation included Democrats Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) and Jason Crow (CO-06), along with Republicans Jeff Hurd (CO-03) and Gabe Evans (CO-08).
Working across the aisle on practical solutions that strengthen our communities is exactly what Coloradans expect from their representatives.
Unique ZIP codes are not a symbolic gesture.

They are tangible changes that improve mail delivery accuracy, help emergency services respond to the right location, strengthen local identity, support businesses in operating and growing, and ensure that tax and census data accurately reflect the communities that actually exist.
For the 73 communities included in this legislation, unique ZIP codes are long-overdue practical relief.
I have heard from Coloradans who live this frustration every day.
Residents who watch packages go to the wrong place.
Local leaders who struggle to market their town when it shares a ZIP code with a larger city.
Families who simply want their community recognized for what it is.
This bill answers those concerns with a common-sense solution.
Small towns are the backbone of Colorado and our nation as a whole.
They deserve the same basic tools and recognition that larger communities take for granted.
A unique ZIP code is a simple, common-sense reform that strengthens communities without adding bureaucracy or cost.
Senator Joni Ernst of Iowa successfully led S.
4505 out of committee; now our coalition is seeking every opportunity to get this legislation across the finish line.
And this legislation has garnered support from more than just Colorado’s lawmakers.
It is backed in both chambers by a bipartisan coalition of members from 17 states, including California, Connecticut, Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Oklahoma, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and more.
I will continue to work with my colleagues and Congressional leadership to get this legislation passed and signed into law, so that all local voices continue to be heard.

added: top of page DONATE HERE Meet Lauren Road to Prosperity Voter Info Get Involved Events News Everything Is Not 'Fine' edauer18 #ago 1 min read Kansans understand the importance of separation of powers, and are frustrated that this President is making decisions that are the job of Congress, while our Congressperson is standing by and letting it happen.

In a conversation with Matt Matson on his podcast, Within Reason, Lauren stated it is time for Kansans to come together and vote on our common issues, noting that things are very different now and party politics is not working.

"We are all experiencing the same problems, the same higher costs of living, and the loss of the American dream." In the face of these shared struggles, Lauren noted that incumbent Tracey Mann has been largely absent, primarily only showing up at private events, and sending newsletters that indicate 'everything is fine,' when we know everything is NOT fine across District 1!
She is committed to representing everyone in this district, adding she will be voting for the interests of Kansans, not the party line.
Explaining that people have been betrayed by the people in power, she noted that Kansans did not vote for increasing corporate control.

Having already traveled 35,000 miles across the Big First already, Lauren stated she was kicking off a two-week listening tour, opening the floor to local communities to ask questions and express their concerns about what is going on at the federal level.

She added she is dedicated to government efficiency, which she contrasted with this administration's record spending, increasing national debt, and wasteful cuts to federal agencies that did not provide much savings and instead reduced government efficiencies while opening the door to fraud and other abuses.

added: top of page DONATE HERE Meet Lauren Road to Prosperity Voter Info Get Involved Events News The Current Proposed Farm Bill Falls Short! edauer18 #ago 1 min read Lauren talked with Dylan Domangue on KWCH 12 about the priorities that must be included in a Farm Bill, and that such a bill needs to be passed ASAP.
She also stressed the need for stable trade policies, citing beef prices, adding that she supports 'country of origin' labels.
In addition, Lauren discussed the significant impact on the overall community in SW Kansas during the recent ICE raids, which she noted are likely to occur again.

Regarding data centers, she noted that while there are some roles for the federal government to play (multistate waters such as the Ogalala aquifer, and environmental impacts), the decisions should be under local control.

In contrast to the incumbent representative, Lauren committed to voting to protect Kansans from the stark costs of going to war, and to protect Kansans healthcare, noting the cuts in the so-called 'Big Beautiful Bill' will cause further closures of rural hospitals.

DONATE Log In All Posts EXCELLENCE in Education FINANCIAL Reform SAFER Communities Campaign & PSA Search McHenry County Voter Guide: Key Dates for November 2026 Judi Zapp #ago 1 min read ELECT LAURIE PARMAN for IL 66 House Representative laurie Parman for the People McHenry County, IL • General Election 2026 Your Civic Guide to the Upcoming November 2026 Election Democracy works best when every community member participates.

As we look ahead to the November 2026 General Election, Laurie Parman is providing this non-partisan guide to ensure all McHenry County residents have timely, accurate voting information and essential resources ready at their fingertips.

View Your Sample Ballot Key Election Deadlines Mark Your Calendar for November 2026 Early Voting Oct 19 – Nov 2 In-person early voting available across select McHenry County regional locations prior to Election Day.
Vote by Mail Request by Oct 29 Ballot requests must be received in advance; completed ballots must be postmarked by Nov 3, 2026.
Election Day Tuesday, Nov 3 Polls open across all county precincts from 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM CST for regular voting.
Election Day: November 3, 2026 Ensure your voter registration is up to date, review the candidates and referendums on your ballot, and locate your assigned precinct polling site ahead of time.
Find Your Polling Place Resource 01 Official Sample Ballots Take the time to review your localized sample ballot prior to entering the booth.
Knowing what measures and offices are being voted on simplifies your voting experience.
Resource 02 Precinct & Drop Box Locations Verify your designated voting site or secure ballot drop box location in McHenry County to ensure your vote is received and counted on schedule.

added: Policy Interest Areas 1 Lower Cost of Living Affordability starts at home by addressing healthcare and childcare costs.
Federal policy changes and global conflict have led to our families struggling to make house payments, have money for gas, and pay for childcare.
I'm committed to lowering childcare costs so no parent has to choose between a paycheck and their kids.
Workers across the board have seen healthcare cost increases.
Federal funding cuts paired with administration requirements will mean that plans will cost more to provide less.
No one should have to put off care when they’re sick.
I’ll fight for lower insurance costs and to keep care close to home.
2 Quality Education Right now our schools are facing rising healthcare costs, an increase in transportation costs, and funding gaps for special education.
Part of this is due to federal funding deficits, but we need to do what we can to find other ways to support our schools so they don’t need to turn to local taxpayers.
I'll fight for schools that are fully funded and focused on preparing students for real careers here in Minnesota.
3 Responsible Technology & Energy Technology should power Minnesota’s future without draining our water, worsening climate change, or compromising our data and privacy.
Projects coming into our communities and greenspaces should show concrete evidence that they’ll run on clean energy and protect our water and natural areas.
We should also reinvest in natural areas that need support, because Minnesota’s resilience against climate chaos depends on both a thriving environment and how thoughtfully we live within it.

added: Skip to main content Greg Leman Home Issues Priorities for Montana Property Taxes Data Centers Volunteer Donate Home Issues Priorities for Montana Property Taxes Data Centers Volunteer Donate Issues Property Taxes Property Taxes are Too High Property taxes are hitting homeowners and renters hard because, over the last few decades, the system has gotten out of balance.
Industry used to carry a much bigger share of the property tax load.
Then the legislature started handing out tax breaks to favored businesses, and homeowners got stuck with the difference.
That’s crony capitalism, and it’s the government picking winners and losers.
It’s time to stop.
Make the favored industries pay their fair share, and cut the tax on the roof over your head.
Here's a paragraph that sums up this position nicely: You know where that quote came from?
That's a snapshot of my opponents website from October of 2024.
Wayback Machine October 2024 (opens in a new tab) As we can now see, she went to Helena and did nothing of the sort.
In fact, she did a complete 180.
There was no rebalancing of residential property taxes and favored industries.
In fact, it became much worse.
She voted Yes on HB 424. (opens in a new tab) That bill extended and expanded the property tax cuts for data centers, which were one of the favored industries that gets a huge tax break.
This bill gave them an 85% tax break on their power generation.
She broke her promise and then made it worse.
The property tax bill that passed, HB 231, didn't fix the break on favored industries, and it didn't reduce the total amount of residential property tax.
It just moved things around in a giant shell game.
Some people did well, others not so well.
But everybody's property taxes are still going to be going up.

added: Skip navigation menu About Priorities Endorsements Events Volunteer Media Donate MEDIA About Priorities Endorsements Events Volunteer Media Donate MEDIA Updated October 15, 2026 Overview Alex Mealer is an out-of-touch Californian who does not live in the district and cannot be trusted to fight for working families or lower costs.
She is a billionaire-backed extremist politician who will be a rubber stamp for Washington politicians and their cost-raising agenda.

That’s why Big Tech pro-data center super PACs and dark money special interests are spending more than $1 million to prop her up because they know that she will be a puppet for special interests in Washington.
Leticia Gutierrez is a military mom, former fraud analyst, and community leader who will fight for lower costs, hold corporations accountable, and put working families first.

Summary Starting as soon as possible, independent and Democratic-leaning voters in the TX-9 portion of Harris County and in the Houston Media Market, especially Latino voters and voters under 35, need to see positive and contrast ads on broadcast TV, Spanish and English on YouTube, connected TV and streaming platforms about how: Alex Mealer is a Californian who doesn't even live in this district and has said she will only move here if she wins.

Mealer supports the policies that are making things more expensive for Texans, including the largest cut to Medicaid in history, cutting healthcare access for over 1.6 million Texans and raising premiums by an average of 35% – all to fund tax breaks for billionaires.

She's backed by national special interests who have spent more than $1 million to buy her seat and a super PAC backed by companies building data centers all over Texas because they know she will prioritize their profits over hardworking families in our community.

Houston Public Media- May 26, 2026: “She does not live in the boundaries of the congressional district, which is not required, but has said she would move into the district if she wins.” Houston Chronicle: And in the 9th, Anthropic's Public First Action network spent almost $750,000 to boost Mealer, an Army veteran who worked on energy deals at Wells Fargo.
Texas Tribune: Mealer, running for Texas’ 9th Congressional District in east Harris County, was backed by the same PAC with about $234,000 spent in support of her campaign.

As a lifelong Texan (Tejana) and single mother who raised her children in this community, Leticia Gutierrez understands that what Texans want is for our hard work to be enough to provide for our families, and she's not afraid to stand up for what's right.
When her oldest son, who now proudly serves in the U.S.
Army, developed asthma, she became an advocate for children's health.
Now she's running for Congress to fight for lower costs for working families in Texas and fix the corrupt system that is hurting us.
Houston Chronicle Editorial Board – October 14, 2026 : “There’s no denying that both her [Leticia’s] roots and commitment to this district are deep.

We can’t say the same about her Republican challenger Alexandra Mealer, a 40-something California native whose most recent registered home address is in the Woodland Heights — nowhere near District 9.” Starting as soon as possible, Democratic-leaning, Latino and Black voters in the TX-9 portion of Harris County who plan to vote for Talarico and Hinojosa, in the zip codes 77049, 77013, 77044, 77015, 77521, 77078, 77020, 77011, 77012, 77587, 77506, 77087, 77547, 77017, 77034, 77502, 77503, 77530, 77504, and 77520 need to hear from bilingual canvassers in Spanish and English at their doors about how: Leticia Gutierrez is a military mom and our neighbor of 45 years who will fight for our kids' health and lower costs, while Alex Mealer doesn't even live here.
Texas has no straight-ticket voting, so voters must find Leticia Gutierrez on their ballot, next to Talarico and Hinojosa, and vote all the way down.
ADDITIONAL RESOURCES Hispanic voters who consume at least some of their news and information in Spanish need to see ads that feature both Spanish and English.
During early voting, short ads should remind voters that Texas has no straight-ticket voting, so they must find Leticia Gutierrez on their ballot.

added: top of page Home About Lex Social Media Platform News Yard Signs Voter Education Donate Voter Education All information listed comes directly from the Kansas Secretary of State website: sos.ks.gov Click on any blue text to be taken to the appropriate page.
What are the requirements to vote in Kansas?
Anyone who is a US citizen, 18 years or older, a resident of Kansas, and has completed the terms of any sentence from a felony conviction, is legally qualified to vote.
(Voting rights are restored upon completion of the terms of a felony sentence, including all supervised release.
Registration is not automatic - the ex-offender must act to register to vote.
Unpaid criminal fines, restitution, or court costs may make you ineligible to vote.
Verify with the court if any amounts owed prevent the restoration of your civil rights.) Per state law, the voter registration books close 21 days before an election until the election is completed.
This means for 2026, all voter registrations must be completed by October 18th to be considered valid.
Any registrations received in that period will not be processed until after the election.
Always make sure to double check your voter registration before the deadline to ensure your voting eligibility for the election. ​ What are the Photo ID requirements?
State law requires voters to show photographic identification when casting a vote in person.
If the photo ID has an expiration date on it, the ID must not have expired at the time of voting.
An acceptable photo ID does not have to have an expiration date on the document in order to be valid.

Acceptable forms of photo ID include: A driver’s license or nondriver’s identification card issued by Kansas or by another state or district of the United States; A concealed carry of handgun license issued by Kansas or a concealed carry of handgun or weapon license issued by another state or district of the United States; A United States passport; An employee badge or identification document issued by a municipal, county, state, or federal government office; A military identification document issued by the United States; A student identification card issued by an accredited postsecondary institution of education in the state of Kansas; A public assistance identification card issued by a municipal, county, state or federal government office; and An identification card issued by an Indian tribe.
Exemptions exist for individuals 65 years of age or older who may use expired photo IDs or individuals whose religious beliefs prohibit photographic identification.

Voters with religious objections may sign an affidavit before the election or at the poll on election day to be exempt. ​ Registered voters who do not have an approved government-issued photo ID and would like one to vote may apply for a free nondriver identification card with the Kansas Division of Motor Vehicles.
To get a free photo ID, individual must fill out a Certification Requesting Fee Waiver for Nondriver Identification Card.
This form is available at all driver’s licenses offices, all county election offices and online. ​ How do I register to vote?

You can go to your county election office and fill out a paper form in person. ​ If you have a valid Kansas ID, you can register online . ​ How do I check my voter registration status? ​ Check your voter registration status HERE ​ When do I vote? ​ Election dates can be found HERE ​ How do I vote early?
Individuals can vote early in person at the county election office or at a satellite location, and must show photo ID.
If an advance voter does not provide identification, the county election officer will issue a provisional ballot to the voter.
The provisional ballot will not be considered valid until the voter submits their photo ID before the county canvass.
Apply for an Advanced Ballot ​ What is the county canvass?

The canvassing process includes counting ballots, tabulating votes by election district and certifying the results of all official primary and general elections and question submitted elections held pursuant to federal or state law.

It is the process which produces official election results, whether it is the official number of valid votes cast for each candidate for each elected office, or the official number of valid Yes and No votes cast on an issue in a question submitted election.
For local elections, there are always two canvasses: the original canvass and the final canvass.
For national and state elections, there are always three canvasses: the original, intermediate and final canvass. ​ How do I vote by mail?
Voters may vote by mail prior to election day in the state of Kansas.

To do so, you must complete an application for an advance ballot and include your driver’s license number or a copy of your photo identification. ​ Under Kansas statute, the deadline to return your ballot is the close of the polls on Election Day.

A district court in Douglas County entered a statewide injunction requiring ballots postmarked by election day to be counted if a ballot arrives by the last postal delivery on Friday after the election.
The Kansas Court of Appeals rejected the Secretary of State’s appeal to stay the injunction.
Regardless of the decision, voters are urged to return their ballots by the close of polls on Election Day.

Doing so will ensure that their ballots will be counted. ​ Military and overseas citizens: Uniform and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA) allows for overseas voting , or federal services voting, for active duty military and family members and individuals, living abroad.
To qualify, voters must meet the criteria set out in the Federal Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act.
Absentee voters who qualify under this act should apply for a ballot in the county election office in the Kansas County where their residence is located.
It is not necessary for qualifying individuals to be registered to vote in the county which they vote (K.S.A.
25-1215 ). ​ The Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) provides a ballot application HERE called the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA).
Voters who file the application before a primary election will automatically receive a ballot for the general election that year (K.S.A.

Although there is no statutory deadline for applications to be submitted, they must be submitted with enough time to allow transmittal time to and from the voter. ​ Submit a ballot application to the county election office that you consider your residence.
Complete your ballot.
Starting # days prior to an election, ballots will be sent to all voters with an active federal post card application.
Return your ballot to the county election office by mail, fax, or email.
Verify your ballot was received and counted by contacting your county election office. ​ How are mail in ballots verified?
K.S.A.

25-1122(e)(1) requires county election offices compare the signature on the advance by mail ballot application with the signature on voter registration records to verify the voter, and not a third party, requested the advance by mail ballot.

If the signatures do not match, the signature may be challenged, and the county election office will contact the voter to verify the signature. ​ Voters must provide the number of their photo identification (e,g., driver’s license) on the advance by mail ballot application.
In the event identification information cannot be verified, K.S.A.

25-1122(c) states the applicant must provide a copy of an acceptable form of photographic identification. ​ When a voter has completed their advance by mail ballot, they must sign the outside of the ballot envelope.
That signature is then reviewed with voter registration records.
If the signatures do not match, the signature may be challenged, and the county election office will contact the voter to verify the signature. ​ How do I know if I need a provisional ballot?
Provisional voting provides individuals with the opportunity to vote even though questions exist on their eligibility.
Kansas law encourages individuals to participate in an election by allowing any individual with an eligibility issue to cast a provisional ballot.
There are a number of instances where an individual may be provided with a provisional ballot.

The most common include: -Failure to provide photographic identification -Address change -Name change -Already issued a ballot ​ How do I find out where to vote? ​ Find my voting location ​ Where do I vote if I just moved?
If you move to a new county in Kansas before the registration deadline, you must complete a new voter registration application.
If you move after the registration deadline, you can still vote at the precinct assigned to your old address, but you will be required to complete a new voter registration application.
If you moved from another state, you should register to vote in Kansas as soon as possible after moving.
If 45 days before an election and the deadline to register has passed, you may vote a president-only ballot.

To vote a president-only ballot, you must go to your local election office by noon on the day before the election and complete voter registration forms. ​ ​ ​ ​ © # by The Goff Family, Powered and secured by Liberty and Justice for All bottom of page

added: I was honored to be named to the Georgia Association of Educators 2023 and 2024 Legislative Honor Roll for dedication to public education in Georgia.

READ January 23, 2026 Several Cobb County lawmakers have introduced legislation in the Georgia General Assembly that would require public school districts to broadcast or record public comments at school board meetings if those meetings are aired to the public.

House Bill 989 would amend state law governing local boards of education to require that any public comment period be recorded or broadcast “in the same manner and to the same extent” as the rest of the public portions of their meetings.
During a Thursday town hall at Jim Miller Park, Rep.
David Wilkerson, D-Powder Springs, one of the bill’s co-sponsors, said the bill was about consistency and transparency.
Wilkerson chairs the Cobb Legislative Delegation.
The bill’s other co-sponsors include Rep.
Mekyah McQueen, D-Smyrna; Rep.
Solomon Adesanya, D-east Cobb; Rep.
Mary Frances Williams, D-Marietta; Rep.
Jordan Ridley, R-Woodstock; and Rep.
Lisa Campbell, D-Kennesaw.
READ January 30, 2025 Along with many of you, I have a deep respect for our former President Jimmy Carter as a human being, statesman, humanitarian and a devoted environmentalist.

Indeed, an important part of his presidential legacy is his awareness of the vulnerability of our planet to human activities and climate change, and his many substantive actions to protect our environment.

President Carter was a first-of-his-kind environmental advocate who encouraged decreased reliance on fossil fuels, less energy consumption at the individual level, and decreased American dependence on foreign oil.
He created the U.S.
Department of Energy and more than doubled the land protected by the National Park Service.
In addition, President Carter believed we should get 20 percent of our power from solar energy and other renewables by the year 2000.
In true Jimmy Carter style of practicing what he preached, President Carter even installed 32 solar panels on the roof of the White House to heat water in 1979!

READ August 25, 2023 Our schools should be places where students and families come together to learn to how to think, how to read, how to build healthy relationships based on respect, integrity, and inclusion.Our teachers have an important and trusted role in our schools to help inspire a love of reading, discussion, and critical thinking .

READ August 8, 2022 Today, the Georgia AFL-CIO, the state federation of labor representing more than 120,000 members, endorsed Georgia House District 35 candidate Lisa Campbell in recognition of her commitment to defending the right of all working people to good jobs, fair wages, and safe working conditions.
“I am honored that our campaign has earned the endorsement of the Georgia AFL-CIO,” said Lisa Campbell.
READ May 4, 2022 Today, EMILY’s List, the nation’s largest resource for women in politics,endorsed Ga.
House District 35 candidate Lisa Campbell in recognition of her commitment to defending reproductive justice.
“EMILY’s List is excited to endorse Lisa Campbell to represent Georgia’s 35th House District,” said Sarah Curmi, Vice President of State and Local Campaigns at EMILY’s List.
READ March 5, 2022 Lisa Campbell hopes to bring 30 years of business experience to the Georgia legislature as the representative for newly-redrawn House District 35.

We collect personal information that you voluntarily provide to us when you register on the Services, express an interest in obtaining information about us or our products and Services, when you participate in activities on the Services, or otherwise when you contact us.
The personal information that we collect depends on the context of your interactions with us and the Services, the choices you make, and the products and features you use.
The personal information we collect may include the following: • Your Name • Your Email • Your Phone Number We automatically collect certain information when you visit, use, or navigate the Services.

This information does not reveal your specific identity (like your name or contact information) but may include device and usage information, such as your IP address, browser and device characteristics, operating system, language preferences, referring URLs, device name, country, location, information about how and when you use our Services, and other technical information.
This information is primarily needed to maintain the security and operation of our Services, and for our internal analytics and reporting purposes.
Like many businesses, we also collect information through cookies and similar technologies.

We process your personal information for a variety of reasons, depending on how you interact with our Services, including: • To facilitate account creation and authentication and otherwise manage user accounts. • To respond to user inquiries/offer support. • To send administrative information to you. • To enable user-to-user communications. • To request feedback. • To protect our Services. • To identify usage trends. • To determine the effectiveness of our marketing and promotional campaigns. • To save or protect an individual’s vital interest.
We may process your information when necessary to save or protect an individual’s vital interest, such as to prevent harm.
Third-Party Sharing: We will not sell, rent, or otherwise share your personal data to third parties for promotional/marketing purposes.
However, we may share your information with service providers for business operations and/or legal authorities when required by law or to protect our rights.
Mobile opt-ins are excluded from third party sharing for marketing purposes.
Opt-Out: You can opt out of receiving text messages at any time by texting STOP to any text you receive from us.
SMS Terms and Conditions: By providing your cell phone number, you agree to receive texts to your number from Elizabeth Pannill Fletcher for Congress.
Texts will include messages about voter engagement, volunteer engagement, and election information.
We will not solicit donations over text.
Msg frequency varies.
Reply STOP to opt-out.
Reply HELP for help or more information.
Msg and data rates may apply.

For the first time, two traditional Navajo women are running for the Arizona Legislature.
Each bring essential experience and has deep roots as longtime residents of Legislative District 6.
Together, they have lived in and traveled throughout the largest legislative district in Arizona.
Jamescita Peshlakai will be serving as your State Senator and Mae Peshlakai as your State Representative.
Elect these 2 highly qualified women to the 2 Open Seats!
Jamescita Peshlakai has a distinguished record of public service, including one term as a State House Representative and two terms in the State Senate.
She served as the tribal liaison for the U.S.
Department of the Interior under President Biden and, in 2025, was appointed by Governor Hobbs to the Arizona State Transportation Board.
Representative Mae Peshlakai is seeking a third term in the State House.
Overcoming her experience as a federal boarding school survivor, she has become an internationally celebrated artist and a revered elder dedicated to preserving and sharing Indigenous knowledge.

added: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Jamescita Peshlakai Matriarch I am Navajo of the Tangle People Clan, born for the Red House clan, maternal grandfathers are of the Deer Water clan, and paternal grandfathers are of the Cliff Dweller clan.
I was born north of the sacred mountain of the west, Doo'ko'osliid (the San Francisco Peaks).
Combat War Veteran I am a combat veteran of the Persian Gulf War.
I previously served in the Arizona legislature as a Representative and a Senator for this district.
I earned my bachelor's and master's degrees at NAU in Flagstaff, and I am currently a student at ASU's Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law.
Knowledge of policies and the legislative process is essential for representing Arizona's citizens.

Proud Democrat Protect our Democracy: Countering extremism Protect our fundamental rights Protect social security and healthcare Lower food and energy costs Job creation and stability Climate change solutions Gun violence prevention Home ownership and housing affordability Protect reproductive rights Immigration and humanity Tribal sovereignty and inclusion Veterans benefits and services Who is Arizona?
We are!
Established Navajo Code Talkers Day in Arizona in 2021 Taking Care of our Home I am committed to civil rights, equity, and justice in Arizona.
This includes educating our citizens about living together.
Arizona needs a leader who can lead by educating and building bridges.
In 2021, I sponsored the legislation (SB1802) that established August 14th as "Arizona Navajo Code Talkers Day", an official state holiday.
My work ensured the recognition of Navajo Code Talkers' contributions to world stability during World War II.
I am one of thousands of federal employees who have lost their jobs.
Many in rural Arizona are finding fewer job opportunities in their home communities.
Some folks are seeing their homes valued less than they had hoped in prior years.
Essentially, their nestegg and savings are dwindling before their eyes.
The American Dream seems lost to us.
It is not lost; we need to elect people who represent the citizens of our amazing state.

added: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Arizona's Legislative District 6 DISTRICT 6 is truly unique and diverse LD 6, the largest state legislative district in Arizona and the United States.

LD 6 includes some of the most beautiful parks and natural wonders in the world, including the Grand Canyon, the San Francisco Peaks, Monument Valley and the White Mountains, and the Colorado and Little Colorado Rivers.

Eight tribes make up the majority of district’s constituents; Hualapai, Havasupai, Kaibab Paiute, San Juan Southern Paiute, Navajo, Hopi, White Mountain Apache, San Carlos Apache and some Zuni Pueblo.
The district spans 7 counties and includes Flagstaff, Winslow, Page, Holbrook, Pinetop, Fredonia, and more!

added: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Mae Peshlakai Experienced Advocate As a Precinct and State Committee Member of the Arizona Democratic Party, Mae has worked or volunteered on the majority of tribal, county, state and federal elections since 1974.

She has traveled all of Arizona’s Legislative District 6 to register voters, collect signatures for candidate petitions, referendums, and educate constituents on the US census and the 2021 redistricting.
Mae is committed to be the voice of the people of rural and tribal Arizona.

Leader and Elder Representative Mae Peshlakai is Diné - Tangle People Clan and born for the Deer Water Clan, maternal grandfathers are of the Salt clan and paternal grandfathers are of the Rock Gap clan.
She is a boarding school survivor.
Mae attended a U.S.
Federal Bureau of Indian Affairs Boarding School in Tolani Lake, Arizona, 100 miles northeast of Flagstaff, Arizona..
Mae was married to James Peshlakai, an accomplished silver and goldsmith.
She took up silversmithing and, to this day, makes jewelry every day as well as weaves.
She and her husband worked with prestigious colleges and universities across the nation sharing the Navajo culture and assisting scholarly research.
Mae knows the issues and challenges of District 6 and has worked tirelessly for two terms representing all the communities of District 6.

Budget Champion Missing and Murdered Indigenous People Hope and Opportunity In 2025, Representative Peshlakai fought and voted for a budget that made historic investments in Indigenous Tribal healthcare and traditional healing practices.
Rep.

Peshlakai was elated to support an opportunity to leverage $100,000 from the state to secure more than $220 million in federal matching funds to cover culturally relevant traditional healing practices that are vital to our way of life and well-being.
Representative Peshlakai co-sponsored Emily's Law, HB2281, which created the new statewide "Turquoise alert" system for missing indigenous people.
The new law was named for Emily Pike, a 14-year-old Indigenous girl who went missing and was murdered in 2024.
Mae has the knowledge and experience to work for our citizens by representing your values, and needs.
Infrastructure investment is a priority for our rural district.
In the 2025 budget Mae also supported $30 million for fire suppression and better pay and training facilities for Northern Arizona firefighters.
Representative Peshlakai understands change in laws and policies are key to creating a home of hope and opportunities.

added: top of page Home Jamescita Peshlakai Mae Peshlakai Policy Legislative District 6 Event RSVP Media Policy Platform Veterans Advocacy Jamescita Peshlakai joined the military for a job at the age of 20 years old and to be able to afford school, just as many young people in our country do.
Jamescita is a combat war veteran of the Persian Gulf War, Desert Storm and she knows the United States government has failed veterans.
Indigenous people serve at the highest percentage in the military, more than any other population.
The Trump administration's cuts to the VA and healthcare, the massive lack of mental healthcare, and lack of support in general has led to the millions of veterans living on the street.
These are policy failures from our Government that must be addressed.
Protecting the Environment Our world is a living being and all life is tethered to Mother Earth.
We are all in this together.
We must focus on de-growth and slowing gas production.
The best solution is to switch to renewables immediately.
Nuclear energy is a false climate solution.
The burden should not be on Indigenous, low income communities, but Indigenous and low income communities should be at the forefront of planning the solutions.

Missing & Murdered As indigenous women our candidates know that Missing and Murdered Indigenous People issues are directly connected to lack of housing, lack of economic opportunities, loss of culture, domestic violence, and just surviving.
Representative Mae Peshlakai is extremely proud to co-sponsor and pass Emily’s bill into law creating the “Turquoise Alert System”.
Emily’s bill was named after Emily Pike, a 14 year old who went missing from a group home and was later found murdered.
Despite the passing of Emily’s Bill there is still so much that needs to be addressed to protect vulnerable people.
The Republicans in control of the legislature have stopped creative legislation addressing this epidemic.
Save Public Education Public Education is the most important investment we can make as a state.
Our youth are our future and a strong public education system is needed to set our young people on the right path.
Over the last few decades in Arizona we’ve seen the result of our underfunded public school system.
We rank near last in the nation in most categories and that is because we’ve refused to properly invest in our children.
With the recent expansion of the ESA program to allow for universal vouchers we are now seeing; 1.
Schools closing around the state 2.
Over $1 billion being looted out of the system.
Over $124 million of these dollars are approved with 0 oversight and have been used to pay for luxury items like diamond rings and electric bikes .
This will have the most negative impact to our rural communities where our public schools have been dealing with decades of budget cuts and under-funding.
This is the wealthy stealing and ensuring that the majority of public schools students in Arizona have less opportunity for a decent future.
We must repeal the universal voucher program, pay teachers and staff a fair wage, and support our students' mental health.
We must once again prioritize public education in our state.
Our legislature is one of the only guardrails to this injustice.
Tribal Sovereignty Arizona has 23 indigenous tribes.
Arizona must recognize the authority and sovereignty of the tribes to govern themselves.
For far too long the federal and state governments have exploited indigenous people.
If the state legislature plans to sell state lands, it should be first offered to indigenous tribes for $1 (which is more than what the US Government paid to tribes).
Medicare for All Healthcare is a human right, and providing that care is the responsibility of the government.
Healthcare on Tribal lands is mandated by treaties and we must respect those treaties.
Additionally, let us expand on that idea.
Healthcare should be a right for everyone.
Legislative oversight is key to ensuring Federal commitments are adhered to.
We will raise our voices and ensure that allocation of funds meet the guidelines of Federal commitments.
Angela, Mae, and Jamescita will also push our state towards Medicare-For-All in any way they can at the state level.
Human Rights Regardless of gender, race, religion, or sexual orientation you should be treated with equality and respect.
The trailblazers are committed to honoring our values and protecting our communities.
Abolish ICE Immigration Customs Enforcement (ICE) is a new agency, it was only created in the last 25 years.
It has become a cruel, broken way to engage in immigration enforcement.
The agency is rotten to its core.
We must completely abolish ICE and create a humane immigration policy.
Being a border state, Arizona has a key role in the national conversation.
We must support our immigrant neighbors.
Remember that you live on stolen land.

We use your information solely for communications and support related to the Mae Peshlakai for AZ House campaign.
D) Opt-Out Instructions You can opt out of receiving text messages at any time.
You can opt out of receiving text messages at any time by texting STOP to any text you receive from us.
