E) Information Sharing and Sale Policy Mae Peshlakai for AZ House does not sell, rent, or share your personal information with third parties for marketing purposes.

All personal data is used only by the campaign and authorized staff or vendors who assist in campaign operations (e.g., communications or donation processing) and who are bound by this Privacy Policy.
We will not sell, rent, or otherwise share your personal data to third parties for promotional/marketing purposes.
However, we may share your information with service providers for business operations and/or legal authorities when required by law or to protect our rights.

F) Mobile Opt-In Information Mae Peshlakai for AZ House confirms that mobile opt-in information will not be shared with third parties, except as necessary to send you campaign-related communications using secure messaging platforms.
Your mobile information will never be sold, rented, or distributed for any external use.
G) Data Security We implement industry-standard security measures to protect your information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction.
While no system is fully secure, we strive to ensure your personal information remains private and safeguarded.

added: About Issues District Map Get Involved Donate Donate About Issues District Get Involved Donate TEXAS SENATE DISTRICT 19 Fighting for the Heart of Texas Marcus Cardenas is a proven small business owner who understands what it takes to create jobs, support families, and keep our communities safe.
Join Our Campaign Our Priorities Texas families deserve a senator who will fight for economic opportunity, public safety, and the values that make our state great.

Together, we'll build a stronger future for District 19. — Marcus Cardenas MEET MARCUS A Leader Who Cares About Texas A True Texas Success Story Marcus Cardenas was born and raised on the Southside of San Antonio, where family, faith, and community shaped every part of his life.
Marcus grew up learning the values of hard work, integrity, and service to community.
As a small business owner Marcus has created jobs, supported families, and contributed to the economic vitality of District 19.
Building a Life Through Perseverance After attending St.
Joseph's Catholic School, Kazen Middle School, and South San High School—where he played basketball—Marcus began his studies at Palo Alto College.
In 2007, tragedy struck when his older brother passed away in a motorcycle accident.
Marcus made the difficult decision to set aside his education and step into the family plumbing business to help support his loved ones.
Through hard work and determination, Marcus built Vertex Concrete, a thriving business that has served District 19 for over a decade.
As a proud father to his daughter Isabella and uncle to his nieces and nephews, Marcus understands what Texas families need: opportunity, safety, and a brighter future.
Invest in Texas' Future Your contribution helps us reach more voters, spread our message, and win this critical race.
Every dollar makes a difference in building a stronger District 19. $25 $50 $100 $250 $500 Cover the processing fee? +$ 1.06 Contribute Now Paid for by Marcus for Texas.
Contributions are not tax-deductible.
OUR PRIORITIES Fighting for What Matters Marcus is focused on the issues that impact District 19 families every single day Economic Development Creating Jobs.
Growing Businesses.
Building Prosperity.
As a successful small business owner, Marcus knows what it takes to create jobs and drive economic growth.
He'll work to attract new businesses to District 19, reduce regulatory burdens on job creators, and ensure Texas remains the best state in America for entrepreneurs and workers alike.
Marcus will fight for policies that support small businesses, lower taxes, and create high-paying career opportunities for Texas families.
Economic prosperity isn't just about numbers—it's about giving every Texan the chance to achieve their dreams.
Public Safety Backing the Blue.
Protecting Families.
Securing Communities.
Every family deserves to feel safe in their home and neighborhood.
Marcus will be a strong voice for law enforcement, fighting to ensure our police have the resources and support they need to keep our communities safe from crime and violence.
Marcus opposes any effort to defund the police and will work to strengthen penalties for violent criminals.
He believes in smart, effective policies that protect law-abiding citizens while holding criminals accountable.
Public safety is not negotiable.
Education & Opportunity Investing in Our Future.
Empowering Parents.
Supporting Teachers.
Quality education is the foundation of opportunity.
Marcus supports increased funding for schools, better pay for teachers, and empowering parents to make the best decisions for their children's education.
Every child in District 19 deserves access to excellent schools.
Infrastructure & Growth Building Better Roads.
Modernizing Systems.
Planning for Tomorrow.
District 19 is growing, and our infrastructure needs to keep pace.
Marcus will fight for investments in roads, bridges, water systems, and broadband internet to ensure our communities can thrive now and in the future.
Smart infrastructure investment means better quality of life for all Texans.

added: 0 Skip to Content Home About Mark Issues FAQ Register to Vote Press News Events Volunteer Contact DONATE Open Menu Close Menu Home About Mark Issues FAQ Register to Vote Press News Events Volunteer Contact DONATE Open Menu Close Menu Home About Mark Issues FAQ Register to Vote Press News Events Volunteer Contact DONATE NEWS October 15 - Mark Releases Video of Debate with Cardboard Adrian Smith Today we released a video of my debate with a cardboard cutout of Adrian Smith.
You can watch the full debate here: DEBATE In July Nebraska Public Media, KRVN, and the Omaha World-Herald invited the candidates to debate.
The Democrat missed the deadline to respond by several weeks, so those media outlets decided not to hold any debate.
According to Matt Olberding of Nebraska Public Media, Mark was the only candidate to respond to the debate invitation in a timely fashion.
October 15 - Mark Hosts Ag Summit in Wood River On October 15th I hosted an ag summit in Wood River.
Our panelists included Nebraska Farmers Union President John Hansen and broadcaster Trent Loos.
While John and Trent don’t agree on everything, we found some common ground.
I found this very helpful and was proud that we had an event that fostered genuine discussion.
October 14 - Mark Hosts Town Hall in McCook On October 14th I hosted a Town Hall at the Pour Farm in McCook.
Great venue.
I enjoyed answering questions from area residents and learning about their concerns.
October 14 - Mark Visits Imperial On October 14th Solomon and I visited Imperial, NE.
We hosted a Meet and Greet at a local restaurant and I met with local residents.
It’s a small town, but we gave away ten yard signs.
People want change.

The revised proposal addresses constitutional concerns raised during the legislative process while preserving a two-year revival window for certain claims, and now returns to the House for further consideration.

Critics are underwhelmed.

By: Nancy Lavin May 18, 2026 Senator Mark McKenney's legislation to restructure Rhode Island's coastal management system was highlighted in ongoing discussions about the future of the Coastal Resources Management Council.

The article examines competing approaches to CRMC reform, including proposals supported by environmental advocates and state leaders as policymakers consider changes to the agency's oversight and decision-making structure.

Read the Full Article Rhode Island Senate unveils 2026 healthcare legislation package By: Gino de Angelis Mar 12, 2026 Rhode Island Senate leaders unveiled a 17-bill healthcare package aimed at expanding behavioral health services, protecting patients and providers, and strengthening the state's healthcare workforce.

The legislation addresses issues ranging from crisis response and insurance coverage to workforce development and medical education, reflecting ongoing efforts by Senate lawmakers, including Senator Mark McKenney, to improve access to quality healthcare across Rhode Island.

Read the Full Article Bill would create advocacy office for older Rhode Islanders By: Alexander Castro Mar 11, 2026 Senator Mark McKenney and Representative Joseph Solomon have introduced legislation to establish a Rhode Island Office of the Elder Advocate, a proposed independent office dedicated to protecting the rights and well-being of older adults.

The office would assist seniors in navigating state services, addressing issues such as age discrimination, financial exploitation, housing, access to benefits, and guardianship, while also advocating for improvements in elder care and government responsiveness.

Mark McKenney, a Warwick Democrat and chair of the Senate Committee on Rules, led a successful push for rules revisions that will requires the Senate to publish online any written testimony related to bills.
The rules change, mirroring a similar change made by the House four years ago, has been pushed for by good government groups and media members without success until Sen.

Senator.
“From Cordova to the Interior to Nome, I’m traveling to every corner of our state because every Alaskan deserves a voice,” said Mary Peltola.
“The skyrocketing cost of fuel, groceries, and housing is making it harder and harder for families in Cordova and across Alaska to get by.

As an independent voice for Alaska, I will stand up to anyone to restore our fisheries, strengthen the Marine Highway System, bring down costs on groceries and energy, and put Alaska first.” At the meet and greet and in meetings with local community leaders and officials, Mary heard from Alaskans suffering the fallout of DC price hikes who are finding it harder and harder to afford gas and housing and make a life in Alaska.

Across every conversation, the message from Alaskans is clear: the rigged system in DC is harming our Alaska way of life, and they want a senator who will actually bring down costs and put Alaska first.

Yesterday’s visit follows Mary’s announcements of bold plans to lower costs , save our fish , boost oil and gas production , take care of our veterans , and fix the rigged system in DC that is harming our state, and comes as over 15,000 Alaskans have signed up to help elect Mary to the Senate.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/853819445_122125774395364925_4610386654667661927_n.jpg|Show up. Do the job. Follow the money. I went to the Creeds Ruritan Club Candidate Forum tonight. Thank you first and foremost to the Creeds Ruritan Club for hosting the event. Eight City Council candidates, three School Board candidates, and about 50 community members were there. What I learned: 1. Show up. It was humbling to be around people so expert in things I'm not. Candidates and residents alike cared deeply about southern Virginia Beach and its agriculture. By being there, I learned a lot, from why holding the Green Line matters to how wind-driven tides push water up Back Bay and the North Landing River and onto farmland. 2. Do the job. Congress has to do better. — Pass a 5-year Farm Bill, not another stopgap. Same for budgets: on time. — Most of "the government" isn't elected. Congress has to set the deadlines, fund the people needed to meet them, and hold agencies to the results. — Farm labor depends on the H-2A visa. Fix it: faster processing, lower fees, and access for year-round work like dairy. 3. Follow the money. I don't take party or special-interest money, because that money comes with lanes. Voters deserve someone who can vote outside them. Finally, I met people who had no idea I was running. That's tough to hear, and I know it's my responsibility. Please like, comment, and most of all, SHARE THIS POST WITH YOUR NETWORK. mattbakerindependent.com #VA02 #𝐯𝐢𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐚𝐛𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡

added: Home About Matt Admin Donate Open main menu State Representative Matt Longjohn MD Re-election 2026 • Serving Michigan's 40th District Our Priorities Join Us Our Priorities Fighting for a Healthier Michigan As a physician and policy expert, I have spent my career fighting for patient advocacy and public health.
Now, I am bringing that same dedication to Lansing to ensure every family in the 40th District has access to quality healthcare, clean water, and economic opportunity.
Dr.
Longjohn is a nationally recognized leader in public health and health systems innovation.
For over 25 years, he has led non-profit organizations to integrate community resources into equitable, effective, and sustained population health initiatives.
Notably, he was identified by the Obama Administration as one of the top 100 health innovators in the country.
Reduce healthcare costs and expand access to high quality, equitable healthcare so everyone can get the care they need.
Protect our lakes, rivers, and farmland and hold polluters accountable to ensure clear air and drinking water.
Support families by building an economy with good paying jobs and career pathways for young people.
Meet Matt About Matt Dr.
Matt Longjohn is a physician, a public health expert, and a dedicated community leader.
With over 25 years of experience in healthcare innovation, Matt has dedicated his life to improving the lives of others.

removed: Home About Matt Admin Donate Open main menu State Representative Matt Longjohn MD Re-election 2026 • Serving Michigan's 40th District Our Priorities Join Us Our Priorities Fighting for a Healthier Michigan As the only physician in Michigan's Legislature and a first-term state representative for the 40th House District, Matt Longjohn is focused on one thing: making sure Michiganders can live their healthiest possible lives.

In Lansing, Matt is fighting to: Lower health care and prescription drug costs Strengthen primary care access across the state Invest resources in accessible, life‑long public education Defend Medicaid from federal cuts Bring state dollars back to our communities Ensure we all have the clean air and water our families need Expand breast cancer screening, immunization education, and other preventive health services Protect the safety net families rely on for food, housing, transportation, and utilities Meet Matt About Matt Dr.
Matt Longjohn is a first-term member of the Michigan House of Representatives, where he has the honor and privilege of serving the City of Portage, and Oshtemo and Texas Townships.
He wakes up every day thinking about how to improve the health and quality of life of every Michigander.

In Lansing, he serves on the appropriations committee, as the minority vice chair of the higher education appropriations subcommittee, and as a member of the human services appropriations subcommittee.

In his first year in office he introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of prescription medications, increasing parents’ access to information about immunizations in schools and child care centers, ensuring breast cancer patients have insurance coverage for critical tests and treatments, increasing housing options, and addressing the epidemic of gun violence.
In December 2025, Dr.
Longjohn was nominated by the Lansing political press as “Freshman Lawmaker of the year”.

Open the Media Kit Announcements Press Releases October 15, 2026 · Indianapolis, Indiana Engling to Bayh: Drop the Lies, Explain the Money and Your 2014 Voter Registration Republican candidate for Indiana Secretary of State Max Engling today pushed back against Beau Bayh’s desperate, false campaign attacks, calling them a pattern of claims designed to distract voters from the Bayh family’s corruption.
“Beau keeps repeating false claims that I'm a multimillionaire profiting from data centers and insider trading.
This is unequivocally false; I have no connection to either, and the four stocks I own are worth less than $50,000 total, and I have never sold them,” Engling said.
“The lies don’t end, and it's shameful that the media will not report on how his false and separate attacks are baseless and frankly disqualifying.
Now he’s bizarrely lying, claiming I have reckless driving tickets, which is also false.
It’s just more lying from a desperate and losing campaign,” Engling said.

Engling called on Bayh to answer for his family’s ties to Leon Black, the Apollo Global Management co-founder who paid Jeffrey Epstein more than $# million and was repeatedly named in the Epstein case.
Leon Black’s donations to Evan Bayh now directly fund his own campaign per public record.
After leaving the Senate in 2011, Evan Bayh joined Black’s firm as a senior adviser and was later named in the Epstein files.
That network is now heavily funding Beau Bayh’s campaign.
Today, it was confirmed that Evan Bayh gave the Indiana Democratic Victory Committee $700,000 from his former federal campaign committee, which then passed it to Beau’s campaign.
The campaign expects that number to rise to about $2.3 million after further public disclosures.
Moreover, Beau Bayh still hasn’t answered as to why he registered to vote in Indiana in 2014 when he clearly didn’t live here.

Voter records indicate that Bayh claimed his family’s 996-square-foot, one-bedroom Indianapolis condo as his Indiana residence after turning 18 while he was at the same time enrolled in a Washington DC private high school full-time, in-person.
The records also indicate that his absentee-ballot materials were mailed to the Bayh family’s home in Virginia.
Indiana code is explicit: you must reside in the state for # days to be eligible to register to vote.
Beau Bayh’s father was not serving in the U.S.
Senate; Beau was not in college or the military when he registered to vote in Indiana.
“Beau Bayh is asking Hoosiers to put him in charge of Indiana’s elections.
He owes them a clear account of where he lived when he registered and voted in Indiana,” said Engling.

“The records raise straightforward questions about the Indianapolis condo, his time in Washington, and why his election materials went to Virginia.” Engling’s latest ad, “Only One,” highlights his support for the SAVE America Act and his commitment to verifying citizenship for federal voter registration, while drawing a sharp contrast between him and Bayh.
“Indiana’s Secretary of State is a position of public trust, not a family inheritance,” Engling said.
“That trust starts with telling the truth.

If Beau can’t be honest with voters while asking for the job, why should they trust him once he has it?” Watch “Only One” on YouTube maxforindiana.com ### Paid for by Max for Indiana Website Designed by Argo Strategy

Rent goes to someone else's asset.
Retirement savings feel out of reach.
And the wealth that gets passed from one generation to the next never quite gets started.
That gap between working hard and getting ahead is why so many families feel stuck no matter how many hours they put in.
Solutions ​ What Dr.
Maxime will do in Congress For more than 30 years, Dr.
Maxime has worked as an accountant — sitting across the table from families trying to make the numbers work.

He knows the difference between earning and owning, and he'll fight for policies that help working families cross that line: 01 Expand responsible first-time-homebuyer assistance so renting doesn't have to be forever.

The Promise The goal isn't just to survive the paycheck.
The goal is to build something that lasts — for your family and for the next generation.

added: Menu Home About Priorities Endorsements News Join Our Team Donate Middleton Announces Major Law Enforcement Endorsements Over 30 Cities and Local Associations Join TMPA, Fraternal Order of Police, CLEAT and Texas Sheriff’s Regional Alliance FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: October 15, 2026 Galveston – Today, in a massive show of support from law enforcement, the Mayes Middleton Campaign released the endorsement of 31 local police associations (POAs), including those in every one of the largest 10 cities in Texas.
These 31 POAs represent officers in departments responsible for the public safety of over 11 million Texas citizens.

The Texas Municipal Police Association, Texas State Lodge - Fraternal Order of Police, and Combined Law Enforcement Associations of Texas, also endorsing Middleton, cumulatively represent over 81,000 police officers across Texas.
Sen.

Middleton was endorsed by the Texas Sheriff’s Regional Alliance, an alliance of 16 Texas sheriffs committed to promoting and advocating for responsible policies that strengthen communities and curb crime in Texas.
Also endorsing Middleton are sheriff and law enforcement associations in Dallas, Tarrant, Harris, and Montgomery counties.

The endorsements include the Dallas Police Association, Garland Police Association, Mesquite Police Association, Richardson Police Officers Association, and Dallas County Sheriff’s Association, all in the home county of Sen.
Middleton’s opponent.
Sen.

removed: Home ABOUT PRIORITIES CONTACT DONATE Proven Leadership for Eagle River, Chugiak, & Peter’s Creek Ken McCarty is a proven community leader focused on responsive representation, Alaska values, economic opportunity, and a stronger future for Eagle River, Chugiak, and Peter’s Creek.

DONATE ABOUT KEN MCCARTY Known by Relationships, Not Just Recognition Ken McCarty has spent decades serving the Eagle River, Chugiak, and Peter’s Creek community through leadership, counseling, education, healthcare, and public service.
As the owner of Discovery Cove Counseling and a former Trustee of the Alaska Mental Health Trust, Ken has worked directly with individuals and families facing real-life challenges.
His experience as a State House Representative for District 13 gave him firsthand insight into the importance of responsive, accountable leadership that listens to the people it serves.
Beyond public office, Ken has remained deeply involved in the community through local organizations, youth programs, aviation advocacy, healthcare initiatives, and volunteer service.
Whether helping improve community spaces, supporting local schools, or attending community council meetings, Ken believes leadership starts with being present and involved.

Ken is committed to protecting Alaska values, supporting local families and businesses, and ensuring Eagle River, Chugiak, and Peter’s Creek continue to have a strong voice and dependable representation.  Former State House Representative – District 13  Former Trustee Alaska Mental Health Trust  Community Advocate & Volunteer  Owner of Discovery Cove Counseling  President – Birchwood Airport Association  Marital & Family Therapist WHY I’M RUNNING Eagle River, Chugiak, & Peter’s Creek Deserve More I’m running because our community deserves leadership that listens, responds, and stays connected to the people it represents.
Eagle River, Chugiak, and Peter’s Creek are built on strong families, hard work, independence, and neighbors who take care of one another.
I believe leadership should reflect those same values through honesty, accountability, and real community involvement.
My goal is simple: protect Alaska values, support local businesses and families, strengthen our economy, and help build a stronger future for the next generation.
Leadership is not about politics alone; it’s about relationships, service, and showing up for the community.
OUR PRIORITIES Priorities That Put Alaska First Fair & Transparent Elections Support simple, transparent, and easy-to-understand elections for every Alaskan.
Protect Alaska’s PFD Ensure Alaskans receive their fair share and protect the Permanent Fund Dividend.
Strong Local Communities Empower and support communities across Eagle River, Chugiak, & Peter’s Creek.
Experienced Leadership Bring experience, leadership, and practical solutions to Juneau.
Mental Health Expand access to care, support recovery, and strengthen community resources.
Aviation & Infrastructure Invest in systems that connect communities and support Alaska’s economy.
CONTACT US  ken@mccartyforalaska.com  (907) 406-2300  mccartyforalaska.com Paid for by McCarty for Alaska PO Box 771777, Eagle River, AK 99577

title.before: Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY – Delegate Marvin E.

removed: Skip to content Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Menu Close Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Blog Home / Latest News / Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY Florida collapse raises concerns about condominium oversight in Maryland; here’s what the legislature should do | COMMENTARY Post author: admin Post published: July 8, 2021 Post category: Latest News The sudden collapse of the 12-story Champlain Towers South condominium building in Surfside, Florida, was a tragedy of a scale normally associated with natural disasters or terrorist attacks.
The exact cause is not yet known and may not be well understood for months yet.

But while the investigation, cleanup and search for missing people efforts continue, the circumstances strongly point to deterioration in the concrete structure that for several years had not been sufficiently addressed by the governing board of the building’s condominium association .
As recently as April, condo owners had been warned that a major renovation was needed in response to serious water damage evident in the basement garage at a cost of more than $15 million.

While few communities have witnessed a sudden building failure of this magnitude, what is far more commonplace is a condominium development — whether a high-rise, collection of townhouses or low-rise apartments — facing insufficient investment in maintenance and replacement of common assets.
Civil lawsuits arise from these circumstances fairly routinely.
Someone’s roof leaks, and the board is alleged not to have kept up with repairs.
The costs add up quickly: Siding needs to be replaced periodically, outdoor spaces replanted, pools resurfaced.
Cracks in the foundation or support columns might be the most expensive (and scariest) possibility of all.
Yet for many condo boards, the focus is always on keeping fees to the minimum.
After all, the higher the fee, the lower the resale price of the unit as buyers look at the total monthly cost of ownership.
In Maryland, government has always treated such arrangements with a relatively light regulatory hand.
Only two counties, Prince George’s and Montgomery, formally review condominium documents, and only Montgomery has the authority to enforce them.
Prince George’s County has taken a slightly different tack that is especially instructive, however.

Since last year, the county requires condo associations and similar bodies to conduct a review every five years to see if they’re collecting enough money (and holding enough in reserves) to meet their projected maintenance costs.
The governing boards must then set fees based on meeting those anticipated needs.
In other words: If your roof needs to be replaced in 10 years, you had better be collecting sufficient money to cover that cost between now and then.
And such studies can’t be conducted by just any Tom, Dick or Harry.
The law requires the contractor to be well-qualified and experienced, recognized by the state board of architects or engineers, for example.
In the wake of the Florida disaster, this appears to be an excellent idea.
Earlier this year, Del.
Marvin E.
Holmes Jr., a Prince George’s Democrat, offered legislation to take his home county’s approach statewide .
It passed the House of Delegates by a 2-to-1 margin but never got serious consideration in the state Senate.
It needs to become a much higher priority in the next legislative session in early 2022.
As Assistant Maryland Attorney General Karen S.

Straughn testified in a House committee in January, such assessments may raise fees in the short-term, but they spare homeowners major increases in the long-term when the bill suddenly comes due for major repairs that had not been properly anticipated.
The measure even allows condo associations to raise fees higher than whatever local cap may exist.
Again, that’s because it’s in the owners’ collective financial interest.
Some developers may oppose the measure.

But during testimony on House Bill 313 , builders did not object to the periodic studies, only asking that there ought to be an exemption for smaller developments with few common assets that are unlikely to generate major new costs.
That seems a reasonable point, particularly for projects where the only common spaces are walkways, parking lots and signs.
There is certainly no reason to make this unduly burdensome.
Indeed, it’s likely that the folks who will appreciate this level of protection most may be the homeowners who volunteer to serve on the governing boards of common ownership communities.
Few enter such arrangements with a deep background in construction, engineering or property management.
The more guardrails the better for these potentially fraught circumstances, particularly for projects like beachfront high-rises where the risks are so high, as the Surfside disaster demonstrated.
Surely, the owners will sleep better knowing that there are periodic assessments of maintenance needs — and the funds to cover them are going to be there when needed.
Baltimore Sun editorial writers offer opinions and analysis on news and issues relevant to readers.
They operate separately from the newsroom.

title.after: The Maryland House of Delegates – Delegate Marvin E.

added: Skip to content Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Menu Close Home About Marvin Issues District 23 Endorsements Up Coming Events Covid-19 Contact Us Get Involved Blog Home / Latest News / The Maryland House of Delegates The Maryland House of Delegates Post author: admin Post published: November 6, 2020 Post category: Latest News November 5, 2020 Dear Members: I want to thank you for your patience and perseverance during this interim.
I know that this has been a difficult time for each of you, your constituents and your communities.
I am hopeful that Maryland will continue to stay ahead of the curve on managing the COVID-19 pandemic.

My staff and I have spent the interim meeting with public health officials and experts in the infectious disease field; other state legislative leaders from across the country; contractors who specialize in air flow and surface cleaning; operations teams on Capitol Hill; advocacy and community groups; and House members from both parties to craft a plan for the 2021 legislative session.
The main goal of this plan to allow all of us to execute our constitutional responsibilities to the fullest extent possible, in the safest way possible, for the full # days of the regular session.
The pandemic is a constantly evolving situation and I want to assure you that we have contingency plans in place should the trends get better or worse.
However, based on what we know now, we will move forward with a hybrid plan for the legislative session, as detailed below.

FLOOR SESSION : Since the House is the largest legislative body that operates in the State of Maryland, we have had to make a few changes to our process to protect the health of members and staff while ensuring that each of you has the ability to fully participate on behalf of your constituents.
Some of these changes are by policy and some will require adoption of a new House rule that we will circulate to the members ahead of Opening Day.
To adhere to public health guidance: Meetings as One Body : The House will meet simultaneously in two locations on campus that will act as one legislative body.
We have made accommodations for 70 members to sit in Rooms 170-180 in the House Office Building as the “Chamber Annex,” at assigned, socially-distanced desks.
The proceedings will be livestreamed, in real-time, into 170-180, and each member sitting in the Chamber Annex will be able to vote, offer amendments and debate legislation real-time as well.
Delegates will be required to wear face coverings, and staff will be limited to core staff on floor.
Delegates in the Chamber will also be assigned new seats, at an appropriate distance from one another.
We will determine what members are in which space by a lottery system.
Frequent Breaks: We will not meet for more than two hours at a time without a break, to allow for the Chamber and the Chamber Annex to be thoroughly cleaned and sanitized and to give members a break.

Extra Precautions for any immuno-compromised members: While we believe that all of the precautions enumerated in this memo will keep members and staff as safe as possible during the legislative session, I understand that some of you may have unique circumstances due to being in a higher risk category.
Our public health experts have advised that we make accommodations for any of you who have additional healthcare needs to have the option of participating from the gallery facing me.
We have wired the gallery for Wi Fi and power and can equip you to vote from the gallery, however, we cannot accommodate you to be able to debate legislation, due to limitations on A/V wiring.
If you want to be seated in the gallery, recognizing the A/V limitations, please contact Alex Hughes in my office.
Transparency: All House proceedings will be livestreamed.
I know some of you were concerned about the problems with the livestream last year, as was I.
OIS has worked throughout the interim with our vendors to ensure that these problems do not persist in 2021.
Additionally, the press will be permitted in limited numbers in the gallery above me, socially distanced, and, in the Chamber Annex.
Air Flow : Increased HVAC protocols to maximize fresh airflow into chamber have been implemented, and the windows above the Tiffany glass ceiling have been opened.

Additionally, air purifiers have been placed in the Chamber Limited people on the floor: For the 2021 legislative session, we will only permit members and essential staff in the Chamber and Chamber Annex.

Additionally, under changes to the House Rules for this extraordinary circumstance, we will: Allow for bill introduction and the exchange of messages between the House and the Senate and the Governor with a limited number of members from both parties in attendance.
You will still need to submit your blue back to the Clerk’s office in person to introduce your bill.
Move the Bill Request Guarantee deadline up to January 19 th and the Hopper deadline up to close of business on February 5 th to be able to better manage work flow.
Sponsor only bill introduction, to avoid unnecessarily passing blue backs around to multiple members.
As a result of these changes, after Opening Day, I do not anticipate that we will be on the floor daily for the first third of session.
I also do not anticipate that we will be on the floor on Monday nights until March.
We will consolidate the work schedule of the House to minimize the number of people who need to be on campus each day.
COMMITTEE WORK : House Committees will operate virtually this year, with bill hearings beginning on the second day of session.

Each of your Chairs will get in touch with you in the coming weeks as to the anticipated work schedule for each committee, however, everyone should be prepared for bill hearings to start in earnest on January 14 th .
You can participate in hearings from your home or your Annapolis office, should you choose, but you must remain on camera while you are participating in committee hearings.
You should prioritize your legislation this year and get bills in early to provide more time for the possibility of passage.
Hearing Schedule : All committees will provide at least 48-hour member and public notice as to which bills will be heard during which time slot on which day via the MGA website.
Online Testimony Submission : OIS has designed a system to allow the public to upload written testimony.
Members of the relevant committee will be able to access the written testimony for each bill through their floor system.
Online Bill File Availability : The testimony file for each bill will be posted on the MGA website after a bill is voted out of the relevant standing committee.
Any bill file not up on the website by Sine Die will be publicly released after session.
Online Sign Up : OIS has designed an online testimony sign up system through the MGA website.
Each Committee Chair will provide time slots per bill for members of the public to sign up the day before the bill is scheduled to be heard.
Subcommittee meetings : While subcommittees do not fall under the Open Meetings Act, all subcommittee meetings will be livestreamed through the MGA website.
Voting Sessions : All voting sessions will be livestreamed through the MGA website.

LEGISLATIVE CAMPUS State House : We are working with the Governor and the State House Trust to keep the State House closed to the public for the legislative session to prevent large crowds from congregating inside.
Construction on Lawyer’s Mall will be completed by January, so outdoor rallies will still be permitted if socially distanced and masked, based on City of Annapolis guidelines.
House Office Building : While we are discouraging in-person meetings for public health reasons, we recognize that such meetings may occasionally need to occur.
We will allow access to the public and other non-legislative officials by appointment only, to avoid unnecessary crowding in hallways.
Any meeting guests will have to be escorted to and from the main entrance to the House Office Building and your office.
District Nights, Legislative Receptions and Committee Dinners : All such events are cancelled for in-person participation for the 2021 session.

Member Availability : We have worked with OIS to add a section on each member’s webpage to list office hours and best way to contact each member (by Zoom, by appointment etc.) on your webpage on the MGA website.
I encourage each of you to set specific times that members of the public can schedule to meet with you.
Senate Canteen : We are working with DGS to have expanded hours and food runners available for the Senate Canteen so that each of you have access to food without having to leave campus.

HEALTH & SAFETY Face Coverings: Masks will be required on the legislative complex and on the floor of both the Chamber and Chamber Annex for the 2021 legislative session, including during legislative debate.
The Anne Arundel County Health Department has also offered to have member’s properly fitted for N-95 masks, in the event you want to purchase and use this type of mask.
You can contact my office for assistance.

Testing : The Senate President and I have worked with the Department of Health and Department of General Services to stand up a testing tent five days a week in the B Lot adjacent to the House Office Building.
Both rapid tests and PCR tests will be available to members and staff who are on campus.
Health Challenge App : OIS has designed an app that all members and staff will be required to use to gain entry to the building each day.

This app can be downloaded on your phone (instructions will follow in an email) to allow Capitol Police and State Police to see that you have answered the health challenge questions for the day for COVID-19 risk status to allow building entry.
These include the standard questions regarding your temperature and overall health.

Cleaning : DGS is cleaning all high-touch surfaces and restrooms in the House Office Building three times per day in the common areas and we have hired additional cleaning staff to supplement these services.
We also have specific disinfecting plans in place on a daily basis for all buildings and the Chamber and Chamber Annex in particular, as well as on an as-needed basis for other operations.
Air Flow: We have worked with DGS to ensure that the HVAC systems are operating with maximum fresh air flow, as well as top quality filters for air purification.
We have purchased air purifiers, based on the square footage, for the Chamber and Chamber Annex to add an additional layer of protection.
Additionally, we have authorized the purchase of one air purifier for use in your Annapolis office out of your budget.
Hand Sanitizer : There are hand sanitizer stations throughout the House Office Building and State House in high traffic areas, including elevators.
PPE Supplies : The Senate President and I have authorized members to pay for PPE (masks and gloves) in reasonable quantities for your use and your staff’s use out of your member budgets.

Contact Response Team : In the event of a positive case of COVID-19, we have hired a small team to work out of the Human Resources Office to provide rapid outreach to any member or staff that may have come in to contact with that positive case.
STAFFING : In general, the Senate President and I are encouraging everyone to telework to the extent possible.
OIS has enabled every member to use Google Voice to roll your phones over to a different number off campus.
The fewer people that we have on campus, the less likely we are to create a higher risk of COVID-19 spread, in the event that we have any positive cases.

Member’s Staff : All members will be required to file a staffing plan with Human Resources, identifying: (1) what staff member, if any, will be working on campus, (2) their cellphone number and (3) what days and hours they will be working on campus.
If you are in shared office space and you feel that you absolutely must have your staff person on campus, we will work with you to determine the safest way to have your staff operate.

Session secretaries: Since the work flow of session will be more remote this year, please consider carefully whether you will need a session secretary and, if so, please strongly consider accommodations for them to work remotely.
Interns and pages: The General Assembly will continue to operate both of these programs virtually.
Contact Carol Pelli if you are interested in a virtual intern or Tawanna Offer if you’re interested in supporting the virtual page program.
DLS : We have asked Vicki Gruber to pare down on-campus staff to the extent possible in order to minimize the number of people on campus.
As a result, please email or call the staffer you need to reach instead of walking over to their office.
Speaker’s Office and Minority Office : Speaker’s and Minority staff will be available and on campus daily.

LODGING Booking Accommodations : While the full House will not be meeting daily, especially in the beginning of session, we will allow members to book whatever lodging they deem necessary in Annapolis for their own safety and work schedule.
I would encourage those of you that do not need to be in Annapolis every day to not stay in Annapolis to the extent possible.
Tax Exempt Status : Members can book rooms on a daily basis without having to pay the lodging tax out of pocket, based on advice from the Attorney General.
Please be sure to use your tax exempt card at the time of booking.
Again, thank you for your patience during this interim.
If you have any questions, please contact Alex Hughes in my office.
Sincerely, Adrienne A.

removed: Melanie Medley-Thomas for Texas House 103 Home About Issues Donate Contact About Melanie A life dedicated to service, faith, and community Colorado Roots Melanie grew up in a rural farming and ranching community in Colorado, where she learned the values of hard work, perseverance, and community.
Her upbringing instilled in her a deep appreciation for the land, family, and the importance of supporting one another.
Gold Star Sister As a Gold Star sister, Melanie understands the profound sacrifice made by military families.
This personal experience has shaped her commitment to honoring veterans and supporting those who serve our nation.
Faith-Centered Values Faith is the cornerstone of Melanie's life and leadership.
Her unwavering belief in doing what is right guides every decision she makes and fuels her dedication to serving others with integrity and compassion.
Education Melanie earned her degree in Psychology with a minor in Sociology from Oral Roberts University.
Her education provided her with a deep understanding of human behavior, community dynamics, and the importance of empathy in leadership.

Professional Career With a successful career in the health insurance industry in Dallas, Melanie has gained valuable experience in navigating complex systems and advocating for individuals and families.
Her professional background equips her with the skills to tackle challenging policy issues.
Athletic Background Melanie's athletic background taught her the importance of discipline, teamwork, and perseverance.
These qualities continue to drive her approach to leadership and her commitment to achieving results for Texas families.
Community Service Throughout her life, Melanie has been deeply committed to community service.
Whether volunteering, mentoring, or advocating for those in need, she believes in the power of giving back and making a positive impact in the lives of others.
A Leader for Texas Melanie Medley-Thomas brings a unique combination of personal experience, professional expertise, and unwavering values to her campaign.
She is committed to fighting for Texas families, protecting our freedoms, and building a brighter future for all Texans.

Menu FEC Complaint Accuses Aisha Wahab of Laundering Corporate Money Into Her Campaign for Congress August 12, 2026 FEC Complaint Accuses Aisha Wahab of Laundering Corporate Money Into Her Campaign for Congress Complaint Traces $# From Wahab’s Fossil Fuel and Pharmaceutical Corporation-Funded State Senate Account to the Alameda County Democratic Party, Which Was Paying for Pro-Wahab Campaign Mail Within Weeks DUBLIN, CA — On Monday, Alameda County Supervisor Nate Miley filed a formal complaint with the Federal Election Commission against State Senator Aisha Wahab and the Alameda County Democratic Party.

The complaint alleges that Wahab’s state Senate campaign committee illegally funneled $60,000 to the county party as the party began spending tens of thousands of dollars to support Wahab’s campaign for Congress in California’s 14th District.
The complaint was drafted by Kaufman Legal Group, and filed as vote-by-mail ballots sit in voters’ hands ahead of the August 18 special election.

The money trail described in the complaint comes directly from Wahab’s and the party’s own campaign finance filings: On May 5, 2026, Wahab for State Senate 2026 reported a $60,000 contribution to the Alameda County Democratic Party.
According to state campaign finance records, it was the first contribution the committee had ever made to the party.
On May 21, 2026, the party’s federal committee reported two independent expenditures, of $12,037.21 and another $12,037.21 , for postage on mailers supporting Wahab’s congressional campaign.
On May 26, 2026, the party reported another $7,318.32 for printing and design of pro-Wahab mailers, bringing its reported spending for Wahab to $31,392.74 in the three weeks following the transfer.
Federal law prohibits corporations from contributing to congressional campaigns.

California law does not, and Wahab has taken full advantage: a memo shows that corporate and industry money accounts for 50.1% of everything her state Senate committee has raised in the current reporting period , including: Thousands of dollars each from Amazon, Google, Meta, AT&T, and Comcast Donations more than half a dozen casinos and card rooms Tens of thousands of dollars from fossil fuel companies, including Sempra Energy and an Occidental Petroleum subsidiary Thousands of dollars from Pfizer, PhRMA (pharmaceutical lobby), and Novo Nordisk The complaint alleges that routing that money through the county party and into federal campaign mail laundered contributions that are illegal in a congressional election, in violation of federal campaign finance law.
“I have spent more than two decades in local government, and I have never seen a money trail this brazen.
Aisha Wahab’s state committee had never given the Alameda County Democratic Party a dime.
Then, with ballots about to drop, it handed the party $60,000, and within weeks the party was paying for her congressional campaign mail,” said Alameda County Supervisor Nate Miley .
“Corporate money that is banned from federal elections does not become legal because it takes a detour through a party committee.

Voters deserve answers from the FEC, and they deserve them before this seat is decided.” “Sacramento politicians play by their own rules while families here pay the price, and this complaint shows exactly how that game works,” said Ajay Mohan, Campaign Manager for Melissa Hernandez .

“Aisha Wahab built her state account on checks from fossil fuel, pharmaceutical, and gambling companies, money that is illegal in a race for Congress, and the public record indicates it was funneled into this election anyway.
Voters are tired of it.

More Sacramento politics isn’t how we change Washington.” The complaint asks the FEC to investigate the transfer and the expenditures that followed, and to enforce federal campaign finance law to the fullest extent.
A copy of the filed complaint is available here .
To learn more about Melissa Hernandez and her campaign, visit melissahernandez2026.com .

### California’s 14th Congressional District lies entirely within Alameda County in California’s East Bay, encompassing the cities of Hayward, Livermore, Pleasanton, and Union City in full, along with portions of Castro Valley, Dublin, Fremont, and San Leandro.
The district has roughly 429,000 registered voters; 50% Democrats, 27% with no party preference, and 18% Republicans.
CA-14 residents are approximately 40% Asian, 24% Latino, 23% non-Hispanic White, and 5% Black, with the remainder multiracial, Pacific Islander, or Native American.
There are two upcoming general elections, a special general election on August 18, 2026, to complete the term vacated by former Rep.

Melissa Hurtado Oct 14 2026 PRESS RELEASE “It will go quick” – $171 million in one-time funding cobbled together to save state’s drinking... ... water program An all-hands-on-deck effort saved one of the state’s most effective drinking water programs, at least for next year.
But what happens after that?

The SAFER program, which had received $130 million annually to provide emergency water and long-term solutions for families whose wells go dry, was set to be cut by nearly half until an unlikely coalition of social justice, farmer and water manager groups rallied to save it.
The Okieville Recharge Basin completed in 2024.
Lisa McEwen / SJV Water The Okieville Recharge Basin completed in 2024.
Lisa McEwen / SJV Water On Oct.
8, about 40 people gathered on the dusty bank of a Tulare County recharge basin to celebrate that win, which resulted in one-time funding of $171 million for SAFER in the 2027-28 fiscal year.
About $71 million of that will come from the state’s greenhouse gas reduction fund and the rest is Proposition 4 money.
Even with that money secured, those gathered at the recharge basin recognized SAFER’s uncertain future and the need for San Joaquin Valley communities to seek resilience beyond SAFER.
“The objective is not to become better at delivering emergency drinking water,” said Eric R.
Quinley, general manager at Delano-Earlimart Irrigation District, at the Oct.
8 event.
A permanent funding solution for SAFER must be found as long-term solutions are identified and sustainable groundwater management practices are implemented, he said.
“The objective is to build communities where emergency drinking water is no longer necessary.
The objective is sustainability, not only for ag but for everyone who drinks water.” In that vein, the event’s location, the Okieville Recharge Basin , was key.
The basin was built just upstream from the tiny community of Okieville in Tulare County, where residents have suffered dry wells off and on for years due to drought and over pumping.
As water is recharged in the basin, it will replenish the aquifer for farmers and Okieville wells.
It took a decade of work between farmers, nonprofits, such as Self-Help Enterprises, and water agencies to build the 1,400-acre-foot basin using money from Proposition 68.
But the work isn’t over.

The Tulare Irrigation District is hoping to secure SAFER money to leverage federal funding so it can help provide Okieville residents the “ultimate resilience portfolio,” according to Tulare ID General Manager Aaron Fukuda.
That includes a new well, a back-up well, generators and a storage tank for fire flows.
“This is how it happens,” Fukuda said.
“Locals working with nonprofits and the state to help communities.
We need to leverage SAFER funding to bring anxiety levels down so when they turn on the faucet, the water will be there.” State Sen.
Melissa Hurtado, who helped get the 2027-28 SAFER funding package across the finish line, said the group won this battle but the fight for clean drinking water will continue.

“What good is recognizing the Human Right to Water if we’re not willing to provide the resources to make it a reality?” she asked, referencing the “Human Right to Water Act” passed by the Legislature in 2012.
Aaron Fukuda, General Manager of the Tulare Irrigation District.
Lisa McEwen / SJV Water Aaron Fukuda, General Manager of the Tulare Irrigation District.
Lisa McEwen / SJV Water Money is the bridge that makes that concept a reality, as proven by SAFER.

Since it was created in 2019, the program has provided $900 million in grants giving more than a million Californians access to clean drinking water by helping communities drill new wells, consolidate with larger systems and making sure residents have clean, emergency water, if needed.
State figures indicate there are still another 1,052 water systems that are failing and in need of permanent solutions.
Allensworth resident Sherry Hunter said she was shocked to learn SAFER funding had been in jeopardy earlier this year.
SAFER funds helped her small, southern Tulare County community pay for a new well and a 500,000 gallon storage tank.
“My community almost died because of a lack of water,” she said.
“It’s hard to imagine them not being there when we needed them.” Of the $171 million in next year’s kitty, she predicted: “A lot of communities will be vying for that money.
It will go quick.” Paid for by Valley Families for Melissa Hurtado for Senate 2026 You need to enable JavaScript to run this app.

added: DONATE find your voting location Home About Issues News Volunteer Shop Home About Issues News Volunteer Shop Home About Issues News Volunteer Donate Home About Issues News Volunteer Donate DONATE Michael Whatley Hosts Make More Keep More Press Conference In Brunswick County October 15, 2026 BRUNSWICK COUNTY – Today, Michael Whatley Hosted a Make More Keep More press conference in Bolivia.
Whatley and local leaders discussed how costs rose under Cooper’s watch including healthcare, energy, and housing.
Whatley also covered how Cooper will take the same tax and spend agenda to Washington, where he will make life cost more for every single North Carolina family.
Click HERE to see photos of the event “Roy Cooper was an utter disaster for North Carolina seniors.
He raised costs for energy, housing, and healthcare – and he wants to tax Social Security.
Seniors in Brunswick County and across our state cannot afford to send Cooper to the Senate.
I will fight for our seniors by lowering costs and making the crucial No Tax on Social Security provisions permanent, so our seniors keep more of their own money,” said Michael Whatley.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Accused Cocaine Trafficker Was on Healey’s Payroll, Then Received a $31,000 Payout After Being Fired Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — A former Healey administration employee now charged with trafficking nearly 18 pounds of cocaine through the governor’s Springfield office also received a $31,000 payout after he was fired.
The episode reflects a failure of basic management by Maura Healey.
LaMar Cook was hired as Western Massachusetts Deputy Director at a salary of $115,968.
According to a Boston Herald public records request, the governor’s office and State Police were aware of his criminal history before he was hired.
That history includes a 2001 arrest in connection with a Springfield shooting, which the Springfield Republican reported involved two men allegedly firing at people on a porch.
State Police say they intercepted a package containing nearly eight kilograms of cocaine addressed to Cook’s office.

He was indicted on five charges: trafficking in 200 grams or more of cocaine, conspiracy to violate drug laws, possession of a gun without a firearms identification card, possession of ammunition without a firearms identification card, and unlicensed operation of a motor vehicle.
After Cook was fired, the administration paid him $31,000 for unused vacation time.
The Executive Office of Administration and Finance says he was not entitled to the money because he was fired with cause, and the administration has called the payment a mistake.

Cook has said he spent it, intends to keep it, and told reporters, “I earned it.” A judge appointed by Healey also reduced Cook’s bail from $75,000 to $25,000, with conditions that he surrender his passport and not travel internationally.
Cook then enrolled in SNAP, and the Department of Transitional Assistance says the state is prohibited from denying him benefits.
He reportedly used them to help pay for a family trip to Walt Disney World and has said he plans to take more.
Maura Healey is responsible for who she hires and for every dollar her administration sends out the door.
Healey’s administration hired someone with a violent history, lost $31,000 of taxpayer money to him after he was fired for cause, and has not recovered it.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

It comes after Healey rejected an invitation to debate on WFXT-TV, despite telling voters on September 2nd she and Lt.
Gov.
Kim Driscoll would “show up.” “I know where Kim and I are, and I know where we’re going to continue be the next 62 days, including showing up for debates,” said Healey.
“I don’t know if he’s going to.” Minogue has shown up, accepting all four invitations for televised debates on WFXT, WWLP, WBZ, and WCVB.
Now, Minogue says, it’s Healey’s turn.
“Maura Healey has spent three years driving up energy and housing costs, failing to conduct the audit, and making it harder to live and work in Massachusetts.
Voters deserve to hear how she tries to defend her disastrous record.
Hard-working families are struggling to get ahead on her watch.
They deserve direct answers.
They should be allowed every opportunity to contrast our two clearly different paths in this tipping-point election.
But most of all, they deserve a governor who keeps their word,” said Minogue.
Minogue now calls on Healey to accept WWLP’s invitation and commit to a televised one-hour primetime debate in Western Massachusetts.
WWLP-22News has a long history of providing voters with direct access to candidates seeking public office.
The station has expressed its commitment to hosting a substantive discussion focused on the concerns and priorities of Western Massachusetts residents.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Five Weeks Out From Election, Minogue Momentum Grows Press Release | September 28, 2026 HAMILTON, Mass. — With # days until the election, gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue continues to gain momentum.
The increasingly competitive contest was featured on the cover of Sunday’s Boston Herald , underscoring the growing focus on the race in the final weeks before Election Day.
“I’m humbled by the support that’s come in from across the political divide,” said Minogue.
“This is a tipping-point election.
Massachusetts is working for some, but not all.

In joining together, we can defeat the political establishment that’s been failing working families for far too long.” Out on the trail, meanwhile, Minogue continues to propose solutions to the problems voters care most about while meeting with residents across the Commonwealth.
On September 10, Minogue called for a suspension of the state’s gas tax whenever per-gallon prices reach $4.
Twelve days later, Healey called a press conference to respond.
Healey previously termed a gas tax pause a “gimmick,” but on Sept.
22 proposed halting the gas tax for two months, just until the election.
Minogue highlighted the duration of Healey’s proposed gas tax halt, arguing that her plan appears focused on getting through Nov.
3 and then “go back to overtaxing.” In four years as governor, Maura Healey is projected to have spent almost double what Governor Charlie Baker spent in his first term.
Minogue has also resonated with voters over Healey’s approval of a $2 billion contract awarded to a politically connected partnership to construct a courthouse in Springfield.
He said the contract award to winning bidder Liberty Junction “is not only the most corrupt business deal ever done in Massachusetts history, it’s the worst, most incompetent financial deal.
No businessperson would ever do that deal, this waste of taxpayer money.” Minogue has called on the U.S.
Attorney for Massachusetts, Leah Foley, to launch an immediate investigation of the courthouse contract award.

You Got the Bill.

Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Massachusetts residents pay 34 cents per kilowatt hour for electricity, the second-highest rate in the country, compared with about 12 cents in much of the nation.
Maura Healey’s long record of opposing affordable energy sources is a major reason families are paying so much each month.
In 2022, Healey said she had stopped two gas pipelines from entering the state.
Those pipelines would have added supply to a region that now has some of the nation’s highest prices.

Her campaign website that year called for electrifying everything, including gas furnaces, oil-fired boilers, water heaters, and gas stoves in homes and businesses, and said cities and towns should be able to ban gas in new construction.
Healey has told families what she would take away without explaining how they are supposed to afford the replacements.
A 2025 MIT study found that stringent building energy codes in Massachusetts are contributing to higher home prices and a smaller housing supply.
Homes built under the Stretch Energy Code sold at a 4 percent premium compared with conventional homes.
Healey praised updates to that code in 2023 as a step toward the state’s clean energy transition.
In a state that ranks last in building permits per capita, that choice made homes more expensive to build.
Healey has also supported expanding MassSave, which has driven up costs for ratepayers.
Residents reported steep jumps in their energy bills in the winter of 2025, largely because of higher delivery charges attributed to the program.
MassSave funds efficient electric appliances, weatherization upgrades, and other climate-related priorities through those charges.
As of 2024, mandatory efficiency charges added roughly $200 a year to the average residential electric bill and about $150 a year to the average gas bill.
Families had no vote on the charge and cannot opt out.
After 20 years and billions of tax dollars, renewables supply only about 6 percent of the state’s total energy.
Vineyard Wind, a centerpiece of the state’s clean energy plan, is inefficient and harmful to the ocean environment.
Healey is asking families to pay more for a strategy that has delivered far less than promised.

Mike Minogue’s plan for energy: Invest in safe, clean, and reliable energy that lowers monthly costs Build new natural gas pipelines to bring affordable energy into the state Expand nuclear power, including the Seabrook plant, which supplies about 20 percent of the region’s electricity, and evaluate new modular nuclear options Pursue access to electricity from Canada to add supply and bring prices down From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Healey on Housing: Prices, Rents, and Homelessness Are All Up Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Maura Healey has had nearly four years to address the housing crisis, and she has not.
The problem has worsened under her watch, while Massachusetts ranks last in the nation in building permits per capita.
The median single-family home price has climbed steadily during Healey’s time in office, reaching $665,000 in May 2026.
In 2025, the state’s median home value ran $200,000 above the national median.
First-time buyers have been priced out.
Renters are struggling too.
The National Low Income Housing Coalition ranks Massachusetts as the third most expensive state for renting a two-bedroom home.
Monthly rent in the state averaged roughly $2,708 in 2025, compared with a national average of $2,068, and nearly half of the state’s renters are cost burdened.
Homelessness rose about 74 percent from 2023 to 2024, a jump attributed in part to rising housing costs.
More families have lost their homes during Healey’s tenure.
Mike Minogue would take a different approach on two fronts.
Local control.
Minogue would end enforcement of the MBTA Communities Act and provide legal support to cities and towns that decline its terms because of limits on water, sewer, infrastructure, and school resources.
The Healey administration has used state power to push mandates on communities that lack the capacity to meet them.
Minogue would return decision-making to local communities so they can preserve the character of their towns.
Tax dollars for building.
Minogue would return more tax dollars to communities, up to 35 to 40 percent, compared with the 26 percent they retain today.
To qualify, cities and towns would eliminate stretch building codes and cut permitting times for single-family homes to 45 days or less, compared with roughly a year and a half today.
This would make it easier to build and buy a home in Massachusetts.
The Commonwealth cannot afford four more years of the same.
Mike Minogue’s focus is making Massachusetts the best place to live, work, and raise a family.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Healey Should Put Kids Ahead of Politics and Opt Massachusetts Into Federal Scholarship Tax Credit Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue is urging Governor Maura Healey to enroll Massachusetts in the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, now that the Treasury Department has issued the program’s final rules.

The Boston Globe’s editorial board made the same case on October 2, writing that Healey “should take the money.” The paper noted that opting in is the only way Massachusetts can keep the hundreds of millions, potentially billions, of federal dollars set aside for education in the state.

The Washington Post’s October 1 coverage of the final rules pointed out that the program is financed entirely with federal funds, so states that sit it out forgo a chance to direct more money toward their public schools.
The Post also reported that Treasury estimates 95 percent of children live in families that meet the income threshold, which is set at less than three times the area median income.
“The Federal Scholarship Tax Credit could provide up to $5,000 for every eligible child,” said Minogue.
“By refusing to opt in, Governor Healey is choosing party politics over Massachusetts families, and kids are paying for it.
Education is one of the most powerful tools we have to break the cycle of poverty.
When I’m governor, Massachusetts will opt in on day one.” The program neither cuts nor diverts public school funding, locally or nationally.
Unlike the traditional voucher programs some states run, it is built to widen educational options for students in public and non-public schools alike.
Priority goes to low- and middle-income families, with a focus on expanding access for students in lower-performing schools.

Families could use the benefit for things that are often out of financial reach, including tutoring and academic support, enrichment and after-school programs, career and technical education, and services for students with special learning needs.
That support could matter most in communities where school budgets are stretched and towns are weighing tax overrides or other steps to cover rising education costs.
By drawing additional private resources into the education system, the program could supplement what public school students can access without putting the full burden on local school budgets.
It is designed to complement public education, not compete with it.
Massachusetts can stay committed to its public schools and still give families more ways to meet their children’s individual needs and interests.

The need is clear: a recent poll found that 60 percent of Massachusetts students in grades 3 through 8 did not meet expectations, and 77 percent of public school teachers believe public education is headed in the wrong direction.
Minogue said “Big Education” has pressed Healey not to opt in.
Her unwillingness to act, he argued, is a textbook case of putting politics ahead of students and parents, and it hurts affordability across the state.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Healey’s Parole Board Chaos Puts Mass Families at Risk Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Governor Maura Healey built a parole board that has lost sight of public safety.
Five of the six members now sitting on the Massachusetts Parole Board were nominated by Healey, and the board’s record is her record.
In 2025, Healey’s parole board granted early release to Tyler Brown, a career criminal convicted in 2020 of shooting at Boston Police officers.
The board pointed to his completion of violence reduction training and said he was remorseful for the attacks.
One year later, Brown was accused of erratically shooting a rifle at motorists in Cambridge and critically injuring two drivers.
The governor’s board took a man who had fired on police officers, accepted his word, and sent him back to the street.
Brown is not an isolated case.
As of December 2025, the parole board had released 39 murder convicts who were originally sentenced to life without parole.
From 2021 to 2025, the board voted to release parole applicants in two-thirds of its hearings.
Under Healey, release is not the exception at the Parole Board.
It is the norm.
Healey chose these board members, and she is accountable for every decision they make.
She has had years to see where this board’s judgment leads, and she has done nothing to course-correct.
Families in Cambridge are living with the consequences, and the governor has yet to answer for them.
A leader who truly puts public safety first would have demanded accountability from her appointees long before two drivers were critically injured.
Massachusetts needs a different approach.
Massachusetts families must be kept safe.
Families deserve a governor who treats public safety as a promise, not a probability.

Yet, in March of 2024, after a 15-year-old disabled girl was allegedly raped at a state-run emergency shelter in Rockland, Governor Healey said, “From time to time things will happen .” The governor should: Appoint a strong parole board that prioritizes and protects the safety of our people.
Eliminate cashless bail.
Create mandatory jail time for any conviction of violence against law enforcement agents.
The men and women in law enforcement who put their lives on the line, and the families who rely on them, deserve better than a governor who stacked the board and looked away.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Massachusetts is Nation’s Most Expensive State: Residents Are Leaving Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — A recent report ranks Massachusetts as the most expensive state in the country for families to live comfortably.
A family of four now needs an annual income of $329,555 to get by, nearly 6 percent more than in 2025.
It happened on Maura Healey’s watch.
Raising a child costs more here than anywhere else in the nation, at $35,841 a year for two working adults.
That figure includes more than $21,000 in annual childcare, nearly $5,000 in additional housing costs, and about $2,200 in food.
Many residents are choosing to leave.
In the 12 months ending July 1, 2025, Massachusetts lost 33,340 more people to other states than it gained, and the number of people moving out has climbed significantly.
A 2024 analysis by Boston University pointed to taxes, housing costs, and health care expenses as the top reasons people leave the Commonwealth.
Voters have taken notice.
An August 2026 poll found that majorities of Massachusetts residents disapprove of Healey’s handling of housing and the cost of living.
Respondents named those two issues as the most important problems facing the state.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Mike Minogue Calls on Healey to Call Special Session and Deliver Gas Tax Relief Press Release | September 30, 2026 HAMILTON, Mass. — Candidate for governor Mike Minogue today called on Governor Maura Healey to call a special session of the Massachusetts Legislature and pass the gas tax holiday she announced last week, saying Massachusetts families should not have to wait any longer for relief at the pump.
Minogue first called for a gas tax holiday on September 10.
Twelve days later, Maura Healey announced a proposal to suspend the state’s 24-cent-per-gallon gas tax until Election Day.
But the proposal has not taken effect, and drivers continue to pay the full tax.
“I’m glad Maura Healey followed my lead in announcing a gas tax holiday, but hard-working Massachusetts families are still waiting for the relief she promised,” said Minogue.
“A press conference doesn’t put money back in people’s pockets.
Be a leader and push back on the Legislature.
This is another example, like the audit, where Maura Healey failed to support the people and lower costs.

The Legislature should be convened for a special session to get this done.” Minogue is also launching a Gas Tax Holiday Clock on MinogueForMA.com , tracking the time that has passed since Healey announced her proposal without the tax holiday taking effect.
“A gas tax holiday is a common-sense solution for immediate relief.
The Legislature must put the people first and get this done.
Every day Maura Healey doesn’t act is another day Massachusetts drivers are paying a 24-cent-per-gallon state tax that should be suspended.
Right now, the clock is running, and families are still paying,” said Minogue.
Minogue said his proposal goes far beyond Healey’s weeks-long suspension.
His plan would provide a gas tax holiday whenever the price of gas rises above $4.00 per gallon.
As governor, he’ll move to eliminate the tax completely.
Minogue has committed to an audit of the entire budget to uncover hundreds of millions of dollars in waste, fraud, and corruption.
He says eliminating that unnecessary spending creates an opportunity to give money back to taxpayers and eliminate the gas tax.
The Gas Tax Holiday Clock and information about Minogue’s plan are available at MinogueForMA.com .

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Mike Minogue: Springfield Courthouse Contract “the Most Corrupt Business Deal” in Massachusetts History Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Candidate for governor Mike Minogue calls the Healey administration’s $2 billion Springfield courthouse contract “the most corrupt business deal ever done in Massachusetts history” and is demanding that the governor explain how it was awarded.
The contract went to Liberty Junction, a partnership that includes CoJo Partners.
CoJo is co-owned by Conan Harris, the husband of Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, and John Barros, the interim executive director of the Massachusetts Convention Center Authority.
Minogue questions how the team won and is demanding answers.
He has called on US Attorney Leah Foley to investigate.
Minogue says the governor has not responded to unanswered questions, which are accumulating.
Court documents show Barros met with senior Healey staff just hours before the deal was announced.
Barros divested his interest only after public backlash, and Minogue says he has still not provided specifics.
Minogue also says the contract does not match what the state asked for.
“The RFP was for best value, and it’s not best value,” he said.
“The RFP said they wanted gross spending, and it would include infrastructure and maintenance.
They didn’t do that.
A normal bid would have also had parking on site.
There’s no parking on site.
The mayor and the city wanted a different location.” He called the agreement a financial failure as well.
“No business person would ever do that deal,” Minogue said.
“This is a waste of taxpayer money.” “Massachusetts taxpayers deserve answers,” Minogue said, “and if the governor won’t give them, the U.S.
Attorney should.” From the press office of Mike Minogue.
