Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Mike Minogue Welcomes NEPBA Support Press Release | September 15, 2026 HAMILTON, Mass. — Candidate for governor Mike Minogue welcomed the New England Police Benevolent Association’s decision to support his campaign for Governor of Massachusetts.

NEPBA represents more than 5,000 law enforcement professionals throughout New England and cited public safety, accountability, leadership, recruitment and retention, and support for law enforcement among the reasons for its decision.
“Law enforcement officers put themselves on the line every day to protect our communities, and I am grateful for the support of the men and women who serve,” said Mike Minogue.
“The fundamental role of the governor is to keep our communities safe and uphold the law.
Maura Healey’s failed leadership has made the Commonwealth less safe.
We must return to prioritizing the safety of our people and law enforcement.” In making their announcement, NEPBA said they were proud to offer their strong support to Mike Minogue.

“At a time when the men and women of law enforcement are being asked to do more with fewer resources, when departments across Massachusetts continue to confront serious recruitment and retention challenges, and when public safety professionals too often feel that their voices are an afterthought on Beacon Hill, Massachusetts needs a Governor who understands that safe communities begin with supporting the people who protect them.
NEPBA believes Mike Minogue is that leader,” the organization said.
Minogue says the support of NEPBA reinforces his commitment to working with law enforcement to remove violent criminals and drug dealers from our communities.

He will appoint a strong parole board that prioritizes public safety, supports mandatory jail time for convictions involving violence against law enforcement officers, and protects constitutional rights.
Minogue also pledges to fully fund and protect qualified immunity for law enforcement while respecting citizens’ privacy and ensuring that communities remain safe.

NEPBA showed its support for Minogue by issuing the following statement: NEPBA PROUDLY ENDORSES MIKE MINOGUE FOR GOVERNOR OF MASSACHUSETTS The New England Police Benevolent Association is proud to announce our strong endorsement of Mike Minogue for Governor of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

At a time when the men and women of law enforcement are being asked to do more with fewer resources, when departments across Massachusetts continue to confront serious recruitment and retention challenges, and when public safety professionals too often feel that their voices are an afterthought on Beacon Hill, Massachusetts needs a Governor who understands that safe communities begin with supporting the people who protect them.
NEPBA believes Mike Minogue is that leader.
Mike has built his life around service, leadership and accountability.
A graduate of the United States Military Academy at West Point, Mike served as an Infantry Officer in the United States Army and earned the Bronze Star for his service during Operation Desert Storm.
He later spent nearly two decades leading Massachusetts-based Abiomed, helping build an innovative company, create jobs and develop lifesaving medical technology.

Whether leading soldiers or thousands of employees, Mike understands something that resonates deeply with our membership: leadership means taking responsibility for the people you are entrusted to lead.
His commitment to public safety is equally clear.
Mike has made keeping Massachusetts communities safe a central pillar of his campaign.

He has committed to removing violent criminals and drug dealers from our communities, restoring accountability to the Parole Board, supporting cooperation between law enforcement agencies, and seeking stronger consequences for those who commit acts of violence against police officers.
We recognize that other law enforcement organizations have chosen a different direction in this race.
We respect their right to make that decision.
NEPBA has chosen to look forward.
Our endorsement is not based on political convenience, access, or preserving the status quo.
It is based on where we believe Massachusetts must go from here and which candidate we believe is prepared to confront the challenges our members experience every day.
For NEPBA, being present for law enforcement is appreciated.
Standing up for law enforcement when the decisions are difficult is what matters.

Massachusetts cannot simply accept chronic staffing shortages, forced overtime, deteriorating morale and an increasingly difficult environment for recruiting and retaining the next generation of police officers as the new normal.
Our members deserve more than recognition.
They deserve results.
That is why this endorsement is also about the future of the law enforcement profession.

We want Massachusetts to be a place where qualified men and women once again want to become police officers; where experienced officers want to remain on the job; and where those who dedicate their careers to protecting others know that their government will stand behind them.
Mike Minogue has demonstrated that he understands those challenges and, more importantly, is prepared to listen to the law enforcement professionals experiencing them every day.
This election presents Massachusetts with a choice about what kind of leadership we expect from the Governor’s Office.

NEPBA is supporting a candidate who has led in the military, led in business, created jobs, solved difficult problems and has made accountability and public safety fundamental priorities of his campaign.
Our more than 5,000 members throughout New England know what leadership looks like.
They demonstrate it every day when they put on the uniform and report for duty.
We believe Mike Minogue will bring that same commitment to service, accountability and results to the Governor’s Office.

The New England Police Benevolent Association is proud to stand with Mike Minogue, and we strongly encourage our members, their families and supporters of law enforcement across Massachusetts to support him for Governor.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Minogue Campaign Launches “Insiders” Ad Calling for Transparency and Accountability Press Release | October 5, 2026 HAMILTON, Mass. — Candidate for governor Mike Minogue today released a new statewide ad titled “Insiders,” highlighting what the campaign describes as a lack of transparency and accountability in Massachusetts government and calling for greater oversight of state government.

The ad opens by laying out a series of issues facing the Commonwealth, including Massachusetts being the least-transparent state, $120 billion and growing in debt, last in the nation in job growth, insider deals, and a lack of accountability.
“I’m Mike Minogue,” the ad states.

“I believe the government has to answer to you, not the other way around.” The ad then focuses on the voter-approved audit measure and the campaign’s argument that Massachusetts voters have demanded greater transparency from their government.
The ad goes on to criticize Governor Maura Healey and what it describes as “political insiders” for refusing to comply with the audit.
“Working families are falling behind while Maura Healey’s political establishment looks out for itself,” said Minogue.
“When it comes to what matters to Massachusetts families – housing, health care, and utility bills – her failed record speaks for itself.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate Minogue Dominates WCVB Debate as Healey Dodges the Audit, Ignores Energy Costs, and Defends the Indefensible Press Release | October 15, 2026 NEEDHAM, Mass. — Mike Minogue won the WCVB debate against Governor Maura Healey, who had no answers on the issues Massachusetts families care about most: the state audit, soaring energy prices, and the crushing cost of living.
Voters wanted solutions.
They got a governor who could not defend her own record.
Minogue made clear that Healey and her political insiders are out of ideas and out of excuses.

Under her watch, families are being squeezed by sky-high costs, punishing taxes, a housing shortage, failing student scores, inflated energy bills, unfunded state pensions, and record-breaking state spending.
Healey’s response on the debate stage was to dodge, deflect, and hope voters wouldn’t hold her accountable.
On education, Minogue called out Healey for refusing to opt in to the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, which thirty states have already joined.
Even The Boston Globe’s editorial board urged her to take the funding.
She still refuses, leaving money on the table while student scores fall short.
Minogue said she is putting party politics ahead of kids from hard-working families, and those kids are the ones who pay for it.
Massachusetts cannot afford a governor who turns away help for its children.
Minogue also went after the culture of Beacon Hill, where insiders have run the state for decades under a broken one-party system.
He pointed to the $2 billion Springfield courthouse as a textbook example of the sweetheart deals insiders collect while taxpayers foot the bill.
Minogue pledged to put the people of Massachusetts first on the audit and every other issue, ahead of party politics.
The debate, Minogue said, made the choice clear: more one-party control and a record no one can defend, or a new kind of governor who works for the people of Massachusetts.
Voters can learn more about Mike Minogue’s plan for Massachusetts at MinogueForMA.com .
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

Home Meet Mike Meet Renee Blueprint for a Better Future In The News Events Get Involved Make a Plan to Vote Store Donate On Maura Healey’s watch, Massachusetts Is the Nation’s Most Expensive State, and Residents Are Leaving Press Release | October 8, 2026 BOSTON, Mass. — Massachusetts has become the most expensive state in the country for families to live comfortably, according to a recent report.
A family of four in Massachusetts now needs an annual income of $329,555 to live comfortably, nearly 6% more than in 2025.
The cost of raising a child shows the same pressure.
Massachusetts is the most expensive state in the country to raise a child, at $35,841 per year for two working adults.
That includes more than $21,000 annually in childcare, nearly $5,000 in additional housing costs, and about $2,200 in food.
Residents are responding by leaving.

The number of people moving out of Massachusetts to other states has climbed significantly, and in the 12 months ending July 1, 2025, Massachusetts lost 33,340 more people to other states than it gained.
A 2024 analysis by Boston University finance professor Mark Williams identified taxes, housing costs, and health care expenses as the top factors driving people to leave the Commonwealth.
Voters have noticed.

A poll released in August 2026 found that the majority of Massachusetts residents disapprove of Governor Maura Healey’s handling of housing and the cost of living, which respondents named as the two most important problems facing the state.
From the press office of Mike Minogue.

The Onyx are Colorado’s only professional rugby team and the reigning national champions.
This week’s tailgate is specially designed to be family-friendly and to celebrate dad.
We’ll have bubbles, sidewalk chalk, poster making, food, juice boxes and someone who’s NOT a dad manning the grill so he can relax and enjoy a sports day.
Tailgate is in the parking lot northeast of the stadium and starts two hours before kickoff at 1pm.

Tickets for the game which kicks off at 3pm are available at https://www.universe.com/events/denver-onyx-vs-ny-exiles-tickets-2YTD5W Previous Previous June 21 Canvassing for Monica (and a rugby tailgate afterwards) Next Next June 23 Talk to neighbors with Monica (daily shifts) Paid for by Monica for Colorado.

added: alt://instagram.fsdv2-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t39.30808-6/798785219_1513135330620064_1075958829499673980_n.jpg|The future of Del Rio and Val Verde County deserves conversations that lead to action. I recently brought together local elected officials, community leaders, and private-sector partners to discuss the priorities shaping our region, from infrastructure and transportation to healthcare access and economic growth. Having local and state leaders at the same table helps us identify challenges, strengthen communication, and keep important projects and community needs moving forward. My commitment is to represent every corner of House District 74 and ensure our local leaders have a direct line of communication with their state representative. Thank you to everyone who joined us and continues working on behalf of Del Rio and Val Verde County. #DelRio #ValVerdeCounty #HD74 #WestTexas #CommunityLeadership #TexasInfrastructure

Residents were also able to learn about transportation services available from Del Rio to San Antonio. The goal is to reduce the cost of living, not line the pockets of a few.

added: top of page for State Representative Fighting for District 23 — Every Day, For Every Family Vote in the Primary on September 9, 2026 Home About Meet the Candidate Legislative Homepage Accessibility Statement Meet the Candidate Legislative Homepage Accessibility Statement Events Community Calendar Campaign Photo Gallery Community Calendar Campaign Photo Gallery News & Press In the News Press Releases Endorsements Social Media In the News Press Releases Endorsements Social Media Get Involved Volunteer Form Contact Us Volunteer Form Contact Us Voter Information Menu Close Contribute Accessibility Statement This statement was last updated on May 23, 2026.
Site developers at AuroraIQAdvisory are working to make our site https://mutoforwarwick.com , accessible to people with disabilities.
What Web Accessibility Is An accessible site allows visitors with disabilities to browse the site with the same or a similar level of ease and enjoyment as other visitors.
This can be achieved with the capabilities of the system on which the site is operating, and through assistive technologies.
Accessibility Adjustments on This Site We have adapted this site in accordance with WCAG 2.2 guidelines, and have made the site accessible to the level of AAA.
This site's contents have been adapted to work with assistive technologies, such as screen readers and keyboard use.

As part of this effort, we have also: Used the Accessibility Wizard to find and fix potential accessibility issues Set the language of the site Set the content order of the site’s pages Defined clear heading structures on all of the site’s pages Added alternative text to images Implemented color combinations that meet the required color contrast Reduced the use of motion on the site Ensured all videos, audio, and files on the site are accessible Declaration of partial compliance with the standard due to third-party content ​The accessibility of certain pages on the site depend on contents that do not belong to the organization, and instead belong to Google.
The following pages are affected by this: https://www.mutoforwarwick.com/accessibility-statement.
We therefore declare partial compliance with the standard for these pages.
Accessibility Arrangements in the Organization Bill Muto for State Representative does not have a physical location, and maintains an online presence only.

Requests, Issues, and Suggestions If you find an accessibility issue on the site, or if you require further assistance, you are welcome to contact us through the organization's accessibility coordinator: AuroraIQAdvisory; bjt@bjtcivicsolutions​.com Contribute Report a Website Issue: Click Here © # Bill Muto for State Representative .

added: top of page for State Representative Fighting for District 23 — Every Day, For Every Family Vote in the Primary on September 9, 2026 Home About Meet the Candidate Legislative Homepage Accessibility Statement Meet the Candidate Legislative Homepage Accessibility Statement Events Community Calendar Campaign Photo Gallery Community Calendar Campaign Photo Gallery News & Press In the News Press Releases Endorsements Social Media In the News Press Releases Endorsements Social Media Get Involved Volunteer Form Contact Us Volunteer Form Contact Us Voter Information Menu Close Contribute All Posts Endorsements Warwick Councilman Bill Muto announces run for State Representative, District 23 William Muto May 26 3 min read Lifelong Warwick resident will continue serving Ward 6 while seeking the open seat WARWICK, R.I. — Warwick City Councilman William (Bill) Muto announced today that he is running as a Democrat for State Representative in District 23.
He plans to keep his Ward 6 seat while he campaigns, bringing to the General Assembly the same approach he has taken at City Hall: show up, do the work, and be straight with people.
“Representing Ward 6 has been one of the greatest honors of my life,” Muto said.
“I have worked every day to lead with integrity and a commonsense approach to city government.
I’m running for State Representative because the challenges facing our neighborhoods demand steady leadership and real collaboration.

District 23 deserves a representative who understands this community, stands with it, and works hard for it.” Why He Is Running Now For Muto, this campaign is a continuation of his Council work, not a break from it.
Sitting on the budget side of city government gave him a direct view of how state decisions land on Warwick.
Unfunded mandates show up in tax bills and in cuts to services families count on.
“When you sit on the budget side of city government, you see clearly how state mandates—especially unfunded ones—show up in our tax bills and in the services families rely on,” Muto said.

“I’ve seen where those pressures come from, and I believe I can keep making a difference for Warwick by serving at the state level while continuing to show up for Ward 6.” A Warwick Native Muto grew up in a family of eight in the Buttonwoods section of Warwick and went to the city’s public schools.
He still lives in the home his parents built more than #ago.
He and his wife Joanne—an English teacher at Pilgrim High School—raised their two children, Michaela and Alexander, there, and cared for their parents as they got older.
“Warwick is not just where I live.
It’s who I am,” Muto said.
“My parents raised six of us here and taught us to work hard, keep our word, and give back.

I know our neighborhoods and our schools because I’ve lived them.” His Record on the Council On the Council, Muto has focused on the basics: showing up, following through, and helping residents cut through city bureaucracy.
He has worked on street safety, government transparency, and building relationships with labor, small businesses, school officials, and city departments.
His background in business intelligence—more than 30 years helping organizations turn data into decisions—shapes how he approaches problems.
“The issues in front of us—workforce development, affordability, education, infrastructure, public safety, economic competitiveness—are not solved with speeches,” Muto said.
“They require steady, collaborative leadership.
I want to be a partner who understands the issues, respects the process, and works with people to build practical solutions.” Where He Stands Warwick roots.
Lifelong resident with board service at Boys Town New England and Bridgemark.
Accountable spending .
Muto backs Council motions that include built-in outcome measurements and public reporting—he wants the public to see where the money goes and whether it worked.
Plain-language policy.
Committed to making state legislation readable: plain summaries, infographics, and regular feedback channels so residents actually know what their government is doing.
Constituent engagement.
Open-office hours in neighborhood parks and libraries, combined with paper surveys and digital polling, so every resident has a way to be heard.
The Road Ahead “Rhode Island succeeds when its leaders work together,” Muto said.
“Times are tough for a lot of families, and there are no easy answers.
Warwick has always met its challenges by working hard and being straight with one another.
I’m asking my neighbors for their support and their ideas, and I’m ready to get to work.” Learn more, volunteer, or donate at www.mutoforwarwick.com.
About Bill Muto: William (Bill) Muto is a lifelong Warwick resident, business consultant, and Ward 6 City Councilman.
He serves on the boards of Boys Town New England and Bridgemark.

added: Skip to content Facebook X-twitter Instagram Menu Contribute Dallas Morning News Dallas Morning News Endorses Nathan Johnson for Texas Attorney General October 15, 2026 There is at least one silver lining to Ken Paxton’s decision to run for the U.S.
Senate : It opens the office of Texas attorney general to new management.
The question is whether voters will elevate someone who can wash away the stench of the Paxton years .
The race pits two state senators against each other: Democrat Nathan Johnson of Dallas and Republican Mayes Middleton of Galveston.
Forget about Rs and Ds.
This is a choice between the candidate who vows to get back to the meat-and-potatoes duties of this office and the candidate who has committed to more culture wars.
We think most Texans want the former because they’re tired of the latter.
Their votes should go to Johnson.

Many of us forget about the core duties of the attorney general’s office because the dominant parties in Texas and other states have turned what should be an apolitical role protecting consumers and state agencies into a lawsuit cannon aimed at political enemies.
Paxton waded into outright corruption.
His top aides provided damning evidence that he had deployed his office to protect a political donor.
Legal talent has fled the office or been forced out.
If someone can restore honor to the attorney general’s office, it’s Johnson.
He became a state senator in 2019, after flipping a red district in Dallas County.
In the years since, we have commended him for his pragmatic style.
In an interview with us, Johnson, 58, said he’s promising voters he won’t politicize the office.
“I have pledged that I will sue Donald Trump if and when he breaks the law,” Johnson said.

“Otherwise, I have better and more important things to do with the time and the resources of the attorney general’s office.” To prove his point, Johnson highlighted instances in which he bucked fellow Democrats based on principle.

For example, his concern for free markets drove him to oppose a bipartisan “anti ESG” law in 2021 that barred the state from investing or contracting with companies boycotting the fossil fuel industry.
A federal judge this year ruled the law unconstitutional.
In 2023, citing property rights, Johnson sided against the Sierra Club and Texas officials who proposed saving a state park on private land by using eminent domain.
Johnson told us he wants to strengthen the enforcement of consumer protection laws, and he even praised some of the work that Paxton’s office had done going after social media titans.
However, he pointed out that Elon Musk, owner of X and a GOP donor, had not been a target.
Middleton didn’t respond to an invitation to meet with us or fill out our Voter Guide.
He seems interested only in speaking to the far-right echo chamber.

added: “Support first-time homeowners, lower prescription drug costs, take on what people are feeling at the grocery store and the gas pump, and reduce childcare costs.” Read the Stillwater Gazette article here: https://www.hometownsource.com/stillwater_gazette/community/fraud-and-affordability-dominate-first-stillwater-gazette-candidate-forums/article_69b6b827-9a75-4d30-bad5-a3a356f3cb0a.html Watch the forum here : https://www.youtube.com/live/mrZu9aQdLJ0 Smith Opening Remarks “Happy to be here.
Happy that my wife and I have chosen this community to raise our family.
I’m the proud new dad of a 5-month-old baby girl and I look forward to helping build a brighter future for her.
My name is Nat Smith and I’m running for state senate here.
I’m a first-time candidate and I’m running because I was tired of sitting on the sidelines waiting for change that just never seemed to come.
And I wanted to be somebody that was willing to be an independent voice that was going to put people over politics and work to deliver real results for Minnesotans.
My work ethic is grounded in my time working for my stepdad’s small business as an interior / exterior painter.
I worked on homes around the Twin Cities.
Did all that work by hand starting when I was 13.
The skills I think we need in the senate are grounded in my legal work combating fraud, not only here in Minnesota, but all across the country.
It’s in-depth problem solving, deep dives into statutes and regulations, and bringing people together to get the job done.

And I’m really excited to be running for senate and having the opportunity to serve my community and to pave a brighter future for not only for District 33, but the state of Minnesota.” Smith Closing Remarks “Thank you again for having us.
I’m thrilled to be a new candidate here and be a change in our voice and representation here for district 33.

It’s something I hear a lot about at the doors that people are looking for someone who is willing to be that independent voice, that is willing to put people over politics and is someone that is not going to play the blame game, because I’m tired of it and that’s what I hear about, people are tired of it at the doors.
I’m not going to be a rubber stamp for my party or for special interest groups, I’m going to be advocate for the people here in district 33.
Thank you to my wife and my daughter for the sacrifices that they are making so that I can be here tonight and so that I can be running this campaign… We are out there knocking doors.
We are out there talking to community members.

And I look forward to the opportunity to earn your vote and I hope you’ll vote for me on November 3rd or before.” Nat Smith Next Next Nat Smith Pledges to Continue Fighting Fraud and lower costs in First Digital Ad Contact the Campaign Email us Follow us PREPARED AND PAID FOR BY NAT SMITH FOR MN STATE SENATE COMMITTEE PO Box 116, Stillwater, MN 55082 Photo Gallery | Privacy Policy

Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed SB 56 September 17, 2019 admin Consumer Protection Comments are Closed 0 This Act modernizes the process and requirements for issuance of liquor licenses for off premises consumption.
The current process and requirements do not consider population growth.
Minimum distance requirements are enhanced while increases in population growth will now be considered to arrive at a safety and convenience balance.
This Act also grandfathers existing licensees into the current process.

removed: HB 94 September 17, 2019 admin Criminal Law and Courts Comments are Closed 0 This Act will increase payments of child support arrears or retroactive support from payments for settlements and awards from negligence, personal injury, and workers compensation cases by requiring that all insurers share information with an insurance claim data collection organization.

The Division of Child Support Services (“Division”) uses an insurance claim data collection organization to match individuals who are in arrears on child support or who owe retroactive child support with individuals with insurance claims based upon negligence, personal injury, or workers’ compensation cases.
The data collection organization performs a data match of the claimants provided by insurers and child support obligors provided by the Division.

The data collection organization provides reports of matches to the Division so that the Division can issue a lien against the insurance claim to collect the child support arrears or retroactive support.
Currently, some insurers voluntarily submit claim information to the insurance claim data collection organization and in 2018, $424,977 in unpaid child support was collected through this process.
This Act requires that all insurers submit claim information to the insurance claim data collection organization and is expected to collect an additional $150,000 – $200,000 in unpaid child support.
This Act also allows written notice of a lien or action to perfect the lien to be sent by electronically or by first class mail to conform to industry practices.
This Act also makes technical corrections to conform existing law to the standards of the Delaware Legislative Drafting Manual.

Co-Prime Sponsor: Poore; Status: Signed HB 102 September 17, 2019 admin Criminal Law and Courts Comments are Closed 0 This bill allows a person who is arrested or convicted of any crime, except a violent felony, which was a direct result of being a victim of human trafficking may file an application or for a pardon or expungement or make a motion to vacate judgment.
This bill also makes changes to the Human Trafficking Interagency coordinating by adding another member of the judicial branch and a representative of the Department of Education.
This bill also adds locations where a public awareness sign must be placed.

added: Press: Reflecting on Progress: What’s Next… One Month Left of the… Emergency Closure of Lorewood Grove… New Air Quality Initiatives Launching… Legislative Recap: April 2026 info@nicolepoore.com Donate About About Senator Poore FAQs About Senator Poore Delaware Voting Information Endorsements Delaware Democrat Values 12th District Legislation Social Policy Guns Education Consumer Protection Crime and Public Safety Criminal Law and Courts Business & Economic Development/Policy Energy and Environment Health and Social Services Joint Sunset Committee Open Government/Government Operations Contact Volunteer News News/Blog Senator Poore 12th District Newsletter About About Senator Poore FAQs About Senator Poore Delaware Voting Information Endorsements Delaware Democrat Values 12th District Legislation Social Policy Guns Education Consumer Protection Crime and Public Safety Criminal Law and Courts Business & Economic Development/Policy Energy and Environment Health and Social Services Joint Sunset Committee Open Government/Government Operations Contact Volunteer News News/Blog Senator Poore 12th District Newsletter June 2025 – Updates from Senator Nicole Poore Home Consumer Protection / June 2025 – Updates from Senator Nicole Poore June 2025 – Updates from Senator Nicole Poore June 23, 2025 admin Consumer Protection , Energy and Environment , News/Blog , Senator Poore 12th District Newsletter , Social Policy Comments are Closed 0 Friends and neighbors, In Delaware, our regular legislative session runs each year from the second Tuesday in January through June 30.
As our legislative session begins to adjourn for the 153rd General Assembly, I want to inform you of the finals bills, resolutions, and policies I have been introducing in the Senate.
To watch Senate proceedings live or if you want to come back later to watch recordings of past proceedings, click here .
To view daily Senate Agendas, click here .
To view upcoming committee meetings, legislative session start times, and more, click here .
As always, please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions, comments, community concerns, or just to say hi.
I can be reached by email at nicole.poore@delaware.gov , on Facebook , Instagram , or by calling my Senate office at (302) 744-4164.
Sincerely, Nicole Poore Senator, District 12 Legislative Updates House Bill 1 (HB 1) As Chair of the Veterans Affairs Committee, I was proud to lead the charge on House Bill 1 in the Senate.
This is a game-changing bill that creates a Cabinet-level Office of Veterans Affairs here in Delaware – a long-overdue requirement for our vets.
This office will give our veterans the voice, support, and representation they’ve long deserved.
After years of advocacy by Rep.
Bill Carson and many others, we’re finally getting this across the finish line.
Thank you to my colleagues for standing with me and our vets.
I hope to bring this home with a unanimous vote in the House on Thursday!
If you are a vet or currently serving in our military, please join us in Legislative Hall on Thursday, June 26 to see this legislation pass in the Senate.
Senate Bill 174 (SB 174) For many of us, our pets are irreplaceable members of our families.
Sadly, too many animals find themselves in the hands of people who pose a serious risk to their welfare.
That’s why I’m proud to sponsor Senate Bill 174 , establishing an animal abuse offender list under the Office of Animal Welfare.
This legislation not only makes offenses of animal abuse public information – it also legally prohibits shelters from approving adoptions to people on the list.
House Bill 210 Introduced Earlier this month, I held a joint town hall meeting with Rep.

Minor-Brown , Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC) Secretary Greg Patterson , and the Delaware City Refinery General Manager Mike Capone to discuss the excess levels of sulfur dioxide that had been caused by a water leak in their boiler.
We wanted to come together to explain this issue, let us hear directly from our constituents, and inform everyone of our next steps collectively.
With the assistance of many legislators, including House sponsor Rep.
Lambert , we were able to introduce House Bill 210 , legislation that will create the Pollution Accountability Act.
This bill will increase penalties for environmental violations and directs shares of fines to the communities being affected by it.
HB 210 is a necessary step forward in protecting our environment and maintaining public health and safety.
By increasing the fine structure for our biggest polluters, we’re not only deterring future violations, but also directing revenue back into the neighborhoods most affected.
Around the 12th District Juneteenth Celebration I had the honor of speaking at this year’s Delaware City-Polktown Juneteenth Commemoration .
This is not my first year being invited to celebrate with the African Union Church Cemetery , and I am always so overjoyed to celebrate this important holiday with this community.
On Juneteenth, we honor the strength of those who waited for freedom—who built, prayed, sang, and hoped, even when justice was delayed.
Juneteenth is not just a date in history—it is a story of resilience.
It reminds us that freedom didn’t come all at once.
It came late.
And for many, it’s still coming.
As Maya Angelou said, “You may not control all the events that happen to you, but you can decide not to be reduced by them.” On this day, we remember.
We teach, we vote, we rise—because Juneteenth is not only about what happened in 1865, it’s about how we keep showing up for justice, for truth, and for each other.
May freedom continue to ring—louder, stronger, and with purpose.
249th Annual ‘Separation Day’ Festival Separation Day is one of my favorite traditions, and this year’s celebration was something special.
From the parade route to Battery Park, I got to hug old friends, meet new faces, and soak in the pride that makes Old New Castle feel like home.
Thank you to everyone who worked behind the scenes to make the weekend such a success, and to everyone who came out to celebrate our shared history and community.
Until next year, New Castle.
You really showed up.

As always, please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions, comments, community concerns, or just to say hi.
I can be reached by email at nicole.poore@delaware.gov , on Facebook , Instagram , or by calling my Senate office at (302) 744-4164.
Sincerely, Nicole Poore Senator, District 12 Bill Signings & Legislative News Delaware is not only the First State, but we are also the first to become a ‘no kill’ state.
We have always been a leader in speaking for the voiceless and standing up for animals, and we continued that work today with the signing of SB 174 .
This legislation will add further protections for animals by bringing those that commit evil in private to the light, and holding them accountable for their actions.
Last month during the General Assembly’s special session, we swore in Karen Berry, Brigadier General (Ret.) as the new Secretary of the Delaware Department of Veterans Affairs .
It is an incredible honor to see this vision for Delaware’s veterans become a reality.
The implementation of this department is a proactive approach to giving our vets a voice – and when Rep.
Carson and I introduced HB 1, our main goal was to ensure our state had a strong advocate that intrinsically understood our veterans’ obstacles and lived experiences.

With the swearing in of Brigadier General Karen Berry, we are not only seeing that commitment executed, but also entrusting its leadership to someone whose career embodies service, sacrifice, and integrity.
This is a monumental stride for the state of Delaware, and I look forward to the impact it will continue to have on our veterans and their families.

This past month, I held two separate community conversations with Secretary Berry and General Frank Vavala to discuss the new updates coming to the Department of Veterans Affairs and the plans she has in store to improve veterans resources across the state.
Reminder: Parents’ Rights in Education During the 147th General Assembly, I introduced SB 299 , legislation that gives parents the freedom to opt their children out of the DCAS standardized test.
As the parent of a child with a cognitive disability, I understand that every child learns differently — and that each one’s abilities and potential cannot be captured by a test score.
I wanted school to be a place that enriched my son’s life, not one that mesured his worth against academic benchmarks.
My son’s value was never defined by a DCAS Alt-1 score.
Our family understood his strengths, challenges, and what success looks like for him — not what a test says it should be.
But this legislation wasn’t written just for parents like me.
It also supports students who are still learning English and may struggle to understand test questions, or children who experience test anxiety and cannot perform their best under pressure.
SB 299 is about giving parents the right to decide what’s best for their child’s academix journey.
As we enter a new school year, let’s continue to remember that every child is unique, and that education should lift them up, not limit them.
If you are interested in opting your child out of DCAS testing, please talk with their school administrator and teacher.
Events in SD 12 I had a wonderful time joining April and John from the Pet Pawcast in Wilmington to talk about SB 174 and the importance of protecting animals here in Delaware.
As an owner of three beloved dogs, I know firsthand the unconditional love pets bring to our lives and the deep responsibility we share to care for them.
But that care shouldn’t stop with our own pets; it extends to every animal without a voice of their own.
SB 174 gives us the opportunity to be that voice.
It ensures that all animals are treated with the compassion they deserve and that those who harm them are held accountable.

Thank you to the Humane Animal Partners for inviting me onto your show to share why this work means so much – not only to me, but to our animals and shelters who have continued to advocate for this legislation.
To view the podcast, you can visit their website here .

I extend a heartfelt thank you to Judy Barthel, Tish Gallagher, Susuan McLaughlin, and the entire Board of the New Castle Senior Center for organizing another successful year of the Old New Castle Block Party .

This block party not only brought over 200 neighbors together to enjoy great food and live music from local bands Seven Rings and Somethin’ Like That, but also raised important funds to support the Senior Center and the vital work they do for our elders.
I am always inspired to see our community come together in celebration and support of great causes.
Thank you to everyone who attended including my colleagues Rep.
Melissa Minor-Brown and Rep.
Franklin Cooke , and I look forward to joining you again next year!
I had the privilege of meeting Coach Kenya Sloane , the first women’s wrestling head coach in Delaware State University history!
Anyone who knows me knows how much I love school sports – especially wrestling.
As a mom to a wrestler, the sport has always been close to my heart, and I couldn’t be more excited to see the strength and passion Kenya brings to the Hornets.
With an undefeated 87-0 high school record, four state championships, and a gold medal from the Berlin Open, she’s already proven she has what it takes to lead this team to new heights.
Sen.
Eric Buckson and I had the honor of joining her for the coin toss at Saturday’s football game, which was the perfect way to celebrate Delaware sports and this historic milestone for DSU wrestling.
Congratulations, Coach Sloane!
We can’t wait to cheer you and the Hornets on this season!
I was honored to spend the day at the 2025 Vet Fest in Town of WhiteHall!
From the moving memorial for the fallen to the energy of the 5K, live music, and community spirit — Delaware truly came together in support of our veterans and the mission of Stop Soldier Suicide.
A special thank you to Brian DiSabatino and the entire Vet Fest committee — your dedication is as strong as the men and women who serve our country.

We were also privileged to have former President Joe Biden join us this morning to deliver heartfelt remarks, honoring those currently serving, their families, and our Gold Star families who have sacrificed so much.
Community Bulletin Board It’s important to make plans for your future, but sometimes it can be difficult to understand where to start.

Ciro Poppiti and I will be co-hosting an Estate Planning Q&A session in November to discuss the importance of having a will, how trusts can protect your assets, and the key steps needed to begin your journey.
This information can be invaluable to making informed decisions about your family’s future, and I hope to see you there.
You can register for the event using this link , or by calling 302-744-4314.
The 5th Annual Holiday Race for Recovery 5K Walk/Run will be held on Saturday, December 7 , in beautiful Historic New Castle .
This family-friendly event brings together runners, walkers, families, and neighbors to celebrate the start of the holiday season while supporting a meaningful cause.
Proceeds from the race benefit two of CCD’s cornerstone programs: CARE Program – our transitional sober living program, providing individuals in recovery with a safe and supportive environment.
CORE Program – our community outreach initiative, connecting individuals and families with resources, education, and recovery supports.
Your participation or sponsorship would demonstrate a shared commitment to strengthening our community and supporting those on the path to recovery.
It’s also a wonderful opportunity to connect with residents and local organizations in a positive, family-centered setting.
To register for this event, scan the QR code above, or visit the link here.

DONATE All Articles Search Washington Supreme Court races Alan Nolan #ago 1 min read While the initiatives deservedly get a lot of attention, the Washington State Supreme Court races are the most consequential decisions on this year's ballot.
Five of the nine seats are up for election.
That is over half of a court that has repeatedly ignored the will of the people and the actual text of Washington's Constitution.
Here are some of their recent greatest hits: Overturned Spokane's anti-camping ordinance, approved by 75% of the voters to protect our school and parks.

Struck down Energy Choice Initiative, which protected access to natural gas and received over 1.9 million votes Upheld the Capital Gains Tax as constitutional, somehow finding capital gains somehow are not income like they are everywhere else I like the initiatives and will vote "YES" to protect girls' sports, parents' rights and stop another unconstitutional income tax.
I will vote for supreme court races to ensure my YES vote isn't discarded by activist in robes.
Below are my picks to start upholding the law.

Position 1 - Scott Edwards - https://votescottedwards.com/ Position 3 - David Stevens - https://www.judgestevensforwa.com/ Position 4 - Sean O'Donnell - https://www.odonnellforjustice.com/ Position 5 - Dave Larson - https://larsonforjustice.com/ Position 7 - Todd Bloom - https://www.electtoddbloom.com/ Justices serve six-year terms.
This is a unique opportunity to make a big change that will last a long time.
Tell your family, friends and neighbors to vote 'YES' on initiatives, but don't let them seal up their ballot until they've also voted to elect justices who will be faithful to the law.

added: DONATE All Posts Search Senator O'Mara's weekly column 'From the Capitol' -- for the week of October 12, 2026 -- "Ratepayers (and taxpayers) can't afford a 'POWER' check" omaranysenate #ago 5 min read Updated: #ago There's a long, extensive list of priorities to address that, if done right and we get started on them now, could begin to provide real and meaningful short- and long-term relief to overburdened New Yorkers.

Specifically, Governor Hochul and the all-Democrat majorities in the New York State Legislature included $1 billion in this year's state budget to fund this one-time "Protecting Our Wallets Energy Rebate (POWER)" giveaway to provide $200 to joint filers with incomes under $150,000 and $150 to joint filers with incomes between $150,000 and $300,000.

added: Home Issues 2026 Ballot Questions Positions Meet Ed Yard Signs Fundraiser Events Contribute Volunteer Professional Endorsement Voter Endorsements News Photos Contact Endorsements Events The Dartmouth Democratic Town Committee will host a Candidates Night for the Massachusetts House 9th Bristol District race on Tuesday, August 11, at 6:00 p.m. in the Select Board Room (Room 304) at Dartmouth Town Hall.
Doors will open at 5:00 p.m.
The event will feature Democratic candidates seeking to represent the 9th Bristol District in the Massachusetts House of Representatives.
This seat will be a vacant seat for the first time in over 14 years!

Ed will participate in the forum and welcomes the opportunity to continue to speak directly with residents about the future of the district, the priorities facing local communities, and the issues affecting families throughout Dartmouth and New Bedford.

The forum is designed to give voters the opportunity to hear directly from the candidates, learn about their positions on key issues, and gain a better understanding of their vision for the 9th Bristol District and the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

The evening's program will include: Candidate introductions and opening statements Questions focused on priorities for the communities of the 9th Bristol District Discussion of statewide issues affecting Massachusetts residents Audience questions Candidate-to-candidate questions The event will also be recorded and broadcast by Dartmouth Community Television, giving residents across the district the opportunity to watch and stay informed.
Community members are encouraged to attend, engage in the discussion, and learn more about the candidates seeking to represent the 9th Bristol District .

removed: Skip to content Time For A Change Home September 30, 2026 energy policy , politics , public health Green Energy is Energy Sovereignty If there is one thing the Iran war has taught us, it is that having lots of oil in your country does not shield you from the consequences of a global shortage.
We are a major oil- EXPORTING nation.
We have scads of crude.
But for one reason or another, we don’t have the refined products we need.
We export one grade of crude and import a different one.
Our refineries have been allowed to age and close instead of being upgraded, because that takes capital ($$$) and companies are averse to spending it.
But you know what?
Nobody can tariff the wind.
The sun doesn’t have to go through a strait on the other side of the world.
And we all live on a gigantic ball of superhot rock that won’t run out of heat for billions of years.
There are also locally available resources like hydropower, tidal energy, and more.
Energy generated in our own locale is the safest, cheapest way to power our future.
We should be promoting the renewable energy industries in every way possible.
While we in Idaho cannot do a lot about federal policies, we can: Restore a fair export credit to promote solar and wind installation.
Allow “balcony solar” as several other states already have, so that renters and people with less capital to spend can also generate some power.
Promote agrovoltaics, where solar panels and row crops or pasture share the same land, to the benefit of the crops.
Panels also pair very well with pollinator meadows and bee keeping.
Streamline permitting for smaller-scale wind projects.
We also have the local ability to promote energy efficient buildings and public transportation to save fuel.
Electric school busses not only cost less to run, but save the children riding on them from diesel fumes that cause respiratory problems.
Induction stoves in place of gas stoves cut the rate of asthma attacks by a lot.
Heat pumps are the most efficient way to heat and cool a building, and buildings can be far better insulated than is currently common.
Clean energy is a win-win situation.
Except for the fossil fuel barons currently gouging us for every penny.
They can go jump in a lake.

removed: top of page PMK'S ISSUES & SOLUTIONS Eliminate Corruption & Money in Politics Learn More End Wealth Inequality More Info Economic Empowerment More Info Healthcare is a Human Right More Info Education First More Info Build Our Infrastructure More Info Social Justice & Human Rights More Info Take Care of our Veterans & Millitary More Info Environmental Reform More Info Housing & Transportation More Info More Info Reform Regulations & Reduce Beaurocracy More Info Eliminate Corruption and Money in Politics ​ Americans overwhelmingly support reducing the role of money in politics, but real change requires strong public pressure and legislative action. ​​​​​ Campaign finance reform Overturn Citizens United Lobbying and ethics reform Stronger anti-bribery and dark money laws End gerrymandering with independent redistricting/voter protections Transferring to publicly funded campaigns End self-funding loopholes Lobbying & PAC reforms Simplify confusing ballot language Term limits Prohibit stock ownership in office We can do these things.
Economic Empowerment ​ ​All work has value, and I'm focused on restoring dignity to those who build this country​.
Economic empowerment strengthens our communities, creates opportunities, and ensures financial stability for working families.
The GOP has destroyed Ohio's economy which is now ranked #43 in employment and #36 in growth.
In addition, working families are crippled by the cost for infant care, requiring a household income of nearly $149,000 to be considered “affordable”.

Ohio ranks third worst in the nation for childcare eligibility, with only 145% of the federal poverty level qualifying for assistance ​​​​​ Stronger unions $20 minimum wage Worker's compensation expansion Job training & apprenticeships - invest in vocational training Manufacturing & infrastructure jobs Invest in clean energy infrastructure Workplace protections - strengthening worker safety laws Protections for small businesses and family farms Healthcare & Retirement Security Invest in Affordable Childcare: Cap childcare at 7% of income and stabilize the workforce We can do these things.
End Wealth Inequality - Taxes, Pay and Training The United States faces extreme wealth inequality, with the top 10% of households owning nearly 75% of total wealth, while the bottom 50% hold just 2%.
The richest 1% of Ohioans earn nearly as much as the bottom half of the population combined.
Despite overall economic growth, disparities have widened—CEO-to-worker pay ratios have skyrocketed, with executives earning over 350 times the average worker’s salary.

The tax system, corporate influence, and stagnant wages contribute to this divide, leaving millions without financial security. ​ Close corporate tax loopholes and fix the tax code Increase taxes on wealthy Super Owners Support thriving families tax credit Strengthen our unions and their protections $20 minimum wage Expand the Earned Income Tax Credit Expand job training programs Strengthen food assistance programs Universal healthcare Remove the cap on social security Expand education and training access We can do these things.
Fix the Housing Crisis The Problem ​Rent has doubled while wages stayed flat — and families need a chance to catch their breath.
Every Ohioan — in cities, rural areas and suburbs — deserves a shot at affordable housing. ​ Severe Housing Shortage: Ohio underbuilt housing for over a decade, especially affordable units.
After the 2008 housing crash, construction slowed dramatically and never fully recovered.
Nationally, Freddie Mac estimates a housing shortfall of 3.8 million units, and Ohio is part of that gap — especially in urban areas like Columbus and Cincinnati.
The pandemic made this worse: material shortages, labor disruptions, and local permit delays stalled new construction.

And the impact left more renters chasing too few units, where landlords can raise prices dramatically — especially on lease renewals. ​ Investor and Corporate Landlord Takeover: Since 2020, institutional investors have bought thousands of Ohio rental properties, especially single-family homes in suburbs.
These firms often hike rents aggressively and charge junk fees.

Local landlords are now “competing” with Wall Street pricing models. ​ ​ ​Inflation + Interest Rates Rising property taxes, insurance premiums, and maintenance costs pushed some landlords to raise rents to preserve margins. ​ Mortgage rates doubled (from ~3% to ~7%), discouraging people from buying homes and keeping them renting longer.
Renters stayed renters longer, increasing competition — and rents rose. ​ End of Pandemic-Era Tenant Protections ​During COVID, there were eviction moratoriums and rental assistance.
Many landlords couldn’t raise rent or evict non-payers.
Once those protections ended (2021–2022), landlords “caught up” on deferred rent hikes, raising prices by 10–30% in one year.
There was little-to-no regulation in Ohio to limit how high rents could go.
Impact: Sudden, large rent hikes — especially in previously stable, low-income areas. ​ Solutions: ​ Ohio has the tools and the money — what we need now is the political will to act.
Housing is a foundation for everything else — work, health, and family.

Let’s act now so Ohioans can afford to live where they work and raise their kids in the communities they love. ​ Immediate relief through smart reforms Cap rent increases at 3% statewide for one year, under a declared Housing Affordability Emergency.

Apply the cap to large landlords only (e.g., owning 25+ units), exempting small mom-and-pop landlords to build political support. ​Stop Displacement: Enact Just Cause Eviction protections and require 90-day rent increase notice.​​ Provide Emergency Relief: Expand rental assistance and tenant legal aid statewide.
Build Faster: Fast-track permitting and zoning reform with state incentives.
Expand Affordability: Launch an “Ohio Homes Now” fund to support new affordable construction.

Track Corporate Landlords: Create a statewide registry and transparency rules for large property owners. ​ PMK's plan won’t just ease the housing crisis — it will: Prevent homelessness Boost local economies Reduce long-term social service costs Support working families and keep Ohio communities strong We can do these things.
Education First Education and training are the foundations for economic success and prosperity in a globalized world.
Every child deserves access to high-quality education and training regardless of their background.

Ohio’s public schools are facing significant challenges from the GOP, including funding threats, ideological shifts, and policy changes that will devastate public education in all communities from rural to urban. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Universal Pre-K Subsidized daycare Expand the child tax credit Tuition-free public college Reduce student debt Free meals for students & expanded nutritional programs Increased teachers’ pay and funding for public schools Desegregation and equity of districts Curriculum reform Academic freedom Opposition to charter expansion and school privatization We can do these things.
Healthcare ​ Ohio ranks #36 and #40 in Health Care Access and Public Health in 2025.
Proposed Medicaid cuts, hospital closures and rising costs will continue to cause chaos to Ohioans.

The GOP led changes will harm low-income families, seniors and rural communities. ​ ​ ​ Healthcare is a human right, not a privilege Universal healthcare Expand rural healthcare programs Protect and expand Medicaid Cap on all prescription drugs and price transparency Mental health & addiction treatment investment Defend reproductive rights and access to contraceptives Codify Roe v Wade We can do these things.

Infrastructure ​ We must focus on outcomes over process and bring in abundant energy, internet and infrastructure to Ohio. ​ ​ ​ Adoption to renewable energy and expand incentives Modernize power grids Invest in clean energy infrastructure Provide rural areas with broadband infrastructure Subsidize rural internet access Improve digital infrastructure Rural transit expansion through public transit investment Strengthen highway corridors and improve logistics hubs We can do these things.
Environmental Crisis ​The environmental crisis is one of the most pressing global challenges, affecting ecosystems, economies, and human health.
The disastrous GOP policies of the past 30 years have wreaked havoc on our state that ranks 43rd in pollution, facing challenges in air quality, water contamination, and extreme weather.

In Ohio, worsening climate conditions threaten agriculture, infrastructure, and community resilience. ​ ​ Create good paying union jobs away from fossil fuels to sustainable energy Statewide clean energy mandates Regulations on industrial pollution Sustainable infrastructure Flood prevention measures Agriculture sustainability Improve Water Protection Laws Support Energy Efficiency Programs Expand Public Transit & EV Infrastructure We can do these things.

Our Veterans ​ We must stand up for our veterans who stand for us. ​ ​ ​ Expand VA healthcare access and funding Improve mental health services Affordable housing with veteran housing assistance Rental subsidies and homeownership grants Job training for transitioning to civilian careers Ensure state funded veteran programs are strengthened, not reduced We can do these things.
Protect Voting Rights ​ Across Ohio, voting rights are under mounting pressure from laws that disproportionately affect seniors, students, low-income voters, and communities of color.

Legislation like House Bill 458 and Senate Bill 153 has imposed strict ID requirements and threatened to add burdensome proof-of-citizenship rules, even though voter fraud remains virtually nonexistent.
Meanwhile, partisan gerrymandering has skewed representation—despite multiple rulings against the current maps—and massive voter purges have quietly erased thousands from the rolls.

These policies, taken together, don’t just chip away at access—they erode confidence in the promise of a fair and inclusive democracy. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Online voter registration Restore the voting rights act Expanded early & mail-in voting Fight restrictive ID requirements Protect election workers End gerrymandering National holiday for voting days Abolish the electoral college Rank choice voting in all elections Eliminate the SAVE Act and Senate Bill 153 Ohio We can do these things.

Criminal Justice Reform ​ ​ ​ ​​​ End cash bail and reform sentencing laws that disproportionately impact marginalized communities Expand police accountability measures to prevent racial profiling Sentencing reform Expand reentry and fair hiring practices Juvenile sentencing reform We can do these things.

Common Sense Gun Reform ​ ​ ​ Universal background checks Close loopholes on domestic abusers and felons Implement red flag laws Require safe storage Ban assault-style weapons and high-capacity magazines Stronger licensing and training requirements Increase funding for mental health resources We can do these things.
Immigration Reform ​ PMK's plan for common sense immigration reform is a combination of both compassion and pragmatism.

Common sense immigration reform doesn’t mean choosing between security and humanity; it means designing a system that does both well. ​ ​ Smart Surveillance & Tech Investment Targeted Enforcement that focuses on dismantling transnational criminal networks and drug cartels—not on low-risk individuals or families seeking asylum Modernized Ports of Entry Most drugs enter through legal checkpoints.
Upgrading scanning tech and staffing at these sites is critical to stopping trafficking.
Cross-Border Collaboration Work with Mexico and Central American countries to disrupt smuggling operations and address root causes of migration like violence and poverty.

Reforming the Legal Immigration System Fast-Track Pathways for Workers & Families Streamline green card and work visa processes for essential workers, especially in agriculture, healthcare, and construction—sectors that rely heavily on immigrant labor.
Earned Legalization for Undocumented Immigrants Allow long-term residents with clean records to earn legal status through work, taxes, and community contributions.
Dreamer Protections (DACA) Provide permanent legal status and a path to citizenship for those brought to the U.S. as children who know no other home.
Asylum System Overhaul Increase immigration judges and legal aid to reduce backlogs and ensure fair, timely decisions for those fleeing persecution.
Mandatory E-Verify: Require employers to confirm legal work status, reducing the incentive for illegal hiring.

Regional Processing Centers: Set up safe, legal application hubs in migrants’ home countries to reduce dangerous journeys. ​ Protect Marginalized Communities ​ In Ohio, over 460,000 adults—about 4.3% of the population—identify as LGBTQ+, including tens of thousands of transgender individuals.
Many are raising families, contributing to their communities, and striving to live authentically.
Yet despite their visibility, they remain largely unprotected under state law and increasingly targeted by politicians.

In just the past two years, Ohio lawmakers have introduced and passed bills restricting gender-affirming healthcare, mandating the forced outing of students, and censoring LGBTQ+ materials in schools and libraries.
State budget provisions have gone so far as to redefine sex in binary terms and defund programs that serve trans youth.

With no statewide nondiscrimination protections, only about a third of LGBTQ+ Ohioans live in places with local safeguards—leaving the rest vulnerable to discrimination in housing, jobs, and public life.

This is not abstract policy—it’s a lived, daily risk for hundreds of thousands of Ohioans. ​ ​ ​ Pass the Ohio Fairness Act: Enact statewide nondiscrimination protections in housing, employment, and public services based on sexual orientation and gender identity.
Restore Access to Gender-Affirming Healthcare : Repeal bans on gender-affirming care for minors and ensure Medicaid and private insurance cover trans-related healthcare.
Protect LGBTQ+ Youth in Schools : Ban forced outing policies, require inclusive sex education, and fund mental health services that affirm LGBTQ+ identities.
End Censorship and Promote Representation : Protect access to LGBTQ+ books and materials in public libraries and schools.
Encourage inclusive curricula that reflect diverse identities.

Create a Statewide LGBTQ+ Commission : Establish a permanent advisory body to monitor legislation, advise on policy, and ensure LGBTQ+ voices are represented in state government. ​ Other Initiatives ​ Updates to be added: ​ ​ ​ Bring back the fairness doctrine for all media Ensure separation of church & state Reinstate the FDA Reinstate the CDC Reinstate USAID Reinstate NIH Reinstate WHO Reinstate the Department of Education Reenter the Paris Climate Agreement Support Affordable Housing Development Expand the REDD program and rural housing infrastructure funds Offer down payment assistance and rent stabilization programs Create a State Child Tax Credit A $1,000 refundable credit per child under 7 could help over 1 million families Working families in Ohio are squeezed by sky-high childcare, hefty housing and property costs, rising health insurance premiums, and one of the nation’s highest tax burdens.

At the same time, limited economic opportunity, perceived weak public services, and harsh climate are contributing to ongoing outmigration, particularly among young professionals and families seeking more affordable, opportunity-rich lifestyles. ​ HOME MEET PAUL ENDORSEMENTS ISSUES GET INVOLVED More Use tab to navigate through the menu items.

added: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate About Howard Pearl My Story As a lifelong resident of Loudon and a sixth-generation farmer operating Pearl and Sons Farm on Loudon Ridge, I believe in New Hampshire's traditional “Common Sense” values.
My strong business ethic is deeply rooted and has steadily grown since I took over the farm at age 20.
I've made real strides in improving and growing the farm, utilizing a strong commitment to sound business principles combined with sensible financial strategies.
And I've also worked hard to successfully promote collaboration within our local business community.
My three terms in the N.H.
House of Representatives provided me withgreat insights, a working knowledge of how to get things done, and countless new positive relationships.
I successfully sponsored many bills aimed at preserving a way of life that families like mine have enjoyed for generations.
It was an honor to be entrusted by legislative leadership with the chairmanship of the House Environment and Agriculture Committee.
It was similarly an honor to be entrusted with the position of Loudon Town Moderator by the folks who know me best.
The experiences and knowledge I gained from serving in these roles readied me for new opportunities to serve my fellow Granite Staters.
My commitment to agriculture and to the greater New Hampshire community remains profound.
I still serve on the N.H.

Farm Bureau's state board of directors as treasurer, on the Executive Committee of the Concord Grange Chapter, and as a member of two statutory committees relating to solid waste and weights and measures.
Over the last 20 years I've held many different positions within community and trade-based organizations to include the Loudon Zoning Board, the Loudon Trust Fund Committee, the N.H.
Maple Producers, the Merrimack County Farm Bureau, the Speedway Childrens Charities, and the Farm Credit East Customer Service Council.
With the full support of my fiancé Heather, I remain deeply committed to continue to serve constituents as well as the greater Granite State community.

My beliefs in hard work, a positive attitude, and compassion have served me well in all my roles as I seek to continue to make a difference for the better for my family, my community, and our wonderful Granite State.
Endorsements ”Count me in as an enthusiastic supporter of Howard Pearl for State Senator.
As a State Representative, Howard is a proven leader who gets the job done and always fights to protect our New Hampshire Advantage.

The families and small businesses of Senate District 17 will be well served by Howard, and I urge everyone to vote for him.“ Chris Sununu Governor Can You Help?​ We need Howard Pearl in the Senate to stop the Washington socialist agenda from impacting New Hampshire!
Donate to Howard today!
Donate Now Your contribution will benefit Friends of Howard Pearl.

added: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate Issues My Priorities No Income or Sales Tax We have what is called the "New Hampshire Advantage" over other states because we have no income or sales tax.
Democrats have tried to pass one for years but it would dramatically increase the tax burden for everyone Granite Stater and I will fight tooth and nail against one.
Lowering High Prices Howard Pearl understands that rising prices are squeezing New Hampshire families and small businesses.

He is committed to keeping taxes low, cutting unnecessary regulations, expanding housing opportunities, supporting local agriculture, and creating an environment where businesses can grow, compete, and create good-paying jobs.
Strong fiscal leadership helps keep everyday costs affordable for Granite Staters.
Work to Lower Property Taxes The best way to stop higher property taxes is to control government spending.

As President Ronald Reagan said, "The problem is not that people are taxed too little, the problem is that government spends too much." Protect Our Constitutional Rights There is a full on assault of our Constitutional rights.
Whether it's the freedom of speech, or our right to bear arms, the Constitution is being trampled by radicals.
I am a Constitutional conservative and will fight to protect and preserve our Constitutional rights.
Fight the Status Quo Howard Pearl believes New Hampshire succeeds when leaders challenge outdated ideas and pursue practical solutions.
He isn't afraid to ask tough questions, reform government where needed, and stand up to special interests.
Howard will continue fighting for transparent, accountable government that puts taxpayers, families, and local communities first.
Copyright © # Howard Pearl for State Senate Paid for by Friends of Howard Pearl.

added: Skip to content Home About Issues Contact Donate Home About Issues Contact Donate Privacy Policy Last updated: October 28, 2022 Overview Welcome to the official web site (the “Site”) of Howard Pearl for State Senate.
This Privacy Policy outlines our practices for collection, use, and disclosure of your information that you provide to us when you use our Site and see or engage with our advertisements.
By using this Site, you agree that your use of the Site is governed by this Privacy Policy and our Terms of Service.
From time to time, we may update this Privacy Policy.
We encourage you to periodically check this Site for updates.
Your continued use of the Site affirms your agreement to any changes we make to this Privacy Policy.
Please note the distinction between our privacy practices in connection with your visit to the Site, and our Terms of Service.

Information Collected and how it is Collected Voluntary Information : We may collect personal information you voluntarily provide to us including your name, e-mail address, postal address, phone number, mobile number and geographic location.
You may provide this information when you request information, register, make a purchase or for other purposes.
We may also collect demographic information such as gender, date of birth, occupation, employer name and zip code.
In limited circumstances, we may collect payment information such as credit card number where needed to complete a requested service or transaction.

By requesting information to your mobile phone, we may obtain the following information from you in connection with our SMS service: your cell phone number, your carrier's name, and the date, time and content of your messages, as well as other information that you provide.
We will use such information in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

Automatically Generated Information : We may also collect non-personally identifiable information that is generated automatically while you are visiting the Site or elsewhere on the Internet when our advertisements are served, also known as log files.

This data includes, but is not limited to, information such as IP address, web pages visited before and after visiting the Site, date and time, domain type, type of mobile device you use, your device’s unique ID, web pages you view and links you click on within the Site and interactions with our advertisements delivered by us or advertisements delivered by a third party advertising technology vendor.
This type of information may be collected using different types of technologies, such as cookies and pixels.
An IP address, for example, is a unique identifier that certain electronic devices use to identify and communicate with each other on the Internet.
When you visit our Site, we may view the IP address of the device you use to connect to the Internet.
We use this information to determine the general physical location of the device and understand from what regions of the world our Site visitors come.
We also may use your non-personally identifiable information to enhance our Site.
All Site users remain anonymous unless they choose to give us their personal information.
You may elect not to allow us to collect and use this non-personally identifiable data as part of our Service by following the Opt Out procedures described below.

Overview : Currently, we do not use our own cookies to obtain certain types of information when your web browser accesses the Site or advertisement or visits a web site in our network, but rather, we may use other companies to set cookies on our Site and advertisements to gather non-personally identifiable information for us.
“Cookies” are small pieces of information that are stored by your browser.
In some cases, we may also use another company to operate web servers or process credit card purchases for our Site.

The Site may use cookies and other technology to speed navigation and keep track of items and to gather anonymous traffic data that we may use to enhance the Site, our Services, marketing, and other internal purposes.

Remember me : If you select “remember me” on your computer when logging on to the Site, Howard Pearl for State Senate will set a persistent cookie to retrieve your username and password when you return to the site so that you do not have to enter it more than once.
It also allows us to send confirmations, receipts, updates, alerts and support and administrative messages and otherwise facilitate your use of and our administration and operation of the Site.
The persistent cookie also enables Howard Pearl for State Senate to track and target the interests of users to enhance the experience on the Site.
The persistent cookie is removed when you uncheck the “remember me” check box.
Google Analytics collects information anonymously.
Google will not associate your IP address with any other data held by Google.
Neither Howard Pearl for State Senate nor Google will link, or seek to link, an IP address with the identity of a computer user.
We will not associate any data gathered from this site with any Personally Identifiable Information from any source, unless you explicitly submit that information via a fill-in form on our website.
It reports website trends without identifying individual visitors.

You can opt out of Google Analytics without affecting how you visit our site – for more information on opting out of being tracked by Google Analytics across all websites you use, visit Web Beacons : Pages of our Site, advertisements, and/or e-mails may contain small electronic files known as web beacons (also referred to as clear gifs, pixel tags, and single-pixel gifs) that permit us, for example, to count users who have visited those pages, engaged in our advertisement or opened an e-mail and for other related web site statistics (for example, recording the popularity of certain web site content and verifying system and server integrity).
