Use of Personal Information : If we do receive your personal information, we will only use it for the purposes described where it is collected or otherwise described in this Privacy Policy.

We may share this information outside of Howard Pearl for State Senate if (1) you authorize us to do so; (2) it is necessary to allow our service providers or agents to provide products or services for us, (3) it is necessary in order to provide our products or services, to you (and contacting you when necessary), (4) subject to applicable contractual or legal restrictions, it is disclosed to entities that perform marketing services on our behalf or to other entities with whom we have joint marketing agreements, (5) subject to applicable contractual or legal restrictions, it is necessary in connection with a sale of all or substantially all of the assets of Howard Pearl for State Senate or the merger of Howard Pearl for State Senate into another entity or any consolidation, share exchange, combination, reorganization, or like transaction in which Howard Pearl for State Senate is not the survivor, (6) it is necessary in connection with other business purposes including, without limitation, responding to your inquiries or requests for information or services, customer care, service quality, business management and operation, risk assessment, security, fraud and crime prevention/detection, monitoring, research and analysis, marketing, customer purchasing preferences and trends, dispute resolution, credit checking and debt collection, (7) it is necessary to disclose in order to protect or defend our rights or property or those of our users, (8) it is necessary to disclose in order to protect the personal safety of our users or the public, (9) it is necessary for us to provide it to our attorneys, accountants, regulators, auditors or other advisors, or (10) otherwise as we are required or permitted by law or required to comply with legal process served upon us, our agents, representatives or our affiliates.

We may also aggregate your personal information with the information of others and may disclose such information in aggregate form for marketing and promotional purposes in a way that would not identify you individually.

Use of Non-Personally Identifiable Information : Howard Pearl for State Senate or our service providers or agents that provide services for us may use non-personally identifiable information as part of the Services to better tailor advertisements and other content in an effort to create a more relevant experience for each person that visits the Site or elsewhere on the Internet.

This non-personally identifiable information may also be used to predict responses to advertisements, to help determine which ads perform best and which content is most appropriate for different individuals, to measure and optimize the effectiveness of advertisements, and to provide aggregate reporting to our service providers or agents and for our and their internal purposes.
We use various web site analytics tools and technologies regarding activities on our Site that require storage of web session data.
The overall aim of these tools is to aid in making our Site easy to use, to proactively identify and correct error conditions and to provide more relevant advertising and content to you.
These tools and technologies are also used to assist Site visitors who report problems in the use of our Site.
Stored web session data is used in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

Third Party Use of Cookies : We use cookies to compile aggregate non-personally identifiable data about Site traffic and Site interaction so that we can offer better Site experiences and tools in the future.

We may also share non-personally identifiable information with companies such as agencies, ad networks, or exchanges to enable them to analyze user behaviors or to customize the ads that you encounter.
Contests, Sweepstakes and Other Promotions : On our Site, you may wish to participate in contests, sweepstakes and other promotions that we may offer from time to time.
Through these promotions, you may choose to participate in activities such as sharing information found on our Site with others and sending e-mail invitations.

In connection with any contests, sweepstakes and other promotions that we may offer from time to time via our Site, we use the information you provide to administer the contests, sweepstakes and other promotions.

Subject to applicable contractual or legal restrictions, we also may use the information to communicate with you, or the other people you select, about our ’ products and services or our service providers or agents partners may use such information to communicate with you about the contests, sweepstakes or other promotions or their products and services.
If you choose to participate in these promotions, and are eligible to do so, we may ask you for information such as your name, e-mail address, date of birth and telephone number.
Third Party Features Third Party Links : For your convenience, we may include or offer third party offers, products or services on our Site.
Third party vendors may use cookies or other technologies to serve ads on other web sites based on your visit to this Site and other web sites on the Internet.

We cannot be responsible for the privacy practices of any web sites or pages not under our control and we do not endorse any of these web sites or pages, the services or products described or offered on such sites or pages, or any of the content contained on those sites or pages.
Nonetheless, we seek to protect the integrity of our Site and welcome any feedback about these web sites.

Social Media Platforms and Web sites : Any information, communications, or material of any type or nature that you submit to our Site (including, but not limited to any of our pages contained on a social media platform or web site such as Facebook or Twitter) by e-mail, posting, messaging, uploading, downloading, or otherwise (collectively, a “Submission”), is done at your own risk and without any expectation of privacy.
We cannot control the actions of other users of any social media platform or web site and we are therefore not responsible for any content or Submissions contained on such sites and platforms.

By visiting any of our pages or web sites that are contained on a social media platform or web site, you are representing and warranting to us that you have reviewed the applicable privacy policy and terms of use of such platform or web site and that you will abide by all such provisions contained therein.

Additionally, in the event that we offer a message board or any other interactive or social-type feature on a web site administered directly by us, please be aware that these areas may allow you to publicly post, and share with other users, certain messages, content, or other information (e.g., stories, pictures, ingredients, tips, etc.).
Although we may take certain precautions to protect those who use these areas of one of our web sites, we encourage you to be wary of giving out any personal information in such public forums.
The information you post can be collected and used by people you don't know.
We cannot guarantee the privacy and safety of these areas and are therefore not responsible for any information you choose to post.
Your use of these features is fully at your own risk.
Email Signups E-mail : We appreciate your questions and comments about our Site and services and welcome your e-mails and questions submitted to our Site.
We will share your messages with those within our organization who are most capable of addressing the issues contained in your message.
We may archive your message for a certain period of time or discard it, but your e-mail address and message will only be used in accordance with this Privacy Policy.

Submitting your e-mail : Submitting your address anywhere on the Site may result in your e-mail address being added to the Howard Pearl for State Senate e-mail list, in addition to the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy.
You may unsubscribe to Howard Pearl for State Senate e-mails at any time by opting out of e-mail subscriptions with the “unsubscribe” link included in each e-mail.
Your e-mail address will be removed from our marketing list.
Please allow us a reasonable period of time in order to satisfy your request, as some promotions may already be in process.

Suggesting the Site to a Friend : If you elect to use any feature that includes suggesting a page to a friend or to inform a friend about the Site or solicit donations or pledges or otherwise communicate, Howard Pearl for State Senate may ask for your friend's name and e-mail address.
The Site may automatically send the friend a one-time e-mail inviting them to visit the Sites or otherwise provide the information requested by you.
Howard Pearl for State Senate will store and use this information in accordance with this Privacy Policy.
Your friend may contact Howard Pearl for State Senate to request the removal of this information from our databases.
Security We employ and maintain technology and security measures designed to protect your personal information.
However, no data transmission over the Internet can be guaranteed as 100% secure.
As a result, while we strive to protect your information, we cannot ensure or warrant the security of any information you transmit to us or receive from us.
This portion of our Privacy Policy describes specific rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”).
Please note that we will seek to verify your identity when we receive an individual rights request from you in order to ensure the security of your information.

Please direct any rights requests (as further described below) or additional questions you may have regarding this Privacy Policy via email to: hpearl56@gmail.com​ If you do, we will need to collect your information such as your name, email or transaction history in order to verify your identity.
You may also authorize an agent to make a request on your behalf, who will need to provide similar information for verification.
Deletion California residents have the right to request the deletion of information.
Howard Pearl for State Senate may not delete some or all requested personal data as required or allowed by applicable law.
Access You may request to receive details about how we collect, use, and share your personal data.
Specifically, you may request to receive the specific pieces of personal data that we have collected about you.

Opt-out of Sale If you would like to opt-out of the sale of your information, Non-Discrimination We do not discriminate against you for exercising any CCPA rights, such as the access and deletion rights described above.

If we choose to offer a product enhancement or financial incentive that is contingent on you sharing personal information, we will ensure that the value provided to us by that collection is reasonably related to the value of the product enhancement or financial incentive.

Shine the Light Under California Law, California residents have the right to request in writing from businesses with whom they have an established business relationship, (a) a list of the categories of personal information, such as name, e-mail and mailing address and the type of services provided to the customer, that a business has disclosed to third parties (including affiliates that are separate legal entities) during the immediately preceding calendar year for the third parties' direct marketing purposes and (b) the names and addresses of all such third parties.

To request the above information, please contact Howard Pearl for State Senate on our Site or write to us at (with a reference to California Disclosure Information): Email: hpearl56@gmail.com​ We will respond to such requests for information access within 30 days following receipt at the e-mail or mailing address stated above.
Please note that we are only required to respond to each customer once per calendar year.
Like many other websites and online services, we do not currently alter our practices when we receive Do Not Track signals.
To find out more about "Do Not Track," you may wish to visit http://www.allaboutdnt.com .
Children We strongly encourage parents and guardians to regularly monitor and supervise their children’s online activities.
We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.

Donations When you make a contribution to Howard Pearl for State Senate], federal law requires us to obtain the following information: name, mailing address, employer, occupation, and amount of contribution.
Federal law also requires us to report this information to the Federal Election Commission if an individual’s contributions aggregate in excess of $200 in a single calendar year.
Any credit card information provided is only used to immediately process your donation.
All contributions made to the Site are considered final unless the donation is not in compliance with federal election law and/or Federal Election Commission regulations.
All purchases from the online store are considered contributions to Howard Pearl for State Senate.

Special Statement for Job Applicants Any personal information that you provide to us when applying for a career position with Howard Pearl for State Senate will be used solely to consider and act upon your application.
We may retain your personal information for a period of time, but only for as long as necessary for such purposes or as otherwise required by law.

We may disclose your personal information to our agents for the purpose of evaluating your qualifications for the particular position you applied for, for other available positions or as otherwise required by law.
We may also disclose your personal information to third parties hired by us to collect, maintain, and analyze candidates for career positions or as otherwise required by law.

Visiting our Site from outside of the United States If you are visiting our Site from outside of the United States of America, please be aware that your information may be transferred to, stored or processed in the United States, where our servers are located and our central database is operated.
The data protection and other laws of the United States and other countries might not be as comprehensive as those in your country, but please be assured that we take steps to protect your privacy.
By using our Site, you understand that your information may be transferred to our facilities and those third parties with whom we share it as described in this Privacy Policy.
Contact Us Please contact us if you have questions about our Privacy Policy at: hpearl56@gmail.com​ Copyright © # Howard Pearl for State Senate Paid for by Friends of Howard Pearl.

item_pages.value: ENDORSED BY John Carlson New Haven RTC Chairman "I endorse Peter Lumaj as Secretary of the State for several reasons.
To begin with, he has the qualifications required to do the job.
His familiarity with law and running a business will no doubt be a huge boon in running SOTS.
Secondly, he has the character to ensure the job gets done without bias, and with honesty and integrity.
As we’ve seen from recent events, not only in BPT, but elsewhere, we need someone who will take the appointment seriously and without fear of political backlash from any party or backers.
“Fear not”, Peter is the candidate who is not afraid to let everyone know what he stands for and what he won’t stand for.
Lastly, he is an experienced candidate which will aid him in this run." View all endorsements →

added.text: ENDORSED BYHenri MartinState Senator 31st District"Peter Lumaj has lived the American Dream. He loves our country and our state, and I am proud to call him a friend. Connecticut is a national embarrassment when it comes to election integrity. The Bridgeport ballot stuffing video went viral, prompting news outlets across the nation to mock the fraud. Yet under one-party rule in Connecticut, Democrats have zero interest in making reforms that will restore public confidence in our elections. The embarrassments and the fraud that have made Connecticut a national punchline will continue until we elect different leaders. As our new Secretary of the State, Peter Lumaj will make those reforms his top priority. He will be a voice for the people of our state who are sick and tired of the seemingly endless voter fraud in Connecticut. I wholeheartedly endorse Peter Lumaj. He will be an excellent Secretary of the State and will work tirelessly to restore trust and integrity in our elections."View all endorsements →

added.text: ENDORSED BYAlan ColombieHarwinton RTC Chairman"I’m proud to endorse Peter Lumaj for Secretary of the State of Connecticut. Peter understands that election integrity is not partisan, it’s about trust between the government and the people. Having fled to America from a communist regime, where elections were meaningless, he knows firsthand why secure, transparent, and accountable elections matter. He will ensure every lawful vote counts while strengthening safeguards to restore public confidence in our system. Peter represents principled leadership that protects the process, not a political party, and I encourage Republicans, independents, and all voters who care about election integrity to support him this fall."View all endorsements →

removed: Skip to content Rebecca Bennett for Congress Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Meet Rebecca News Priorities Endorsements Events Store Volunteer Vote Facebook X-twitter Threads Instagram Youtube Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Home Meet Rebecca Priorities Endorsements News Store Upcoming Events Volunteer Donate – ActBlue Donate – Numero Donate with ActBlue Donate with Numero Amalgamated Transit Union Endorses Rebecca Bennett for Congress FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE July 31, 2026 CONTACT : press@rebeccabennettforcongress.com Amalgamated Transit Union Endorses Rebecca Bennett for Congress SOMERVILLE, NJ — The Amalgamated Transit Union (ATU) endorsed Rebecca Bennett for Congress because of her commitment to supporting transit workers and investing in New Jersey’s aging infrastructure.
“As a former U.S.
Navy helicopter pilot and aircraft commander, Rebecca Bennett knows what it means to serve and lead.
A mom to two young girls, she understands the challenges facing workers, including transit workers and their families in New Jersey’s 7th District in my home state.
The ATU is proud to endorse Rebecca Bennett.

A next-generation candidate, we will be mobilizing to send Rebecca Bennett to Congress in this key race to flip the House of Representatives in November,” said ATU International President John Costa .
“I am so excited to have ATU as part of the team as we work to take back NJ-07 in November.
Union workers are the backbone of the Garden State and I am ready to fight to invest in the people who keep our state moving.
Together, we’ll focus on bringing home our federal tax dollars to make much-needed upgrades for our roads, buses, and rail,” said Rebecca Bennett .
Rebecca Bennett, Democratic Nominee for Congress in NJ-07, is a former U.S.
Navy helicopter pilot, officer in the Air National Guard, healthcare leader, and mom of two.
Rebecca served in the Navy for over a decade as a helicopter pilot and aircraft commander.
After serving her country for over fifteen years in the military and making waves in healthcare innovation, Rebecca is running to unseat Tom Kean, Jr. to build a better future for our community.
As a mom to two young girls, Rebecca understands first-hand the challenges of balancing work & family while navigating inflation and the rising cost of living.
For more information, please visit rebeccabennettforcongress.com .

Kean’s office did not respond to a request for comment” SOMERVILLE, NJ — In case you missed it, Congressman Tom Kean Jr. was featured in a New York Times article about members of Congress who have continued to trade stocks and betray the trust of voters.
“Congressman Tom Kean Jr. has spent the past four years trading stocks while voting to drive prices up for all of us.
My husband and I already divested all of our individual stocks because I want New Jerseyans to know that I practice like I preach and will always put our district first,” said Rebecca Bennett .
Let’s not forget: Tom Kean Jr. first ran on a promise to bring ‘ the highest levels of ethics and transparency ’ to Washington.
Instead, he’s become one of the most prolific stock traders in Congress — even trading stocks while missing months of work .

READ MORE: The New York Times: Stock Trading by Lawmakers Becomes a Campaign Attack Line Democrats and Republicans alike are seeking to weaponize incumbents’ trades, particularly those where they can show the appearance of a conflict of interest, and putting them at the forefront of ads and campaign attacks in the country’s most competitive districts.
It is a way to portray their opponents as corrupt and out of touch with the financial realities of working-class Americans.
In Northern New Jersey’s competitive Seventh Congressional District, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee has been targeting Representative Thomas H.
Kean Jr. for continuing to trade stocks while missing more than 100 votes during an extended absence for what he later said was treatment for depression.
Mr.
Kean’s office did not respond to a request for comment.

“SMART-TD is proud to endorse Rebecca Bennett as she runs to represent New Jersey’s Seventh District.
Rebecca is committed to working together to complete the Gateway Tunnel, and after decades of waiting, deliver a one-seat ride to New Jerseyans along the Raritan Valley Rail Line.

She will also stand up against the attacks against collective bargaining to make sure that our rail workers here in New Jersey have a safe workplace, fair wages, and the right to join a labor union,” said Jared Cassity, National Safety & Legislative Director for SMART TD.
“I am grateful for the support of SMART-TD as we work to build a transportation system that actually works for New Jerseyans.

I commuted on NJ TRANSIT and know firsthand how an unreliable train schedule makes it impossible to know if you’ll be back in time to pick up your kids from daycare, coach soccer, or just make it home for dinner.
I am excited to work with SMART-TD to build the Gateway Tunnel because it’s long past time to bring one-seat ride to New Jersey’s seventh district,” said Rebecca Bennett .

Navy helicopter pilot, officer in the Air National Guard, healthcare leader, and mom of two.
Rebecca served in the Navy for over a decade as a helicopter pilot and aircraft commander.
After serving her country for over fifteen years in the military and making waves in healthcare innovation, Rebecca is running to unseat Tom Kean, Jr. to build a better future for our community.
As a mom to two young girls, Rebecca understands first-hand the challenges of balancing work & family while navigating inflation and the rising cost of living.

added: top of page VOLUNTEER MENU Close Home About Get Involved Blog Issues My Priorities Below you can find both my top priorities as well as some concerning votes my opponent has cast during his time in the Connecticut General Assembly.
Affordability & Economic Security Affordability and economic security are central challenges for District 21 and Connecticut.
Families are struggling with housing costs, property taxes, electricity bills, groceries, and child care.

At the same time, we must strengthen public education, expand access to good-paying jobs, and ensure that communities have the resources they need to thrive. ​ ​ If elected, I will advocate for a state child tax credit, meaningful property-tax relief, more affordable child care, and workforce development that connects residents to sustainable careers.
I believe we can make progress by bringing people together around shared priorities, evaluating policies by their results, and making responsible choices with public dollars.
Connecticut should be a place where working hard gives families a fair chance to get ahead.
Affordability & Energy Costs Connecticut families should not have to choose between paying their electric bill and meeting other basic needs.

Addressing affordability requires utility accountability, more affordable energy, and responsible management of public resources. ​ ​ ​​ I will push for greater scrutiny of utility costs, transparent electricity-rate decisions, and more affordable energy supplies without sacrificing reliability.
I would support energy-efficiency programs that lower household and small-business bills, along with assistance for residents struggling to afford utilities.
We must protect essential public services while ensuring families and businesses can afford to live and work in Connecticut.
Affordability & Housing Connecticut needs more housing people can afford, including options for working families, young adults, and seniors who want to remain in their communities.

Housing policy must also account for infrastructure, school capacity, transportation, and neighborhood character. ​ ​ I support collaboration among municipalities, regional partners, developers, and residents to identify appropriate locations for housing and plan for growth.
We should encourage diverse options, including smaller homes, apartments, and affordable and workforce housing, alongside investments in supporting infrastructure.
Local voices matter, as does our responsibility to address the housing shortage.
As State Senator, I will advance policies that expand housing choices, respect legitimate local planning concerns, and help communities accommodate growth responsibly.
My Opponent An overview of some of his votes over the years AFFORDABILITY BILLS 2026 Senate Bill 1: STATE BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS He voted against free breakfast and lunch for kids in school.
He voted against universal pre-k.
He voted against making child care more affordable.
He voted against a tax-free week to buy school supplies.

Put together with 2025 House Bill 7287: STATE BUDGET APPROPRIATION AND IMPLEMENTER: He voted against $660M in municipal aid increases in the biennium budget, money that could have significantly reduced property taxes in our district.​ EMERGENCY STATE RESPONSE RESERVE 2025 House Bill 8003: FUNDS TO ADDRESS REDUCTIONS IN FEDERAL FUNDING He voted against providing food and retaining healthcare coverage for tens of thousands of residents, arguing a one-time fix was not a solution.
DOMESTIC VIOLENCE BILLS 2026 Senate Bill 485: EXPANDING THE ADDRESS CONFIDENTIALITY PROGRAM He voted against letting domestic violence victims keep their home address out of public record.
2025 House Bill 7287: STATE BUDGET APPROPRIATION AND IMPLEMENTER He voted against funding for the domestic violence hotline.
2025 Senate Bill 1356: PRIVACY, MONITORING, AND CONNECTED VEHICLE SERVICES He voted to let abusers keep access to their victims’ cars.
2016 House Bill 5054: PROTECTING VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ​ He voted against providing additional safeguards for temporary restraining orders.

Affordability & Energy Costs Connecticut families should not have to choose between paying their electric bill and meeting other basic needs.

Addressing affordability requires utility accountability, more affordable energy, and responsible management of public resources. ​ ​ ​​ I will push for greater scrutiny of utility costs, transparent electricity-rate decisions, and more affordable energy supplies without sacrificing reliability.
I would support energy-efficiency programs that lower household and small-business bills, along with assistance for residents struggling to afford utilities.
We must protect essential public services while ensuring families and businesses can afford to live and work in Connecticut.
Affordability & Housing Connecticut needs more housing people can afford, including options for working families, young adults, and seniors who want to remain in their communities.

Housing policy must also account for infrastructure, school capacity, transportation, and neighborhood character. ​ ​ I support collaboration among municipalities, regional partners, developers, and residents to identify appropriate locations for housing and plan for growth.
We should encourage diverse options, including smaller homes, apartments, and affordable and workforce housing, alongside investments in supporting infrastructure.
Local voices matter, as does our responsibility to address the housing shortage.
As State Senator, I will advance policies that expand housing choices, respect legitimate local planning concerns, and help communities accommodate growth responsibly.
My Opponent An overview of some of his votes over the years AFFORDABILITY BILLS 2026 Senate Bill 1: STATE BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS He voted against free breakfast and lunch for kids in school.
He voted against universal pre-k.
He voted against making child care more affordable.
He voted against a tax-free week to buy school supplies.

Put together with 2025 House Bill 7287: STATE BUDGET APPROPRIATION AND IMPLEMENTER: He voted against $660M in municipal aid increases in the biennium budget, money that could have significantly reduced property taxes in our district.​ EMERGENCY STATE RESPONSE RESERVE 2025 House Bill 8003: FUNDS TO ADDRESS REDUCTIONS IN FEDERAL FUNDING He voted against providing food and retaining healthcare coverage for tens of thousands of residents, arguing a one-time fix was not a solution.
DOMESTIC VIOLENCE BILLS 2026 Senate Bill 485: EXPANDING THE ADDRESS CONFIDENTIALITY PROGRAM He voted against letting domestic violence victims keep their home address out of public record.
2025 House Bill 7287: STATE BUDGET APPROPRIATION AND IMPLEMENTER He voted against funding for the domestic violence hotline.
2025 Senate Bill 1356: PRIVACY, MONITORING, AND CONNECTED VEHICLE SERVICES He voted to let abusers keep access to their victims’ cars.
2016 House Bill 5054: PROTECTING VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ​ He voted against providing additional safeguards for temporary restraining orders.

Governor nominee, Ruby Barnes register to vote with LMN party We need new leadership in Nebraska that listens to the people, not special interest groups and corporate donors.
We need a governor that pushes the will of your vote and the well being of your community, not a bought and paid for agenda.
I love Nebraska and envision what the Good Life could actually be with proper governance and policy by the people and for the people.

We know what we want and we voted for it.

With Nebraska's cannabis money going to surrounding states, our legislature keeps us a black market state without regulation, testing, or taxation.
This doesn't give anyone medicinal benefits or access to medical grade, regulated, whole plant cannabis.

PROPERTY TAX RELIEF- My plan creates $300,000,000+ annually in new revenue for the state.

NEW JOBS AND SALARIES- Full access cannabis legalization with an industrial hemp business would create roughly 15,000 new jobs for Nebraskans with a $400 million in yearly salaries.
CROP AND BUSINESS OPTIONS FOR FARMERS- In these uncertain times, it's good to have options.
We grew a lot of industrial hemp in Nebraska for WWII.
A strong industrial hemp business would boost agricultural opportunity in our state.
Building materials, human food, animal feed, textiles, biodegradable plastics, and biofuels are a few products we could manufacture from hemp and export.

MITIGATION FOR BRAIN DRAIN AND YOUTH FLIGHT- Our smart young citizens are more likely to leave Nebraska when their vote isn't respected, when taxes are ridiculous, when cannabis isn't legal, and opportunity is limited.

ROAD REPAIR- We drive on rubble.

Some of this new revenue is going to fix the roads.
PRISON AND JAIL REFORM- We need to quit arresting and jailing people for cannabis.
Our current cannabis policy preys on Nebraskans to keep jails and prisons populated.
Over half (53%) of the drug arrests in Nebraska are for cannabis when we know actual drug problems come from meth, fentanyl, and prescription opiates.
Minor cannabis arrests can add up to significant sentences and penalties.
Our law enforcement needs to focus on the problem drugs and not on cannabis users.
AFFORDABLE ACCESSIBLE MEDICINE FOR VETERANS AND EPILEPTICS- Let's get real here.
Servicemen and women laid it on the line for us and got p hysically and psychologically injured and they can't have cannabis?
That's BS.
So is keeping medicinal grade, whole plant cannabis from our epileptic citizens who's seizures could be greatly reduced or eliminated with medical weed.
This cruel and inhumane oppression has to end for us to evolve as a state and a community.
A RESPECT FOR THE VOTERS AND VOTER UNITY- In these days of political divisiveness where leaders pit people and parties against each other, we need to remember that 71% of us voted for this.
That's a higher margin than any other state in the country, and that shows how Nebraskans are more united than they would like us to think.
I truly feel a non-politician, third party, pro-voter, anti-special interest governor would force our legislature to work for us and not for special interest groups.
When WE have a person in power that respects the vote of the PEOPLE, WE start creating sensible policy....

CLICK HERE FOR MY QUICK BIO CLICK HERE TO REGISTER AND VOTE WITH THE LMN PARTY A GOVERNOR FOR THE PEOPLE Lower the Levies With Cannabis Revenue Our property taxes are out of control with no relief in sight.

If we estimate future Nebraska cannabis sales, calculating population differences to Colorado, Nebraska could generate $300,000,000 in yearly state cannabis revenue and receive around $93,000,000 in tax revenue.
We'll fix the roads and fund our schools to stop these higher-than-Cali property taxes.
Other politicians always talk about bringing new industry to Nebraska, we will actually do it.
Our state is in a serious financial crisis and can not afford to dismiss businesses that create massive new revenue for Nebraska.
Corrupt Unicameral Our elected representatives repetitively dismantle voter approved legislative efforts that negatively affect the Good Life.
Voters passed Initiative 437 and 438 in 2024 with a 71% vote to legalize medical cannabis and create a regulatory framework for licenses.
The state senate killed it by refusing to pass LB677.
They signed "emergency rules" prohibiting raw cannabis flower, smoking, vaping, and gummies....only permitting processed pills and tinctures.
Did you know that!!?
We need to fire the Medical Cannabis Commission and revoke their changes to our voter approved legislation.
Then we can start a functioning system.

Blocks, 4x8 panels, flooring, roofing, insulation, rope, yarn, bio-diesel, chicken feed, and fabric for clothing can all be made from hemp.

Dr.
Santra, a hemp research doctor at UNL, confirms through his many studies that Nebraska is the perfect setting for a successful industrial hemp business.

Let's compare some numbers and stop this ridiculous propaganda.
These are Nebraska specific numbers except for the last one--That's worldwide cannabis related deaths ever, in all of recorded history.

Campaign Manager Marion Beard Campaign manager RICK BEARD I've been a Nebraskan since 1972.
As a child, my father was an international exporter of Nebraska-made agricultural equipment.
My mom worked for the Social Security Administration as a claims representative and instilled in me the importance of a government that provides care and benefits for its people.
When I was 21, a part time holiday job brought on a long career in food, wine, and eventually cannabis.
In 1995, I started the Omaha Wine Company which still operates today.
I moved to Napa Valley in 1997 and started working for a wine store that I eventually owned and operated for 19 years.
California had just legalized accessible medical cannabis in 1996.
I saw California's struggles with early legislation when some municipalities participated and others did not.
Did you know only half the counties in California currently participate in the commercial cannabis business, but all the counties receive tax windfall from cannabis taxation?
In effect, every county wins, even if they don't choose to participate.
This is what could happen in Nebraska.
Bring new business and much needed tax relief to the state while giving counties options on levels of involvement.
In 2016 we moved to Calaveras County in the Sierra Foothills.
Here a board of supervisors vote (3/5) revoked 750 commercial cannabis licenses in one of the state's poorest counties, stripping the county of desperately needed industry and massive tax revenue.
Sound familiar?
That's what's happening in Lincoln right now.
Our elected legislators are blatantly ignoring your vote and destroying our democracy and economy in Nebraska.
In 2019, my wife and I lived in Norman, Oklahoma.
We heard countless stories of people that had died of opiate addictions.
Almost everyone had a personal loss to the drugs.
Then we heard even more accounts of addiction transference-- people getting off the deadly opiates once cannabis became legal and accessible in the state.
It was awesome to see a community find a solution to a deadly problem through cannabis legalization.
Again, we saw issues with early Oklahoma legislation such as excessive licensing and insufficient background checks.

Now that we've seen what legislation succeeds and what fails for about 30 years, we can draft forward thinking, pro-Nebraska, pro-Nebraskan, "full-access whole-plant" cannabis legislation that protects and benefits our citizens with extensive background checks, seed to sale tracking, rigorous product testing, and safe, proven distribution and retail models.

added: Home Team The Simple Plan Press/Media Contact Events T-Shirts and Gear Menu RICK BEARD FOR GOVERNOR Home Team The Simple Plan Press/Media Contact Events T-Shirts and Gear TAKING IT BACK and THE SIMPLE PLAN: The Good Life is under serious threat, and working-class Nebraskans aren't to blame.
We want decent-paying jobs, the ability to raise a family, affordable health care, clean air, and clean water.
How are people supposed to get ahead when Nebraska fights minimum wage increases while giving tax breaks to corporations that underpay our workers?
Property taxes keep rising while expenses outrun wages.
That's not sustainable.
Large corporations in Nebraska should provide opportunities for our people, not take from them.
We will enforce sections 33, 37, and 66 of the ImagiNE Nebraska Act to pursue the recapture of tax credits from corporations that fail to meet their agreed-upon job requirements.
If a corporation takes years of tax breaks while failing to deliver the jobs it promised, those credits deserve a serious review—and, where the law requires it, repayment to the state.
Earlier this year, State Auditor Mike Foley alerted Nebraskans about the Nebraska Advantage Act and it's replacement, the ImagiNE Nebraska Act in a letter to the Nebraska Department of Revenue.
Mr.
Foley noted that both programs have resulted in nearly $1.2 billion dollars in lost revenue during the last four years.
From his letter, "Millions of dollars are actually going to companies that are no longer providing any jobs whatsoever in the state of Nebraska..........That's not right.

It's not fair to the taxpayers." I completely agree with our state auditor and commit to putting an end to these schemes accommodating out of state corporations that view Nebraska as nothing more than a zone for extraction.

I have a common sense plan to eliminate the state's unacceptable deficit without raising taxes, and without cutting funding to our critical agencies that ensure a functioning state that serves its people, and not the corporations.

On my first day in office I will utilize all available and appropriate means to recapture unqualified corporate tax credits and begin full implementation of Nebraska's Medical Cannabis ballot initiative that was overwhelmingly approved by voters, and projected to generate as much as $400 million annually.
We will get Nebraska back on track and prevent cuts to state programs and agencies as proposed by Jim Pillen.
It's time to end the culture and acceptability of corporate handouts and tax breaks for the rich that come from the pockets of hard working Nebraskans.
It's high time we rein in the corporate heist of our state's finances and natural resources before the takers leave our state in ruins.
As your governor I will send a clear message on day one that while Nebraska has always been open for business, it is no longer for sale.
Taking back our state......
Many think our campaign is a single issue campaign around medical cannabis, when in fact, the single issue is money.
Almost every problem we face in Nebraska can be solved with money or was caused by political influence money.

Obviously, Pillen and the Republicans don't want a profitable cannabis system for the state, the Medical Cannabis Board doesn't want it, Walz and Steffen barely speak of it, and Lindstrom didn't mention it once in his plans.
While they all speak of ways to prevent youth flight and brain drain from Nebraska, none of them address the cause and the solution to this issue.
Cannabis use in the United States recently surpassed alcohol consumption, and the main reason for this is younger people use cannabis more than they drink.

So when an entire administration elected by the people works against the vote of it's younger generations, it creates a situation where many other states look more appealing and hospitable without the risk of antiquated persecution for cannabis and a real respect for the will of the voters.
Imagine how many people would leave the state if alcohol was made illegal.
Below is a list of actions for key issues in Nebraska.
Eliminate the ability for corporations, PACs, and special interest groups to funnel money into elections and to our elected officials.
This will be accomplished through legislation similar but not limited to The Montana Plan I-94 and Hawaii's S.B.
This is probably the most critical and important action we can take to recover our state.
Corporate and special interest groups give money to our elected representatives to uphold their wishes over the will of the voters.
If you've ever wondered why our votes aren't respected, this is why.
This plan will take 2 years to accomplish through a Constitutional Ballot Amendment signed by 10% of voters and then voted on by the people in our 2028 state election.
The Montana Plan uses the state's authority to define what powers corporations get and stops giving them the right to spend in our politics.
This is a top issue for voters across the entire country, with very little open discussion regarding this in Nebraska.
This is how we actually deal with and remove the corruption in Nebraska politics.
Enact a statewide pause on new data center permits and require intense environmental impact studies on all data centers.
We will have state auditors run full audits on all data centers receiving tax incentives through the ImagiNE Nebraska Act.
By enforcing sections 33, 37, and 66 of the ImaginNE Nebraska Act, Nebraska can recapture years of tax credits from corporations failing to uphold their requirements set forth in the legislation.
This is fairly cut and dry and appears it will not require extensive litigation and large funding from the state.
Lynne and Jim say businesses will leave Nebraska without incentives.
But if those businesses are not upholding their requirements to the state while receiving massive incentives that are financially wrecking Nebraska, why do we pay to keep them here?
Now that the humanity ending threat of AI data centers has surfaced and been publicized......we are going to quit building these things that threaten our existence.
When other candidates and elected officials do not champion this or similar policy, it's obviously because they are getting paid off by the corporations building the data centers and power plants.
Immediately fire the entire Medical Cannabis Board and personally take over all of their duties and responsibilities as governor.
My short term plan to immediately implement a functioning and highly profitable medical cannabis program for Nebraska looks like this. a.

Due to recent federal rescheduling of cannabis from schedule one to schedule three, Nebraska can begin by importing medical cannabis products from other states with medical cannabis programs and production. b.
Like state run liquor programs, Nebraska will have a state run cannabis program with wholesale, retail, testing, enforcement, and distribution.
We start this systems as we license Nebraska farmers to grow medical cannabis in controlled environments (indoors).

This creates a system that is more profitable for the state with wholesale profit AND sales tax revenue, regulated with oversight that prevents bad players, cartel, and out of state corporations from taking profits that should remain in Nebraska.

We can't afford to dismiss this serious revenue stream for Nebraska, especially considering the condition of our state's finances. ***We put cannabis profits and tax revenue directly into our schools, preventing further levy and property tax increases.
This is a real solution to our runaway property taxes, for the farms and the metros.*** c.
Nebraska immediately starts making revenue before investing in heavy infrastructure.
This all happens through licensing existing hemp and CBD shops to sell medical cannabis while giving doctors the protections they need to write recommendations for patients.
We import the bulk of products to start while our farms and processors are licensed and come into production. d.
The federal rescheduling also makes possible medical cannabis contracts with the Unites States Government (Veterans) and biomass export to other states or countries for processing.
The potential profits are too good to ignore considering the struggles our farmers are experiencing. e.
Donald Trump, who most of our rural farming communities voted for, rescheduled cannabis making it a legal and viable crop for Nebraska.
Let's grow! f.
Stop arresting citizens for cannabis possession.
23% of all drug arrests in the US are for cannabis, mostly for low level possession charges.
This needs to end.
Kick start Nebraska's new industrial hemp business with incentives for growers, processors, and production centers.
We'll connect homebuilders and hemp product manufacturers to create new building systems incorporating Nebraska grown and manufactured hemp building products.
Blocks, 4x8 panels, flooring, roofing, insulation, rope, yarn, bio-diesel, chicken feed, and fabric for clothing can all be made from hemp.
Unlike any other state, Nebraska is poised to do this with its heavy agricultural infrastructure, highly capable farmers, and the environment to realistically grow heavy crops of hemp.
Dr.
Santra, a hemp research doctor at UNL, confirms through his many studies that Nebraska is the perfect setting for a successful industrial hemp business. a.
When we remove the lobby money that works against a successful hemp industry we will start seeing real change and business options for our farms. b.
We can be leaders in renewable green building supplies and the. hemp textile industry, creating rural revenue while cleaning nitrates from our soil and water through hemp farming. c.
I will work with our universities to promote industrial hemp curriculum to our students, future farmers, and future Nebraska hemp industry professionals.
Promote local, alternative food production for rural and urban communities through state and federal programs. a.
Establish Greenhouses and container grow systems in grade schools, high schools, churches, hospitals, jails, old folks homes, restaurants, and community gardens. b.
Develop and promote school programs that teach our children how to grow food for themselves and for their community. ​ To summarize.....
Property tax relief will come from state cannabis revenue going to our schools and preventing levy hikes.
We will use sections 33, 37, and 66 from the ImagiNE Nebraska Act to recapture unqualified tax credits from corporations.
These two sources alone can correct our budget issues within a couple years.

Government Accountability & Anti-Corruption will come through legislation preventing corporations and PAC's from funding our candidates and through extensive corporate audits recapturing unqualified tax credits.
New Jobs & Economic Development come from a vibrant industrial hemp business across Nebraska, providing rural and metro jobs while birthing a new industry for the state.
Youth Flight and Brain Drain is easily mitigated by having a compassionate and accessible cannabis program, job pathways with better paying jobs, and lower property taxes.
Education Funding comes from our highly profitable state run cannabis program directly funding schools and from properly taxing large corporations.
This elevates our schools and mitigates property taxes.
Alternative Healthcare through medical cannabis lightens the load of our healthcare systems by providing alternative medicines for pain, PTSD, inflammation, epilepsy, opiate abuse & addiction relief.
Criminal Justice Reform happens when we stop arresting and jailing our citizens for cannabis possession.
No more for profit policing.
Infrastructure Updates become possible when we free up tax dollars and have matching funds for federal infrastructure assistance.

added: Home | Menu | Sign Up | Donate | En Español Rick Larsen for Congress - https://www.ricklarsen.org Meet Rick Updates Issues Accomplishments Endorsements Get Involved Donate En Español Addressing two crises at once: Recently, I joined Representative Pramila Jayapal and Senator Edward Markey to reintroduce legislation to break down barriers to employment for people in recovery and fund local organizations to help address the nationwide behavioral health workforce shortage.
This legislation would: Create job opportunities for people affected by substance use.
This includes helping workers move into careers that support others in recovery, such as addiction treatment, peer support, pain management, emergency response, or mental health care.
Offer real support, not just a job listing.
Participants would have access to treatment, peer mentors, networking opportunities, and help connecting with other federal, state, Tribal, or local assistance programs.
Work with employers .
This means helping businesses create training programs and find practical ways to hire and support workers in recovery.
Help people build lasting careers.
This includes job training, professional skill-building, and covering costs like job applications, testing fees, and certifications that can otherwise stand in someone's way.
Track what works.
Programs would be built around approaches with a proven track record, and outside experts would independently review results to make sure the program is helping people and communities.
Ensure these programs and stakeholders have the funding they need to succeed.

The bill would reauthorize and expand a pilot grant program and provide a total of $187.5 million in funding for state and local workforce development boards so they can partner with treatment providers, employers, education providers, Tribal organizations, legal services organizations, and other community-based organizations.
These partnerships would support individuals impacted by substance use through innovative, wraparound services designed to help them succeed.
This work builds on efforts I have led for several years.

This epidemic has touched families in every corner of Northwest Washington, and I remain committed to doing the work required to address it, from supporting people in recovery to cutting off the trafficking networks that fuel this crisis.
I will continue to update you as this legislation moves forward.
More soon, Rick Posted on October 15, 2026 .

Naquetta Ricks Morgan Anker October 15, 2026 In this episode of Industry Shakers, Adlane Fellah, Founder and Chief Analyst at Maravedis, speaks with Colorado State Representative Naquetta Ricks (House District 40, Aurora), a co-sponsor of HB24-1334, the law that lets tenants in apartment buildings and mobile home parks request service from the internet provider of their choice.
Rep.

Ricks explains why the bill was introduced, how it works in practice (60 days' written notice to owners, with silence after two attempts counting as permission), and why she sees connectivity as a necessity for homework, work, and telehealth.

Adlane also puts the industry's case to her: what happens to the 20-40% savings bulk agreements can deliver, to the credit-check-free, day-one service many affordable and student housing residents rely on, and to buildings when a second provider installs its own wiring.
It's a candid conversation about one of the central policy questions in multifamily connectivity: how to balance the savings of bulk deals against a renter's right to choose.

When my mother brought my sister and I to the U.S. after we ran from a bloody military coup in Liberia, she emphasized the value of education and pushed us to learn as much as we could.

Source: https://sentinelcolorado.com/opinion/ricks-fostering-diversity-among-colorado-educators-benefits-all-students/ Morgan Anker April 12, 2021 Immigrants, as well, have a right to an attorney Morgan Anker April 12, 2021 As a 13-year-old girl, I fled a civil war in my native country, Liberia.
I watched as armed individuals held my mother at gunpoint, attempting to find her fiancé, who, at the time, was a high-ranking government official.
Despite everything, my family and I were able to flee Liberia and settle in Aurora.

Source: https://www.coloradopolitics.com/opinion/immigrants-as-well-have-a-right-to-an-attorney/article_5555de6e-9b43-11eb-9e42-5b90235572c2.html Morgan Anker March 31, 2021 From refugee to Colorado House representative Morgan Anker March 31, 2021 Naquetta Ricks was a young child when strangers stormed her house and held her family at gunpoint in their driveway.
It was 1980, and the armed dissidents were part of a bloody military coup unfolding in her home country of Liberia.

Source: https://red.msudenver.edu/2021/from-refugee-to-colorado-house-representative.html?fbclid=IwAR1BXEEhyOo0kgDorxX_NGT1nqntMO4KvMf4tCk0e1WlTe5e_lwkK2djx6E Morgan Anker March 25, 2021 Representative Ricks Inspired to Serve as a Voice for Immigrants Morgan Anker March 25, 2021 As the first African immigrant elected to the Colorado State Legislature, newly sworn-in Representative Naquetta Ricks is no stranger to breaking the glass ceiling.
Looking back at her life, Ricks said that she has had the opportunity to live what once seemed like an impossible American dream.
Source: http://denverurbanspectrum.com/articles/540941 Morgan Anker February 17, 2021 Black Woman Makes Colorado Black History and Where are Blacks in the Immigration Conversation?
Morgan Anker February 17, 2021 30 Minutes with Rep.
Naquetta Ricks, Shay Johnson and Jon Bowman.

Source: https://www.facebook.com/100000234522533/videos/5493074904043606/ Morgan Anker February 17, 2021 COVID in Aurora: Pop-Up Vaccine Clinic at Church Helps Sooth Uncertainties Morgan Anker February 17, 2021 A pop-up coronavirus vaccine clinic aimed to get Aurora’s immigrant community immunized.
By now you may have heard that Black, Hispanic and indigenous communities have been hit hard by the pandemic.
Many people of color are hesitant to get vaccinated, but one group within those communities is especially struggling.
“We have a lot of people who live in intergenerational households, and so we’ve had deaths in the community,” said State Rep.
Naquetta Ricks.

Source: https://denver.cbslocal.com/2021/02/13/aurora-covid-vaccine-pop-up-clinic/?fbclid=IwAR1hxyNXkeGYt5KqoNUmdoPxfKoLuaHGkW59_rXay_oyVSP3fCFGh_BzCok Morgan Anker February 10, 2021 Lawmakers want legal representation fund for immigrants housed in detention centers Morgan Anker February 10, 2021 In order to qualify, you must live within the city and county of Denver.

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?fbclid=IwAR2_glR44ndS8H4Vx98jD_UUGZMzxSq9eTmQRU-yKTqKyiAZJhKLDxtzbC0&v=JOx0pwb_dug&feature=youtu.be Morgan Anker February 1, 2021 Biden executive order brings hope and memories to one Liberian immigrant Morgan Anker February 1, 2021 Among the lesser publicized executive orders signed by President Joe Biden on his first day in office: one that would reinstate a delay on enforced deportations for Liberian immigrants.

Recent Posts See All Liberty Beagle is Ready for Early Voting!
More than 400 signs delivered across Tennessee.
Six days of forums, podcasts, emails, questionnaires, sign placing, and conversations.
A lot of miles - and so many people who made every one worthwhile.
We have two weeks of early voting ahead, a brief pause, and then Election Day on November 3.
We’re pushing to the very end!
I hear this question a lot.
After traveling Tennessee throughout the campaign, my answer has changed: A WORKING tour of all 95 counties.
I’ve seen with my own eyes how divided we’ve become — and how obvious it is which communities get attention and which get passed over due to politics.
Too many public servants seem to stop showing up where they think they can’t win votes.
The people living there still have needs.
NAACP and UAW Candidate Forum in Maury County A big THANK YOU to the people and organizations who have made the last few days so special!
Thank you to the NAACP and UAW of Maury County, with a special shoutout to Maury County NAACP President Tamera Sangster.
Tamera was incredibly kind and welcoming, and I truly appreciated the opportunity to connect!

Looking for visibility all over our state.
If you'd like a sign, please let me know.
High traffic areas would be amazing!
Over the next few weeks, I'll have stops in Clarksville, Knoxville, Chattanooga, and Nashville.
Would love to say hi and drop the signs off personally whenever possible.
Robert was able to visit every county seat and leave behind 95 Peace dollars (one in each county) in 86 hours and eight minutes.
Check back for more picture hints and updates from Robert's 95 Counties in 95 Hours Challenges.
Here are pictures and hints from the rest of the counties visited this evening on May 16th - early May 17th.
Robert is finishing the last few counties and should head home ahead of schedule sometime after midnight.
Check out the pictures from today's county visits as of 5 pm (eastern time) and hints for the locations of the Peace dollars.

#ago 1 min read NAACP and UAW Candidate Forum in Maury County A big THANK YOU to the people and organizations who have made the last few days so special!
Thank you to the NAACP and UAW of Maury County, with a special shoutout to Maury County NAACP President Tamera Sangster.
Tamera was incredibly kind and welcoming, and I truly appreciated the opportunity to connect!
Thank you also to Cassandra Geeter for having me on her podcast, “Chasing Prudence.” It’s wonderful to see people working to inform, educate, and engage our young people!

Meanwhile, we’re still BEAGLING THE STATE! 🐶🗽😂 With folks helping from every corner of Tennessee, we’re working to have Liberty Beagles in all 95 counties and at as many early voting locations as possible by October 14!
Thank you to everyone helping make it happen.
Unity through Community in action!
AROOOO!

#ago 1 min read Updated: #ago The first stage is complete!
More than 400 signs delivered across Tennessee.
Six days of forums, podcasts, emails, questionnaires, sign placing, and conversations.
A lot of miles - and so many people who made every one worthwhile.
We have two weeks of early voting ahead, a brief pause, and then Election Day on November 3.
We’re pushing to the very end!
A HUGE thank you to Anthony, Miree, Cindy, Meredith, Brian C., Brian B., Justin, Kendra, Lara, Paul, Liliana, Michael, Ray, and Gary!
Getting these signs across the state in just a few days took a community.
Every stop you made and every moment you gave helped make this possible.
When you vote, please know there is a real community behind the name on that ballot.
People showing up, pitching in, and believing we deserve a government that listens and serves us equally.
My name is on the ballot.
However, this effort belongs to all of us - and so should our government.
Unity through Community.
AROOO!

#ago 1 min read I hear this question a lot.
After traveling Tennessee throughout the campaign, my answer has changed: A WORKING tour of all 95 counties.
I’ve seen with my own eyes how divided we’ve become — and how obvious it is which communities get attention and which get passed over due to politics.
Too many public servants seem to stop showing up where they think they can’t win votes.
The people living there still have needs.
Still pay taxes.
Still deserve representation.
They are not enemies!
Your ZIP code and your ballot should never determine whether your senator shows up for you.
We should all be sick of politics that turns neighbors into enemies and treats entire communities as lost causes.
Every county will get meaningful time with me — to tell me what’s working, what’s broken, and what they need from the federal government.
Then comes the responsibility to act and follow through.
No victory lap.
No grand speeches.
Just work.
I’m running to serve Tennessee.
All of it.
Representation should walk beside you.

removed: Robin Scheu Home Meet Robin Issues Legislative Updates Endorsements Get Involved Home / Meet Robin / Issues / Legislative Updates / Endorsements / Get Involved / For Middlebury Issues Home / Meet Robin / Issues / Legislative Updates / Endorsements / Get Involved / Below are some of the key issues that I will be working on in the next biennium.
There are many other matters of course, so please contact me if you have other ideas you'd like me to know about.
An Economy that Works for All Vermonters, Not Just a Select Few The future of Vermont depends on a healthy economy.
A strong economy provides jobs, lifts people out of poverty, and reduces the pressure on an already overburdened social services system.

With a virtually flat rate of growth, an aging population, fewer young people and young families in Vermont, we need to develop policies and practices that provide opportunities for our citizens which will in turn strengthen our economy.
Today, too many Vermonters struggle to care for and support themselves and their families.

I will continue to fight for: Paid family leave - Working Vermonters should have the security of being able to welcome a new child or care for a sick family member without fear of losing income or being fired.
Increasing the minimum wage - So families can meet the basics.
Their spending will boost Main Street, create jobs, and help Vermont communities to thrive.
Workforce development - We must continue to increase access to training, career and tech education so every Vermonter has a fair shot.
Healthy Environment Vermont is one of the cleanest, most environmentally pristine states in our country.
Our environment, and the health and economic benefits it provides, is under threat from long ignored pollution to our streams and lakes and from climate change.
Clean, renewable energy will safeguard the health and futures of our families and communities.
Weaning our economy off fossil fuels and generating more of Vermont’s energy locally not only addresses climate change, it strengthens our economy by keeping our energy dollars in-state.
Cleaning up our water - We can’t kick the can down the road, especially when it comes to cleaning up our lakes and streams.
We must take action now to secure a long-term plan because our drinking water, tourist economy, property values, and quality of life depend on it.
Reducing our dependence on fossil fuels – Climate change is real and it’s here.
We need to take steps to reduce our carbon footprint and increase our use of renewable energy sources.
Strong Schools, Strong Future Our public schools are the bedrock of our Vermont communities and provide our children the opportunity to reach their potential and succeed in life.

With the additional demands placed on our schools from addiction, mental illness, and poverty, great public schools in our communities are more important than ever in giving all children a fair shot at a bright future.
Education funding – It’s been nearly two decades since Vermont rethought how we fund our schools.
It’s time to find a new solution upholds our support for great public schools, with local accountability, and with all Vermonters contributing their fair share, including the wealthiest.
Universal Pre-K: A quality education is key to lifting people out of poverty.
It begins with early childhood education.
Universal Pre-K helps make child care more affordable, gets children better prepared for school, and increases the chances for all children to succeed in school and beyond.
Tech Centers: Not all of our students will go on to a 4-year college and not all jobs require a 4-year degree.
Our tech centers, including the Hannaford Career Center here in Middlebury, play a critical role in providing educational and career opportunities for those not college bound.

Investing in our tech centers allows students and adults to get the knowledge and skills they need through secondary and post-secondary training so they can enter the workforce and get a good job with a livable wage.
Internships and apprenticeships are additional pathways to successful careers.
Addressing Child Trauma - We can take action now to prevent the stress and trauma in children’s lives that too often leads to drug use and mental health issues.
Healthy Families, Healthy Communities The cost of health insurance and housing are the biggest challenges faced by many Vermonters.
Republicans in Washington are dismantling the Affordable Care Act and cutting funding for Medicare and Medicaid.
Making health insurance more affordable and ensuring Vermonters have access to treatment without barriers for drug addiction and mental health is critical.
All Vermonters should be able to afford to rent, buy, and own a home.
Resources for opiate addiction and mental health – Continue to prioritize funding to ensure that every Vermonter suffering from addiction or mental illness gets timely treatment.

Defending the Affordable Care Act – As Republicans in Washington try to dismantle the ACA and disrupt health insurance markets driving premiums up, we will fight to make health insurance affordable for working families and children.
Continue to push for universal primary care – Support a study to determine a responsible way to pay for this program that will save Vermonters money and increase access to health care.
Access to safe and affordable housing - Work to fund programs that protect and create safe and affordable housing for working families and vulnerable seniors.

added: Robin Scheu Home Meet Robin Legislative Updates Contact Me Home / Meet Robin / Legislative Updates / Contact Me / For Middlebury Meet Robin Home / Meet Robin / Legislative Updates / Contact Me / I moved to Middlebury from Boston in 1992 with my husband, our two children, aged 3 and 6, and two dogs.
In the 34 years we've lived in Middlebury, I have been very active in public and nonprofit service.
I also served as Treasurer on the board of the Vermont Sustainable Jobs Fund.
In the legislature, I serve as Chair of the House Appropriations Committee which appropriates money and establishes the budget for the State of Vermont.
In this capacity, I also serve on the Emergency Board, the Joint Fiscal Committee, the Health Reform Oversight Committee, and the Joint Transportation Oversight Committee.
I am also a member of the Vermont Climate Solutions Caucus and the Women’s Caucus.
In 2017, I was nominated by the Speaker and subsequently accepted to the Emerging Leaders Program of the State Legislative Leaders Foundation .
I am currently co-chair of the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) Budgeting Working Group.

In the 28 years we've lived in Middlebury, I have been very active in public and nonprofit service.
I remain on the board of the Vermont Sustainable Jobs Fund and serve as its Secretary/Treasurer.
In the legislature, I serve on the House Ways and Means Committee and am also the Clerk of the committee.
As one of the two major money committees, Ways & Means considers matters relating to the revenue of the state.

The committee page further states that Ways & Means “shall inquire into the state of the treasury; ascertain the amount of debt due the state, and the claims against it; report the amount of taxes necessary to be raised for the support of the government and inquire what measures, if any, ought to be adopted, the better to equalize the public burdens, secure the accountability of public agents, and otherwise improve the financial concerns of the state, including all matters relating to taxation, local or otherwise and all matters relating to the grand list.” I am also a member of the Vermont Climate Solutions Caucus and the Women’s Caucus.
Two years ago I was nominated by the Speaker and subsequently accepted to the Emerging Leaders Program of the State Legislative Leaders Foundation .
In our spare time, Ted and I like to canoe, bike, and hike.
We also like to travel and to visit our children.
Both of our children are married and we have three adorable grandsons who are 4, 1, and 2 months old.

added: Skip to main Become a Sustaining Donor Donate now Volunteer Donate Return to all news Rob Sand Meets with Seniors, Cancer Survivors, and Health Care Professionals on “Iowa for All” Tour For Immediate Release Contact: press@robsand.com Rob Sand for Iowa 10/15/2026 DES MOINES, IA – This week, candidate for governor Rob Sand continued his statewide “Iowa for All” tour, visiting the Edgewater Senior Living facility in West Des Moines for a town hall with residents, to tour the facility, and discuss his plan to end Iowa’s failed Medicaid privatization system.
Later, Rob joined cancer patients and survivors, their families, and health care experts for a roundtable discussion on Iowa’s cancer crisis and his plan to tackle it head-on starting on day one.

While Rob is focused on expanding access to cancer prevention, treatment, and research, his opponent has called for banning some of the most promising cancer treatments on the market and worked as a paid political operative to block Medicaid expansion .

Learn more about Rob’s recent “Iowa for All” tour stops below: WATCH: WHO13: Rob Sand stops at Edgewater, a WesleyLife Community for Healthy Living READ: Radio Iowa: Sand says Iowa needs ‘to get to work’ on reducing cancer rates Democrat Rob Sand says if he’s elected governor, he’ll appoint a Cancer Task Force, support more research to identify the causes of Iowa’s high cancer rates, and push to improve Iowa’s water quality.
Sand met today with a group of doctors and parents whose children have been diagnosed with cancer.
Sand said Iowa needs to catch up with Nebraska, where the state is spending $4.5 million a year on pediatric cancer research.
Sand would also support regional agreements among cancer treatment centers.

“If a kid from Florida or Nebraska comes into Iowa to get treatment, but it’s under an agreement that means that Iowa kids can go somewhere else in Florida or Nebraska for their form of cancer that’s treated better there,” Sand said, “then everyone’s winning for that arrangement.” Nearly all of the participants in the discussion had attended today’s Iowa Cancer Summit.
One woman expressed concern [that] cancer treatments for children aren’t getting enough attention because the rates of pediatric cancer aren’t rising as much as cancers diagnosed among adults.
Sand said there’s a bipartisan [consensus] around expanding cancer treatment options.
He praised the Republican-led Iowa legislature for voting this spring to set aside money exclusively for pediatric cancer research.

“Not only is it a health issue, not only is it an issue for families with kids who get diagnosed with cancer, I actually think that it’s also an economic development issue right now,” Sand told reporters after the event.

“I hear from people regularly who are so concerned about it that they wonder whether or not they want to be in Iowa.” ### Become a Sustaining Donor of our campaign We need your help to ensure we have the resources to win.
