SHANNON TAYLOR’S ROLE IN THE HENRICO NICU ABUSE CASE Bottom Line Nine premature infants suffered serious physical abuse at Henrico Doctors’ Hospital between 2022 and 2024, including multiple fractures to their arms, legs and ribs.
Four infants were injured in 2023, prompting an investigation in which Shannon Taylor’s office participated.
Although investigators established that abuse had occurred, prosecutors did not pursue charges at that time.
Instead, Taylor’s office negotiated an agreement requiring surveillance cameras and additional training rather than pursuing charges related to the hospital’s delayed reporting of suspected abuse.

In August 2024, when hospital counsel asked whether nurses previously placed on leave could return after completing training, Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Alison Martin responded: “No objection at all.” The original August 2024 email exchange, obtained and published by CBS 6, documents that response.
Erin Strotman returned to the NICU on September 17, 2024.
Additional premature infants subsequently suffered serious injuries.

Following Strotman’s prosecution, Taylor personally negotiated a plea agreement resolving 20 original charges through nine felony child-abuse convictions and limiting active incarceration to three years.

At sentencing, Judge Richard Wallerstein expressly found that Virginia’s sentencing guidelines failed to account for the extent of the mental and physical harm inflicted on these exceptionally vulnerable infants.
The judge imposed 45 years in prison but was required to suspend all except three years under the plea agreement Taylor negotiated.

Taylor later publicly criticized the hospital’s decision to return Strotman to patient care, despite her own office’s documented involvement in the earlier corrective agreement and its written response to hospital counsel, raising questions about the decisions and oversight exercised by Taylor’s office.
The severity of the abuse ● Exceptionally vulnerable victims.
Strotman’s convictions involved nine premature infants.
One family had twins born at 28 weeks; at sentencing, the parents displayed their babies’ tiny diapers and premature-infant clothing. [2, 6] ● Four babies injured in 2023.
The infants suffered fractures to their arms, legs and ribs, sometimes with bruising.
CPS made a “Founded, Level 1 for physical abuse” finding, but investigators could not then identify a perpetrator beyond a reasonable doubt. [1] ● Extensive injuries after Strotman returned.
In 2024, Baby L.M.-B. was preparing for discharge when doctors found fractures of both femurs, both tibias, both radii, both ulnae, a hand bone and multiple ribs.
Baby Y.H. suffered serious leg fractures and possible rib fractures. [1] ● Video showed forceful handling.

The special grand jury described footage of Strotman pushing infants’ limbs beyond their normal range of motion, squeezing an infant’s rib cage and pressing her body weight against a baby with enough force to shift the mattress.
Infants showed distress, including increased heart and breathing rates. [1] ● Medical evidence ruled out routine care.
Child-abuse pediatrician Dr.
Robin Foster testified that the fractures could not be explained by ordinary diapering or accepted NICU handling.
The medical evidence did not support spontaneous fractures from fragile bones in the 2023 cases. [1] ● A striking timeline.

The grand jury reported that similar unexplained fractures stopped during Strotman’s absence of more than a year, resumed after she returned to work in September 2024 and stopped after she was removed again. [1] Four decisions involving Taylor and her office 1.
The 2023 abuse cases did not proceed to prosecution.
A prosecutor from Taylor’s office participated in the CPS/police investigation.
Investigators concluded that the injuries were nonaccidental but could not identify the perpetrator beyond a reasonable doubt. [1, 2] 2.
Shannon Taylor’s office negotiated a corrective agreement instead of delayed-reporting charges.
The hospital formally reported the 2023 fracture cluster weeks after the first discovered injury.
Taylor’s office did not pursue failure-to-report charges and instead obtained cameras in NICU rooms and mandatory child-abuse/reporting training.
Taylor later said the measures were intended to prevent another occurrence and acknowledged that they did not. [1, 4] 3.
Shannon Taylor’s office said it had “No objection at all” to nurses returning.
In August 2024, hospital counsel asked Taylor’s office to confirm its understanding that suspended nurses could return after completing training.

On August 26, Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Alison Martin responded: “No objection at all.” The original August 22–26, 2024, email correspondence, obtained and published by CBS 6, documents the exchange.
Strotman returned on September 17, 2024; additional injuries were discovered beginning in November. [1, 4, 5] 4.
Taylor personally negotiated the three-year active-sentence ceiling.
Strotman faced 20 charges involving nine babies, including malicious-wounding charges, before pleading no contest to nine Class 6 felony child-abuse counts on January 15, 2026.
CBS 6 reported that Taylor personally negotiated the agreement.
On June 5, the judge imposed five years on each count—45 years in total—but suspended all but three years because of Taylor’s the plea cap.

Three active years averaged across nine victims equals four months per victim. [2, 3, 8, 10] Taylor’s public explanations and unresolved questions On Taylor’s claim that the sentence was six times tougher than recommended: Taylor compares Strotman’s three-year active prison sentence to Virginia’s discretionary sentencing guidelines, which placed the recommended incarceration range between one day and six months.
Those guidelines are advisory—not a statutory limit on the sentence a judge may impose.
Strotman originally faced 20 criminal charges involving nine premature infants, including malicious wounding.

In his written explanation at sentencing, Judge Richard Wallerstein explained why the guidelines did not adequately account for the severity of the abuse, stating: “Guidelines fail to take into consideration the extent of the mental & physical harm to the most vulnerable children.” [11] On June 5, 2026, Judge Wallerstein imposed five years on each of the nine felony child-abuse counts, totaling 45 years in prison.
However, because the plea agreement Taylor personally negotiated capped active incarceration at three years, the judge was required to suspend all but three years of the sentence.

The three-year active sentence was therefore the maximum permitted under Taylor’s negotiated agreement—not the maximum sentence authorized by Virginia law for the nine convictions. [2, 3, 11] On the plea: Taylor publicly described obtaining accountability for all nine babies as “a win.” After sentencing and the grand-jury investigation, she said she was “proud of the work” her office had done. [2, 3] On the hospital and return to work: Shannon Taylor misrepresented her office’s involvement after the fact.
After Strotman’s sentencing, Taylor criticized hospital leadership and its decision to return Strotman to work in 2024.

However, In an August 7, 2026, interview with CBS 6, Shannon Taylor acknowledged that her office developed the cameras-and-training agreement following the 2023 investigation rather than pursue charges for the hospital’s delayed reporting of suspected abuse.
She explained that prosecutors hoped those measures would prevent additional abuse but acknowledged that they failed to do so.

Taylor also disputed HCA’s statement that prosecutors had been consulted before Strotman’s return, telling CBS 6: “I’m surprised to hear that, because that is not what happened.” She emphasized that her office had no authority over hospital employment decisions.

However, following the interview, HCA supplied an August 2024 email exchange in which hospital counsel explicitly asked whether Taylor’s office objected to the suspended nurses returning after completing training.

In the August 22 email, hospital counsel wrote: “My understanding is that your office does not object to the nurses put on leave returning to HDH once they’ve received the training.” On August 26, Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Alison Martin responded: “No objection at all.” The actual August 2024 email exchange, obtained and published by CBS 6, directly documents that Taylor’s office was consulted and expressed no objection to the nurses’ return after training. [4, 5] Accountability Questions Supported by the Record ● Taylor’s public statements: Why did Taylor criticize the hospital’s handling of the 2023 investigation and its decision to return Strotman to the NICU without publicly addressing her own office’s involvement in the corrective agreement and its written response of “No objection at all”? ● The return-to-work decision: What review preceded her office’s “No objection at all” response?
What safeguards, if any, did prosecutors request before the suspended nurses returned?

Did Taylor know about or authorize the response at the time? ● The corrective agreement: Why did Taylor’s office pursue cameras and mandatory training instead of charges related to the hospital’s delayed reporting of suspected abuse?

How did her office evaluate whether those corrective measures were sufficient, properly implemented, and followed? ● The plea agreement: Why did Taylor personally negotiate an agreement limiting active incarceration to three years for nine felony child-abuse convictions?
What evidentiary concerns and input from the victims’ families informed that decision?

Read the report. [3] CBS 6, “Former NICU nurse Erin Strotman sentenced to 3 years in prison in Henrico baby abuse case,” June 5, 2026.
Read the report. [4] CBS 6, “NICU nurse broke babies’ bones; Virginia prosecutor says hospital blocked full probe,” August 7, 2026.

Read the report and interview with Shannon Taylor. [5] Original August 22–26, 2024, email correspondence between hospital outside counsel and Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney Alison Martin, obtained and published by CBS 6.
View the actual email exchange.

Also documented in CBS 6’s August 7, 2026, report. [9] WAVY, “Report finds Henrico Doctors’ Hospital threw ‘cloak of secrecy’ over internal investigation into NICU nurse.” [10] The Washington Post, “Virginia NICU nurse accused of abusing infants takes plea deal,” January 18, 2026. STOCK TRADING Rob has never personally selected, purchased, sold, or directed the timing of an individual stock trade.
Rob’s opponent claims that he “may have” had confidential information about companies held in his managed accounts.
This is not accurate.
Rob has never personally made an investment decision, and he has never used nonpublic congressional information to make any financial decision.
Rob’s opponent also claims he traded millions in stocks.
This is not accurate.

Congressional financial disclosures report individual transactions in broad dollar ranges rather than precise amounts, so any cumulative total requires assumptions about where each transaction falls within its range.
Any attempt to calculate a cumulative transaction total therefore requires assumptions about where individual transactions fall within those ranges.
A cumulative figure constructed from those disclosure ranges is an estimate, not an exact amount Rob personally traded or earned.

When an investment is sold and the proceeds are reinvested, both transactions can be reflected in cumulative transaction activity even though the same money is simply moving from one investment to another.
If the new investment is later sold, those same dollars can appear again in the cumulative total.
Over years of professional portfolio management and rebalancing, gross purchases and sales can therefore accumulate without representing an equivalent amount of income, profit or new wealth.
Trading volume is not an increase in net worth.
On July 22, 2026, he voted for H.R.
7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act.

The legislation prohibits Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing securities issued by individual publicly traded companies, requires advance public disclosure of intended sales, and establishes financial penalties for violations.

As Rob said when he voted for the bill, “Members of Congress were elected to serve their constituents, not their stock portfolios.” THE STOCK ACT Rob’s opponent says he “violated an anti-insider trading law.” This is not accurate.
The violation at issue was a financial disclosure compliance issue, not a finding of insider trading.

His opponent is conflating two distinct provisions of the law: requirements to disclose securities transactions and prohibitions against using material nonpublic information for personal financial benefit.
Rob has never personally selected, purchased, sold or directed the timing of an individual stock trade.
His investments are managed by a financial adviser and independent third-party investment managers who make those decisions without consulting him.
Federal law prohibits Members of Congress from using material nonpublic information obtained through their official positions for personal financial benefit.
The bipartisan STOCK Act of 2012, signed into law by President Barack Obama on April 4, 2012, expressly applies federal insider-trading rules to Members and employees of Congress.
Rob voted for the STOCK Act.

The STOCK Act of 2012 contains distinct requirements: certain securities transactions must be disclosed on a Periodic Transaction Report within the applicable deadline, and Members are separately prohibited from trading on material nonpublic information.
The 2023 issue involved transaction reports that were not filed on time.

Under the law, certain securities transactions over $1,000 must be disclosed on a Periodic Transaction Report (PTR) by the earlier of 30 days after the filer learns of the transaction or 45 days after the transaction occurs.
There are no extensions for PTRs.
A report filed after the applicable deadline is late and can result in a late-filing fee.
That reporting requirement is what was at issue in Rob’s case.

In June 2023, during a review of Rob’s financial disclosures, professional staff with the House Committee on Ethics informed his office that transactions handled by the outside financial professional responsible for preparing the disclosures had not been reported on PTRs in a timely manner.
Ethics counsel specifically raised concerns about a history of “late or missing transactions” and advised the office to ensure that future transactions were reported timely and accurately.
Rob’s office received the full scope of those concerns on June 2, 2023.
The financial professional responsible for the filings was terminated effective June 14, 2023.
Rob’s office subsequently hired a new financial administrator to oversee financial disclosure compliance going forward.
Rob has also supported stronger restrictions on congressional stock trading.

7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act, which restricts purchases of individual publicly traded company securities by Members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children, requires advance disclosure of intended sales, and establishes financial penalties for violations.
What happened: Required financial disclosures were not filed within the applicable deadlines.
Rob took corrective action by replacing the professional responsible for preparing the filings and establishing a new compliance process.
What did NOT happen: Rob was not found to have engaged in insider trading.
THE “VOTED TO RAISE HIS OWN PAY” CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims he voted to raise his own pay 10 times.
This is not accurate.
The easiest way to evaluate that claim is to examine both Rob’s actual congressional salary and the legislation involved in the votes his opponent cites.
Rob’s congressional salary has not increased since 2009.
THE “40 TIMES RICHER” CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims he became “up to forty times richer” during his time in Congress.
This is not accurate .
This figure is an outside estimate constructed from congressional financial disclosures that report assets and liabilities in broad ranges rather than precise amounts.

Changes in Rob and Kathryn’s reported assets over nearly two decades also reflect retirement savings accumulated throughout their careers, long-term investments, real estate, market appreciation, and family inheritances.
These assets have multiple sources, including savings and investments established well before Rob entered Congress.
Rob spent more than 26 years working for the Commonwealth of Virginia before entering Congress, earning income and saving for retirement.
Rob and Kathryn also received family inheritances over the years, which contributed to their household assets.
Rob does not maintain a primary residence in Washington and drives himself between Montross and Washington on his own dime when congressional business requires him there.

STOCK TRADING CLAIM Rob has never personally selected, purchased, sold, or directed the timing of an individual stock trade.
Rob’s opponent suggests that he “may have” had confidential information about companies held in his managed accounts.
But that suggestion does not identify what information Rob supposedly possessed, when he possessed it, or how that information was connected to any particular investment transaction.
Rob has not used nonpublic congressional information to make an investment decision.
The “millions” figure cited by Rob’s opponent is not an exact amount reported on Rob’s financial disclosures.
A cumulative figure constructed from disclosure ranges is an estimate, not an exact amount Rob traded — and it is not an amount Rob earned.

When an investment is sold, and the proceeds are reinvested, both transactions can be reflected in cumulative transaction activity even though the same money is simply moving from one investment to another.
If the new investment is later sold, those dollars can appear again in the cumulative total.
Over years of professional portfolio management and rebalancing, reported purchases and sales can therefore accumulate without representing an equivalent amount of income, profit, or new wealth.
And trading volume is not an increase in net worth.
7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act, legislation restricting stock trading by Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children and establishing penalties for violations.

As Rob said when he voted for the bill, “Members of Congress were elected to serve their constituents, not their stock portfolios.” He supports stronger transparency and accountability standards for public officials.
THE STOCK ACT CLAIM Rob’s opponent says he “violated an anti-insider trading law.” The violation at issue was a late financial disclosure — not a finding of insider trading.
In 2023, Rob learned that the accounting professional responsible for his financial disclosures had failed to file a required Periodic Transaction Report by the deadline.
Rob replaced that professional, instituted a new compliance process, and retained a new accountant who works closely with the House Ethics Committee.
What happened: A required financial disclosure was filed late.
What did NOT happen: Rob was NOT found to have engaged in insider trading.
He was NOT found to have used nonpublic congressional information to make stock trades.
And he was NOT found to have personally traded based on information obtained through his official duties.
A late filing is a compliance violation.
But the distinction matters: a disclosure violation is not a finding of insider trading.
THE “VOTED TO RAISE HIS OWN PAY 10 TIMES” CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims he voted to raise his own pay 10 times.
But the easiest way to test that claim is to look at Rob’s actual congressional salary.
THE NET-WORTH CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims he became “up to forty times richer” during his time in Congress.
But the “40x” figure is not an actual net-worth figure reported by Rob.
It is an outside estimate constructed from congressional financial disclosures that report assets and liabilities in broad ranges rather than precise amounts.

An estimate constructed from disclosure ranges is not the same thing as a documented net-worth figure, and the disclosures themselves do not establish that Rob became “40 times richer.” Changes in Rob and Kathryn’s reported assets over nearly two decades also reflect retirement savings, long-term investments, real estate, market appreciation, and family inheritances dating back well before Rob entered Congress.
Rob spent more than 26 years working for the Commonwealth of Virginia before entering Congress and earning and saving for retirement.
Rob drives himself between Washington and Montross in his Toyota RAV4.
Rob’s opponent also conflates the value of Rob’s reported assets with the value of transactions reported by his managed investment accounts.
Those are not the same thing.
Transaction volume is not income, profit, or an increase in net worth.
An increase in estimated household assets over nearly two decades does not establish what caused that increase.

Rob’s opponent provides no evidence establishing that Rob’s congressional actions caused the increase in his reported household assets or that congressional stock trading was the source of that increase.
An estimated increase in family assets over nearly 20 years is not evidence that Rob used his congressional office for personal enrichment.

THE “PERSONALLY PROFITING WHILE VIRGINIANS PAY MORE” CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims he was “personally profiting while we pay more.” But that allegation attempts to connect several separate things: an investment held in Rob’s managed accounts, a congressional vote, a company’s subsequent pricing decisions, and personal financial profit.
Congressional financial disclosures do not establish that connection.
They generally report transactions and asset values in broad ranges, and the existence of a sale does not establish how much profit, if any, was realized from the transaction.
The suggestion that Rob has been making Virginians “pay more” also leaves out relevant parts of his record.
On data-center costs specifically, Rob cosponsored and voted for the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R.
9340), legislation intended to ensure that large customers bear the incremental infrastructure costs required to serve them rather than shifting those costs onto families and small businesses.
Rob does not personally select individual stocks, decide when they are bought or sold, or direct his investment managers to make particular trades.

THE “TAX BREAKS TO COMPANIES HE OWNS” CLAIM Taylor claims Rob “pushed billions in tax breaks to companies he owns, like utility monopolies and data centers.” Rob does not personally select the individual stocks held in his managed accounts, direct their purchase or sale, or control the business decisions of companies whose shares may be held in those accounts.
Rob’s legislative record on data-center costs also includes direct action intended to protect residential and small-business ratepayers.
On September 16, 2026, Rob voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R.
9340), bipartisan legislation he also cosponsored.
The bill passed the House 417–3.

The legislation establishes a federal standard concerning recovery of the full incremental costs of infrastructure upgrades serving large energy customers and requires state regulatory authorities and certain utilities to consider that standard.
That record is directly relevant to the suggestion that Rob has supported shifting data-center costs onto Virginia families.

Rob has supported legislation intended to ensure that large energy customers bear the incremental infrastructure costs associated with serving them rather than shifting those costs onto residential and small-business ratepayers.
THE “$60,000 BEACH-HOUSE TAX BREAK” CLAIM Rob’s opponent claims Rob voted to give himself a tax break worth approximately $60,000 on his Outer Banks rental property.
That figure is not taken from Rob’s tax return, is not a documented amount of tax savings, and is not a calculation of the tax benefit attributable specifically to the Outer Banks property.

The figure comes from an estimate by the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy (ITEP) that Rob’s total potential tax reduction under the 2025 tax law could range from approximately $19,900 to $59,300.
That is a range of nearly $40,000.

Taylor takes the highest number in that estimated range, rounds it to approximately $60,000, and presents it as though it were a documented tax benefit tied specifically to Rob’s Outer Banks property.
Reducing tax liability is not the same as a check from the IRS.
Rob is subject to the same tax code as any VA-01 resident.
The ITEP estimate relies in part on congressional financial disclosures, which report income and assets in broad ranges rather than precise amounts.
Those disclosures do not establish Rob’s actual taxable income or provide enough information to determine his precise tax liability.
The provision Taylor cites is Section 199A, the Qualified Business Income deduction.
It is a generally available provision of the federal tax code that allows eligible taxpayers to deduct a portion of qualifying business income, subject to applicable requirements and limitations.
It has been in place since 2017, and the 2025 law made the Section 199A deduction permanent.
Congress did not create a special tax provision for Rob or his Outer Banks property.
Section 199A is broadly available to qualifying taxpayers, and qualifying rental real estate may constitute a trade or business for purposes of the deduction when federal requirements are met.
The Outer Banks property itself is a rental investment, not Rob’s personal vacation residence.
The capital used to acquire it came from the sale of inherited family property.
Rob and Kathryn continue to live in the same Montross home they purchased in 1985.
The distinction is straightforward: an estimated overall tax reduction ranging from $19,900 to $59,300 is not evidence that Rob received a $60,000 tax break on one rental property.

A Steady Hand for Western North Carolina.
Jimmy Rogers has spent his life working, serving, and raising a family right here in Western North Carolina.
A lifelong Haywood County resident, Jimmy believes leadership is not about titles or politics, but about responsibility.

From running a small family business to serving on local boards and more than two decades on the school board, he has learned that good leadership means listening carefully, making thoughtful decisions, and being accountable to the people you serve.
Guided by faith, grounded in family, and deeply connected to his community, Jimmy brings a steady, common-sense approach to public service.
He understands the importance of fiscal responsibility, respect for local institutions, and decisions being made closest to home.
Jimmy is running for the North Carolina House to represent Western North Carolina with integrity, care, and sound judgment — always putting service before self and the needs of the community first.

Use of Campaign Communications By voluntarily providing your contact information, you authorize the Campaign to communicate with you regarding campaign-related matters, including responses to inquiries, updates, events, volunteer opportunities, and lawful fundraising communications.
Providing your contact information is voluntary and not required to access general campaign information.

Text Messaging Terms (SMS/MMS) By opting in to receive text messages from Jimmy Rogers for NC House , you agree to the following: You may receive recurring text messages related to campaign activity, responses to inquiries, updates, events, volunteer opportunities, and fundraising.

Donations All donations are voluntary and subject to applicable state and federal election laws.
Online donations are processed through secure third-party payment processors.

Donation limits, reporting requirements, and eligibility are governed by applicable election laws.

Content may not be copied, reproduced, or distributed without prior written consent, except as permitted by law.

Use of those services may also be subject to the vendors’ own terms and policies.
Disclaimer of Warranties Campaign communications and website content are provided “as is” and for informational purposes only.
The Campaign makes no warranties regarding uninterrupted access, accuracy, or completeness of information.

Limitation of Liability To the fullest extent permitted by law, Jimmy Rogers for NC House shall not be liable for any damages arising from use of Campaign communications, website access, or participation in Campaign activities.
Modifications to Terms The Campaign may update these Terms from time to time.
Any changes will be posted with an updated effective date.
Continued interaction with the Campaign constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms.
Governing Law These Terms are governed by the laws of the State of North Carolina , without regard to conflict-of-law principles.

The 30 second ad will run statewide across digital and streaming platforms.
The ad specifically emphasizes how Democrat failures have already given Michigan the highest energy rates in the Midwest.
And if Abdul has his way, he’d push extreme Green New Deal policies that would spike utility rates, taxes, and gas prices even further.
The bottom line: Michigan can’t afford Abdul El-Sayed.
Watch the video here or read the full video transcript below: BARB: Our utility bills are already the highest in the Midwest.
CASEY: And Abdul El-Sayed wants us to pay even more.
CHRIS: Abdul’s energy tax would jack up our utility bills $2,000 a year.
MELISSA: And El-Sayed would increase our gas prices, too–20 cents a gallon.
CASEY: Abdul El-Sayed means higher taxes and higher prices.
CLINT: We can’t afford Abdul.
CHRIS: Mike Rogers will lower our costs and cut our taxes.
BARB: That’s money back in our pockets.
MIKE ROGERS: I’m Mike Rogers, and I approve this message.
Learn more about Mike Rogers and his plans to Get Michigan Working Again at RogersForSenate.com .

Senate Mike Rogers today called for the suspension of both the state and federal gas tax.
“Lansing Democrats have made abundantly clear that they want more money out of your pocket and in the government’s.
Last year alone, they raised our gas tax from 31 cents on the gallon to 51.
That’s unconscionable,” said Rogers.
“Abdul and the Democrats already gave us the highest utility rates in the midwest with their failed energy policies.
Working families need leaders who will bring the costs of energy down, not ones who will make their lives less affordable.

That’s why I’m calling for a suspension of both the state and federal gas tax–because hardworking Michiganders deserve relief at the pump.” Michigan’s gas tax is currently 52.4 cents a gallon, which is about 19 cents higher than the national average.
It’s also a more than 20 cent raise from last year, when Lansing Democrats voted to raise the gas tax from 31 cents on the gallon to 51.
The federal gas tax is an additional 18.4 cents .
With the suspension of both the state and federal gas tax, Michiganders would save a total of nearly 71 cents per gallon.
This would be an absolute game-changer for working families.
Learn more about Mike Rogers and his plan to Get Michigan Working Again at RogersForSenate.com .

Senate Mike Rogers today launched a new, 30 second ad hitting “ Doctor ” Abdul El-Sayed on calling to defund breast cancer research.
The six-figure buy will run statewide across digital platforms.
One in eight women will be diagnosed with breast cancer in her life.
More than 42,000 are expected to die from it this year alone.
As a cancer survivor himself, Mike Rogers will stand with Michigan women.
This launch comes on the heels of Mike Rogers’ ad released Monday about how we will take on Big Pharma , hospitals, and insurers to lower costs.
It also follows the release of Mike Rogers’ healthcare plan : Healthcare that Works for Working Families.
Mike’s healthcare plan has three pillars focused on affordability, accessibility, and transparency.
More specifically, he is fighting to lower prescription drug prices, add requirements to prevent excessive denial rates, and improve transparency on pricing from hospitals and insurance companies.
Watch here or read the full video transcript below.
Breast cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in women.
One in eight women will be diagnosed with this disease during their lives.
But Abdul El-Sayed blasted breast cancer patient advocates.
Saying increased funding for breast cancer research was disturbing.
Because it benefitted women with “social power and privilege.” What is wrong with Abdul El-Sayed?
As a cancer survivor, Mike Rogers will stand with Michigan women.
Read the full Townhall exclusive here .

Senate Mike Rogers today welcomed Vice President J.D.
Vance to Monroe, Michigan.
In his remarks, Mike emphasized that the stakes have never been higher than in this election and highlighted Abdul El-Sayed’s lies to cover up his family’s dangerous ties to terrorist organizations.
Listen to his remarks HERE or read the transcript below: “I am Mike Rogers – husband and father, Army officer, special agent with the FBI, Chairman of the House Intelligence Committee.
Thank you for being here.
You probably have heard some news about my opponent in the last week, so I say it's time to have a serious conversation.
Abdul El-Sayed cannot be allowed anywhere near the United States Senate.
He is the most extreme, dangerous candidate to ever run for the United States Senate in the history of our country, and we have to stop him right here in Michigan.
He is lying about his ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.

The IRGC, the Iranian Republican Guard — that is the enforcement mechanism for the largest state sponsor of terrorism in the world — which he refuses to condemn, is telling Americans to vote for Democrats like El-Sayed.
Think of it: the IRGC telling you to vote Democrat for guys like El-Sayed.
Well, I know you won't listen.
Some of the other folks we got to work on a little bit.
The Muslim Brotherhood celebrated just one candidate's primary election.
Just one.
You know who that was?
Abdul El-Sayed.
Front page of their newspaper, celebrating his primary win when he won.
Why are they only supporting one candidate, Abdul El-Sayed?
In college, Abdul was a member of the Muslim Students Association, a feeder organization for the Muslim Brotherhood.
In 2012, he signed a letter supporting the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt, which called to ‘purge the media and the police.’ He's your candidate for the United States Senate.
Let me rephrase that.
He is a candidate for the United States Senate.
Abdul's immediate family openly talks about their close involvement.
His sister said, ‘My family has long been Muslim Brotherhood.’ Just yesterday, Abdul refused to acknowledge his family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood for the second time.

If you think about what's at stake in this election, and you think about the things that have just happened, people who fund his campaign fund the Muslim Brotherhood, his family and ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.
He has lied about that.
As a former FBI agent, I can tell you this: we used to call that a clue.
We brought receipts, Abdul.
What we know for sure is that Abdul El-Sayed does not belong anywhere near that United States Senate.
If his sympathy for terrorists and terrorist organizations isn't bad enough, Abdul wants to have you pay more for just being an American.
We already have the highest utility rates in the Midwest, thanks to the Democrats.
They passed a Green New Deal, a mini Green New Deal in 2023, that drove our utility rates through the roof.
Now, Abdul wants to add a new energy tax that will increase utility bills by $2,000 a family.
Yeah, you're right.
He also wants to add 20 cents to the cost of every gallon of gas.
You're good about your gas going up?
You cannot afford Abdul El-Sayed, and we certainly cannot risk his dangerous ideology in the United States Senate.
Michigan was once the envy of the country.
We can get there again, but we can't do it alone.
With your help, we're going to get our kids reading at grade level again.
We're going to make housing more affordable, so every Michigander can achieve the American Dream.
We're going to bring back those 200,000 manufacturing jobs that the Democrats chased out of our state and overseas.
And we're going to make sure that our kids have the tools to succeed to achieve their dreams right here in the great state of Michigan.
Yeah, you bet.
You bet.
So I hope you guys are ready.
It will take every single one of us.
This is the fourth quarter.
We're in the red zone.
Every voter needs to go vote.
If you have your ballot, turn it in.
And grab a friend or two, and bring them to the polls.
This is about the heart and soul of the country.
When you think of what's at risk on this ballot for this election, there is no other option but victory, faith, family, freedom.
Let's get this done.

Senate to make life more affordable for North Carolina families.
WGHP: Roy Cooper Continues “Make Stuff Cost Less” Tour in Greensboro Reporter: “He spoke to supporters about how, if he wins, he will work in the U.S.
Senate to make life more affordable for families here in North Carolina .
A lot is at stake for this midterm election, including control of the Senate.” Greensboro News & Record: Democratic U.S.
Senate candidate Roy Cooper stops in Greensboro ahead of early voting Kevin Griffin Democratic U.S.
Senate candidate Roy Cooper rallied supporters in Greensboro on Wednesday, a day before the start of early voting.
Cooper also addressed affordability, a key theme of Cooper’s campaign captured in his slogan “Make Stuff Cost Less.” He outlined some of his proposals for doing that at the meeting.
“It starts with working with Congress to roll back these chaotic tariffs that we know are adding to the cost of everyday families,” Cooper said.
“It means finding a way to end this war in Iran.” On Wednesday, Cooper criticized Whatley, a former chairman of the Republican National Committee and N.C.
Republican Party, as a “D.C. insider” who was beholden to President Donald Trump .

WFMY: Roy Cooper Continues “Make Stuff Cost Less” Tour in Greensboro Roy Cooper: “It starts with working with Congress to roll back these chaotic tariffs that we know are adding to the cost of everyday families.

It means finding a way to end this war in Iran.” Cardinal & Pine: Roy Cooper talks AI, war, and healthcare in Greensboro Dylan Rhoney For months, the former governor has traveled across North Carolina, pledging to push for policies that will lower costs if he’s elected and discussing how high prices are impacting families. “ Like with so many North Carolina families, you look at your budget and there’s too much month at the end of the money,” Cooper told the crowd.
“As we look at the cost of gasoline, housing, healthcare, and the financial pressure, it only grows.
These are not just economic statistics, these are real people.
These are our neighbors.
These are our families in our churches.
These are the people who make our community strong, and they deserve to be heard.” Rev.
Frank Thomas, the senior pastor of Mt.

Zion Baptist Church in nearby High Point, introduced Cooper. “ As a pastor, I hear the concerns of hardworking families who are doing everything they know to do, yet still find themselves falling behind,” Thomas said.

added: Skip to content Donate to become a founding member of our campaign now Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Facebook Instagram X-twitter Tiktok Threads Flickr Donate Roy Cooper for North Carolina Roy Cooper Casts Ballot on First Day of In-Person Early Voting October 15, 2026 RALEIGH – Today, on the first day of in-person early voting, Roy Cooper cast his ballot and discussed his plans to Make Stuff Cost Less for working North Carolinians.
“I’m proud to have voted early and I encourage my fellow North Carolinians to make a plan to do the same,” said Roy Cooper.
“So much is at stake in this election.
Costs are rising across the board and everyday people in our state are hurting.

My opponent, Michael Whatley, is a Washington DC Insider and Big Oil and utility lobbyist who is running to boost his own stock portfolio and help his billionaire buddies get even further ahead while working families struggle.

I’m ready to take some North Carolina common sense to Washington and work with anyone I can to make stuff cost less.” North Carolinians can vote early in the general election in-person from now until 3 PM on Saturday, October 31.
Visit IWillVote.com to check your county’s schedule, make a plan to vote today, and bring a friend!

Review the Democrats running for statewide office , and remember to vote all the way down your ballot.
Supporting the statewide candidates AND your local representatives is crucial.
Flipping a chamber would allow us to pass meaningful legislation that helps hardworking Georgians.
It would also allow us to push back against likely efforts to redraw maps this December.
What you can do now Confirm your voter registration and make any necessary updates by October 5.
Make a plan to vote—and encourage your friends and family to do the same.
I strongly recommend voting early in person if possible.

Early voting offers flexibility (you may vote at any early voting site in your county), helps avoid long lines, provides time to resolve issues, and reduces the risk of encountering disruptions at your polling place.
There is good additional voting guidance at the Democratic Party of Georgia website .
Voters with disabilities can find excellent information on voting rights, accessibility tools, and available resources at REV UP Georgia .

added: Back PRIVACY POLICY Last update: April 24, 2026 This Privacy Policy explains how information about you is collected, used, and disclosed by Sam Gallucci (“we,” “us,” or “our”) when you access or use our website and other online services (collectively, the “Site”) or otherwise interact with us.
Changes to This Privacy Policy We may update this policy periodically.
If we make changes, we will revise the date at the top and, in some cases, provide additional notice (such as via email or alerts on the Site).
Information We Collect 1.

Information You Provide We collect information you provide directly to us, such as when you: Donate Volunteer Sign petitions Register for events Subscribe to updates or SMS alerts Contact us This may include: Name Email address Social media handles Postal address Phone number Payment information Occupation and employer (when legally required) Any other information you choose to provide Campaign Finance Disclosure: We collect information you provide directly to us, such as when you: 2.

Automatically Collected Information When you use our Site, we may automatically collect certain information, including: IP address Browser type Device and operating system details Pages visited Time and date of visits Referring URLs 3.

Information from Third Parties We may receive additional information about you from third-party services, including: Social media platforms Payment processors (e.g., WinRed) Advertising and analytics providers We combine this information with other data we collect to improve campaign communications and operations.

How We Use Your Information We use the information we collect to: Operate, maintain, and improve our Site Process donations and transactions Send campaign updates, newsletters, and alerts Deliver SMS and email communications you opt into Respond to inquiries and provide supporter assistance Comply with campaign finance and other legal obligations Analyze user behavior and improve outreach efforts Personalize your experience Connect you with campaign events, volunteer opportunities, and activities We use collected data solely for campaign-related purposes.

Sharing of Information We may share your information only in the following circumstances: With vendors, consultants, and service providers who perform services on our behalf (such as payment processing, email distribution, SMS platforms, analytics, and hosting services) To comply with campaign finance reporting laws To comply with legal obligations, court orders, or lawful government requests To protect the rights, property, or safety of the Campaign or others In the event of a campaign reorganization or asset transfer With your explicit consent No Sale or Marketing Sharing: We do not sell, rent, trade, or otherwise share your personal information with third parties for their own marketing purposes.
SMS Data Protection: SMS opt-in data and consent information will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
SMS data may only be shared with trusted service providers solely for the purpose of delivering campaign communications, or as required by law.

Online Petitions By signing a petition, you understand that your name, city, state, and any comments you provide may be made public or shared with public officials or members of the media in connection with the petition’s purpose.
Third-Party Links Our Site may contain links to third-party websites.

description.after: Sam Ronan's plan to improve internet domain ownership rights protecting small businesses and individuals online. OH-15 candidate for Congress.

title.after: Internet URL Ownership Reform | Sam Ronan for Congress OH-15

added: top of page Log In IMPROVED OWNERSHIP OF INTERNET URLS Previous Next Federalization of ICANN ICANN shall be federalized, and all other similar domain related services, providers, or industries headquartered in the United States, or under US jurisdiction shall be similarly federalized This shall include cloud server hosting, server hosting, and any other method of controlling, storing, or maintaining domains Transparency and Oversight of Domains Given that domains and servers shall become federalized there will likely be grave concerns of abuse, and mistreatment of persons, or industries who utilize those services in a way that may be dissenting to the government, her agencies, elected officials, or other representatives.
In order to alleviate those concerns, IP addresses shall be encrypted, and domains shall be registered through an encryption mechanism that cannot be investigated without a warrant.

Domains, once purchased by an entity or individual, shall become the property of the purchasing party, and the federal agency tasked with maintaining the integrity of that domain, and server shall be designated as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) until or unless a different agency is deemed necessary to manage and maintain the integrity of the internet, and integrity of US based servers Domains shall remain a first come first serve acquisition right, with precedence belonging to current owners of the domain, or those who have proven a justified stake in the IP, such as Google, or WhiteHouse.gov Domains shall remain at a fixed price of $20, annually with the option for discounter rates for consecutive year purchases, or the acquisition of a lifetime domain for $500 to be returned to the public access in the event of death, or dissolution of the organization, business, or agency that used it.

Domains with government affiliations remain accessible solely to government bodies Given the nature of protecting IP, many interested parties would prefer to acquire domains that include their intended naming convention and any that can be indirectly related, this shall continue to be allowed, however, excessive acquisition of “affiliated” domains shall require proof of IP integrity, and concerns, that can be filed with the FCC, and to accommodate the volume of requests, the FCC, or other authorized body shall have staff commensurate to the volume of requests.

Since all activities concerning domains and webhosting shall become federalized, encryption, and security services notwithstanding, it shall become the mandate of the FCC, or authorized agency to facilitate webhosting services, web development services, and their full stack equivalents, to be made publicly available, at nominal cost to the consumer, commensurate to the level of use.
Specifically, individuals who want to create a blog website for their cooking hobby, shall not be charged the same fees as enterprises, and vice versa.

Nominally webhosting should include unlimited bandwidth, traffic, and other standard consideration for any user, however, online storage, and data storage considerations should be stratified based on need and charged accordingly along with any other similar provisions that would not be considered individual, or small scale use STAY INVOLVED Stay updated on Sam's campaign for Congress in Ohio's 15th District.

title.before: City of Grafton facing food insecurity after local grocery store closed over a year ago

removed: top of page Menu Schmidt for IA House Donate Close State Politics Religion Education Health Agriculture Economy Terms & Conditions Privacy Policy Accessibility Statement Contact Us State Politics Religion Education Health Agriculture Economy Donate All Posts Health Politics Education Religion Rural Iowa Agriculture Economy Environment City of Grafton facing food insecurity after local grocery store closed over a year ago Apr 2 2 min read Updated: Apr 5 February 4, 2025 by Alexander Schmidt for KAAL-TV (ABC 6 News) — Since losing their local grocer, the small north Iowa town of Grafton is finding itself on the front lines in the battle against food insecurity.
It is an issue being seen across the State of Iowa as according to Feeding America, around 344,000 people are facing hunger in Iowa with about 110,000 of those people being children.
That breaks down to one in nine people and one in six children being in need of food.
The Grafton J-Mart closed a year and a half ago, and as a result, people living in the city have to drive up to 20 miles away to get a loaf of bread, a container of milk, and a stick of butter.

That means the city and the more than 200 people that live there are now in what is called a “food desert.” A food desert is a community where people have limited access to healthy and affordable food.
Sandy Brusewitz, a resident in Grafton, said fundraising efforts are coming in from the non-profit Grafton Community Action.
“Our last owner had it for over 30 years, I believe, and he did a good job with it and had a good produce.

And, you know, provided the town with was what we needed. really hoping to get some kind of maybe at least a co-op going here, They’ve talked about having some vending machines, maybe to start out with, with some primary things that people are always looking for,” Brusewitz said.

According to Brusewitz, efforts are still in the planning stage, but one upcoming event that will benefit those efforts is Grafton’s annual adult prom, which will be held at the community center on March 1.

top of page Menu Schmidt for IA House Donate Close State Politics Religion Education Health Agriculture Economy Terms & Conditions Privacy Policy Accessibility Statement Contact Us State Politics Religion Education Health Agriculture Economy Donate All Posts Health Politics Education Religion Rural Iowa Agriculture Economy Environment Campaign Blog: Schmidt earns Iowa Federation of Labor endorsement May 15 3 min read by Alexander Schmidt, candidate for Iowa House District 60 I'm incredibly honored that our campaign has earned the endorsement of the Iowa Federation of Labor, AFL-CIO.
As North Iowans are facing an aging population and an ever-shrinking workforce, I believe the labor union movement should be supported now more than ever before.
I live paycheck-to-paycheck.
I'm a journalist and a retail worker, and I have seen firsthand that strong jobs lead to strong communities.

Drive through the 60th District in North Central Iowa, and you’ll find that in the most rural places that it gets, places like Nora Springs, Carpenter, Stacyville, and Mitchell, the empty storefronts almost outnumber the townsfolk.
The few businesses remaining are the lifeblood of their communities.
In between those towns, you’ll find the skeletons of towns like Meltonville and Otranto, Hanlontown and McIntire.
After the businesses disappear, it’ll be the street signs, followed by the label on the map.
Job shortages in the healthcare, manufacturing, service and ag sectors are indicative of a full-blown crisis in Iowa's job market.
The April jobs report showed 52,000 job openings in the state of Iowa, with a majority in those aforementioned sectors.

But "policymakers at the Statehouse," writes Pete Hird (AFL-CIO) and Erica Johnson (IA Migrant Movement for Justice) in the Des Moines Register, "continue to ignore the reality that Iowa does not have enough workers." The Republicans’ regressive tax policies, stagnant minimum wage and their determination to fight their ass-backwards culture wars are succeeding only in driving away an entire generation of Iowans from their homes and families.
Ask a young (under 50) Iowan why they live here, and they’ll tell you it’s because their parents did.
That’s true for me too, but I haven’t lost hope in my home state yet.
My partner Emily and I want to build a home here because it’s where home is.
We want our parents to become grandparents here, and we want their grandchild to be raised in an Iowa that we recognize as our home; one where they feel safe and supported.
Securing jobs for North Iowans, ensuring their right to a living wage and for a safe and equitable workplace will be my priority as your legislator.

I believe the state’s minimum wage should be adjusted by the legislature accordingly (potentially annually) keeping pace with all factors, including at least matching the federal minimum wage, and making statutes that consider worker production and inflation as factors when setting the minimum wage.
House District 60's Republican incumbent in 2017 voted to weaken Iowa's worker's compensation laws .
I believe that, when injured, workers have the right to be treated by their own doctor.
Since these laws were passed, costs have predictably shifted drastically to the injured party, despite the disproven claim that fraud was running rampant.
I believe public employees should have the same collective bargaining rights as in the private sector, including over wages, hours, terms and conditions of employment.
The Republicans also voted for rolling back child labor protections that allow 14-15 year-olds to work 28 hours per week during the school year, 10 hours more than federal law permits.
I'm in favor of certain exceptions for family farm work, but these "reforms" are endangering the safety of children by putting them in potentially unsafe work environments.

The AI revolution is already transforming our economy and our everyday lives, and this technology has the potential to either drive humanity to extinction or to take it to new unimaginable heights of innovation.
The difference will be whether or not our elected officials have the courage to regulate it.
I am the only candidate in the House District 60 race who will be a leader with courage, a listener with compassion and an advocate for all my constituents in North Iowa.
Please consider voting for me in the Democratic primary on June 2, and in the general election November 3.
I am only accepting grassroots donations, and rejecting corporate PAC money.
You can donate here.
Any amount will go directly to my fight against unfettered greed and corporate cronyism in Des Moines.
Thank you for your support, and Power to the People!
Let's get to work!

Chestnut Street, Mt.
Vernon, OH, 43050 Your candidates for U.S.
Congress, Ohio House, and Ohio Senate are coming to Mount Vernon (and they're bringing pizza)!
If you want leaders who represent the people instead of corporations and mega-donors, look for the candidates who WANT to hear from you.

Join Jerrad Christian, Scott Grund, Scott Charland, and Vince McGrail to find out how we can use Congress and the statehouse to fix the data center takeover, ban Flock cameras, and fight for the working class.
LOCATION: In downtown Mt.
Vernon at the ReStore/Habitat for Humanity meeting room This event is free and open to all constituents.
If you are unable to attend but would like to submit a question or share your thoughts, please email info@ScottGrundForOhio.com We look forward to a productive, community-driven conversation.

title.after: IDAHO VOICES: “Jim Risch and the Idaho approach to affordability, energy, and security” - Senator Risch

added: About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign Menu IDAHO VOICES: “Jim Risch and the Idaho approach to affordability, energy, and security” “Idaho seniors don’t need Washington to explain inflation to them.
They see it at the grocery store, pharmacy, gas pump and in their monthly utility bills.
Sen.

Jim Risch has made reducing those everyday costs a central part of his 2026 agenda, combining tax relief with something Washington too often forgets: government eventually has to control its own spending.
Risch supported and applauds the new $6,000 tax deduction for qualifying seniors, along with broader tax changes intended to allow Idaho families and small businesses to keep more of what they earn.
He will fight to renew the Big Beautiful Bill tax cuts when they expire in 2028.

His affordability agenda also includes his Zero-Based Budget Act, which would require federal agencies to justify spending rather than simply assuming yesterday’s budget should become tomorrow’s starting point.
That idea should sound familiar to anyone who has ever managed a household.
When expenses increase faster than income, families make choices.
Businesses make choices.
Washington should too.

Fiscal responsibility is a senior issue because America’s enormous debt ultimately competes with Social Security, Medicare, veterans’ benefits, defense, infrastructure and practically every other federal priority.
Energy is another area where Risch’s Idaho perspective matters.
Idaho is home to the Idaho National Laboratory, one of America’s premier nuclear research facilities.
Risch has become one of the Senate’s leading advocates for advanced nuclear power and co-founded the Senate Advanced Nuclear Caucus.
In 2026, Idaho reached an important milestone when a new advanced reactor achieved criticality at INL— the first new reactor there to do so in nearly 50 years.

Risch argues that nuclear energy can simultaneously provide reliable electricity, strengthen American energy independence, create high-paying jobs, and help the United States compete technologically with China and Russia.
He has also defended Idaho’s hydropower system and pushed development of geothermal energy.
His CLEAN Act would require annual federal geothermal lease sales and streamline permitting.
That’s an authentically all-of-the-above energy strategy.
For seniors, the important words are reliable and affordable.
An older Idahoan shouldn’t have to worry about whether turning up the heat during winter will wreck the household budget.
Risch’s work on veterans provides another important connection to older Americans.
In 2026, he joined Sen.
Angus King of Maine on the bipartisan Veteran Burial Benefit Correction Act.
The legislation would correct a disparity affecting veterans who die from service-connected disabilities by increasing their burial benefit and tying it to inflation.
Risch has also introduced legislation addressing veterans’ access to disability benefits when separation pay is being recouped.
These aren’t enormous ideological battles.
They’re examples of government keeping promises.
Someone who served the United States shouldn’t discover that an unintended technicality in federal law leaves his or her family receiving less than Congress intended.
Rural Idaho also shapes Risch’s priorities.
Nearly two-thirds of Idaho is public land.
Federal land-management decisions therefore affect communities, agriculture, recreation, infrastructure and local economies in ways politicians from heavily urban states may not fully appreciate.
Risch is both a rancher and the Senate’s only trained forester.
That background is especially relevant to wildfire prevention.
His bipartisan Wildfire Prevention Act seeks to remove federal obstacles to forest-management projects and make greater use of existing tools for reducing wildfire risk.
For seniors living in vulnerable communities, wildfire isn’t an environmental-policy abstraction.
It can mean losing a home, evacuating under dangerous circumstances, breathing unhealthy smoke or watching insurance become increasingly unaffordable.
Risch has also worked to protect the Secure Rural Schools program, which delivered $24 million to Idaho counties for schools, roads, bridges and other essential infrastructure in fiscal year 2025.
Taken together, these issues reveal something important about retirement security.
It isn’t just Social Security.
It’s whether seniors can afford electricity.
Whether rural communities have roads and infrastructure.
Whether veterans receive the benefits they earned.
Whether government spends responsibly enough to preserve important programs.
And whether America’s economy remains strong enough to support the next generation.
Jim Risch’s work reflects a distinctly Idaho approach: use America’s resources, encourage innovation, protect rural communities, honor veterans and make government justify what it spends.
Washington could benefit from paying closer attention to those principles.” Saulius “Saul” Anuzis is the president of the 60 Plus American Association of Senior Citizens.

Senator Jim Risch will be on the ballot this November for reelection.
Here are reasons to vote for him: He consistently supports legislation that values liberty, independence, and the success of small business.
His availability to constituents is outstanding.
He demonstrates a personal commitment to integrity and virtue.
A constitutional Republic relies on virtue for its longevity.
In the U.S.
Senate, membership on committees carries the biggest influence for change.
Senator Risch’s years of honorable work have earned him membership on key committees.
He is chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations committee.
He is on committees for Energy and Natural Resources, Small Business, Intelligence, and Ethics.
These committees deal with issues dear to the hearts of Idahoans.
Here are some: The Columbia River Treaty with Canada regulates the Upper Columbia River Basin waterways and dams.
Senator Risch recognizes the agricultural and economic value of the dams (including the Port of Lewiston) and is opposed to breaching them.
He supports local geothermal and nuclear energy development.
He opposes amnesty but supports legal migrant workers.
His positive relationship with the White House has led to the renovation of veterans facilities in Boise and stopping the Lava Ridge wind farm.
Todd Achilles is Senator Risch’s opponent.
He has recently been part of Democrat leadership in the Idaho House but now calls himself “independent.“ To be on a committee a Senator is appointed by caucus leadership.
There is no “independent“ caucus.
Is it not then likely that Todd Achilles would caucus with Democrats?
Senator Risch has done well representing Idaho in D.C.
Let’s vote so he can continue his considerable influence on our behalf.” William Green is a Coeur d’Alene resident.

Jim Risch provided support.
One of the most recent examples took place when the university’s Army Reserve Officer Training Corps, or “ROTC” program, was threatened.
A proposed Army restructuring put the University of Idaho’s status as a host institution in jeopardy.
Sen.
Risch didn’t simply voice his support for keeping the ROTC program at the U of I.
He took the matter all the way to the White House, personally bringing it to the president’s attention.
The president intervened, and a program that has been developing Army officers for generations was preserved.
Sen.
Risch’s leadership matters.
ROTC gives young people the opportunity to earn a college education while preparing to serve our country as a military officer.
Along the way, they develop leadership, discipline, responsibility and a commitment to something larger than themselves.
As a University of Idaho graduate himself, Sen.
Risch understood what was at stake.
More importantly, when the program needed someone with the experience and relationships to get something done, he acted.
There are plenty of things in politics that divide us.
Supporting young people who are willing to learn, lead and serve our nation as an Army officer shouldn’t be one of them.
I’m grateful Sen.

Risch went to bat for the University of Idaho and helped preserve this proud tradition for future generations.” Caroline Nilsson Troy, of Genesee, served in the Idaho Legislature and was the Special Assistant to UI President Scott Green for Governmental Relations.

removed: About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign About Jim Get Involved Endorsements Issues Articles DONATE Request a Yard Sign Menu New program casts ‘Spotlight’ on those who deserve it Coeur d’Alene Press We like it.
On the 136th anniversary of Idaho statehood, Sen.
Jim Risch announced a new initiative that deserves support from citizens across the Gem State.

The Idaho Service Spotlight, a biweekly recognition program honoring individuals whose courage, leadership, and sacrifice strengthen their communities, reflects the best of Idaho’s traditions and values.
Too often, it seems our attention is focused on division, controversy, and the loudest voices in the room.
Yet the true character of Idaho is found in the acts of service performed every day by veterans, first responders, teachers, coaches, community leaders, and volunteers.
We know this because we have such people right here in North Idaho who do this every day.
These individuals rarely seek recognition, but their contributions are essential to maintaining the quality of life we in Idaho cherish.
The Idaho Service Spotlight provides a way to acknowledge these unsung heroes and ensure their stories are shared statewide.
Idaho has long been known for its spirit of independence, hard work, and commitment to neighbors.
Idahoans can be counted on to step forward when help is needed.

Whether responding to natural disasters, mentoring young people, serving in uniform, supporting local charities, or lending a helping hand to those facing challenges, countless residents make sacrifices every day for the benefit of others.
They don’t ask for credit, and they usually don’t get it.
That is why Risch’s decision to recognize these individuals in the Congressional Record and on social media is important.
Public recognition not only honors the recipients but also highlights positive examples of citizenship and leadership.
And Lord knows such examples are welcome and needed.
When communities celebrate service, they encourage others to become involved and demonstrate that making a difference matters.
Let’s encourage each other rather than belittle each other.
By partnering with people to identify deserving awardees, the Idaho Service Spotlight ensures recognition comes from those who witness these acts of service firsthand.
Local residents know who has dedicated decades to volunteer work, who has shown extraordinary courage in moments of crisis, and who consistently puts community needs ahead of personal gain.
Their voices will help ensure the honorees represent Idaho’s finest.
Again, if we only look, such people are all us.
Perhaps most importantly, the program sends a message to younger generations.
In a culture often focused on cell phones, personal achievement and recognition, the Idaho Service Spotlight elevates values like selflessness, duty, and commitment.
These are the kind of qualities that build strong communities.
As Idaho celebrates 136 years of statehood, there is no better time to recognize the people who embody the principles that have defined the Gem State for generations.
The Idaho Service Spotlight is more than an award program; it is a reminder that Idaho’s greatest resource has always been its people.
To nominate an individual for the Idaho Service Spotlight, please contact one of Senator Risch’s regional offices at https://www.risch.senate.gov/ .

added: Campaign finance should be illegal.
It is the first step in the bribery chain.
Big money comes from big promises.
Penalize those who do the favors, as well. ​ -De-monetize our elections.
The big donors expect to get more money back than they gave.
Our elected officials are bought out before they serve a day in office.

Prevent artificial entities from participating. ​ -Create central, federal repository for candidate and platform info for all registered candidates at all phases of elections. ​ ​ Platform Email: adamwithrowforcongress@gmail.com About Contact DONATE bottom of page

Senate Race Oct 15 2026 PRESS RELEASE Alme and Bankhead Back Out, Forcing Cancellation of Second Montana Senate Debate in Two Weeks With both opponents refusing to show up, City Club Missoula cancels its Senate debate.
Seth Bodnar was ready to take the stage.
MISSOULA, MT — For the second time this month, Montanans have lost a chance to hear from their U.S.
Senate candidates side by side because Seth Bodnar’s opponents won’t show up.

On Monday, Democrat Alani Bankhead backed out of her commitment to participate in the City Club Missoula Senate debate, and Republican Kurt Alme formally declined his invitation, continuing his months-long strategy of avoiding answering questions in an open, public forum.
Former Green Beret and Independent candidate Seth Bodnar remained committed to the debate.
The cancellation follows a now-familiar pattern.
Earlier this month, the debate hosted by Montana Free Press and Nonstop Local, scheduled for October 7th, was cancelled after Alme refused to participate.

Alme has also skipped the American Association of University Women forum in Glendive, the Indivisible Missoula forum, the Montana Electric Cooperatives Association forum in Great Falls, and the Beer, Buds, Big Sky debate.

“Seth Bodnar has shown up everywhere across Montana, from Glasgow to Libby to Lame Deer, because he believes anyone who wants your vote should be willing to stand in front of you and answer your questions,” said Bodnar campaign spokesperson Kelly Webster.
“Kurt Alme and Alani Bankhead are doing the opposite, backing out of public appearances and leaving Missoula voters with an empty stage and a cancelled debate.

Montanans deserve a senator who shows up, and that’s exactly what Seth has done every single day of this campaign.” While his opponents continue to avoid voters, Seth Bodnar has consistently met them.
Since launching his campaign in March, Bodnar has held events open to the public in every corner of the state, taking every question from Montanans of every political stripe.
According to recent polling, Bodnar currently leads Bankhead by 18 points, and after voters hear his message, he leads the race outright over Alme.
Republicans, Democrats and Independents alike are consolidating around Seth Bodnar.
Seth Bodnar is a Green Beret, business leader, and former president of the University of Montana running for the U.S.
Senate to be an independent voice for Montana.
Seth is guided by a lifelong commitment to duty, honor, and country.

He graduated first in his class at West Point and served multiple overseas deployments, leading soldiers in the 101st Airborne Division and the 1st Special Forces Group, and serving as a special advisor to the commanding general in Iraq.
After his military service and a successful career in business, Seth spent the last eight years leading the University of Montana.

Under his leadership, the university achieved record high graduation rates, doubled research funding, launched the largest infrastructure renewal in campus history, restored financial stability, and was named the #1 military-friendly university in the country.
Raised by two public school teachers, he believes leadership is about service, not party loyalty.
Seth and his wife, a fifth-generation Montanan, are raising their three children in Montana.

added: Skip to content Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Facebook Instagram X-twitter Donate Thu, October 15, 2026 Press Release Fact-Check: Wittman’s NICU Attack Ad on Shannon Taylor Rated FALSE As Victim’s Parent Calls for Ad to be Taken Down 12 On Your Side Fact-Check Confirms: Hospital – Not Shannon Taylor – Allowed Abusive NICU Nurse Back to Work HENRICO, Va. — A new fact-check from 12 On Your Side (WWBT, Richmond) has rated Rep.
Rob Wittman’s attack ad on Shannon Taylor’s handling of the Henrico NICU child abuse case as FALSE .
Wittman’s ad claims that Taylor’s handling of the case put more babies at risk by allowing the abusing nurse, Erin Strotman, to return to work.

According to the fact-check, that claim is simply not true: it was Henrico Doctors’ Hospital — not Shannon Taylor — that made the decision to let Strotman return to work in late 2024, months after she had first been placed on leave following unexplained fractures found on four premature babies in the summer of 2023.
The criminal case against Strotman did not begin until her arrest in January 2025.

The fact-check’s conclusion was direct: “we will rate this ad as false.” The same fact-check examined a Taylor campaign ad featuring the father of one of the abused babies, which states that Taylor secured a sentence six times harsher than state sentencing guidelines and helped pass a law closing a reporting loophole for hospitals.
The fact-check confirmed both claims as true.

This fact check from 12 On Your Side comes after Dom, the father featured in Taylor’s ad whose child was one of the babies harmed in the NICU, called on Wittman to take down his ad: “Our family’s trauma is not a game or a tool to be used by a politician.

I demand that Representative Wittman take these ads down immediately.” Facts of the case: The abuse: Former Henrico Doctors’ Hospital NICU nurse Erin Strotman abused nine newborns and caused broken bones and other trauma over the course of three years. [ABC News4, 6/6/26] The hospital delayed reporting: Hospital administrators waited 10 days to report suspected abuse to Child Protective Services, even after a radiologist told the hospital’s Chief Medical Officer he believed it was abuse.

A special grand jury investigation found the hospital’s seven week delay in reporting initial cases of suspected abuse led to more patient harm. [WTVR, 8/7/26] ] WTVR, 6/16/26 ] [Richmond Times-Dispatch, 3/13/26 ] The hospital blocked a thorough investigation: A special grand jury’s 74 page report found that the hospital and its CEO had prioritized itself rather than conducting a thorough investigation, calling the hospital’s “loyalty” to Strotman a great “miscalculation.” [WRIC, 6/15/26 ] “Cloak of secrecy”: The special grand jury report also found that there was a “cloak of secrecy” around the hospital’s internal investigation in an effort to shield it from liability. [WRIC, 6/6/25 ] HDH conducted an internal investigation instead of alerting CPS right away: “HDH chose to conduct their own 2023 investigation of Strotman when they suspected she was first abusing NICU babies, instead of immediately alerting CPS.” [WRIC, 6/6/25 ] Shannon got the conviction: Strotman was convicted of nine felony child abuse charges. [ABC News4, 6/6/26] Shannon secured a sentence that was six times tougher: Sentencing guidelines called for one day to six months.
Shannon secured three years, six times the top of the guidelines. [WTVR, 1/16/26] ; [WRIC, 1/19/26] Shannon changed the law: Shannon worked with Del.
Delores McQuinn to strengthen Virginia law with HB 1414.

It passed 92-6 in the House and unanimously in the Senate, and it made failing to report suspected abuse within 24 hours go from a minor fine to a misdemeanor punishable by up to 12 months in jail. [WRIC, 5/15/26 ]; [Richmond Times-Dispatch, 3/13/26 ] ABOUT SHANNON: Shannon Taylor is a battle-tested prosecutor with 25 years of experience and a 90% conviction rate in homicide cases, taking on the toughest threats to Virginia families and delivering justice.

A native of Charlottesville and graduate of the University of Virginia and the University of Richmond Law School, she began her career as a prosecutor in Richmond before serving as a Special Assistant in the U.S.
Attorney’s office.
In 2011, she flipped the Henrico Commonwealth’s Attorney’s office from Republican to Democrat, becoming the first woman elected to the role.
She has since been re-elected three times, proving she knows how to win tough races.

As Commonwealth’s Attorney, Taylor has pioneered programs to support victims of human trafficking, created a task force to tackle the opioid epidemic, and led prosecutors statewide in pledging not to criminalize women or doctors for abortion care.
She has worked alongside law enforcement to keep families safe, fought fraud that harms working people, and partnered with gun safety advocates to take illegal guns off the streets.
Shannon Taylor has built her career on protecting Virginians and delivering justice for families regardless of their politics.
For more on Shannon Taylor’s campaign, visit ShannonTaylorVA.com .
