added: Skip to content Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Facebook Instagram X-twitter Donate Wed, October 14, 2026 Press Release NEW AD: Shannon Taylor Calls Out Rob Wittman for Cashing In on Data Center Stocks While Virginians’ Utility Bills Skyrocket Wittman traded data center stocks while voting to hand the industry billions in tax breaks HENRICO, Va. — Henrico’s top prosecutor Shannon Taylor released a new ad, “ Cashing In ,” which exposes how Rep.
Rob Wittman is personally invested in the data center boom that is driving up utility rates for families across Virginia’s First Congressional District.

The ad highlights that Wittman traded roughly half a million dollars in data center stocks while voting to hand the same industry billions of dollars in tax breaks — even as massive electricity demands push utility costs higher for everyday Virginians.
In the ad, Taylor calls for a ban on congressional stock trading, so politicians can’t cash in while raising our costs.
WATCH “ Cashing In ” HERE: Transcript: SHANNON TAYLOR: Data centers and monopoly utilities are getting rich off of our tax dollars.
And jacking up our rates.
Because politicians, like Rob Wittman, sell us out.
Wittman traded half a million dollars in data center stocks and gave them billions in tax breaks.
Wittman personally gets rich when our costs go up.
That’s why we need to ban congressional stock trading.
I’m Shannon Taylor, and I approve this message.
Because I’m not afraid of this fight.

Rob Wittman Has Used his Office to Get Rich Wittman’s personal wealth has grown as much as 40-fold during his time in Congress, as he traded up to $2.5 million in stocks He voted for an $80 billion tax break for data centers and a 10-year ban on states and localities regulating them — all while owning stock in the very industry cashing in on the data center boom.

Sits on the House Armed Services Committee while buying stock in defense contractors like Lockheed Martin and Honeywell — companies with business before the very committee he serves on, as Business Insider reported.

Traded up to $750,000 in health insurance and Big Pharma stocks — including shares in AbbVie, purchased as the pharmaceutical giant worked on COVID-19 treatments, according to Politico — then voted to raise our healthcare premiums and prescription drug prices.
Violated the STOCK Act – a law aimed at preventing insider trading from lawmakers.

Taylor is Running to Hold Washington Accountable While Rob Wittman has spent his 20 years in Congress cowering to his corporate donors and party leaders at every turn, Taylor has spent her entire career fighting for the safety of her community.

Under her watch, murder rates dropped by over 80% in the county , overall violent crime has trended down in the last five years and she made Henrico a statewide leader in prosecuting sex trafficking cases, and drug overdoses went down by 18%.

Now, she’s taking that same fight to Congress to prosecute the case against the corruption that is hurting Virginians every day and ensure Congress finally starts serving the people they were elected to represent.

Ready to take on politicians across both parties, she released her Serve the People First Agenda to ban stock trading by members of Congress who have information that regular Americans don’t have access to, to stop the revolving door that allows Washington politicians to cash in on their influence by becoming lobbyists, and to mandate jail time for politicians who break the public trust.

### ABOUT SHANNON: Shannon Taylor is a battle-tested prosecutor with 25 years of experience and a 90% conviction rate in homicide cases, taking on the toughest threats to Virginia families and delivering justice.

A native of Charlottesville and graduate of the University of Virginia and the University of Richmond Law School, she began her career as a prosecutor in Richmond before serving as a Special Assistant in the U.S.
Attorney’s office.
In 2011, she flipped the Henrico Commonwealth’s Attorney’s office from Republican to Democrat, becoming the first woman elected to the role.
She has since been re-elected three times, proving she knows how to win tough races.

As Commonwealth’s Attorney, Taylor has pioneered programs to support victims of human trafficking, created a task force to tackle the opioid epidemic, and led prosecutors statewide in pledging not to criminalize women or doctors for abortion care.
She has worked alongside law enforcement to keep families safe, fought fraud that harms working people, and partnered with gun safety advocates to take illegal guns off the streets.
Shannon Taylor has built her career on protecting Virginians and delivering justice for families regardless of their politics.
For more on Shannon Taylor’s campaign, visit ShannonTaylorVA.com .

removed: Skip to content Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Meet Shannon Priorities People First Agenda Endorsements News Store Volunteer Facebook Instagram X-twitter Donate Fri, August 21, 2026 Press Release Rob Wittman Refuses to Oppose NextEra Merger While Maintaining Stock Holdings Henrico, VA – Today, Shannon Taylor, candidate for Congress in VA-01 and Henrico’s top prosecutor, released the following statement in opposition to the proposed merger of Dominion Energy and Florida-based NextEra Energy, currently before the State Corporation Commission: “Handing control of Virginia’s power to out-of-state interests and creating the largest utility monopoly in the country is not the answer at a time of rising energy costs.
In Florida, a NextEra merger was followed by billions of dollars in rate increases for customers.
Congressman Wittman personally benefited from the merger through his stock holdings in NextEra – getting richer while families were forced to pay more.
Virginians already pay too much to keep the lights on.
They cannot and will not shoulder even higher bills so massive corporations can make bigger profits.
Leaders of both parties here in Virginia must oppose this merger.
As a prosecutor, I’ve spent the past 14 years keeping my community safe.
While Rob Wittman invests in the company looking to raise our utility costs here, I’ll fight this deal and anyone who tries to profit at Virginians’ expense.

I’m calling on Congressman Wittman to sell his NextEra shares now and speak out against this merger.” While Virginians have overwhelmingly come out in opposition to the merger due to fear of increases in their already sky high utility bills, Rob Wittman remains invested in the utility company looking to merge with Dominion Energy: NextEra Energy.
And, he has refused to oppose the merger while maintaining his stock holdings .

This same company approved the largest utility rate hike in history after their Florida merger and agreed to pay $150 million to settle allegations that it had lied about its involvement in political interference schemes.

Taylor has been a vocal opponent of Dominion Energy’s ongoing requests to raise rates even further for Virginians, and has made it her top priority to root out this kind of corruption in Washington that allows career politicians like Rob Wittman to get wealthier as they make working families pay the price.

removed: alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/698939189_1369571168328892_6271675812844713660_n.jpg|Redistricting is one of those issues people often consider “inside baseball” until they realize it shapes almost everything else. Who gets heard. Whose communities stay intact. Whose votes carry power. And ultimately… who government believes it is accountable to. For the third time since 2021, the majority party in the Georgia General Assembly will be redrawing district lines now that Governor Kemp has called for a special session beginning June 17th. The maps drawn in this process will not just shape elections. They will shape political power, public policy, and representation for years to come. This moment is another reminder that democracy is not guaranteed by tradition alone. It depends on participation, vigilance, and the courage to stay engaged even when the process feels frustrating or predetermined. And, it requires a willingness to tell the truth about what is happening in plain sight. Langston Hughes once wrote: “O, yes, I say it plain, America never was America to me, And yet I swear this oath—America will be!” That tension — between what this country has been and what it has the capacity to become — is part of the unfolding American story. Georgia has always stood at the center of the struggle for representation, voice, and democracy. And once again, we are being reminded that fair representation does not defend itself. People, pay attention. Ask questions. Speak up. And know that I’ll be fighting for fair representation and our voting rights under the Gold Dome. Because the map is never neutral. And it is never just a map.

added: INFORMATION THAT IS GATHERED FROM VISITORS In common with other websites, log files are stored on the web server, saving details such as the visitor’s IP address, browser type, referring page, and time of visit.
HOW THE INFORMATION IS USED The information is used to enhance the visitor’s experience when using the website to display personalized content and possibly advertising.
E-mail addresses will not be sold, rented, or leased to 3rd parties.

TEXT MESSAGING (SMS) If you provide your mobile number, Esmeralda Soria may send you informational and marketing text messages, including campaign updates, events, volunteer opportunities, and donation requests.
Mobile opt-in information will not be sold or shared with third parties.
Mobile information will not be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
All of the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.
You can opt out at any time by replying STOP.
Reply HELP for help.
VISITOR OPTIONS If you have subscribed to one of our services, you may unsubscribe by following the instructions which are included in the e-mail that you receive.
You may be able to block cookies via your browser settings, but this may prevent you from accessing certain features of the website.

District 1 See also 1st Congressional District debate turns feisty - Talk Business & Politics ; In 1st District debate, Parsons criticizes Crawford for support of Israel; incumbent replies with charge of antisemitism | The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette - Arkansas' Best News Source ; and East Arkansas congressional race debate highlights divide over Iran war Israel has killed over 20,000 Children in Gaza Background: On October 7, 2023, Hamas-led militants launched a horrific surprise attack from Gaza into southern Israel, firing rockets and assaulting civilian communities, a music festival, and military installations.
Approximately 1,200 people were killed, mostly civilians, including women and 40 children.
Another 251 people were taken hostage into Gaza.
The attacks included killings, sexual violence, and other atrocities that UN investigators subsequently classified as war crimes with a particular focus on children.

Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel - Advance unedited version (A/HRC/56/26) - Question of Palestine This triggered world-wide condemnation of the Hamas attack.
It also triggered an approximately 2-year military response in Gaza.

By December 2023 another UN report describes Hamas crimes against children, but also specific information on crimes against children by Isreal Children and armed conflict, Report of the Secretary-General covering the period from January to December 2023 (A/78/842-S/2024/384) - Question of Palestine Before the end of the war world-wide condemnation of the Hamas attack now included condemnation of Israel’s response.

For example United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East Verification of damages to schools based on proximity to damaged sites - Gaza, Occupied Palestinian Territory, Update #10, July 2025 | UNRWA citing 91.8% of Gaza schools damaged.

By June 2026 the UN released the following: United Nations Independent Report : “Israel’s deliberate targeting of Palestinian children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 7 October 2023.” “Between 7 October 2023 and 7 October 2025, at least 20,179 children were killed and 44,143 children were injured as a direct result of the hostilities in Gaza.” And “The Commission examines the use of torture, inhumane and degrading treatment, including sexual and gender-based violence, against Palestinian children, particularly during mass arrests and in detention.” “The essence of childhood has been destroyed”: Israel’s deliberate targeting of Palestinian children in the Occupied Palestinian Territory since 7 October 2023 - Report (A/HRC/62/CRP.2) - Question of Palestine The full report is available at: a-hrc-62-crp-2.pdf Below I provide a list of sources dealing with this topic.

This is, of course, a ludicrous claim; I have friends and colleagues who are Jewish.
I was outraged at the Hamas attack on Israel – as was most of the rest of the world.
But as Israel’s involvement continued, the worlds outrage (and mine as well) slowly came to include Israel’s response in Gaza.
To be clear, I hold no ill-will to the people of Israel, just as I hold no ill-will per se to the people of Gaza or Palestine.
But I do believe that the Hamas fighters and anyone involved in aspect of the Israel attack of October 7, 2023 should be punished for their war crimes.
Similarly, I hope that those responsible in the Israeli government and the Israeli military are ultimately held responsible for their war crimes.
As the war in Gaza continued, an increasing proportion of the population of Israel wanted to end the war and that Netanyahu should resign.

By Rick Crawford’s criteria these Israeli citizens must also be antisemites. https://en.idi.org.il/articles/61845?emci=6fe0e075-93a3-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&emdi=ea000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 Above I have listed some of the sources that indicate that Israel did in fact kill over 20,000 children in Gaza.
Crawford’s response in the debate suggests he felt like his back was against the wall.

It could be that was not aware of the scale of deaths – but, if so, he and his staff (he has a $1.3 million budget for staff) were derelict in their duties; his staff may have known but were unwilling to pass the information along to the Congressman.
This begs the question of: how many children killed in Gaza would the Congressman feel is acceptable in retribution for the 40 children killed in Israel?
The Tora references an “eye for an eye” in the books of Exodus, Leviticus, and Deuteronomy.

title.after: Electric Landscaping Equipment Rebate Program Signed by Governor - Steve Otis for Assembly

added: Home News About Steve Priorities Endorsements Voter Info Volunteer Contribute Contact Electric Landscaping Equipment Rebate Program Signed by Governor September 23, 2026 Albany, NY – State Senator Liz Krueger (SD-28) and Assemblymember Steve Otis (AD-91) announced their legislation to create a rebate program for the purchase of electric landscaping equipment to assist commercial landscapers, local governments, school districts and other institutions (S.1574/A.2657) has been signed into law.
The legislation passed the Senate and Assembly in April.
“Addressing the climate crisis requires action on all fronts," said Senator Krueger .
"Gas-powered landscaping equipment emits a stunning amount of air pollution, not to mention the noise that blights communities across the state.
This new rebate program will make it easier for New York's landscaping companies and institutions to transition to cleaner, quieter equipment.

It's a win for small businesses, workers, communities, and our shared environment, and I thank Governor Hochul for signing it into law today.” Assemblyman Otis said, “New York State ranks fourth in the nation in the highest level of greenhouse gas emissions.

Supporting small businesses and institutions in transitioning to emission-free equipment will improve air quality, public health, and make purchase of new equipment more affordable for local contractors.
Municipalities in New York are increasingly adopting local laws restricting, in a variety of ways, the use of gas-powered equipment.
The rebate program will help local businesses continue to serve their customers.

Senator Krueger and I have worked with a broad coalition of over 100 environmental, public health, and business groups led by NYPIRG to support this program.” Gas-powered landscaping equipment has a significant negative impact on workers, communities, and the environment.
Electric equipment, on the other hand, is lighter, quieter, has lower maintenance costs, a significantly smaller environmental footprint, and is better for workers’ health.
S.1574/A.2657 would create an Electric Landscaping Equipment Rebate Program, administered by the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA).

It would offer point-of-sale rebates to commercial landscapers and institutional users, including municipalities, who purchase battery-powered electric landscaping equipment, such as leaf blowers, weed whackers, or lawn mowers.

Gas-powered landscaping equipment emits large amounts of greenhouse gases and harmful, smog-forming pollution, including hydrocarbons, oxides of nitrogen (NOx), carbon monoxide (CO), and fine particulate matter (PM).

The California Air Resources Board (CARB) has reported that operating a gas-powered lawn mower for one hour creates as much smog-forming pollution as driving an average car 300 miles, the distance from New York City to Portland, ME.
Operating a gas-powered leaf blower for one hour creates as much smog-forming pollution as driving a car 1,100 miles, or from New York City to Tampa, FL.

According to CARB, early in this decade the total smog-forming emissions from small off-road engines, the vast majority of which are residential and commercial lawn and garden equipment, will exceed those from passenger cars in the Greater Los Angeles Area.
Noise is also a significant negative impact from gas-powered lawn care equipment.

According to a 2018 report in the Journal of Environmental and Toxicological Studies, sound levels at distances of 100 to 400 feet were up to 22 decibels louder for gas-powered leaf blowers than their battery-electric equivalents (the decibel scale is logarithmic, so each increase of 10 represents a noise ten times louder).

The report goes on to say, "the routine use of multiple [gas-powered leaf blowers] and other noisy equipment for hours a day exposes not only workers but large numbers of people in the community to harmful levels of noise and threatens not only worker health, but public health, particularly of children, seniors, and other vulnerable populations.” Well over 200 communities in 27 US states and the District of Columbia have enacted restrictions on the use of gas-powered leaf blowers.
In New York State, around 70 cities, towns, and villages have bans or other restrictions on gas-powered leaf blowers during certain times of year.

added: Home News About Steve Priorities Endorsements Voter Info Volunteer Contribute Contact About Steve Otis Clic aquí para español Assemblyman Steve Otis serves Sound Shore communities of Westchester County by using his work on local, county, state and federal issues and long‑time leadership in the environmental community to win results and move issues of importance statewide and to the 91 st Assembly District.

Since the creation of WIIA, the program has provided over $3.4 billion in water grants to over 1200 projects statewide: creating jobs, making environmental projects possible and making these projects more affordable for local taxpayers.
Westchester communities have secured over $132 million in grants for 53 projects.
Each year Steve has been a leader advocating for Clean Water funding in the state budget, which increased to $525 million for the 2026-27 fiscal year.

The committee has co-sponsored hearings and roundtables on a variety of emerging issues, including the use of artificial intelligence systems in the underwriting and pricing of insurance policies, the use of AI in financial technology (FinTech) and its role in New York’s banking industry, and on legislation to prohibit surveillance pricing.
The committee co-sponsored hearings in 2023 and 2025 on AI workplace issues with the Assembly Labor Committee.
Measures signed into law include legislation to improve cybersecurity protection and provide oversight of state government use of artificial intelligence and automated decision-making systems.
Otis sponsors the major EMS reform legislation to provide every New Yorker reliable and timely emergency medical response services.
As part of this effort, his legislation to have counties, cities, towns, and villages work together to draft county EMS plans was signed into law in 2025.
That planning process is now underway.

Other innovative statutes adopted include legislation to make directing laser pointers at airplane cockpits illegal under state law, strengthening child labor law protections for minors working in the modeling industry, enacting rules to prevent dangerous accidents from falling soccer goals, expanding options for consumers holding annuities and increasing the state penalty for stealing a pet, which had not been changed in over 40 years.
A strong proponent of small business and buying local, Otis works with local businesses and chambers of commerce on issues of importance.
He also authored a law to increase the information available to members of Business Improvement Districts about the work of those organizations.
Before joining Senator Oppenheimer, Otis served as Senate Fellow and Legislative Director to State Senator Jeremy S.
Weinstein.

In addition to serving as chair of the Science and Technology Committee, the Assemblyman serves as a member of the following Assembly Committees: Ways and Means; Education; Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; and Environmental Conservation.
He previously served on the Libraries and Education Technology Committee, the Local Governments Committee, and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committee in the Assembly.
In addition, he has served on the Assembly’s Climate Change Task Force and on the Assembly Working Group on Transitioning beyond the Covid-19 Economy.
He serves on the Assembly Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.

added: RE-ELECT STEVE OTIS STATE ASSEMBLYMAN A EFFECTIVE LEADERSHIP RESULTS FOR WESTCHESTER A STEVE OTIS IS ONE OF WESTCHESTER’S MOST HARD WORKING AND EFFECTIVE PUBLIC OFFICIALS.

Serving Larchmont, Mamaroneck, New Rochelle, Port Chester, Rye, and Rye Brook “Every year my focus is to break ground on new issues, to achieve real results, to advance solutions with fresh ideas and innovative approaches to serve the Sound Shore and our state.
My goal is always to secure victories on issues where I play a leadership role.” STEVE’S EXPERIENCE BRINGS THE KNOW-HOW THAT WINS OUTSTANDING RESULTS FOR WESTCHESTER.

A State Assemblyman 91st District A Chair – Assembly Science and Technology Committee A Former long-time Counsel and Chief of Staff to State Senator Suzi Oppenheimer A Mayor of the City of Rye (1998-2009) A Former chair, City of Rye Conservation Commission STEVEOTISASSEMBLY.COM A STEVE OTIS A LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION A Steve initiated the Water Infrastructure Improvement Act of 2015, the largest clean water grant program in the country.
To date - $3.4 billion in water grants to over 1200 projects statewide: creating jobs, making environmental projects possible, and significantly reducing the cost to local taxpayers.
Westchester communities have secured over $132 million in grants for 53 projects, including every Sound Shore community.
A Leading member of the legislature in advancing digital equity and inclusion programs.
Secured federal funding, works with statewide network of digital equity programs to provide digital literacy to individuals excluded from the essential digital world most take for granted.

AChair of Assembly Science and Technology Committee leading legislative efforts on fast-evolving issues, including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data and health record privacy, and electric vehicle charging.
A Tireless and successful advocate for Westchester school districts, local governments, and not-for-profits.

A Each year Steve passes cutting-edge legislation protecting workers, consumers, student athletes, and crime victims and is a leader on issues affecting the environment, reproductive rights, flood mitigation, storm recovery, and coastal resiliency.

“My priority is always to make state government more responsive to the needs of Westchester, to secure state funding to lower the burden on local property taxes, and to fight and win policy battles of importance to the Sound Shore communities I serve.” FOR MORE INFORMATION ABOUT STEVE’S WORK ON ISSUES AFFECTING WESTCHESTER, GO TO: STEVEOTISASSEMBLY.COM RE-ELECT STEVE OTIS STATE ASSEMBLYMAN RUNNING ON DEMOCRATIC (ROW A) AND WORKING FAMILIES (ROW D) LINES ELECTION DAY – NOVEMBER 3 EARLY VOTING STARTS OCTOBER 24 PAID FOR BY FRIENDS OF STEVE OTIS

Local impact.
Steve Rhoads is fighting for public safety, affordability, and a better Nassau County.
Explore the issues Where Steve stands Explore each issue for priorities, actions, and supporting legislation.
Prioritizing Public Safety Restoring Judicial Discretion by repealing bail reforms and restoring judicial discretion in pretrial release decisions.
See More Delivering Affordability & Tax Relief Delivering Historic Tax Relief by proposing the largest personal income tax cut in New York State history.
See More Combating Hate & Antisemitism Protecting Students from Antisemitism by denying state-funded tuition assistance to students who engage in antisemitic behavior.
See More Protecting Our Environment Expanding Environmental Protection by securing more than $2 billion in funding to safeguard New York’s environment.
See More Fighting for Individuals with Disabilities Opposing cuts to the Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program (CDPAP) and joining advocates in the fight to restore CDPAP.
See More Supporting Small Businesses Expanding R&D Tax Relief by expanding the Excelsior R&D Tax Credit to cover additional research and development expenses.
See More Empowering Women Expanding IVF Access by improving access to in vitro fertilization treatments.
See More Preserving Election Integrity Requiring Voter Identification by requiring valid government-issued photo identification for voting.
See More Investing in Education & Protecting Parental Rights Expanding School Mental Health Services by establishing a Mental Health Services Coordinator Program for schools.
See More Protecting Our Seniors Expanding Alzheimer’s Awareness by increasing awareness of programs supporting individuals with Alzheimer’s and dementia.
See More Delivering Results for Our Veterans Honoring Purple Heart Recipients by designating New York as a Purple Heart State.
See More Fighting for NUMC Protecting Local Healthcare by securing $50 million for Nassau University Medical Center to support continued access to healthcare.
See More Investing in Infrastructure Improving Local Roads by delivering a $50 million increase in CHIPS funding for local road and infrastructure improvements.
See More Preserving the American Dream Protecting Affordable Housing by ensuring rent-controlled apartments remain available to those who need affordable housing.

added: Skip navigation menu Meet Dave Issues Events Get Involved Endorsements Plan to Vote Donate Meet Dave Issues Events Get Involved Endorsements Plan to Vote Donate My values The Four Foundations These are the four foundational pillars of a person’s life and a fair society’s health.
When any of the four are missing or deficient, life can be more desperational than aspirational; hope becomes just a distant dream.
As a state representative, I will devote my time and energy to ensuring the Four Foundations are accessible to everyone.
And I'll pursue that goal by reaching across the aisle, because protecting these pillars shouldn't be a partisan issue.
My dream is not just to preserve our heritage, but to build Ohio into a state that invents, leads, and progressively shapes the future.
A place of inclusion, prosperity, and hope that we can all proudly call home.

Shital sagare February 23, 2026 Understanding N-Formyl Peptide Receptor 2: A Key Player in Immune Regulation The human immune system is a highly intricate network designed to protect the body from pathogens, tissue damage, and inflammation.
Among its many components, receptors on immune cells play a critical role in detecting and responding to danger signals.
One such receptor, N-Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 (FPR2), has emerged as a crucial mediator in immune regulation and inflammation resolution.
Click Me FPR2 is a member of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) family, primarily expressed on neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages, and certain epithelial cells.

Shital sagare February 23, 2026 Herpes Labialis Drugs: Effective Treatments for Cold Sores Herpes labialis, commonly known as cold sores, is a recurrent viral infection caused primarily by the herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1).
It manifests as small, painful blisters, typically around the lips and mouth, and can cause discomfort, itching, and cosmetic concerns for affected individuals.
Although there is no permanent cure for herpes labialis, various drugs and treatment strategies can help manage symptoms, reduce the duration of outbreaks, and prevent recurrences.
Herpes Labialis Drugs Market The cornerstone of treatment for herpes labialis is antiviral therapy.
Oral antiviral medications such as acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir are widely used to target HSV-1.
These drugs work by inhibiting viral replication, helping to reduce the severity and duration of outbreaks.

For patients with frequent or severe episodes, physicians may recommend suppressive therapy, which involves taking antiviral medication daily to decrease the frequency of outbreaks and reduce the risk of transmission.

This victory belongs to every mother who fought to be heard, every family who deserved better, every volunteer who knocked on doors, every donor, and every person who believed that a survivor could become a lawmaker.
From surviving a near-fatal postpartum hemorrhage #ago to representing District 68 in the Georgia State House, this moment is proof that lived experience belongs in the halls of power.
We ran on dignity, equity, and action.
Now, the real work begins.
Let’s get to work for District 68.

With so much gratitude, State Representative-Elect Timoria McQueen Saba MY PLATFORM › DONATE › Our priorities Fighting for Our Community Family and Maternal Health I will fight to turn Georgia’s “F” grade in health into an “A”, and expand access to affordable care.
Housing I will fight for affordable housing and emergency rent and mortgage assistance.
Affordability I will work to close the wage gap, expand paid leave, and affordable childcare.
Public Schools I will push for fully funded public schools and increase teacher pay.
Environment I will demand transparency and accountability on the negative impacts of data centers and other environmental issues.
Voting Rights I will protect access to the ballot box for every Georgian.

added: TISHA BENOIT Here’s the Plan DEBATE TALKING POINTS: I’m running to represent the people of Arizona, not a political party.
This campaign is about bringing people together around shared concerns, practical solutions, and a government that listens.
No matter how you are registered or whether you identify with any party at all, you deserve to be heard, respected, and represented.

ECONOMY — Cost of Living, Inflation & Jobs When I talk to people across Arizona, I hear the same thing over and over: “I’m working, but it still feels like I’m falling behind.” That is the economic issue we should be talking about.
Government can tell us inflation is improving, but families experience the economy at the grocery store, at the gas pump, when they pay their insurance bill, and when the rent or mortgage comes due.
Arizona’s unemployment rate was about 4.9% in August, but simply having a job isn't enough if that paycheck doesn't cover basic living expenses.
My approach is neither Republican nor Democrat.
It's practical.
First, we need to stop policies that unnecessarily increase the cost of everyday goods, energy and housing.
Second, I want to make it easier to start and grow a small business.
Small businesses create opportunity, but they're buried under paperwork, regulations and rising costs.
Third, we need workforce training tied to actual jobs: construction, healthcare, advanced manufacturing, technology and skilled trades.
Not everyone needs a four-year degree.
I would support apprenticeships, vocational education and micro-grants that allow someone to gain a marketable skill quickly.
And Washington must recognize something very simple: government spending has consequences.
We cannot spend endlessly and then act surprised when Americans feel the consequences.
The economy should work for the nurse, the teacher, the small-business owner, the retiree and the young family trying to buy their first home.
My economic philosophy is simple: make it easier to work, easier to build, easier to start a business and easier for families to keep more of what they earn.
HOUSING Housing has become one of the clearest examples of how government can fail people from several directions at once.
Young people wonder whether they'll ever be able to buy a home.
Seniors worry about rising property taxes and rents.
Working families may have good jobs and still struggle to find something they can afford.
I don't believe the answer is simply another giant federal housing program.
We have to increase supply.
That means working with state and local governments to reduce unnecessary barriers that make housing more expensive and slower to build.
It means encouraging starter homes, townhomes, smaller homes, accessory dwelling units and housing designed for seniors who want to downsize.
We should look at federal land where appropriate and determine whether portions can responsibly support housing and infrastructure.
But I also believe we need to protect existing neighborhoods and recognize that Arizona cannot approve unlimited development without considering water, roads, schools and public safety.
Those two ideas can coexist.
I also want greater transparency around institutional investors buying large numbers of single-family homes.
Families shouldn't have to compete on an uneven playing field with enormous investment funds.
And homelessness requires more than simply putting someone into temporary housing.
Mental health, addiction treatment, employment services and transitional housing need to work together.
Housing policy doesn't have to be ideological.
Build more.
Remove unnecessary barriers.
Protect Arizona resources.
Help people move toward ownership rather than permanent dependency.
Because the American dream shouldn't become something only wealthy Americans can afford.
WATER AND CLIMATE In Arizona, water isn't an environmental talking point.
Water is economic security.
Water is housing security.
And frankly, water is Arizona's future.
As of late August, Lake Mead was only about #% full and Lake Powell about #% full.
Arizona is already transitioning from simply banking excess Colorado River water toward using stored reserves to help manage shortages.
So I don't think we have the luxury of turning water into another partisan fight.
I support conservation, but conservation alone isn't enough.
Arizona needs an aggressive water innovation strategy.

That means wastewater recycling, aquifer recharge, better agricultural technology, leak reduction, capturing stormwater where practical, and researching desalination and new water-generation technologies.
Agriculture matters, cities matter and economic development matters.
The goal shouldn't be pitting one against another.
I also believe future large developments and water-intensive industries should demonstrate where their water is coming from before taxpayers inherit the problem later.
On climate, I take a similar approach.
I believe in science, innovation and environmental responsibility.
But I don't believe working families should be punished with dramatically higher energy bills in the name of environmental policy.
We should pursue solar, nuclear, geothermal, storage, efficiency and emerging technologies while maintaining a reliable electrical grid.
Arizona can become a laboratory for water technology and next-generation energy.
My position is conservation without extremism, innovation without ideology and a commitment that Arizona families come first when we make decisions about our natural resources.
BORDER SECURITY AND IMMIGRATION I believe two things can be true at the same time.
A sovereign country has an absolute right and responsibility to secure its border.
And America can still be a country that welcomes legal immigration.
For too long, Washington has forced Americans into choosing between those two ideas.
I reject that choice.

Border security means adequate Border Patrol personnel, technology, physical barriers where they're effective, surveillance, roads and infrastructure, and stopping fentanyl, trafficking and criminal organizations from entering this country.
Arizona understands this better than Washington because we live with the consequences.
But our immigration system itself also needs reform.
Someone who wants to immigrate legally shouldn't have to navigate a dysfunctional system for years while people who ignore the process move ahead of them.
We need faster immigration courts, faster decisions on asylum claims, stronger verification systems and a modern legal immigration system that responds to America's workforce needs.
And Congress needs to do its job.
Immigration should not remain permanently broken because both political parties find it useful during elections.
People who commit violent crimes or pose national-security threats should be removed.
At the same time, enforcement should be professional, constitutional and humane.
This shouldn't be about being anti-immigrant or pro-open border.
I'm neither.
I'm pro-legal immigration, pro-border security and pro-common sense.
Secure the border.
Fix the legal system.
Stop trafficking and fentanyl.
And give people who follow the rules a functioning pathway.
Most Americans are somewhere in the middle on this issue.
So am I.
HEALTHCARE I've spent much of my professional life in healthcare, and one thing is painfully obvious: America doesn't really have a healthcare system.
We have a sick-care payment system.
We need to end the chronic disease epidemic.
We spend enormous amounts of money, yet patients still delay care because they don't know what something will cost.
In 2025, approximately 26.7 million Americans went the entire year without health insurance.
I was one of them.
But insurance coverage is only part of the problem.
You can have insurance and still struggle to afford the deductible, medication or specialist visit.
I want healthcare reform centered around four things.
First: price transparency.
Patients should know the price before receiving routine care.
Second: competition .
Hospitals, insurers, pharmaceutical companies and pharmacy benefit managers should not be protected from competition.
Third: prevention .
Medicare and other programs spend enormous amounts treating chronic illness after it develops.
We should place much greater emphasis on nutrition, metabolic health, early screening and evidence-based preventive care.
And fourth: patient choice .
Patients should be able to choose qualified practitioners and treatments without Washington unnecessarily standing between the patient and their healthcare provider.
I don't support throwing out everything we have and starting over with a massive government-controlled system.
But maintaining the status quo isn't acceptable either.
My goal is not government-run healthcare or corporate-run healthcare.
It's patient-centered healthcare.
More transparency.
More prevention.
More competition.
More choice.
And ultimately, healthcare that ordinary Americans can actually afford to use.
EDUCATION Arizona has fallen to 50th on the national education lists.
We need to fix that now!
Education should prepare a young person to build a life.
There’s no reason why Arizona couldn’t be in the top 10 when we are leading the way in technology and engineering with some of the best companies at forefront of these industries.
Somewhere along the way, we started acting as though success meant every student following exactly the same path.
I don't believe that.
Some students should go to universities.
Others may become electricians, nurses, welders, coders, dental hygienists, plumbers, technicians or entrepreneurs.
Every one of those paths has value.
Arizona should have excellent public schools, strong charter schools, career and technical education and meaningful options for parents.
I support school choice, but I also believe public schools must be strong because the majority of our children will continue to attend them.
Teachers should spend their time teaching, not drowning in bureaucracy, or spending their own money on school supplies.
We need to reallocate funding to support our teachers who are preparing the next generation of our future.
And we need much stronger financial literacy, civics and practical life skills.
Before a student graduates, they should understand credit, compound interest, taxes, budgeting, student loans and basic entrepreneurship.
I also want employers partnering directly with high schools and community colleges so education reflects the jobs that actually exist.
Washington's role should be limited.
Most education decisions belong with parents, teachers, school boards and states, not federal administrations.
But Congress can support apprenticeships, career training and greater transparency around federal education spending.
My standard isn't whether an education policy came from the left or the right.
It's much simpler: Can a child read?
Can they think critically?
Do they understand their choices?
And when they graduate, do they have a skill that allows them to support themselves?
If the answer is yes, we're succeeding.
DATA CENTERS Arizona has become one of America's major technology hubs, and that's good for our economy.
But growth has to make sense.
Data centers are a perfect example.
They support artificial intelligence, cloud computing and technologies our economy increasingly depends upon.
But they also consume enormous amounts of electricity, and some facilities can require significant water and infrastructure.
APS says an average-sized data center in its territory can require as much electricity as roughly 64,000 homes , and Phoenix ranks second in North America for proposed data-center development.
SRP similarly says large-scale facilities can consume hundreds of megawatts and that data centers are projected to be its fastest-growing customer segment.
So my position is not, “Stop data centers.” My position is: growth should pay for growth.

If a billion-dollar corporation needs new substations, transmission infrastructure or significant water resources, Arizona families shouldn't unknowingly subsidize those costs through their utility bills.
We should require transparency regarding water consumption, electricity requirements, backup generators, noise and infrastructure needs before projects are approved.

And I'd encourage next-generation facilities that use recycled water, closed-loop cooling, renewable and nuclear energy, battery storage and technologies that dramatically reduce resource consumption.
Arizona should absolutely welcome innovation.
But economic development should improve the quality of life of the people already living here.
Technology should serve Arizona.
Arizona shouldn't become a utility company for the technology industry.
That's the balance I would bring to Congress.
FEDERAL SPENDING AND NATIONAL DEBT This may be the least exciting subject in Washington, but it may eventually become one of the most important.
The federal government has normalized spending far more money than it collects.
For fiscal year 2026, the Congressional Budget Office projected approximately $7.4 trillion in spending against $5.6 trillion in revenue.
That’s a $1.9 trillion deficit.
And net interest on the debt alone is projected to exceed $1 trillion this year.
Think about that.
We're spending roughly a trillion dollars just servicing debt and, money that can't fix a bridge, educate a child, protect the border or help a veteran.
And both parties contributed to this.
Republicans cannot call themselves fiscally conservative while ignoring deficits under Republican administrations.
Democrats cannot pretend every problem can be solved with another federal spending program.
As an Independent, I don't owe either side an excuse.
I would require major legislation to clearly identify what it costs and how we're going to pay for it.
I'd push for aggressive audits of federal programs, elimination of duplicative programs and stronger efforts against fraud and improper payments.
I also want a bipartisan long-term commission addressing our fiscal trajectory before a crisis forces decisions on us.
I don't support suddenly cutting benefits people spent their lives paying into.
But refusing to discuss long-term solvency isn't compassion.
It's avoidance.
We inherited this country.
We don't own it.
We have a responsibility to leave the next generation opportunity, not simply a stack of unpaid bills.
FOREIGN POLICY My foreign policy begins with a very simple question: How does this protect the security, prosperity and freedom of the American people?
I don't believe America should retreat from the world.
And I don't believe America should police every conflict in the world.
Those are the two extremes.
America should maintain the strongest military in the world, not because we want war, but because strength helps prevent war.
Our allies matter.
NATO matters.
Our relationships in Asia matter.
But alliances have responsibilities on both sides, and our partners must contribute meaningfully to their own defense.
China is both an economic competitor and our most significant long-term strategic challenge.

We should protect American technology and critical infrastructure, strengthen domestic manufacturing, protect semiconductor supply chains and reduce dangerous dependencies without pretending we're going to completely disconnect the world's two largest economies.
Regarding conflicts such as Ukraine and the Middle East, I believe Congress has a responsibility to ask hard questions before committing American money or weapons: What is the objective?
What is the cost?
What is the exit strategy?
And how does this advance American interests?
We should support our allies while continuously pursuing diplomacy and preventing regional wars from becoming global wars.
And Congress must reclaim its constitutional responsibility over war.
Presidents: Republican or Democrat, shouldn't have unlimited authority to involve America indefinitely in foreign conflicts.
My philosophy is peace through strength, diplomacy before war, strong alliances and America strategically engaged without becoming the world's permanent policeman.
That's not isolationism.
And it's not interventionism.
It's responsible American leadership.
removed: TISHA BENOIT Here’s the Plan HERE'S THE PLAN: In Arizona, I’ve watched the same systemic problems: health crises, water shortages, crime, and broken immigration go unaddressed for too long.
I’m ready to bring real-world experience and innovative thinking to a system that desperately needs both.
Her campaign focuses on seven pillars of renewal : Strong Economy and American Dreams — Arizona isn’t just growing, it’s driving the next chapter of America’s economy.
From semiconductor production to aerospace, defense innovation, and logistics, we’re at the center of it all.
Leadership means staying bold and forward-focused.
In Congress, I’ll push to cut unnecessary regulations, strengthen pro-growth tax policies, expand American manufacturing, and tackle inflation head-on.
Our economy should work for the people who show up every day, not just large institutions or bureaucratic systems.
When we support working Americans, we create strong, stable jobs across the Valley and put our country on a more responsible fiscal path at the same time.
Public Health & Wellness — Advancing “Make Arizona Healthy Again” initiative to strengthen access to preventive first healthcare and fix the bankrupt system.
The U.S. healthcare system spends more per capita than any other developed nation, yet struggles with chronic disease, access disparities, and rising costs.
Restructure discussions need to focus on shifting from reactive disease treatment to proactive health optimization.
We need to provide safety and shelters to protect vulnerable women and children through safe houses with enhanced security and survivor-led mentorship programs.
Transparency in Government — Trust in government isn’t something we can talk about, it’s something we have to earn back through action.
Washington has operated behind closed doors for far too long, and it’s time to return power where it belongs: with the people.
I believe those elected to serve shouldn’t be using their position for personal financial gain.
That’s why I support clear rules that prevent members of Congress from trading individual stocks so decisions are made in the public’s best interest, not for private profit.
Transparency also means showing up and doing the job responsibly.

When critical funding decisions put Arizona families at risk, like the threat of missed paychecks or economic instability, I will always push for practical, bipartisan solutions that keep our government functioning and protect the people who depend on it.
Accountability.
Integrity.
Results.
That’s how we restore faith in leadership and build a government that truly serves its people.
Education & Future Generations — Expand federal support for vocational education grants, promote skilled trades partnerships and modernize high school career-track programs.
We can’t fix education with a single policy or quick solution, we’ll fix it by realigning the entire system.
That means creating the right incentives so schools are rewarded for outcomes, not just compliance.
It means empowering parents with choice and giving teachers the support and respect they need to actually lead in the classroom.
And most importantly, it means reconnecting education to the real economy, so students graduate with skills, opportunities, and a clear path to a successful future.

Immigration Revision — Building structured and secure pathways that respect both law and life with secure and orderly border management using policy that focuses on controlling entry while maintaining lawful trade and travel.
Securing our border, reversing failed open-border policies, and focusing on real, enforceable solutions.
That means prioritizing the removal of dangerous criminal offenders, fully supporting our law enforcement, and taking action to stop fentanyl before it reaches our communities.
Arizona families deserve to feel safe, and the men and women who protect us deserve unwavering support.
I’m committed to delivering both.

Opioid Crisis Response & Unhomed — Strengthening prevention, rehabilitation, and mental health access with community outreach partnerships, extend federal grants for recovery centers and incentivizing sober house living.
District 04 keeps chasing the same problem instead of solving it—clearing streets without a real plan, only to see tents return within days or pop-up locations with no longterm stability.
It’s costly, ineffective, and ultimately inhumane.
The solution is a structured, results-driven approach: first, offer immediate alternatives through bridge housing like leased motels or apartments, along with options for family reunification.
No one is left without a path forward.
Then, restore the area by cleaning, repairing, and making it safe again.
Finally, maintain it with ongoing oversight and community-focused improvements to ensure the problem doesn’t return.
This isn’t about temporary fixes, it’s about lasting solutions.
Law Enforcement & Fire Support — Ensuring those who protect us have the resources and respect they deserve.
Public safety systems depend on trained personnel, modern equipment, sustainable funding, mental health support, and strong community relationships.
Effective policy balances operational readiness with transparency and oversight.
Data Centers & Responsible Growth — Arizona can lead in AI and technology without sacrificing our water, health, safety, or quality of life.
Data centers must be held to clear standards for water and energy use, noise, backup-generator emissions, and responsible placement away from homes and schools.

These facilities can require significant electricity and, depending on their cooling systems, substantial water resources, which deserves careful scrutiny in a desert state where every gallon matters.
I support greater transparency and accountability so communities know the true impact before projects are approved.
Innovation should strengthen Arizona, not drain the resources our families depend on.

Senate.
In part, Maggie’s List wrote: “Maggie’s List is proud to count U.S.
Sen.
Tom Cotton of Arkansas among our Congressional Partners supporting the mission to elect more conservative women to federal office.
Before entering Congress, Sen.
Cotton served nearly five years on active duty in the U.S.
Army, including combat tours in Iraq and Afghanistan.
He later represented Arkansas in the U.S.
House before being elected to the Senate.
Today, Sen.
Cotton serves as Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and as a member of the Armed Services, Energy and Natural Resources, and Joint Economic Committees.
He also serves as Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference.
Maggie’s List appreciates Sen.

Cotton’s partnership and his support for increasing the number of conservative women serving in federal office.” “I’m grateful for the support of Maggie’s List, and I’m proud to support their work electing conservative women.
Our country needs strong, conservative leaders to fight the radical left, secure our border, and keep America strong.
I look forward to continuing our partnership to elect more of them,” said Senator Tom Cotton.

Monday through Friday, October 19 - October 30, 8am to 5pm, and Saturday, October 31, 9am to 1pm Sedgwick County Election Office- new location 3639 N Comotara Monday through Friday, October 19 - October 30, 8am to 5pm, and Monday, November 2, 8am to 12pm Satellite Voting Center Locations Tuesday, October 27 - Friday, October 30, 10am to 6pm, and Saturday, October 31, 9am to 1pm NO STATE INCOME TAX ON SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFITS: One of the groups hit the hardest with property taxes are seniors living on a fixed income.
While we were only able to provide them with a $70 additional property tax cut, we did something else that will help them a lot.
We totally eliminated the state income tax on all Social Security Benefits.
The chart below shows how significant this tax cut can be.
For Example, a married couple with total household income of $75,000 or more that receives $50,000 a year in Social Security would receive a $2422.50 tax cut just from the Social Security exemption.
That is on top of the $70 property tax cut and the income tax cut that would apply to their non-social security income.
This cut should help a lot of Kansas seniors pay their property taxes and be able to stay in their homes.
I NCOME TAX CUTS FOR ALL KANSANS- Biggest percentage cuts for lower income taxpayers.
SB 1, the bi-partisan tax cut bill passed during the 2024 Special Session also provides income tax cuts for all Kansans.
The biggest percentage tax cuts are for those making less than $75,000.
For example a married couple making $30,000 would get a 67% tax cut.
Married couples making less than $26, 560 will no longer owe any Kansas Income Taxes. the chart below shows the tax cut at various income levels.
The chart below it shows the tax cuts for Single taxpayers.
The main provisions of this tax cut include raising the Standard deduction for everyone.
And it changes the Kansas tax rates from the current three brackets of 3.1%, 5.25% and 5.7% to a two bracket system of 5.2% and 5.58%.
But for most taxpayers the biggest tax cut comes from the huge increase in the personal Exemption provided by the bill.
For Single Taxpayers the personal exemption is raised from $2,250 to $9, 160.
For Married taxpayers their personal exemption is raised from $4,500 to $18, 320.
That is why this tax bill provides the biggest relief for lower income taxpayers and eliminates income tax completely for many Kansans.

Minnesotans for Affordable Health Insurance • Bob Stein, Chair Facebook: MNforAffordableHealthInsurance Twitter: @AffordableHealthMN Website: www.affordablehealthinsmn.com Email: mnforaffordablehealthins@gmail.com 24 Sep Thursday, 9:41 AM · 2026 Brad attends the Arc Minnesota- SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council and SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota), Forum September 22nd Brad was pleased to attend this forum, sponsored by ARC Minnesota - SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council, SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota, this past Tuesday.
This event focuses on issues that impact people with disabilities in our community.

Questions asked, and addressed were questions on how candidate plan to listen to self-advocates when making decisions on waiver services/supports, Transportation, Housing, and Fraud (to make sure the fraud doesn't negatively impact people who need those services) Brad’s answer to the fraud question was, in part: “Don’t allow it to happen to begin with—in the first place!” Internal controls are designed to identify and prevent fraud before it reaches the level we have witnessed.
When state employees raise concerns about potential fraud and those concerns are not adequately addressed, that demands accountability.
Brad put it this way: “When your checking account shows unusual activity, your financial institution doesn’t simply look the other way.

It will freeze the account and contact you to determine whether the activity is legitimate or whether your account has been compromised.” The federal government took similar action when concerns arose that Minnesota funds were not being used for their intended purposes.
Minnesota has a fiduciary responsibility to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure public funds are being used as intended.
Brad believes that responsibility must be taken seriously.
Whistleblower warnings should be investigated, internal controls should be followed, and fraud should be stopped before it happens, not after taxpayers have already lost millions of dollars.
As Brad said, “FRAUD-FRAUD-FRAUD!” It should be a top priority to protect Minnesota taxpayers and the essential services that depend on those dollars.
This is not simply a federal issue, as our Democratic friends choose to blame.
Minnesota state agencies had responsibility for administering and overseeing many of these programs, and the state’s own Legislative Auditor has found significant failures in oversight.
In the Feeding Our Future case, for example, the Legislative Auditor concluded that inadequate oversight by the Minnesota Department of Education created opportunities for fraud.
The people of Minnesota deserve accountability from those responsible for overseeing these programs, including Governor Tim Walz and state agency leadership.
Minnesotans also deserve to know where elected officials stand when serious failures occur, and whether they are willing to publicly demand accountability, stronger safeguards, and meaningful reform.
Brad's opponent has mostly been silent.

Brad's opponent has spoken publicly about fraud in a newsletter, and a few media outlets, and supported anti-fraud legislation, but we have not found one, not one public press release specifically condemning the scale of Minnesota's fraud or publicly assigning responsibility for the failures to Governor Walz and his administration, nor her party, for allowing this massive fraud to occur.
Some Democrats have called for Minnesota to look forward and avoid politicizing the issue.

But accountability requires more than simply moving forward, it requires asking how these failures happened, who was responsible for oversight, and what must change to prevent them from happening again.
Minnesotans deserve transparency and accountability from their state government.
As your elected State Representative, Brad Trahan will not hesitate to ask tough questions, hold government accountable, and call out fraud, waste, and abuse when it occurs.
As many people know, Brad is the proud father of Reece, a 26-year-old with severe autism.
For the past 23 years, Brad has been not only a dedicated parent and advocate for his son, but also a passionate self-advocate for countless individuals and families facing similar challenges.

His personal experience has given him a firsthand understanding of the importance of ensuring that people with disabilities have a strong voice, access to needed services, and the opportunity to live with dignity and support.
In 2016, Brad led an initiative for 13 years, 8 months, for Mayo Clinic to provide autism therapy, benefits for their employees' dependents, diagnosed with autism.
Just recently in 2026, Brad led initiative to expand access to specialized oral care, in hospital, under anesthesia for individuals with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
There were only five (5) hospitals in the State of Minnesota that provided this case for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities, and Brad was able to add a sixth, Olmsted Medical Center.
A project he started in January 2025, and completed in June 2026.
Also, recently in late August 2026, Brad identified a gap in Mayo Clinic Insurance Policy, regarding oral anesthesia care and provider coverage.
Brad worked closely with Mayo, Medica (Plan Administrator), and MN DHS.
May0 agreed that there was a gap, and effective October 1st, they were going to add OMC as an approved Provider for this Oral anesthesia care for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
Brad achieved this task in just one-weeks time!
In 2007, Brad led an initiative to bring Project Lifesaver to Olmsted County/City of Rochester.
This technology helps those most vulnerable, if they wander away.
It helps law enforcement find those missing individuals quickly.
In 2009, Brad led efforts to raise $25,000 to help get Project Lifesaver implemented in other SE Minnesota Counties.
In 2015, Brad led efforts at the state level for “Lifesaver Technology” grant in St.
Paul, secured $80,000 for 2 years, for law enforcement to invest in this technology for the communities they serve.
Brad has not simply talked about his commitment to the disability community, he has demonstrated it through action, advocacy, and meaningful changes in legislation and insurance coverage.

8 Sep Tuesday, 4:32 PM · 2026 Brad does a Ride-Along with the Rochester Police Department September 5th On Saturday, September 5th, Brad had the opportunity to ride along with the Rochester Police Department from 7:00 p.m. until 4:00 a.m.
Brad can’t tell you enough how blessed we are to have the police officers we do in Rochester, under the leadership of Police Chief James Franklin and his Command Staff.
It was an incredible learning experience!
Throughout the evening, Rochester Police Officers were going from call to call to call.
Domestics, fights, weapons calls, people in crisis, and much more.
These men and women simply kept answering the call.
They don't always get the credit they deserve.
One moment during the night really stuck with Brad.
After responding to a serious call and getting things settled down, an RPD Sergeant noticed a 6-year-old little girl and her teddy bear nearby.
The Sergeant took the time to get police stickers for the young girl and her teddy bear.
They weren't the reason the officers were there.
But they noticed her.
And that small act made that little girl's night.
That's Rochester Police.
Friends, we need to stop talking about the seriousness of mental health in our community without coming together around serious, long-term solutions.
What I witnessed Saturday night reinforced that for me.
Our officers are responding to mental-health crises, domestics, fights, weapons calls and other difficult situations, sometimes simultaneously and just blocks apart.
And when you add drugs and alcohol to the equation, these situations can become even more challenging.
We cannot continue to band-aid mental health in our communities.
We need long-term solutions that address the underlying problems and provide law enforcement with the resources and partnerships they need.
Throughout the night, I saw Rochester Police Officers demonstrate professionalism, patience, compassion and courage.
Brad is a member of the Rochester Police Civil Service Commission, and it's important for him to get out from behind the meetings and see firsthand what is happening in our community.
It also gives Brad the opportunity to reconnect with some of the officers the Commission has helped approve for hire.

If elected to serve in the Minnesota House, Brad intends to make this an annual commitment, staying connected with the Rochester Police Department and the Olmsted County Sheriff's Office and listening directly to the men and women who serve our community.
We must make sure law enforcement has the tools, resources and support they need to do their jobs effectively and safely, both for themselves and for the people they serve.
RPD—THANK YOU.
Every one of you is truly policing from the heart.
You demonstrated courage, professionalism and compassion throughout Saturday night's shift.
And a special thank you to SGT JH and the entire RPD team for an incredible night, and, most importantly, for keeping our community safe with everything you encountered.
You’re all amazing.
Brad will always be a staunch advocate for Law Enforcement, Fire, and ALL First Responders.
Thank you for serving Rochester.

27 Aug Thursday, 10:21 AM · 2026 Brad attends Minnesota Transportation Alliance Meeting August 26th From 1:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.
Candidates were invited to take part in The Minnesota Transportation Alliance with regards to Transportation in Minnesota and why transportation matters.
Representatives from MNDOT, City, and the County were present as well as representatives with public transit.
I then was happy to join a six other candidates, from area races, for a few Q&A questions on Transportation.
We also toured the Rochester International Airport runway, construction project - IMPRESSIVE!
Transportation needs unified cooperation from Federal, State, County, Township, and City government.
Safety is always a priority.
We need to maintain existing infrastructure, and spend tax dollars wisely.
We also must always listen to the stakeholders using our roadways.
Transportation drives economy dollars with our roads, rail, air, and waterways.
Transportation also involves Public Transportation who transport individuals to medical appointments, and more.
And, we can't forget about the need of our rural transportation needs, especially for those that have disabilities and/or are unable to drive for a variety of reasons.
Everyone is fighting for dollars.
One area I would like to see explored (just one idea) is that current purchases of auto parts goes into the Highway User Tax, Transportation, and the "General Fund".
I don't like to see monies always going into the "General Fund" I'd like to explore the idea to put auto parts purchases ALL into Transportation to help them make up some funding.
Funding is allocated in many different ways, but also depends highly on motor vehicle registration tax (license tabs fees).
We need to explore that more.
I do not support our current license tab fee structure.
You can register a 2024 Tahoe in Wisconsin for $95, and in Minnesota for $905.
I would have liked to see more of our 2023 $18 billion surplus used for matters such as this, and imagine if we cleaned up our budget and tackle fraud!
Transportation is bi-partisan issue, but we just need to work hard to determine funding, and explore other avenues perhaps then just depending extremely high license tab fees that are out of control.
We have to be good stewards of taxpayer dollars, as well as assess what is the return on investment on each project.
But, safety is always going to be the top issue!

24 Aug Monday, 10:57 AM · 2026 Brad meet with HHS Secretary RFK Jr., FEMA Director Cameron Hamilton, DOJ and Others - Announcement of Project Lifesaver National Autism Alert System August 21st A Family, a Community, and a Commitment to Protect Our Most Vulnerable For Brad, this moment is deeply personal.
Standing alongside his family—Brenden, Reece, Joanie, and Payton, and with HHS Secretary Robert F.
Kennedy Jr. during the announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system for individuals with autism who go missing was a powerful reminder of why this work matters.
Brad has spent years advocating for programs that help protect individuals with autism and other vulnerable members of our community.
One of those efforts began right here in Rochester and Olmsted County with Project Lifesaver, a program designed to help law enforcement locate individuals who may wander or become missing.
Brad helped bring Project Lifesaver to Rochester and Olmsted County by raising $15,000 to launch the program.
He then continued that effort, raising another $25,000 to help seven additional Minnesota counties implement Project Lifesaver.
In 2015, Brad led an initiative that resulted in an $80,000 Minnesota state grant to help additional law-enforcement agencies establish Project Lifesaver programs.
Brad emphasizes that none of this happened because of one person.
“This has always been about collaboration.
So many people have stepped up and made a difference.

When it comes to protecting our most vulnerable, we have to work together and do everything we can.” Brad is especially proud of the Rochester Police Department and Olmsted County Sheriff's Office Project Lifesaver teams, whose dedication continues to make a difference for families throughout our community.
He also recognizes the continued efforts of Rochester Autism Advocacy, including its work helping families navigate the application process and identify individuals who may benefit from the program.

Brad is grateful as well for the past support of RTAAF, and for the leadership and administrative support provided by Sheriff Borchardt, Sheriff Torgerson, and Police Chief Franklin, whose belief in the program helped make this community effort possible.
For Brad and his family, this isn't simply about policy.
It's about people.
It's about families.
And it's about making sure that when a vulnerable person goes missing, every possible resource is available to help bring them home safely.

The announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system represents an important step forward, and Brad is proud to have been part of the local effort that helped demonstrate what is possible when families, advocates, law enforcement, government, and communities work together.

27 Jul Monday, 5:49 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce Linking Leaders & Industry at Novios Cafe July 27th Brad Trahan attended the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce, Linking Leaders & Industry form at Novios Cafe, and Co-Owner, Dalton Shirley.

Brad was joined by MN House District GOP, 20-B, endorsed candidate, Sara Bertschinger. • Minnesota Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML): Dalton shared that he recently received his updated quarterly tax statement and that his taxes have more than doubled compared to what he was paying before PFML was implemented.
He also shared that, to date, none of his employees have used PFML.
It raises serious questions about whether the program is sustainable in its current form and the impact it is having on small businesses.

(My belief is that it is not sustainable in its current format – Brad) • Small business challenges: Dalton employs between 22 and 30 people, which classifies his business as a large employer under the program.

He reminded everyone that restaurant margins are extremely tight, making every added cost and regulation a significant challenge. • Credit card processing fees: I asked Dalton whether he pays credit card processing fees only on food and beverage purchases or if those fees also apply to customer tips.
His answer was eye-opening.
Dalton does not pass these processing fees on to his customers.
The credit card companies charge processing fees on food, beverages, and tips. • Looking ahead to 2027: When asked about his biggest concerns moving forward, Dalton’s answer was simple: “Regulations.
Regulations make it harder on small businesses to survive.” Once again, referring to PFML.

24 Jul Friday, 3:33 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester's 2026 Disability Summit July 24th Today, I had the opportunity to attend Rochester's 2026 Disability Summit at the Heintz Center.
I attended as a parent, caregiver, employment specialist, advocate, and political candidate.
While tremendous progress has been made to support individuals with disabilities and our aging community, there is still much more work to do.

No matter what role I serve in; parent, caregiver, employment specialist, advocate, or State Representative, you can count on me to work tirelessly for individuals with disabilities, our aging community, and their families.
One of the most important lessons I've learned over the past 24 years, since our son Reece was diagnosed with severe autism, is that disability can touch any family at any time.
We are all just one unexpected moment away from needing the same supports and services that so many rely on today.
Until disability affects you or someone you love, it's often difficult to fully understand how complex, challenging, and overwhelming navigating these systems can be.
That's why it's so important that we continue to listen, learn, and advocate for policies and services that help every member of our community live with dignity, opportunity, and support.
21 Jul Tuesday, 12:01 PM · 2026 Brad attends Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce's Linking Leaders & Industry event at Chick-fil-A Miracle Mile.
It was an honor and a privilege, as a candidate for Minnesota House District 25A, to attend the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce's Linking Leaders & Industry event at Chick-fil-A Miracle Mile.

I want to extend my sincere thanks to Matt and Crystal Stockdale, Owner/Operating Partners, for sharing both their personal journey to becoming Chick-fil-A franchisees and the inspiring story behind the Chick-fil-A brand.
Their presentation highlighted the company's strong values, commitment to servant leadership, and dedication to making a positive impact in our community.
Chick-fil-A employs more than 200 team members across its two Rochester locations, with an annual payroll of approximately $3 million.

Beyond serving great food, they are deeply invested in our community through partnerships with Community Food Response, Channel One Regional Food Bank, and by providing more than 200 meals each month to pediatric patients at Mayo Clinic.
Matt and Crystal also shared valuable insights into the economic challenges facing local businesses with candidates seeking local, county, and state offices.
I appreciated the opportunity to hear firsthand how government policies affect employers and the business community.

Among the topics discussed were: • Rochester's EV charger requirement, which requires one EV charging station for every 50 parking spaces, even when demand is limited. • Extending the allowable work hours for 14- and 15-year-olds from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., which they described as a significant opportunity to better support their workforce. • The financial impact of implementing Minnesota's Paid Family and Medical Leave program. • The need for a more streamlined and accessible pathway to citizenship for individuals who want to live and work in our communities. • Housing affordability and the rising cost of living, which continue to affect employees and employers alike.
These are important conversations that deserve thoughtful discussion at every level of government.
Working together, we can identify practical solutions that help businesses grow, support employees, and strengthen our local economy.
Thank you again to Matt and Crystal, the entire Chick-fil-A team, and everyone who made this event possible.
Your commitment to your employees, your customers, and the Rochester community is truly inspiring.
Thank you for welcoming us into your story, sharing your experiences as franchise owners, and demonstrating what it means to lead with integrity and service.
Thank you, Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce, for creating this opportunity for us candidates.
It was “my pleasure” to learn more about the Chick-fil-A organization and to express my appreciation for everything Chick-fil-A does to make Rochester a stronger and more caring community.

15 Jun Monday, 3:27 PM · 2026 Vehicle Registraton Costs; Wisconsin vs.
Minnesota This is unacceptable for Minnesotans.
The current formula-based system needs to be re-evaluated.
On top of the base registration tax, drivers are also paying a stack of additional costs, including plate fees, filing fees, technology surcharges, and public safety fees.

While funding roads and bridges is essential, and vehicle registration revenue is directed into the Highway User Tax Distribution Fund (HUTDF), the current structure places an uneven burden on Minnesota drivers.
There was some work done on this this year, but it doesn't take effect until January 2027, with some fees reverting back to 2023.
More work needs to be done, however.

If elected to represent MN House District 25A, I will work across the aisle to reform this system and pursue a more reasonable, transparent flat-fee model, similar to what most other states use for vehicle registration.
