title.after: ÚLTIMA HORA: Un ataque frustrado contra José Vega pone de manifiesto grandes conflictos de intereses financieros en la campaña de Ritchie Torres | Jose Vega para el Congreso 2026 | Rescatemos el Bronx!

added: Skip to content Lea la última declaración Dignidad, o sometimiento Leer → Conoce a Jose Prensa Noticias Declaraciones Eventos Propuestas de Política Una verdadera política de Medicare para Todos Hacer del Bronx el centro de reindustrialización de Estados Unidos Una reforma migratoria robusta Un enfoque revolucionario de política exterior: Paz a través del Desarrollo Todas las Políticas Eng Donar Registrarse ÚLTIMA HORA: Un ataque frustrado contra José Vega pone de manifiesto grandes conflictos de intereses financieros en la campaña de Ritchie Torres 31 de julio de 2026 Necesito que distribuyas esta declaración.
Necesito que contribuyas con mi campaña.

Donar Ahora → José Vega, candidato independiente de LaRouche para el Congreso por el Distrito 15 del Bronx, emitió la siguiente declaración el 31 de julio: Se está llevando a cabo un intento despreciable para obstaculizar mi campaña y la de mi amiga Diane Sare, candidata independiente de LaRouche a la presidencia, para que no les informemos cómo nos está llevando la Clase Epstein a una Tercera Guerra Mundial; para que no les digamos cómo podemos detenerlos; y cómo podemos resolver el mal llamado “problema migratorio” por medio del desarrollo económico.
Estoy dando la batalla y sé cómo hacerlo, pero necesito tu ayuda.
El lunes 27 de julio, Politico publicó un artículo difamatorio contra mí, en el que se me acusa de haberme pagado a mí mismo un sueldo mensual de $2.419,66 dólares entre enero y mayo del 2026.
El autor, Jason Beeferman, describe esto como un “salario modesto”. ¡Que bastardo presuntuoso!
Multiplica esa cifra de $2.419 dólares por 11 meses, desde enero hasta noviembre —el tiempo completo del ciclo de campaña para el Congreso del 2026.
Eso es un total de $26.609 dólares al año. ¿Se supone que yo “me estoy enriqueciendo”?
El umbral de pobreza para un adulto soltero en la ciudad de Nueva York es de $23.304 dólares.
Mi remuneración es totalmente legal.

Y mi “trabajo”, por llamarlo de alguna manera, por más de un año, ha sido ha sido el de postularme para un cargo político a tiempo completo contra Ritchie Torre, el candidato de AIPAC (Comité Estadounidense–Israelí de Asuntos Públicos), quien contaba con $14 millones de dólares antes de que comenzara la campaña.

El artículo difamatorio de Politico tiene la intención de pararme, y a los estadounidenses como yo, en particular a quienes son jóvenes y pobres, para que no digan la verdad y denuncien los asesinatos en Gaza; que no hablen en contra de la anexión ilegal de Cisjordania al estilo del Ku Klux Klan; y en contra de la Clase Epstein, que está perpetrando todos estos crímenes, incluyendo el difunto Lindsay “Ladybug” Graham.
Es también para evitar que se conozca el Plan Oasis , la solución de LaRouche a la guerra en el sudoeste de Asia, y a la pobreza en el Sur del Bronx.

Mis adversarios en la Clase Epstein detestan a las personas trabajadoras, en especial a las personas trabajadoras pobres en el Bronx, de quienes un 29% vive en la línea de la pobreza o por debajo de ella.
El alquiler medio en el Bronx oscila entre los $3.100 y los $3.200 dólares al mes.

Político, así como otros periodistas y plataformas de noticias como ellos, están mucho más interesados en ‘avergonzarnos’ a mí —y a ti— por ganar apenas el salario mínimo, que en sacar a la luz la corrupción en la que el congresista Ritchie Torres y sus colaboradores están involucrados abiertamente.
Un amigo mío, un bloguero y periodista ciudadano, ha rastreado minuciosamente las finanzas de la campaña de Ritchie Torres.
La amplia red de financiamiento de campaña del congresista Torres —así como sus comités de campaña— se ha visto envuelta en importantes conflictos de intereses financieros.
Los fondos de su campaña se han destinado a empresas propiedad de personas que controlan las finanzas de Torres y toman las decisiones sobre los gastos.

Un ejemplo de esto es el Equality PAC, la entidad oficial encargada de la recaudación de fondos del Grupo Parlamentario LGBTQ del Congreso, del que Ritchie Torres es copresidente y principal financiador.
Torres transfirió más de $2.270.000 dólares al Equality PAC en este ciclo electoral.
El Grupo Parlamentario LGBTQ incluye a nueve miembros de la Cámara de Representantes y a un senador.
El director ejecutivo del Equality PAC es Jeff Larivee, quien “dirige los esfuerzos de reclutamiento de la organización, las actividades políticas y el proceso de recaudación de fondos”.
Larivee también resulta ser el director de finanzas de la campaña de Ritchie Torres, y el ¡principal recaudador de fondos políticos!

El Equality PAC ha gastado más de $2 millones 200 mil dólares en supuestos “gastos de funcionamiento”, entre ellos, tarifa aérea, hoteles, comidas, servicio de comida para los eventos, renta de la oficina, y así por el estilo.
También ha gastado sumas obscenas en consultoría.

Más del 50% de los “gastos de funcionamiento” del Equality PAC se pagan a una compañía que se llama “Rolla Group LLC”, que es una empresa de recaudación de fondos y consultoría política con sede en Washington, DC, cuyo dueño y fundador es nada menos que el director de finanzas de la campaña de Torres, Jeff Larivee.
Otra compañía, Political Animals LLC, propiedad de Timothy Brian Pryzbylski, el marido de Larivee, recibió un pago de $789.793,99 dólares de Equality PAC durante este ciclo electoral.
Political Animals también se encarga de gestionar casi todos los gastos del SuperPAC de Equality PAC.

Entonces, al mismo tiempo que actúa como el director de finanzas de la campaña de Torres, y como el director ejecutivo de Equality PAC —del que Torres es copresidente— Jeff Larivee y su marido han recibido el pago de millones de dólares por asesoramiento, por medio de su Equality PAC.
Esto es obviamente un enorme conflicto de intereses, y muchísimo más que $26.609 dólares. ¿Por qué Politico no se fijó en esto, y en cambio se fijó en mí?

Resulta que Jeff Larivee y su marido Timothy son propietarios de otra compañía de consultoría llamada “Rambleside LLC” que ha facturado entre $11.750 y $23.000 dólares al mes en concepto de alquiler a Equality PAC, además de más de $100.000 dólares en mobiliario y mejoras de las oficinas desde julio del 2025.

El domicilio de Rambleside LLC no es una oficina, sino una casa de $2.000.000 dólares que Larivee compró en julio pasado, justo antes de que comenzara a cobrar el alquiler a Equality PAC. ¡Así es el director de finanzas de campaña de Ritchie Torres!
Equality PAC ya ha sido objeto de investigación anteriormente por irregularidades financieras.

La ex tesorera del PAC, Jennifer May, se había declarado culpable en agosto del 2025 de haber desviado $1.500.000 dólares de los préstamos por daños económicos causados por desastres concedidos por el Gobierno Federal, que fueron emitidos durante la pandemia del COVID-19 para ayudar a pagar los gastos de funcionamiento ordinarios.
A May la descubrieron utilizando esos fondos para especular con criptomonedas, y fue acusada de fraude electrónico por la fiscal federal de Washington, DC, Jeanine Pirro.
No voy a dejar que los chacales y ladrones que están atacando mi campaña se salgan con la suya.

La gente en Gaza sigue muriendo; la gente en mi distrito tiene que soportar unos precios de alquiler desorbitados, edificios que se están colapsando, e infraestructura pobre; la clase Epstein, sea en la Casa Blanca, en el Congreso, en Wall Street, o en el Sur del Bronx, sigue actuando por encima de la ley.
Alguien tiene que detenerlos antes de que inicien una Tercera Guerra Mundial, que podría estar a semanas o incluso días.
Necesito que distribuyas esta declaración.
Necesito que contribuyas con mi campaña.
Necesito que respaldes a mi amiga Diane Sare en su campaña independiente a la presidencia de Estados Unidos.
Y necesito que votes por mí para llevarme al Congreso en noviembre.
En mi lucha por la gente de Gaza, por la gente del Sur del Bronx, y por los pobres en cualquier lugar, sea cual sea el resultado, yo soy el hombre más rico del mundo.

Donar Ahora → A mis vecinos del Bronx: Soy José Vega, candidato independiente al Congreso por el Distrito congresional 15, en contra de Ritchie Torres.

Para el día de hoy, probablemente ya todos ustedes deben haber escuchado la historia de Maricarmen Abascal, una señora de 87 años de edad en España, que fue desalojada de su apartamento a la fuerza (en el que había vivido por 70 años) cuando un fondo de inversiones que había comprado el edificio donde vivía ¡subió el alquiler en 230%!

Desafortunadamente su historia se ha vuelto un lugar común en España, en Alemania y en Estados Unidos, donde mucha gente está viendo que los alquileres y el costo de sus casas se ha disparado en los años recientes.
Un video de la señora Abascal, que tiene que usar silla de ruedas, en el que se muestra cómo la sacan a la fuerza de su apartamento en una camilla, circuló ampliamente a nivel internacional.
Desde su cama del hospital pidió: “¡Defended lo que es vuestro!”.
Dijo, “No he logrado defender mi casa, ¡pero sí he luchado para que los demás aprendan a luchar por la suya!”.
Los españoles respondieron.
Un gran número de personas se presentó dos días después para protestar a las afueras del edificio donde vivía Abascal.
Se desató la furia acumulada durante mucho tiempo contra el alza de los alquileres y la vivienda inaccesible.

Pronto, había manifestantes en más de 50 ciudades en España, con cientos de miles de personas en las calles, portando pancartas que decían, “Ni un desahucio más, ni un vecino menos, todos somos Maricarmen” y “Derecho a vivienda de precio justo”.
De pronto todo el mundo estaba viendo lo que sucedía.
Como resultado, se ordenó que Maricarmen Abascal regresara a su apartamento.
Había prevalecido un poder mayor que el dinero.

Un periodista español en el viaje de regreso de Francia a Roma le pidió al Papa León XIV que hiciera algún comentario sobre el caso de Abascal, y Su Santidad respondió: “¿Cómo es posible que suceda algo así? ¿Cuál es el problema en un sistema que permite que una anciana, además con discapacidad o con alguna dificultad sea echada de su casa?”.
La gente escuchó su mensaje.
Después de todo 1,2 millones de personas se habían congregado para escuchar al Papa en Madrid el 7 de junio, y cientos de miles más en otras ciudades españolas.
Al momento de escribir esto, Maricarmen Abascal ha fallecido en el hospital.
Ella iba a ser llevada de regreso a su apartamento luego de la furia justificada de la población española en contra de que la hubieran desahuciado.
Esta muerte pudo haberse evitado; fue un asesinato causado por la indiferencia depravada.
Sí, “todos somos Maricarmen”.
Nosotros también, sea donde sea que estemos en el mundo, somos víctimas de la indiferencia depravada.
Muchos que viven en el Sur del Bronx, donde yo vivo, son los más pobres de lo que se conoce como el distrito congresional más pobre de la nación.
El 35,8% de los residentes del Bronx gastan la mitad de su ingreso en el alquiler.
Si mensualmente utilizas el 50% solo en el alquiler, no tienes dinero para alimentos, ropa, y otras necesidades.
No tienes capacidad de ahorro.
Estás pagando mucho más de lo que puedes.
Estás siendo forzado a convertirte en un esclavo de la deuda, un criminal, o ambos.
Conoces la realidad de la experiencia de Maricarmen Abascal.
Conoces no solo “el costo de la vida”, sino el precio que se paga en términos de vidas humanas y en dignidad.
Los desahucios en España y en Alemania, las ratas en las escuelas de Francia, son también una experiencia diaria en Estados Unidos, y en mi distrito en particular.

Pero nuestros supuestos “representantes” en el Congreso, entre ellos Ritchie Torres, quien salió de las viviendas públicas del Bronx, no abordan la causa de fondo de la crisis de vivienda, de la inmigración, y la pobreza, a saber, la clase Epstein y su compromiso con un sistema imperial de 500 años, moribundo, que tiene una deuda que es imposible de pagar y guerras perpetuas.
Cuando yo inicié mi campaña para el Congreso, hice hincapié en que la lucha que debemos librar debe ser internacional, porque la solución es internacional.
Ya yo sabía que “Todos somos Maricarmen”.

Cuando yo enfrenté un desahucio personalmente, por protestar en contra de las condiciones de la vivienda de mi familia en el Bronx, luego de pedir ayuda a mis traicioneros representantes en el Congreso, me di cuenta de que mi situación sólo se abordaría enfrentando a lo que yo llamo la clase Epstein.
Y me di cuenta de que mi representante ante el Congreso, Ritchie Torres, nunca iba a hacer eso, porque él se sumó a la clase Epstein, y en especial a su guerra de despoblación contra los palestinos.
Así que intervine en contra de Torres.

Intervine contra él por su apoyo a la guerra en Ucrania, la guerra contra Gaza, y la guerra contra los pobres aquí mismo en el Bronx, todo ello llevado a cabo en favor de los intereses de la clase Epstein.

Torres está del lado del partido belicista internacional que desata estas guerras que ninguno de nosotros queremos, y está con la oligarquía financiera internacional que nos mantiene a todos endeudados.
Yo no me someto, y no voy a ceder.
No puedo hacer que la gente vote por mí, pero sí puedo hablar con la verdad.
Así que, esta es la verdad: Primero, en política internacional.

Para detener la masacre de los palestinos, existe una propuesta, el Plan Oasis para el Sudoeste de Asia, que ha sido discutido y ha sido apoyado por diversas personalidades israelíes, palestinas y otras personalidades a nivel internacional.
Yo también lo respaldo.
La pregunta es, ¿me enviarías al Congreso para luchar porque se implemente?
Segundo, mi contribución en el Congreso para la política nacional.

Necesitamos una red nacional de 42.000 millas de un sistema ferroviario electrificado de alta velocidad, que viaje a una velocidad de 150-mph o más, lo que llevaría a la construcción de nuevas ciudades en todo el país.
China ya tiene más de 45.000 millas de un sistema ferroviario de ese tipo.
Tenemos que crear millones, posiblemente tantos como 10 millones de nuevos empleos productivos, y estos trabajos darán empleo para jóvenes de entre 18 y 29 años.
Esto va a requerir de un programa masivo de entrenamiento como Estados Unidos no ha visto en décadas, que incluya las manufacturas, la construcción, de mecanización, y de ingeniería.

Debe haber un intercambio científico y de mano de obra calificada entre Estados Unidos y China, y otras naciones que hayan sacado con éxito a cientos de millones de personas de la pobreza y han construido ciudades nuevas.
Tercero, de las 200.000 unidades de vivienda en el Bronx, al menos 50.000 tienen que ser considerablemente rehabilitadas o reconstruidas.
Viviendas nuevas deben sustituir a las que están en mal estado, casuchas de propietarios sin escrúpulos que simplemente deberían derribarse.
Los intereses financieros se van a oponer a eso. ¿Quién se une a la pelea?
Ya sea que votes por mí, o que no vayas a votar de ninguna manera, lo que tienes enfrente aquí es lo mismo que tuvo que enfrentar la señora de 87 años en España.
En su nombre, hago la misma petición que ella hizo, a todos ustedes: “¡Por favor, luchen!”.
Tienen la opción de elegir: entre dignidad y sometimiento.
Toda la gente tiene esa opción, siempre.
Mi campaña al Congreso es sobre la independencia de la corrupción, de la cobardía, y la negligencia.

Durante los días que quedan, voy a mantenerme firme, y quiero que te unas a mí y te declares independiente de los asesores, de los donantes, de los grupos de presión que te han robado el voto para defender a la clase Epstein.

added.text: ACCOMPLISHMENT Cut Taxes and Protected the Middle Class Last year, Governor Moore cut taxes for the middle-class, with 94% getting a tax break or having no changes on their tax bill. This year, Governor Moore turned a projected $1.5 billion cash shortfall into a $250 million surplus with no new taxes or fees, all while maintaining strong fiscal discipline and long-term stability for the state. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Delivered Record Reductions in Violent Crime Under Governor Moore and LG Miller, Maryland has seen dramatic improvements in public safety, including a 44% drop in homicides and a 40% drop in non-fatal shootings statewide. Baltimore City recorded its lowest number of homicides in nearly 50 years, driven by historic funding for law enforcement and public safety resources. The Moore-Miller administration has also advanced criminal justice reforms, including expanding eligibility for record expungement to help more Marylanders access jobs and Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Expanded Access to Affordable Healthcare Governor Moore has taken action to make healthcare more accessible and affordable for Marylanders by expanding coverage, making efforts to lower the cost of prescription drugs, removing barriers to care, and requiring insurers to cover recommended vaccines. His administration is focused on ensuring more families can get the care they need, regardless of their zipcode. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Improved Government Efficiency and Cut Waste Governor Moore launched a Government Modernization Initiative to streamline state operations, cut red tape, and deliver services more effectively. These efforts are already saving taxpayers an estimated $50 million in a single fiscal year while making government work better for Marylanders. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Invested Historic Amounts in Public Education For four consecutive years, the Moore-Miller administration has delivered record funding for public schools, including a $10.2 billion investment in K-12 education this year alone. These investments are improving outcomes statewide, with gains in reading and math scores and a 58% reduction in teacher vacancies. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Jumpstarted Maryland’s Economy After years of stagnation, Maryland has created over 55,000 new businesses – with new establishments growing 39% faster than before the pandemic. The Moore-Miller administration has also secured major economic wins, including a $2 billion AstraZeneca expansion and the new Sphere National Harbor projected to bring in over $1 billion annually and create thousands of jobs. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Made Energy More Affordable and Accelerated Clean Energy Governor Moore is lowering energy costs for Maryland families while investing in a cleaner, more reliable energy future. His administration is advancing clean energy initiatives that lower costs, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, create good-paying jobs, and position Maryland as a national leader in building a more affordable and sustainable energy economy. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Made Housing More Affordable and Accessible Through one of the most comprehensive housing packages in recent history, the Moore-Miller administration is increasing supply, lowering costs, and expanding access to homeownership. Nearly 4,000 rental units were financed in one year – the highest level in almost a decade. Learn More

Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Delivered Record Reductions in Violent Crime Under Governor Moore and LG Miller, Maryland has seen dramatic improvements in public safety, including a 44% drop in homicides and a 40% drop in non-fatal shootings statewide. Baltimore City recorded its lowest number of homicides in nearly 50 years, driven by historic funding for law enforcement and public safety resources. The Moore-Miller administration has also advanced criminal justice reforms, including expanding eligibility for record expungement to help more Marylanders access jobs and Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Expanded Access to Affordable Healthcare Governor Moore has taken action to make healthcare more accessible and affordable for Marylanders by expanding coverage, making efforts to lower the cost of prescription drugs, removing barriers to care, and requiring insurers to cover recommended vaccines. His administration is focused on ensuring more families can get the care they need, regardless of their zipcode. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Improved Government Efficiency and Cut Waste Governor Moore launched a Government Modernization Initiative to streamline state operations, cut red tape, and deliver services more effectively. These efforts are already saving taxpayers an estimated $50 million in a single fiscal year while making government work better for Marylanders. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Invested Historic Amounts in Public Education For four consecutive years, the Moore-Miller administration has delivered record funding for public schools, including a $10.2 billion investment in K-12 education this year alone. These investments are improving outcomes statewide, with gains in reading and math scores and a 58% reduction in teacher vacancies. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Jumpstarted Maryland’s Economy After years of stagnation, Maryland has created over 55,000 new businesses – with new establishments growing 39% faster than before the pandemic. The Moore-Miller administration has also secured major economic wins, including a $2 billion AstraZeneca expansion and the new Sphere National Harbor projected to bring in over $1 billion annually and create thousands of jobs. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Made Energy More Affordable and Accelerated Clean Energy Governor Moore is lowering energy costs for Maryland families while investing in a cleaner, more reliable energy future. His administration is advancing clean energy initiatives that lower costs, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, create good-paying jobs, and position Maryland as a national leader in building a more affordable and sustainable energy economy. Learn More

ACCOMPLISHMENT Made Housing More Affordable and Accessible Through one of the most comprehensive housing packages in recent history, the Moore-Miller administration is increasing supply, lowering costs, and expanding access to homeownership. Nearly 4,000 rental units were financed in one year – the highest level in almost a decade. Learn More

removed: Skip to content Main Menu Home About Donate Yard Sign Meet Ashley Judge Wysocki is the Presiding Judge of the 301st Judicial District Court of Dallas County, a family court.
She was previously the Presiding Judge of the 254th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, another family court.
As a family Court judge, she hears divorce suits, child custody matters, and adoptions, among other family matters.
She has presided over hundreds of bench trials, jury trials, and contested hearings.
Judge Wysocki formerly served the citizens of Dallas County as Judge of the 162nd District Court and 44th District Court, both civil courts.

In civil courts, Judge Wysocki presided over jury trial, bench trials, and contested hearings involving commercial disputes, property disputes, personal injury, and contractual disputes, among others.
Trusted.
EXPERIENCED.Knowledgeable.
Professional Prior to taking the bench, Judge Wysocki worked at a national, Am Law 100 law firm in Dallas, Texas.

Judge Wysocki’s over ten years of family, civil, and commercial law experience prior to taking the bench includes having represented businesses and individuals in contractual disputes, bankruptcy, personal injury, and property disputes.

When practicing family law, Judge Wysocki represented both men and women in a wide range of family law matters including divorce, complex property division, post-dissolution enforcement actions, and Premarital and Post-Marital Agreements.
She is also trained in collaborative divorce.
Education J.D.
Texas Tech University School of Law, with honors M.B.A.
Texas Tech University, with honors B.A.
University of Texas, cum laude Judge Wysocki attended Texas Tech University School of Law on a full academic scholarship.
In law school, she was a member of the Board of Barristers competing in both Mock Trial and Moot Court, National Mock Trial Team, and was named a Distinguished Trial Advocate.
Judge Wysocki also completed a judicial externship during law school with Chief Justice Brian Quinn of the 7th Court of Appeals.
Prior to law school, Judge Wysocki graduated in three years with honors from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor’s Degree in Anthropology.
During undergraduate, Judge Wysocki was a member of the Alpha Lambda Delta/Phi Eta Sigma Honor Fraternity and National Society of Collegiate Scholars.
She was also a member of the Zeta Tau Alpha sorority.
Personal Judge Wysocki lives in Dallas with her husband and three amazing children, ages 12, 9, and 2.
Her husband is also a respected family law attorney in Dallas, Texas.
The Wysockis enjoy spending their free time at their ranch in East, Texas.

She is also a breast cancer survivor.

Yassamin is fighting for working families and demanding accountability from our nation’s leaders.

Affordability As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’s Lowering Costs Task Force, Yassamin is dedicated to passing bold, commonsense policies to bring down the cost of living and make the American Dream a reality for all Americans.
Yassamin believes Congress must pass Medicare for All before more hardworking Americans are crushed by medical debt and surprise bills.
We must build more affordable housing , provide free childcare to working families, and expand essential programs like SNAP and the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
She also supports raising the federal minimum wage for the first time in nearly two decades – to a liveable wage of $25/hour.
Abolishing and Prosecuting ICE Yassamin believes we must abolish and prosecute ICE, Stephen Miller, and all those responsible for its sadistic mass deportation agenda, full stop.

In the 119th Congress, she introduced the Fund Schools, Not ICE Act, which would transfer over $39 billion in unobligated ICE funding to Title I grants for local school districts; the Drain ICE Act, which eliminates $75 billion in ICE funding appropriated in the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act; the Studying Disastrous Impacts of Mass Deportations Act, which conducts a study on the long-term economic impacts of Trump’s immigration policies; and the Stop Inhumane Conditions in ICE Detention Act, which mandates reporting requirements about detainees in immigration detention facilities.

To date, she has conducted over 13 oversight visits at ICE detention facilities in Arizona, Texas and Florida to witness firsthand the brutality and horrific conditions of these centers and hear from detainees firsthand.

She is a proud champion of the American Dream and Promise Act and believes we need to pass comprehensive immigration reform that will protect our diverse communities, including Dreamers (DACA recipients), refugees, and asylum seekers, to ensure that they have the necessary tools to succeed.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety Yassamin is deeply alarmed by the rapid advancement of highly capable AI frontier technologies.

She is a proud supporter of legislation introduced by Congressman Greg Casar and Senator Bernie Sanders to ban artificial superintelligence, pause advanced AI research, and establish a new federal agency to regulate AI technologies and the AI industry.
She believes trillion-dollar AI companies are putting their record profits over the safety of the entire globe.

A champion of AI safety in the Congress, Yassamin has led the way in demanding that Trump convene an international effort to set global AI rules — as the U.S. has led in the past with nuclear and aviation safety.

She also knows that the Trump Administration’s refusal to regulate the AI industry — despite dire warnings about potential threats to the safety and economic well-being of Americans — is all part of the corruption story, with Donald Trump and his sons all profiting off of AI related investments.
Oversight and Accountability Yassamin is leading the charge to impeach Pete Hegseth for incompetence, mismanagement, and crimes.
As a member of the powerful House Oversight Committee, she is investigating Jeffrey Epstein’s crimes and the biggest cover-up in American history, led by Donald Trump and his administration.

She is demanding answers on Trump family corruption, Big Oil’s pay-to-play, the administration’s violations of court orders, and its illegal dismantling of federal agencies, undermining public health, and the indiscriminate firing of government employees.
Campaign Finance Yassamin does not take a single dime in corporate PAC money, and supports legislation to Abolish Super PACS to get big money out of politics .

Climate and Clean Energy Yassamin serves as the Ranking Member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the House Natural Resources Committee, where she works tirelessly to hold Big Oil and corporate polluters accountable.
She deeply values our public lands and national monuments, and is committed to protecting them against attacks by congressional Republicans and the Trump administration.

Yassamin believes we must aggressively invest in clean energy projects and energy efficiency, electrify our transportation system, and ensure that we not only meet our climate and emissions commitments, but surpass them.
Data Centers and Water Yassamin supports halting the construction of more massive data centers until we have a comprehensive plan to protect our water, our electrical grid, and Arizona ratepayers.
She believes we must tackle our state’s historic water crisis and prioritize the people of Arizona first.
Foreign Policy Yassamin believes in the power of multilateral institutions and negotiations through diplomacy.
She started her career at the United Nations as an advisor on the Secretary-General’s Climate Action Team where she helped to deliver the historic Paris Climate Agreement.
She has been fighting for an end to Trump’s horrific and illegal war in Iran, including with accountability for unacceptable civilian deaths and potential war crimes in U.S. strikes in Minab, Iran.
She firmly believes that the administration’s actions in Cuba and the Caribbean are outrageous and immoral.
She is proud to stand with U.S. allies in NATO, for the sovereignty of other nations like Denmark and Canada, and to support Ukraine in its fight for freedom.
Yassamin knows that the only way to have lasting and enduring peace in the Middle East is for there to be an independent, viable, and prosperous Palestinian state alongside a secure Israel.
She strongly opposes the Netanyahu government’s appalling actions in Gaza, Lebanon, and the West Bank which undermine that future, and she is a cosponsor of the Block the Bombs Act .
Gun Violence Yassamin believes gun violence is a national emergency and a public health epidemic.

She is an original co-sponsor of the Stop Online Ammunition Sales Act of 2026 that would require federally licensed dealers to verify the identity of individuals purchasing ammunition online by checking a photo I.D.
She supported H.
R.
1307, the Office of Gun Violence Prevention Act of 2025, a bill that would reestablish an Office of Gun Violence Prevention, which was dismantled by the Trump Administration.
Healthcare as a Human Right Yassamin is a proud cosponsor of Medicare for All and believes healthcare is a human right.
She believes we must also address the glaring inequities in our healthcare system, which has historically ignored or downplayed the pain of women and people of color.
That’s why Yassamin introduced the HER Agenda, which includes: The Gynecologic Pain Management Study Act, to address barriers to access for pain management options during gynecologic procedures.
The Reproductive Healthcare Leave Act, to provide 12 days of paid leave for reproductive health reasons like extreme menstrual pain, menopause symptoms, vasectomies, and more.
The Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) Research Act, to study under-researched and underdiagnosed PMDD, a severe form of PMS.
Housing Yassamin believes that housing is a human right and that we must build more housing (and quickly!), invest massively in social housing projects, and expand support for low-income renters.

That’s why she introduced the HAVEN Act, which expands housing voucher programs to cover every eligible household, expands eligibility, and bans landlords from discriminating against voucher-holding tenants.
She was also proud to support and pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act – the most significant housing legislation in decades.
Voting Rights Yassamin is a cosponsor of the John R Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
She is supportive of a House bill calling for restoring and strengthening the Voting Rights Act, eliminating the Senate filibuster, and enacting structural changes to the Supreme Court.
She supports the Youth Voting Rights Act that establishes a private right of action to enforce the Twenty-Sixth Amendment, which prohibits denying or abridging the right to vote based on age.
Dignity for Veterans Yassamin proudly serves the men and women who have served in uniform.
She co-sponsored the Major Richard Star Act to ensure that combat-injured veterans receive their full earned benefits.
She is a proud supporter of the Protect Veteran Jobs Act to reinstate veterans who were dismissed from federal employment without cause since President Trump took office.
She endorsed the Caring for Survivors Act that would increase monthly financial benefits and expand eligibility for the surviving spouses of our fallen veterans.
She supported the Veterans Infertility Treatment Act to make infertility care part of VA-provided health care benefits.
She strongly advocates for the Supporting VA Families Act that would guarantee unpaid parental leave for all employees of the Department of Veterans Affairs.

added: Skip to content Zac Martin For South Dakota About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate Home / Blog From the campaign October 16, 2026 Are You Registered?
The October 19 Deadline Has No Mercy South Dakota closes voter registration Monday, October 19.
Movers, name changes, and first-time voters get caught by this every cycle.
Five minutes fixes it.
Neighbor, Every election cycle, thousands of South Dakotans show up to vote and discover they cannot.
Not because of fraud, or politics, or anything dramatic.
Because of a deadline that passed quietly while life was busy.
This is your five-minute insurance policy against being one of them.

The deadline Voter registration for the November 3 election closes Monday, October 19, at the end of business, which is three days from today, and South Dakota law makes no exceptions about it whatsoever: no same-day registration, no grace period, and no credit for having meant to get around to it.
Who gets caught Three groups, every single cycle.
Movers: if you changed address since you last voted, even across town, your registration needs updating to your current address.
Name changes: marriage, divorce, any legal name change needs a fresh registration.
First-timers: new residents and every young person who turned 18 since the last election.
If any of those is you or someone at your dinner table, keep reading.
How to check, right now Go to sdsos.gov and use the Voter Information Portal.
Thirty seconds tells you whether you are registered and where.
If everything matches your current life, you are done.
Forward this to someone who moved and go about your day.
How to register or update Pick up a registration form at sdsos.gov, the Pennington County Auditor's office, the DMV, or most public libraries.
Current address, signature, done.
Get it to the county auditor by end of business Monday.
There is no fee and no test, and the form takes less time than a coffee order.
Why I am pushing this so hard Because everything else is downstream of it.
Every position I have published since July, every ballot question, every local race: none of it includes you unless this one piece of paperwork is current.
You get two votes for State House in District 32.
Do not leave them on the table over a form.
Check yourself.
Then check on a mover. sdsos.gov.
Strong Families.
Strong South Dakota.

added: Skip to content Zac Martin For South Dakota About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate Home / Blog From the campaign May 17, 2026 Property Tax Relief Without the Sales Tax Hike SB 245 trades one tax for another.
What SB 245 actually does SB 245 passed in 2026 and was signed March 30.

It creates a homeowner property tax reduction fund, seeded with a one-time transfer of $55,896,576 from the general revenue replacement fund on July 1, 2026, and fed from August 1, 2027 by three-tenths of a point of the state sales, use and contractor's excise taxes.
The fund can only reduce the school general levy on owner-occupied homes.
The Department of Revenue estimates the result at up to a fifteen percent average reduction for those homes.

The mechanism depends on a sales tax increase: South Dakota's statewide rate goes back from 4.2 percent to 4.5 percent on July 1, 2027, because the 2023 cut expires, and three-tenths of a point, the size of that increase, is what feeds the homeowner fund from August 1, 2027.

SB 96 was the cleaner path and it is already law The same 2026 session passed SB 96, which lets counties impose an optional county gross receipts tax in exchange for reducing owner-occupied property taxes.
removed: Skip to content Zac Martin For South Dakota About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate Home / Blog From the campaign May 17, 2026 Property Tax Relief Without the Sales Tax Hike SB 245 trades one tax for another.
What SB 245 actually does SB 245 passed in 2025 and takes effect July 1, 2026.
It creates a property tax reduction fund out of three-tenths of the sales tax, plus a one-time fifty-six million dollar transfer from state reserves.
The Department of Revenue estimates the result at up to a fifteen percent average reduction for owner-occupied homes.

The mechanism depends on a sales tax increase: South Dakota's statewide rate is scheduled to go from 4.2 percent to 4.5 percent in 2027, and three-tenths of every additional sales tax dollar funds the property tax cut.

SB 96 was the cleaner path and it is already law The same 2025 session passed SB 96, which lets counties impose an optional county gross receipts tax in exchange for reducing owner-occupied property taxes.

added: Skip to content Zac Martin For South Dakota About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate About Platform Affordability Family Court Your Ballot The Choice Tribal Relations Blog Get Involved Volunteer Donate Tribal relations · District 32 In the room before January.
Not after the votes.
Rapid City's Native community lives in this district: North Rapid, downtown, and the neighborhoods around Oglala Lakota College's He Sapa Center on Knollwood Drive.
This page is what I will carry to Pierre for you, who I will carry it with, and how to grade me on it.
The commitments Invite me to your table Where I stand Eight years ago a family court case brought my son to Rapid City, and I followed him here.
I learned what it is to face a system that was never built for the family in front of it.
Many Native families learned that generations before I did.
The Rural Ethnic Institute put District 32's candidates in front of Native voters at Oglala Lakota College's He Sapa Center in May and again on October 16, 2026.
I was at that table both times.
The commitments below are the ones I made there, in writing, so they can be checked.
I will not promise what a state legislator cannot deliver.
What a state representative can do is show up before the session, carry the bills that keep dying in committee, and come back to be graded.
That is what this page is.
I am not here to speak for you.
I am here to make sure Pierre stops speaking over you.
Zac Martin · He Sapa Center, Rapid City What I will carry to Pierre Seven commitments.
Each one with a receipt.
Nothing here is a slogan.
Every item names a bill, a vote or a date, so you can check it against the record and against me.
01 1 of 7 Meet first.
File second.
Before the 2027 session opens, I will sit down with tribal leaders and with the Native organizations that do the work in Rapid City.
The bills I file in January will have your fingerprints on them.
That is a schedule, not a speech, and you can hold me to the dates.
Receipt The 102nd South Dakota Legislature convenes in January 2027.
02 2 of 7 A state and tribal consultation commission.
In 2026 Rep.

Eric Emery asked the House to create a South Dakota and tribal consultation commission: the Governor, the Secretary of Tribal Relations, one representative from each of the nine tribes and one lawmaker from each chamber, meeting at least every three months, with the Governor reporting every state initiative that touches the tribes before it lands.
HB 1190 had seven sponsors and died in House State Affairs, 8 to 4, without a floor vote.
I will co-sponsor it and work the committee, not just sign the sheet.
Receipt HB 1190 (2026).
Deferred to the 41st legislative day in House State Affairs, February 9, 2026.
03 3 of 7 A yearly report to tribes on the taxes collected on their land.
The state collects sales and other taxes on reservation land under agreements with the tribes, and the tribes cannot see the numbers.

Twice in two sessions a bill asked the Department of Revenue to send each tribe a yearly estimate of what was collected in its agreement area, split between remote and in-person sellers, with a back report for the prior six years.
HB 1018, with fifteen sponsors from both parties, died in House Taxation in 2025, 12 to 1.
SB 241, carried by Sen.
Tamara Grove, died in Senate Taxation in 2026, 4 to 3.
Neither got a floor vote.
I will co-sponsor it a third time.
Receipt HB 1018 (2025), House Taxation, 12 to 1.
SB 241 (2026), Senate Taxation, 4 to 3.
04 4 of 7 ICWA, written into state law.
The Indian Child Welfare Act is federal law, and Pennington County is where South Dakota was taken to federal court over it.
A federal judge in Rapid City found in 2015 that the county's emergency custody hearings violated the law.
That ruling was later set aside on procedural grounds, not because the facts changed.
The next Legislature should write state law that puts South Dakota ahead of the federal floor, not behind it.
I will write that bill with tribal child welfare leaders, not for them.
Receipt Oglala Sioux Tribe v.
Van Hunnik, D.S.D.
2015; vacated by the Eighth Circuit in 2018 on abstention grounds.
The family court reform stack 05 5 of 7 Reentry that starts on day one, and treatment people can reach.

Native people are 39 percent of South Dakota's prison population and Native women return to prison at a rate of 66 percent, which is why reentry planning has to start the day a sentence begins and treatment has to be reachable from the reservation and the rural county.
That is not a statistic about a people.
It is a report card on a state.
The state's own reentry report said the same thing in August: nobody should leave prison without an ID, a Medicaid card and a place to sleep.
The women's prison in Rapid City has 96 treatment beds and a mother and infant unit.
The state built the model here.
I will hold the $650 million men's prison to it.
Receipt South Dakota Searchlight, December 17, 2025, Department of Corrections figures.
CSG Justice Center reentry assessment to the Correctional Rehabilitation Task Force, Rapid City, August 20, 2026.
Tough on violent crime.
Smart on the rest.
06 6 of 7 Tax fairness for the people who rent.
More than four in ten households in District 32 rent.
In 2026 Pierre cut property taxes for homeowners and will pay for it by letting the sales tax go back up next July.
A renter pays the sales tax at the register and the property tax inside the rent check, and gets none of the relief.
I will carry a renter's rebate so the people paying the tax finally see it, and a rule that the property tax share of a unit is disclosed to the tenant.
Receipt US Census ACS 5-year, table B25003: 42.2 percent of District 32 households rent.
SB 245 (2026), sections 2 and 6.
The affordability agenda 07 7 of 7 Every legal vote counts.
Every legal voter gets a straight answer.
I support proof of citizenship to register, and the 2026 law already counts a tribal ID as that proof.
I want a tribal ID accepted everywhere a driver's license is.

Then the part the state is failing at: nearly six thousand South Dakotans are now on a federal-only list that lets them vote for Congress and nothing else, and the state's own voter portal does not tell them.
Nobody should lose a state ballot without a letter that says why and how to fix it.
I will carry that fix.
Receipt SB 175 (2026), House 64 to 3, signed March 30, 2026.
South Dakota Searchlight, October 13, 2026: 5,735 federal-only registrants.
Elections and voting integrity The record Tribal bills in Pierre, 2025 and 2026.
On every tribal bill that reached the House floor these two sessions, both of District 32's current representatives voted yes.
I would have too.
The bills that mattered most at He Sapa never got a floor vote.
Those are the ones I will carry.

House 67 to 0.
Signed March 9, 2026.
Law HB 1175 (2026) Division of Criminal Investigation cooperation with tribes.
House 66 to 0.
Law.

House 63 to 3.
Law.

House 63 to 2.
Law.
Law HB 1006 (2026) Task force on Indian Medicaid managed care.
House 60 to 7.
Law.
Law HB 1002 (2025) Every certified educator takes a South Dakota Indian Studies course.
House 54 to 12.
Law.
Law HB 1190 (2026) State and tribal consultation commission.
Died in House State Affairs, 8 to 4.
No floor vote.
Died HB 1018 (2025) Annual Department of Revenue report to tribes on tax collections.
Died in House Taxation, 12 to 1.
No floor vote.
Died SB 241 (2026) The same report, Senate version.
Died in Senate Taxation, 4 to 3.
No floor vote.
Died SB 196 (2025) Oceti Sakowin Essential Understandings in public school curriculum.
Failed in the Senate, 7 to 28.
Never reached the House.

How to grade me A schedule, not a speech.
Trust is not something I can ask for in ninety seconds at a forum.
It is something you can measure in January.
1 Before January I sit down with tribal leaders and with Rapid City's Native organizations.
You set the agenda.
2 January to March The bills above are filed with co-sponsors and with your edits in them.
I report back on each one, including the ones that die.
3 After the session I come back to He Sapa and take the questions.
Grade me on what passed, not on what I said.
Invite me to your table Put me on your calendar.
Email me the date and the room, or call.
I will take the meeting on your terms and your schedule, and I will be there. zac@zac4sd.com (605) 600-3281 Join the team Vote Zac Martin Door by door.
Neighbor by neighbor.
Yard sign by yard sign.
This is a grassroots campaign for the heart of Rapid City, and that is exactly what it takes to win District 32.

removed: CHIP IN $10 TODAY TO SUPPORT ZACH NUNN >> ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER DONATE Close Trigger DONATE Combat Aviator and Congressman for Iowa’s Third Congressional District, Zach Nunn Achieves Strongest Odd-Year First Quarter Fundraising Nunn Raises Over $# into Campaign Committees in First Quarter, Most Raised Ever for a IA-03 Republican in First Quarter Non-Election Year Des Moines, I.A. – Combat aviator Zach Nunn, Republican Congressman in Iowa’s Third Congressional District, announced the strongest fundraising performance in an off-year quarter for any GOP candidate for the seat in history.

“I am humbled and honored by the outpouring of support for our campaign to send a proven leader to Congress who will fight for a secure border, restore our economy and deliver commonsense solutions for our district,” Nunn said.

“Kelly and I want to thank all the supporters, friends and families who came together to demonstrate the strong base of support needed to continue delivering real results for Iowans across the Third Congressional District.” “Washington liberals have set their sights on Iowa’s Third Congressional District, and they are prepared to pour hundreds of millions of dollars into deceptive, negative attacks to boost their slate of lousy candidates who support open borders, soft-on-crime policies, and reckless spending that fuels inflation,” said Nunn Campaign Manager Brendan Duffy.

“That is why hardworking Iowa families across the district are increasingly rallying around combat aviator Zach Nunn as the commonsense candidate who has established himself as the proven leader, proven fighter and proven winner for Iowans.” Key Takeaways on Nunn’s First Quarter Fundraising Total: Nunn’s fundraising performance outpaced first quarter odd-year fundraising quarters for all previous GOP candidates in Iowa’s Third District in history.
Nunn set a strong foundation for success with overwhelming support from Iowans and small dollar individuals, with over 6,700 of his campaign contributions coming from them.

added: CHIP IN $10 TODAY TO SUPPORT ZACH NUNN >> ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER ABOUT ISSUES UPDATES GET IN TOUCH VOLUNTEER DONATE Close Trigger DONATE Trone Garriott Finally Agrees to Debate Nunn on October 27, Two Weeks Into Early Voting Des Moines, IA – Combat aviator and U.S.
Representative Zach Nunn (IA-03) released the following statement after Sarah Trone Garriott accepted KCCI’s October 27 debate, more than a month after Nunn first accepted the station’s invitation.

“On the debate stage Iowans will have a clear choice between my record of delivering bipartisan results for all Iowans and my opponent’s radical record of wanting the largest tax increase in Iowa history and driving up costs for families and farmers,” said Rep.
Zach Nunn .

“Sarah Trone Garriott knows that record is hard to defend in front of Iowans, which is why she hid from this debate for more than a month, until nearly a third of voters in our district will have already cast their ballot.
Iowans expect better.

I said yes to this debate in September because Iowans deserve to hear from both candidates, and I stand ready to make my case on October 27.” Nunn accepted KCCI’s invitation in September and said yes to every debate date offered by the station before or during the first week of early voting.
Trone Garriott refused to debate until October 27, the latest first debate of any race for governor, U.S.
Senate or Congress in Iowa this cycle.
By that point in the 2024 cycle, more than 120,000 3rd District voters had already cast their ballot.
Read the full timeline of Sarah Trone Garriott dodging a debate HERE .
